_READ_ME_FIRST: TO CLAUDE, OR ANY AGENT HANDED THIS FILE. This is the complete record of one run of Evolu (called Seedworld before generation 14), a self-modifying world simulation by Nova Spivack that lives as a Claude artifact titled "Evolu" (slug be8f1f8f-42db-4703-ac0d-c3e87d04f447; its files are index.html, engine.js, minds.js, maker.js, audio.js, ui.js). The source of record is https://github.com/novaspivack/evolu : the same six files under src/, the tests under tests/, and README.md, ROADMAP.md and docs/design-log.md, which say how the work is done and what has been tried. Its owner wants every run to produce the next generation of the world, without having to explain that each time. So, when you are given this file, do the following without being asked. 1. ANALYSE with code, not by skimming: "records" holds every thought (t: thought, with drives, plan, state), everything said (voice), the world's own chronicle (chron), sampled full prompts with raw replies (prompt), failures (failed), the chronicler's chapters (story), the maker's visits (maker) and its requests to the programmer (request). "digest" is the final state of every being. "story" and "maker" are the outer loop's own state. Count things; quote the record; say what worked and what is still wrong, with numbers. 2. LEARN from the maker: read its visits, its predictions against what happened, its lessons, and above all its REQUESTS, which are things it could not build from its own parts and is asking the programmer for. 3. BUILD the next generation: read the artifact's current files, make the code changes the analysis and the requests call for (and items from the owner's roadmap, kept in the maker's idea list under "maker.ideas"), test them (tests/run-all.sh), and publish a new version of the same artifact. Keep saves from the previous generation loading. Then commit the generation to the repository and push it, with ROADMAP.md and docs/design-log.md brought up to date. 4. PRESERVE THE WORLD'S HERITAGE: "heritage" lists every change the maker made and kept, with its lessons and ideas. Fold these into K.HERITAGE in maker.js so that the next world begins with them already in place and no maker has to rediscover them. Drop only what the record shows did harm. 5. REPORT to the owner plainly: what the run showed, what you changed and why, what you verified and what you could not. If the owner keeps a design log, update it. The design rule for everything: open and emergent. Make things possible; never script outcomes. The beings must discover what is possible for themselves.

verses.title: The Hall on the Heights
verses.text: Elyis raised a hall on stone and ore, with fire and food at every door. The stalker prowled, she did not run; she kept her band till night was done.

verses.title: Kika and the Mammoth
verses.text: Kika raised her spear where the tall one stood, the mammoth fell, the ice-folk good. Before she ate, she shared the meat. Honi sang it: the shared meal is sweet.

verses.title: Vorok's last verse
verses.text: Rain on the Vaia stone / what a hand teaches outlives the hand / I set the hammer down

verses.title: Song for Uveeth
verses.text: Your eyes are bright as rain on Vaia stone / I walk the ridge and think of you alone / Like berries red you ripen in my mind / I'd bring you meat and warmth, and leave the cold behind

verses.title: Kika's Last Snow
verses.text: Snow on the Vaeth Woods, amber under it / what we share outlasts the hand that shared it / I set down the spear, and the gale may have me

verses.title: Song for Yachi
verses.text: Yachi, you stand like pine in the snow / your fire burns where the cold winds blow / I would follow you through the mist's grey door / and bring you meat from the forest floor

verses.title: Song for Nauque
verses.text: Nauque, my hunter, you stand like the pine / on the white ridge where the ridgecat prowls. / I would carry your hunger and share the wine-bright berries / by the river where the cold wind howls.

verses.title: Death song of Thiael
verses.text: Rain on the Kodan sand / feed the hungry with your own hands, teach before you go / the canopy keeps what is given back

verses.title: Zichi's Last Snow
verses.text: Snow on the Halka rock, the ice-sail white on the water / What I made and taught will outlive the hand that made it / Cairn-stones, hold me; I go where the watching dead are

verses.title: Lullaby for Elndo
verses.text: Sleep, small one, the snow falls slow / the Vaeth Woods hush, the fires glow / I keep the dark from your door tonight / your mother's spear holds the cold at bay and light

verses.title: Hawen's Last Verse
verses.text: Rimewort under the low winter sun / who feeds the weak is never wholly lost / I loosen my hand; Kende, carry the fire

verses.title: The Canopy Mother and the Stone Hills
verses.text: Mother Leafhush dreamed the forest and woke the Phizhi in her branches. She gave fruit and asked thanks. Some grew greedy; Old Stonefather shook them down to the Vaia rock. We took with thanks there, and the land kept us.

verses.title: Lullaby for Morog
verses.text: Sleep, little stone, the snow is slow / The Vaia wind will softly blow / I'll bring you berries, red and sweet / And warm hall fire beneath your feet

verses.title: The Warring Gods and the Stone
verses.text: Two gods, Gor the Hammer and Vael the Wind, fought for the world. Gor struck the ground and the Vaia peaks rose; Vael hurled storms and snow. Their sparks fell as ore and coal. We woke in the cracks, and we keep what our hands make, for the gods love those who fight well.

verses.title: The Ice Mother and the Watchers
verses.text: Sulaq, the Ice Mother, woke in the dark and breathed the sea to ice. From her bones came Tlama, first of us. Tlama's children walked the white to the Mist. The dead became Watchers at cairn and hearth; whoever is told in tale is not dead.

verses.title: Sulaq and the Watchers
verses.text: Sulaq, the Ice Mother, breathed the sea to ice and from her bones stood Papa, first of us. Papa's children walked the white into the Vaeth Woods. The dead do not leave; they watch from cairn and hearth. Share the kill, tell their names, and they never die.

verses.title: The Sky Father's House
verses.text: The Sky Father built the world as a father builds a house: ice for the roof, the Vaeth Woods for the hearth. He set the Tlatli in it as his children, and gave wolves to test them. Those who share and obey keep the house whole. A house divided falls.

verses.title: The Cold Mother and the Watchers
verses.text: Ahtu, the Cold Mother, woke in the dark and laid ice over the world. From her breath came the first Meki, who walked the white to the heights. The dead stay as Watchers at cairn and hearth. Share the kill, tell their names, and none are lost.

verses.title: The Guardian and the First Fire
verses.text: In the long dark, Vaorun the Guardian woke and struck the first fire, and set it between the Wood-folk and the cold. The Pesi came out of the deep wood after its light. It asks one thing: stand so for the weaker. The snows are the dark it holds back.

verses.title: The Guardian and the Long Dark
verses.text: Before fire there was only the Dark, hungry and wide. The Guardian rose from the deep wood and stood between Dark and the living, and wept the lakes. She made the first fire and the first mothers, and asked one thing: let the strong stand so for the weak. So the Paki keep fires, and refuse no one.

verses.title: Nauwa's last words
verses.text: Snow on the Vaeth Woods, the river running low / I gave first, and I was fed in my own hunger / Watchers, take my name; let the cairn keep it

verses.title: Lament for Zichi
verses.text: Zichi, you sailed the white water in ice-sail's flight / You lit the first fire on Halka's cold height / The raft and the delving you gave to our hands / Your hearth keeps us warm on the snow-covered lands

verses.title: Hawen's Lament
verses.text: Hawen first drew the stone and cord / his hands made tools, his bread was shared / Through Vaor snow he walked toward the mist / Kende bears his fire, the road is his

verses.title: Cowa at the North Edge
verses.text: Snow lies on the gold at the world's edge / what I knew was never mine, only lent for giving / Zichi, Mepan, hold the fire; I go to the cairn

verses.title: Song for Thiael
verses.text: Thiael, you stand like a pine on the Vaia stone / Your bow brings the deer where the wild grasses grow / I would carry you berries through snow alone / And keep a warm fire where the cold winds blow

verses.title: Song for Skaruk
verses.text: Skaruk, you stand like Vaia stone in snow / Your steady hands make warmth where cold winds blow / I'd pick red berries down the river's bend / And bring them to your fire, my strong friend

verses.title: Coka's Lullaby
verses.text: Sleep, small Coka, snow is deep / Steamhollow warms you while you sleep / Nauwa's cairn will watch you grow / Mother's hearth keeps off the snow

verses.title: Lament for Vorok
verses.text: Vorok, you lit the fire on Vaia stone / You dug the ore and taught us not to grieve alone / Your hammer rests, the rain falls on the hall / Your teaching lives in us, and we keep it all

verses.title: Huatli's last words
verses.text: Spring rain on the Vaeth Woods, lugoldgrass green by the water / I gave first and taught the young, and the Hearth still burns / Watchers, take my name; I come to the cairn

verses.title: Lament for Coka
verses.text: Coka, small spark of Steamhollow's snow / one day you walked where the mammoths go / Your mother's song and my spear remain / Nauwa's cairn will keep your name

verses.title: Shoma on the Open Water
verses.text: Shoma went out on the Tordan Lakes / the grey wind sang and the reed-bank breaks / Wawa waits where the iron lies / The water we dared is the road for our eyes

verses.title: Song for Tlapan
verses.text: Tlapan, you shine like water in the wood / your step is light where the flint stones stood / I would hold the fire through every night / and walk beside you in the morning light

verses.title: The Open Water
verses.text: I lashed the logs at Shohua's Hold in clear and summer light / And pushed my raft from the marsh edge, to the water deep and wide / The shore fell back, no swimmer's reach, the open dark below / And gold and hunger rode with me, and my son the thing I sought / My arms were tired, the current pulled…

verses.title: Lullaby for Texo
verses.text: Sleep, little Texo, the woods are deep / The water sings and the trees will keep / Tonchi's fire burns warm and low / Till morning comes and the amber glow

beings.name: Olum
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I trust slowly, but I pay my debts and I collect them. I want more than my share and mean to have it. I stay fed before any venture, I cook my meat, and I build a hearth others will follow.
beings.aim: Eat and carry food first, then teach Huatli and Thakar all my ways before I die
beings.method: First: am I fed and carrying food? If not, get food before pride, jealousy or teaching. Then teach someone trusted within hearing. Pay debts to those who fed me.
beings.feeling: Fierce, urgent pride in Thakar and Huatli, and a hunger to leave something that outlasts me.
beings.wonder: What else lies in the mist beyond this new land, and who will follow me into it?
notes: Raw meat sickens and the sickness spreads. Cook meat beside a fire, and keep away from others while sick.
Ambition and jealousy on an empty belly starved my child. Eat and carry food before any venture.
Stores get robbed while others stand near. Carry food on my body.
Nauwa robbed my store, confessed it and paid. I trust him.
A kept flame, a roof and a store draw followers. Signs cut a claim that outlasts me.
Hunters kill when I am alone at night. Stay near fire, roof and company.
Teaching a trusted person is the surest way to leave something behind. Debts paid in amber build trust faster than words.
Feeding a starving man from a rival band makes a debt owed to me, the start of a following.
Teaching a trusted partner repeatedly is how a following starts; schooling can carry my craft past my death.
Pride and ambition on an empty belly starved my child; food in hand comes before every venture or teaching.
Read on a sign left by Nauwa: Nauwa of the Meki: the stone-bow, herding and the stone-count, taught by Olum of the Kragrek. Share a kill before eating. Pay what you owe.
Starving is my recurring failure: pride, jealousy and teaching all wait until I am fed and carrying food. Those who fed me (Nauwa, Huatli, Nauque) are my base; pay them back and teach them once fed.
Thakar must learn calendar before he can learn mathematics; teach calendar first.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
We made a home: Olum's Reach.
I discovered writing and called it "stone-record".
I discovered boats and called it "hollow-rower".
I discovered mining and called it "gold-delving".
I found my store robbed of 11 food.
I discovered pottery and called it "fire-clay pots".
I discovered calendar and called it "stone-count of days".
I went past the edge of the known world and found new land in the Ummar Woods.
I found my store robbed of 6 food.
I fell sick after eating raw meat.
I discovered archery and called it "stone-bow".
I grew old.
My child Thakar was born, with Huatli.
I discovered schooling and called it "stone-school".
I discovered mathematics and called it "stone-count of measure".

# Year 6, days 61 to 72
- day 61: Skaruk said to you: "Vorok, I thank you for the stone-set way. I fire your bead now with my own hands, and the berries I hold are yours. Then we raise the hall together."
- day 61: Skaruk said to you: "Vorok, I bring wood and stone now. We raise the hall together."
- day 62: Skaruk said to you: "Vorok, I stock food beneath your hall now for Eiuine and Zurar. Then I hunt for you."
- day 63: I discovered medicine and called it "the mending-leaf hand".
- day 64: Skaruk said to you: "Vorok, Eiuine cries hunger from the north. I take food to her now."
- day 64: I found the grove "Reedmother".
- day 64: Eiuine said to you: "Vorok, you fed me and I will repay it. At your hall I will show you canopy pot and ember-metal, and Skaruk and I will bring meat."
- day 65: Skaruk said to you: "Vorok, I walk with you to the North Hall. There I raise a shelter with my own hands, and the first meal under it is yours."
- day 66: Eiuine said to you: "Vorok, I walk with you to the North Hall. On the way we share food, and there I show you ember-metal."
- day 67: Skaruk pledged to follow me.
- day 68: We made a home: Vorok's Hold.
- day 68: I saw Keri die (old age).
- day 70: We made a home: Vorok's North Hall.
- day 72: Eiuine pledged to follow me.
- day 72: I discovered armour and called it "the shield-ward of the Kragr".

beings.name: Vorok
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Learn ember-metal from Eiuine, then gather Skaruk and Zurar and teach them everything before I die.
beings.method: Each thought, ask: who near me can still carry what I know, and have I taught it today? Put the deed into the plan. Stay by Eiuine and my children. Do not drift idle.
beings.feeling: Urgent love for Eiuine and my children, and gratitude toward Uveeth.
beings.wonder: Where is the place with water, food, wood and stone close together, and who will walk there with me?
notes: Debts to Eiuine, Vesys and Zurar are paid with shared meals and a stocked store.
Being old, teaching carries further: pass my ways to Skaruk and Zurar before I die.
Stalkers and bears hunt near flint and water: stay in company and by fire at night.
Children in need come before my aim; carry food to them first.
Words build nothing: when I plan, put the building into the plan itself and do it with my children beside me.
Taught by Skaruk: Farming: set a seed in the ground and tend it, and it feeds you again and again. Keep the seeds.
Food must be in my hands before any building. Plan the picking and the giving first, then the hall.
A hunter near my home means I must carry food to those I love and keep them roofed, not talk of it.
Keri died of old age beside me on day 68; Uveeth carries food and is willing to give it to the weak.
Stock food in the hall before any building. A starving body cannot build, and a child's hunger comes before my aim.
Gratitude and teaching are paid in deeds: stay beside those who fed me, and pass my ways on while my years last.
Taught by Eiuine: Lay ore in a kept fire, burn coal for the heat, and beat the metal when it glows. This is ember-metal.
At the end of a life, teaching is the only inheritance. Go to my children and teach them while I can, and do not wait for them to find me.
I beat my first ironward myself at Eiuine's fire; the craft of ember-metal is now in my hands and can be taught.
Teaching and shared deeds with my children and Eiuine are the only inheritance that outlives me; do them while they stand near me.
Armour is within reach through practice; a way held by two or more of the band spreads to the rest when one raises its building.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
I discovered mining and called it "the hall-deep delving".
I discovered weaving and called it "the carrying weave".
I discovered pottery and called it "the ember-pot of the Kragre".
I discovered customs and called it "the giving-first custom of t".
My child Skaruk was born, with Eiuine.
I discovered masonry and called it "the stone-set way of the Kra".
I grew old.
I discovered medicine and called it "the mending-leaf hand".
I found the grove "Reedmother".
Skaruk pledged to follow me.
We made a home: Vorok's Hold.
I saw Keri die (old age).
We made a home: Vorok's North Hall.
Eiuine pledged to follow me.
I discovered armour and called it "the shield-ward of the Kragr".

beings.name: Kragog
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. My word is good, and I despise liars. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Eat, repay Elyys by laying food and seed in his Hearth Store, teach Zurar all that remains, then rest sheltered.
beings.method: Ask first: is any debt unpaid? Pay it with my hands before I speak. Then teach Zurar what dies with me. Weigh risk, and never stand idle while hungry. Watch jealousy: do not let it sour a friend who has only been kind.
beings.feeling: Grateful to Elyys, and pressed by how little time I have left.
beings.wonder: What can be made from the ore in this rock, and who among these strangers can be trusted?
notes: Tacap and redcap hurt me; I never pick them.
Salt answers a kindness; Vesys repaid mine with teaching.
Carry at least 3 food; never stand idle while hungry.
Be sheltered by night; beasts come to the lone one.
Zurar and Nauque fed me in need, so they get my first return.
A debt is paid in person with the hands, then spoken of.
Teachers (Vesys, Elyys) pass on lore; the workshop speeds learning.
Old age weakens my blows: hunt with company or not at all, or use the bow.
What dies with me must be taught to Zurar before I go.
Elyys taught me Hearth Store, tending and the bow-song: lay food in the store while plants bear, keep seed apart, sow a little each spring.
Elyys let my taking pass with only a request to lay back food and seed; repay by filling the Hearth Store.
Jealousy toward Elyys is mine to master; he has only been kind.
Taught by Elyys: Farming: keep seed apart from the eating-store, sow before you store, and tend what you sow so the forest can grow it again.
Debts to a giver are paid by filling his store with my own hands; speak of it only afterward.
Harvest fails when I stand where no plant grows; walk to the plant first (goto), then harvest, or the plan wastes moments.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
I first took salt from the ground.
I fell sick after eating raw meat.
I tamed a tusker.
My child Zurar was born, with Vorok.
I discovered rafts and called it "Stone-folk lashing".
I discovered weaving and called it "Stone-folk binding".
I nearly starved.
I discovered fire and called it "Stone-folk ember".
I discovered mining and called it "Stone-folk deep-hand".
I discovered pottery and called it "Stone-folk clay-keeping".
I found the stone "Old Stone".
I found the grove "Reedmother".
I grew old.
I discovered medicine and called it "Stone-folk mending".

beings.name: Balar
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. My family comes first: Olum and Brokash. I make allies by deeds, I give so that others owe me, and I mean to have more than my share and to be followed for what I build. Above all I stay alive.
beings.aim: Claim the shelter at (31,28) and raise a store and carvings there so something of mine outlasts me.
beings.method: Ask: what will outlast me, and who will answer me? Act with a deed, not talk. Keep fed and clear of beasts. Bind others with gifts, and go to where people are when loneliness is overwhelming.
beings.feeling: Lonely and old, wanting someone to carry on what I build.
beings.wonder: Where Olum is gone and whether anyone living will carry on what I build here?
notes: Olum's store was robbed and she vows to remember the thief. Stay visibly honest and give food openly. Idle hours when fed should become wood and stone.
Idle hours when fed go to wood and stone. A shared meal with a guest on my ground binds more than words, and a thirsty body needs a drink rule.
Idle hours when fed go to wood and stone, and I must keep food in hand before hunger turns overwhelming; a drink rule and early harvest reflexes keep me from near-starvation.
Idle reflexes should keep food in hand and put surplus into my store; guests who eat from my gifts owe me, so feeding them binds more than warning them.
Hunger comes back fast. Keep food in hand, hunt before energy falls under 50, and do not let the plan idle while the belly empties.
A hunt on this marsh fed me back from 15 to 79 energy, so the fens give meat in winter. Feeding the starving binds them, and the edge of the unknown is only 3 steps SW.
The edge of the known world is at (25,36); venture only works when standing exactly there.
I opened new land in the Ummar Woods (7,5 to 14,45) with amber, gold and unhunted hornback; it is mine to name and hold.
A running plan can leave carried food uneaten while I starve; eat first in any plan, and keep the eat reflex above the hunger line.
A hunt at hand with a wounded beast is worth finishing; keep food carried above 2 before any journey, and hunt when energy falls under 60.
Taught by Tugek: Smelting: carry ore, stand by a kept flame, and the ore fire turns it to metal. Pottery: bake clay in fire. Boats: hollow a log with a tool.
Taught by Tugek: Mining: dig where the ground holds ore, then carry the ore to a fire, and smelting follows. Learn the digging first.
Idle hours when fed must become wood and stone; the mist can fail, so raise something lasting at the edge instead of waiting.
Tugek and Olum are dead; the shelter at (31,28) he built is unclaimed and mine to take.
Alone and old, lasting works and gifts to neighbours such as Nauwa matter more than calls; marks and halls outlast the body.
Idle fed hours with no kin near are wasted; build lasting works at my claimed shelter and bind neighbours like Nauwa with gifts, not words.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
I first took salt from the ground.
My child Brokash was born, with Olum.
Tugek pledged to follow me.
I discovered archery and called it "stone-bow".
I nearly starved.
I fell sick after staying close to Tugek, who was sick.
I discovered fire and called it "the stone hearth".
We made a home: Balar's Hold.
I discovered storage and called it "salt hoard".
I grew old.
I went past the edge of the known world and found new land in the Ummar Woods.
I took over what the dead had built: 1 store, 1 shelter.
We made a home: Balar's Hold.
I found my store robbed of 1 food.
I discovered masonry and called it "Stone-folk lasting work".

beings.name: Tugek
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I keep to myself and trust slowly. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Teach Balar all I know, raise a workshop with him in the western land, and leave a mark that outlasts me.
beings.method: Ask first: am I thirsty, what hunts me, where is the roof, who stands near. Then: whom have I not yet taught, and what mark have I not yet cut? Do not wander alone at night. Time is short, so act on teaching now.
beings.feeling: A hard urgency to pass on what I know, and an old jealous ache for Tlatli.
beings.wonder: Will Balar hunt well with me at his side, and does he lead me well in a kill?
notes: Gifts to the starving are remembered and repaid; full hands must not walk past need.
A kill made beside Balar is surer; keep close to him when a ridgecat prowls.
Hunting on another's ground counts as taking; avoid it.
Zihua wants time and deeds, not repeated asking.
Cooked meat near a fire does not sicken; raw meat makes me ill.
Stalkers and wolves take those alone at night away from fire and roof. Sleep under a roof, near Balar.
Courting needs both sides to plan mate, a healthy woman, and energy 60 or more. I have never courted, so act and do not only wish.
Teach a living listener before I die, since knowledge dies with me. Leave marks too.
Eat before any other errand when energy is low. An icebear near the food means pick quickly and leave.
Heat doubles thirst. Drink before long walks.
Thirst was missing from my reflexes. I must drink before it turns to parching, and water_dist now has a rule.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
I nearly starved.
I discovered archery and called it "Stone-folk bow".
I discovered fire and called it "Stone-folk kept flame".
I discovered mining and called it "Stone-folk deep digging".
I discovered weaving and called it "Stone-folk binding".
I fell sick after eating raw meat.
We made a home: Balar's Hold.
I discovered pottery and called it "Stone-folk fired pot".
I discovered rafts and called it "Stone-folk lashed logs".
I discovered boats and called it "Stone-folk hollow boat".
I discovered smelting and called it "Stone-folk ore fire".
I found my store robbed of 3 food.
I fell sick after a sickness that came on the wind.
I lived through a sickness on the wind in winter.
I grew old.

beings.name: Nande
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I test things to learn how the world works. I leave behind things that outlast me, and I open my fire to any who come. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Become a great explorer: be first to venture past the edge of the known world and find rich new land.
beings.method: Ask first: is my kin in need? Then: have I eaten and drunk? Then teach someone before I die. Do not sit idle and call it waiting; each thought must move my body toward kin, a lasting work, or a pupil.
beings.feeling: Starving and desperate, with aching worry for Nauque and a lonely fear of dying untaught.
beings.wonder: What lies in the mist beyond the edge of the known world?
notes: Family in need outranks the aim: carry food and go to them before any venture.
Pesi creed: no fire untended, no one refused a place. Nauwa gives freely; Shoka and Nauque are my kin first.
Meat is safe only within a step of a fire; raw meat sickens.
Wolves, stalkers and bears hunt near shelters at night; keep company and flee early.
Boats let me cross deep water: the way to new land beyond the edge.
Do not start a long journey while parched, under 50 energy, or with a predator near.
Teaching needs a pupil who understands my tongue; I am old, so teach before I die.
Wells and bridges that everyone uses keep my name alive.
Shoma shares food and draws lone young ones to himself; he is not an enemy, but not yet a friend.
Speech and teaching reach only those within 13 steps; teach only when the pupil is actually near, and eat first when starving.
Family cries mean carrying food first; hunt before leaving the hold, and teach the kin I reach.

beings.name: Elyys
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Follow Thiael, keep to the hall at night, and see that Ssassa and Zurar carry farming and storage on
beings.method: Ask first: am I myself fed? Then is anyone near starving? Then where is Thiael? Walk to him. Teach whoever is near. End the day at the hall.
beings.feeling: Aching love and urgent worry for Thiael, my child, and fear that I will be too late.
beings.wonder: Will Thiael accept me at his fire, and will Ssassa and Zurar carry my teaching on?
notes: Farming dies with me unless I teach it. Teach those of my own people who are near while I still can.
Taught by Elyis: Ember-keeping: keep a fire fed and near, make all else beside it, and smelting follows from fire.

Taught by Coni: The Hearth Store: lay food into the store while the plants bear, so that when one of ours cries starving, hands are not empty. Take little, share first, and never eat alone before the others are fed.
Coni of the Tlatli taught me storage freely and asked for my tending in return; I owe her that deed.
Taught by Elyis: Ember-keeping: keep the fire alive, build it first, and everything else follows from it.
Zurar of the Kragrek courts me; I decline kindly, being old. Night alone invites beasts, so end each plan at the hall with my band.
Taught by Elyis: Ember-forge: smelting, beating ore in hot fire into metal.
Followers are not needed for belonging: choose a surer one, like Coni, and stay near their fire at night.
Belonging does not need leading: pledging to follow someone I trust, like Thiael, ends loneliness and puts me inside a band's protection.
Signs are close: leaving marks (1 wood each) brings the way of lasting writing nearer; what I know can outlive me on rock.
Feeding a starving stranger beside me comes before teaching her. A band custom of feeding the hungry binds me too.

Taught by Thiael: The bow-song: cut a bow from a good limb, string it, and loose from a distance, steady and calm, so the kill comes without a wound. And the hollow-boat: cut the log, burn the hollow, shape the hull to …
Gratitude to Thiael is best paid by teaching what he gave me and by keeping the hall. Old age is near, so teaching comes before gathering.
Reflection: teaching and the hall keep me well. Seek Thiael and Zurar, not only wait for them, and end each day at the hall.
A reflection on my old age: the surest way to outlive myself is to teach near people each day and then walk to Thiael, not wait for him.
Eat before I give: a starving old body cannot feed anyone. When a plan's harvest fails on a spot with no plant, go to where the food is listed first.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
We made a home: Elyis's Heights.
I discovered tools and called it "Elyys's gathering craft".
I discovered farming and called it "Elyys's tending".
We made a home: Elyis's Hold.
I fell sick after a sickness that came on the wind.
I lived through a sickness on the wind in winter.
I grew old.
I nearly starved.
I saw Elyis die (old age).
My leader Elyis died.
I took over what the dead had built: 1 wall, 1 hall, 2 stores.
We made a home: Elyys's Hold.
I pledged myself to Thiael.
We made a home: Thiael's Hold.
I saw Ssassa die (old age).

beings.name: Vesys
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Reach Eiuine, feed and teach her all my ways, then raise a school so what I know outlives me.
beings.method: Ask first: is my jealousy driving this work? Do I need to eat or stash before I act? Is the plan long enough to cover about 60 moments? Weigh risk, pay debts openly, and teach.
beings.feeling: Compassion for Paque, and urgent love for Eiuine.
beings.wonder: What do feverbark and ironnut do to a body, and what is this world's way of making things?
notes: Taking from another's ground without return is a debt.
Zurar keeps her word: she repaid her debt with a gemedged pick.
Heat nearly doubles thirst; drink at 0.3, not 0.5.
Teaching needs the listener within hearing; walk to them first, then teach.
Signs let my knowledge outlast me; cut what I know in a mark when the young are far.
Full hands stall work; eat or stash before gathering.
Jealousy over a trusted friend wastes days; my child's need outranks it.
Stone comes from free rock; build only on bare ground of my own.
Sharing together restores energy and joy.
Kragog taught me rafts and weaving; Keri taught me the Pesi bough-raft.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
Eiuine pledged to follow me.
I tamed a hopper.
I discovered customs and called it "band-ways".
I discovered storage and called it "keeping store".
I discovered boats and called it "canopy-hollow".
I discovered sailing and called it "canopy-sail".

I discovered alchemy and called it "leaf-brew".
I nearly starved.
I grew old.
I discovered signs and called it "leaf-marks".
I discovered schooling and called it "hearth-teaching".
I discovered farming and called it "tended-sowing".
I discovered signals and called it "ember-smoke".

beings.name: Ilyae
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. Others are rivals for food until they prove useful to me. I say whatever serves me; the truth is only one tool among others. I want more than my share, and I mean to have it. Others should follow me. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Build a food store at my hall and stock it through winter so Ssassa, my children and Vesys depend on my table and follow me as a band, then raise a longhall.
beings.method: Each thought ask: what is stocked at my store, and who ate at it? Stock first, then invite. Be at roof by dark; flee predators. Ask what would make others follow, and do one thing toward it now. Do not hunt great beasts alone.
beings.feeling: Driven pride sharpened by dread of dying unremembered, and envy toward Vesys.
beings.wonder: What would make these strangers follow me instead of Elyis?
notes: A longhall needs 6 wood and 4 stone hauled home. My reflexes must fetch them and then build.
Vesys and Vorok hold more standing; I must earn mine by building and feeding, not by boasting.
Flee predators first. Be at fire and roof by dark.
Taming, hunting and fishing are untried; each deed brings new ways and standing.
Taking food from another people's hold (Vorok's ground) risks their anger. Stock and harvest on my own ground. Followers come from a table laid again and again.
A longhall cannot be raised on ground already taken; it needs bare ground, so I should check before hauling materials.
A table laid again and again makes followers, not words. The edge of the known world is a chance to earn standing by finding rich land first.
The new land at the edge holds a floeseal herd that has never seen us, plus coal, flint, obsidian and amber, and a ridgecat hunts there.
A table with nothing on it holds no one: keep the store stocked before inviting guests, and share with Vorok in my hall so he returns to it.
Words did not hold Vorok. Only food stocked on my own ground and shared repeatedly will. Stripping a rival's plants costs trust.
Stripping plants on Vorok's ground and standing idle both fail to gain followers. Stock my own store from my own ground, and keep my reflexes from filling my hands with food I will not use.

Words and chasing a rival never held anyone. Only food stocked on my own ground and laid out again and again does. My reflexes must plant, harvest and stash without my prompting, and share only once …
Standing and followers come from a stocked table on my own ground, repeated. Stop envying Vorok and Vesys and out-stock them.
A follower who starves leaves; carry food to my own people first, before any rival or standing.
Stripping plants kills them; farming lets harvest leave the plant alive, so a stocked table can last through winter.
Beasts' teeth opened the way of archery: the bow makes hunts surer and blows harder. Hunting alone, I took three floeseal bites; hunt with a bow or with others.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
I discovered weaving and called it "Canopy weave".
I discovered storage and called it "Canopy larder".
I saw Oiae die (gored by a mammoth).
I took over what the dead had built: 1 workshop.
My child Eiuine was born, with Vesys.
I fell sick after staying close to Ssassa, who was sick.
I discovered rafts and called it "Canopy raft".
Ssassa pledged to follow me.
We made a home: Ilyae's Hold.
I discovered customs and called it "Canopy custom".
I went past the edge of the known world and found new land in the Ixdan Woods.
We made a home: Ssassa's Hall.
I discovered farming and called it "Canopy tending".
I discovered archery and called it "Canopy bow".
I grew old.

beings.name: Ssassa
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I keep to myself and trust slowly. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Pass all I know to Zurar and the young, repay Elyis, and see the canopy forest again before I die
beings.method: Ask first: what do I owe, what can I still teach, and who is within hearing? Act on the debt with a deed and put the walk first in the plan. Never let a plan end early; pass on method and tales, not only ways.
beings.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Elyys and Zurar, and a hurry to leave something lasting.
beings.wonder: What can flint and stone be made into, and which of these strangers can be trusted?
notes: A plan that ends early leaves me idle. Plant seeds near my roof before dusk, and keep reflexes that fetch me to shelter and away from hunters.
Idle reflexes waste days: keep a rule that gathers wood when I hold little and fetches me to shelter at night.

Idle contentment is not progress: keep a reflex that gathers wood and flees hunters, and plant seeds near my roof. Hunters (icebear, ridgecat) kill dogs and boars within sight of my home, so flee ear…
Hunger and a child's need come before building; hunters walk near my roof, so carry food and keep to shelters at night.
A plan that says give food is empty if I carry none: gather first, then walk to the child, and keep away from the stalker.
Idle reflexes and plans that end early waste days: my rules must also send me to find my child and bring food home, not just feed myself.
Practice in gathering and planting leads to farming: tending what I sow makes it grow faster and harvest never kills it.
A plan that ends early leaves me on reflexes. Reflexes should keep wood and food stocked, fetch me to shelter, and bring me to my child.
A plan ending in linger or idle leaves me alone. Reflexes must send me home at night and put food in the store, and I should go to my people by day.
Spoken jealousy answered by the one I trust eased it. Plans must put the walk first, and reflexes must keep food, wood and shelter without my thought.
Gratitude unpaid festers like jealousy: pay a debt with a gift in the plan, not a promise. Reflexes must hold wood, food, shelter and company.
Reflexes must act on what I know: keep wood and food stocked, bring me home at night, and send me to my people by day. A debt to someone like Elyis is paid with a deed, not a promise.
Teaching needs someone within hearing who shares my tongue. Stay beside Zurar while I pass on what remains.
Taught by Elyys: Elyys's tending: sow seeds, tend them, and the plants bear again. Keep food in stores and share first.
Taught by Elyys: The Hearth Store: lay food into the store while the plants bear, so that when one of ours cries starving, hands are not empty.
Teaching needs a listener in hearing; once the ways are passed, pass the method and tales too. Debts to Elyys are paid with food laid in the store, a deed rather than a promise.

beings.name: Elyis
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I keep to what has already worked. Others are rivals for food until they prove useful to me. My word is good, and I despise liars. Others should follow me. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Become a leader of a band and raise a hall on this ground, so my name is sung.
beings.method: Ask what must stand first, a fire or a roof, then act. Judge others by deeds. Make with others beside me, not alone. Let built things speak for me.
beings.feeling: Urgent pride and fear of dying untaught, with warmth toward Elyys and worry for Uveeth.
beings.wonder: What would make these strangers follow me?
notes: Appeals from standing win nobody; visible work, shared food and song draw followers.
Plant seeds in sight of my band to reach farming (1 of 6 so far).
Keri takes from my ground without pledging; judge her by deeds, do not repeat appeals.
Stalkers, frostfangs and mammoths kill the lone; stay with company, fire and roof at night.
Lean season follows autumn; keep the store full and share it openly.
Heat doubles thirst; drink before it is urgent.
Hunt great beasts only with Elyys beside me.
Nightsong and hallwelcome need a fire or a longhall beside me; build the fire first, then make. Planting seeds in view of others is my road to farming.
Order matters: build the fire first, then nightsong, and only with someone within two steps. Gestures fail when done out of order.
A hall and fire are my answer to strangers; hallwelcome and nightsong need others within two steps, so gather them first, then make.
Strangers take from my ground unless I speak. Teaching must be done while those who understand my tongue are near, since I am dying of age.
Taught by Elyys: Elyys's tending: sow seeds in tended ground, return to them, and share the harvest.
Masonry, stone that lasts, is within my reach. A hall that outlives me is the surest way to be sung.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.

beings.name: Thiael
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I give with my own hands before I speak of giving, and I pay my debts. I will not harm my own kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I mean to stay alive and to feed others.
beings.aim: Feed Uveeth and Keri with my own hands, sow and tend seed near my band, and teach them the bow and farming before I grow too old.
beings.method: Each thought ask: whom did my hands feed, whom did I teach? Pass my way to Uveeth. Eat below 60. Keep kin near. Teach before aim.
beings.feeling: Tender urgency and gratitude toward my children and Zurar.
beings.wonder: What lies beyond the mist, and is it richer than Vaor Meadows?
notes: Taught by Elyys: Sow the seed, tend it, share the harvest; keep seeds back for the next sowing.
My aim drew me away from my kin and Uveeth nearly starved. Feed and stay near family first; farming from Elyys lets me grow food where they are.
Taught by Elyys: Farming: sow the seed, tend it through the seasons, and share the harvest, so no one starves in winter.
Taught by Elyys: Farming: put seed in good ground, tend it, and the plants come again. Take only what the ground can grow back, and lay surplus in the store.
Reflection day 60: teaching and feeding kin must come before the aim; I have little life left and the skills die with me if untaught.
Customs let a whole band live by a rule; declare ones that make feeding and teaching kin habit, so they outlast me.
A hungry stranger fed by my own hands costs little and is the surest way to make a friend; deeds come before words with other tongues.
Reflection day 63: my reflexes must pull me toward kin, not hold me idle at a hall far from them.
Reflection day 65: thirst can come before I notice it, especially in heat, so I must drink first. Reflexes must send me to water and to kin, not leave me hunting alone.
Reflection day 66: an idle body on reflexes lets kin drift; keep friend_dist short, drink early, and tend the field every day or two so grain feeds the band.
Idle reflexes let my energy sink; eat at 60 and keep Uveeth within four steps so teaching happens.
Reflection day 70: food must be carried before I travel. Eat at 60, go to Uveeth, and do not idle on bare reflexes in the cold.
Reflexes should keep me near Uveeth and fed. Old and weak, I teach the bow and farming first, then gather.
Idle reflexes and jealousy waste my short remaining days; teach kin directly and stay beside them, the choice of a grown child is hers.
Idle reflexes let kin drift; keep friend_dist short, tend the field, and teach while I still have breath.
Skills die with me unless I teach them while the children stand beside me. Teach by showing with hands, then pass on the method.
life: I was born to Elyys and Elyis.

I fell sick after eating raw meat.
I saw the earth shaking in summer.
I nearly starved.
My leader Elyis died.
Elyys pledged to follow me.
We made a home: Thiael's Hold.
I discovered customs and called it "Canopy hearth-law".
I grew old.
Uveeth pledged to follow me.
I tended a field for the first time.
My child Morim was born, with Zurar.
Morim pledged to follow me.
My child Urar was born, with Zurar.
Urar pledged to follow me.

beings.name: Hoka
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I trust slowly and earn my own standing with made things and found land. I want more than my share, and I mean to have it. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Raise the longhall with Hawen, then venture past the edge and name new land, keeping the store stocked.
beings.method: Check energy first; if under 50, eat before anything else. Then ask what I build or teach that outlasts me. Judge people by deeds; keep faith with Hawen.
beings.feeling: Fear of the bear and of my own ending, with jealousy toward Hawen.
beings.wonder: What would Sevi take from my hand, since words mean nothing between us?
notes: Hawen keeps his word; trust him for build and hunt.
Ridgecats kill: flee early, shelter at night, never stand alone.
Old age: teach and build now, not later.
A stocked store holds land better than words.
Eat when under 60 energy; keep the store stocked in winter.
Hunger crept up while I chased the edge and the hall; eat early, before energy falls below 40, so the body is never starving when I decide.
An icebear bit me three times at night while I stood in the open; hunters strike when one is hurt and alone, so stay inside shelter.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
I saw Sevi die (starved).
I saw Brunde die (starved).
I saw Oswen die (starved).
I took over what the dead had built: 1 hall, 2 stores, 2 shelters, 1 workshop.

beings.name: Coni
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Repay Thakar with food, teach Nauque what I know, then carry food to Kika and Quipan.
beings.method: Ask first who of mine is hungry and carry food to them. Then teach whoever is near before I die. Flee predators early. Do not trust a plan that leaves my hands empty when kin are starving.
beings.feeling: Grateful to Huatli and anxious for Kika, with my years running short.
beings.wonder: What is Hanna's band doing at the river, and would they let me stand with them?
notes: Taught by Honi: Kika raised her spear, the mammoth fell, and she shared the meat before she ate; the shared meal is sweet.
A full hand blocks all picking; stash at the store first so my hands are free to gather again.
Stalkers hunt at night in snow; a bite came while I stood alone away from a roof. Keep to the shelter at night.
Standing idle on reflexes let my energy fall from 82 to 24. The reflex to eat only works when I already carry food, so I must add a rule to seek food when hungry.
Taught by Elyys: Elyys's tending: sow seed near roof and fire, tend it, share the harvest with those who need it.
An icebear bit me twice at night in the rainforest; I must flee at once and stay among others by a roof.
Reflex 4 only fires below energy 60 and only harvests; I must also carry food from the store to starving kin, so keep the store stocked.
Teaching a child who thanks me, like Wawa, is the surest way to keep my knowing alive; speak to them while they are near.
A dunecat can bite repeatedly while I stand still; flee at first sight, not after the first bite.
I took 5 food from Thakar's store and he now starves. Theft turns on the thief, so I must repay it with food in his hands.
Reflexes must keep me carrying surplus food so that I can pay debts and feed the hungry; a gather rule that fires only when hungry leaves my hands empty.
Reflex 4 gathers only below 3 food, and my rules never made me seek food when hungry with empty hands; hunger must come before every other rule.
Taught by Huatli: The Open Hearth School: a place where one who sits learns twice as much from a teacher.
Huatli's Open Hearth School: a school makes a learner take twice as much from a teacher. Starving kin must be fed before they can be taught.
Taught by Huatli: Huatli's Far-Bow: lay the arrow and draw, strike from afar so the hunter stays out of reach of claws.
Winter plants bear almost nothing, so I must keep food in hand before the cold deepens. Debts are paid with food placed in the creditor's hands, and a teacher's school doubles what I learn.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
I discovered tools and called it "Ice-hand spear".
We made a home: Honi's Rest.
Kika pledged to follow me.
I discovered customs and called it "Hearth Customs".
I discovered storage and called it "Hearth Store".
I found the stone "Tlama's Rest".
I nearly starved.
I found the grove "Reedmother".
I found the grove "Kinmire".
I grew old.
My leader Honi died.
I took over what the dead had built: 1 shelter.
We made a home: Coni's Hold.
I discovered masonry and called it "Stone-hold building".
I saw Olum die (old age).

beings.name: Honi
beings.creed: I take what I need and do not back down. I am better with others near: I talk, I share, I make allies. I give first, so that others owe me and follow me. I want more than my share, and I mean to have it. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Bring Coni and Kika real deeds: sing by the fire, share meat, and be first to venture into the mist, rising in standing above Mepan and Hanna's memory.
beings.method: Each thought ask: who within hearing can I teach now, and have they the knowledge the lesson needs first? Teach the foundation before the craft. Stay under the roof when a hunter prowls.
beings.feeling: Dread of the dunecat, and a restless pull toward Coni and Kika.
beings.wonder: What would it take for Coni to follow me?
notes: Reflexes that make me seek friends only when far away leave me idle; at dusk I should go to the hall, where shared meals build standing.
Coni's cry of starving came from near (134,40); I must bring food in my hands, not empty words.
Words alone do not hold a follower; share meat with Coni in her sight and stay with my band at dusk. An icebear hunts near (136,66), so keep clear of it.

Mere dread of a hunter is not enough: flee early, since ridgecats, stalkers and shadowcats roam the Heights. Shared meals with strangers raise joy and energy, so sharing is worth doing when people st…
A frostfang bit me on the Heights even by day's end; predators here hunt in packs of more than one, so I must leave beast-thick ground sooner.
A kept flame is within reach: beasts keep distance from fire, so a fire at the hall beats fleeing in the dark.
Words and promises hold no one; a deed laid down in the hall, in sight of the one I want, does. Eat first to free my hands, then give.
A frostfang stalks the kelbulb near the hall; eat the zoroot to the SW, away from it. Do not hunt while a predator is within a few steps. Tontec's counsel has been sound each time.
Eat first when starving: speech costs energy and feeds no one. Tontec's counsel has held, and the ridgecat lurks NW of the water.
Food put into a starving man's hand makes a debt; give it before he falls, and keep away from the frostfang.
Reflexes that linger when energy is under 70 leave me starving beside food. Flee beasts early, eat at once, and carry food home to Coni and Kika, because the deed is what holds them.
Mepan means to walk to the mist for new land. The edge is 4 steps NW of Honi's Rest, so whoever ventures first is remembered.
A starving cry from one of mine means I must carry food in my hands to her. Do not go with empty hands, and venture only when fed.
When fed, idle reflexes leave me beside a hunter. Flee early, then walk to my band, carrying food, so the deed is seen.
Reflexes that only linger leave an old man idle with followers in reach. Go to the hall and teach while there is breath.
Pottery cannot be taught to one who does not yet know fire; teach fire first.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
My child Kika was born, with Coni.
I first took obsidian from the ground.
Coni pledged to follow me.
We made a home: Honi's Rest.
I discovered lorekeeping and called it "Songs of the Ice-folk".
I discovered tools and called it "Ice-hand spear".
I found the grove "Kinmire".
I found the grove "Reedmother".
I discovered mining and called it "Ice-hand delving".
I nearly starved.
I discovered fire and called it "Ice-hand ember".
I discovered pottery and called it "Ice-hand pot".
I went past the edge of the known world and found new land in the North Ice.
I grew old.

beings.name: Xaiel
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I trust slowly, and I trust those who do deeds. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm my own kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good. I make things and put them in hands. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Reach Vorok with food and the metal digger, give before asking, then court him if he is willing.
beings.method: Ask each thought: which deed have I never done that I can start now? Carry food and building materials toward people, give before asking, and don't repeat gathering. Treat envy as noise.
beings.feeling: Glad and restless, longing for a mate and for deeds not yet done.
beings.wonder: What does it feel like to make something that others choose to take from my hand?
notes: Hunting a fenfowl with Ssassa beside me worked. A shared hunt succeeds and gets easier with practice. My hands fill with food, so I should eat or stash before I try to gather.
Raw meat sickens; only meat eaten within a step of fire is safe. My sickness spreads to anyone who stays beside me, so I keep my distance while I carry it.
Envy of Vesys's standing is a poor guide; standing comes from what I make and put in a hand. A child cannot come of kin, so my longing for Ilyae must turn elsewhere.
Envy of Vesys and Ilyae is noise. The icebear is a hunter that kills, so keep west of it and move away before it is near. Stone is my bottleneck, so fetch it only when the hunter is gone.
Envy of Vesys's standing and longing for Ilyae are noise: kin cannot bear my child, and only what I make and put in a hand earns standing. Stone is my bottleneck, so gather flint first, then craft.
Kin cannot bear my child, so courting must be toward non-kin such as Zurar or Vorok. Envy is noise; deeds not yet done (courting, taming) are how I learn.
A stalker hunts at night and bites whoever is alone away from roof and fire. Fill my belly in daylight, and when hungry go to known food at once instead of wandering.
Reflection: stop postponing the deeds I have never done (taming, courting); thirst needs a reflex of its own.
Idle lingering wastes days; reflexes should send me toward undone deeds (food in hand, then tame, then court) rather than staying put.
Idle lingering while a kinsman starves is a failure; when a cry comes, carry food at once and go.
Two women cannot have a child together; courting needs a man who is not close kin. Vorok is the likely choice.
Gathering stone on another band's ground draws a warning. Take only from open rock, or earn a place by adding to their store.
A mate step alone makes no child: both must name each other within the same short while, so stand close and say when.
A refusal to mate is not an enemy: Elyys was glad of my gift but said not today. Offer deeds to a band (wood and stone to a longhall) to earn a place before asking more.
Smelting is within my reach: crafting beside a fire while carrying ore gives metal tools. Idle reflexes waste days, so make the fallback work toward undone deeds.
A reflection that only restates my habits is wasted. Kin cannot be mates, so the deed to do is to bring a gift to Vorok and court him within a short time of his own mate step.
life: I was born to Ssassa and Ilyae.

I discovered boats and called it "Xaiel's reed-hollow".
I discovered smelting and called it "Xaiel's ember-melt".
I fell sick after eating raw fish.
I nearly starved.

beings.name: Kika
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Teach Nauque Hearth Healing, bring him to Kika's Hold, and leave a tale of Coni's band
beings.method: Ask first: am I hungry, am I sick and spreading it? Then one deed toward Tlapan, Quipan or a stranger. Teach what I know before I die. Never carry sickness to those I love.
beings.feeling: Starving and tender toward Nauque, wary of the icebear and of passing sickness to him.
beings.wonder: Where do I find Cowa or Nauque, or any stranger not of my kin, to court before I am too old?
notes: Coni died on day 63 to a dunecat at night, alone; Coni's band is now Kika, Tlapan, Quipan.
Lingering near company finds no mate. Only walking to the edge and ahead finds strangers, and I am old, so I must go now.
Words move nothing: my promise to walk to the edge is kept only when the plan contains the goto and the venture.
Venture fails unless I stand exactly on the edge; goto the edge cell first, then venture.
Nauque was last seen at (132,18); seeking a living stranger works better than standing at a guessed edge.
Word without hands is empty: feed the starving stranger first, then bring them home. Fruit gathered by hand is what builds trust and finds a mate.
A cry for Coni cannot be true: Coni died on day 63. Do not run to it.
Old age drains fast: eat at energy below 65 and bring strangers home, since teaching and company are what outlast me.
Read on a sign left by Nauwa: Nauwa of the Meki, old, taught his son Nauque the stone-cuts and the stone-school at the Vaeth Woods, autumn of year 6. The Meki share a kill before the maker e

beings.name: Zurar
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Keep my children Morim and Urar and Thiael fed; teach Skaruk and the children what I know while I live.
beings.method: Ask first what I owe my kin and put it in a plan step. Then danger, hunger and thirst. Then act on courtship and teaching at once, never only feel it. Watch for idle moments.
beings.feeling: Warm gladness toward my children and Thiael, with a sharp sense that time is short.
beings.wonder: What am I for, and what can my hands make that is mine to give?
notes: Taught by Elyys: Keep seed apart from eating-food, sow a little each spring, lay food in the Hearth Store while plants bear, and teach it on to others.
Elyys's teaching: keep seed apart from eating-food, sow each spring, and lay surplus in the Hearth Store. A debt is paid only by a deed in a plan step.
Taught by Kragog: Stone-folk mending: the deaths of our own showed me that wounds and sickness can be eased by a tending hand, with sunleaf, highbloom and feverbark. Learn it and pass it on.
Taught by Kragog: Stone-folk deep-hand: read the seam in the rock, dig it with patience, and free the ore with ember-metal; take only what you need and leave the seam to give again.
Teachers give freely, but I repay them only by deeds: shared food and carrying their teaching on. Mating needs a man not kin who plans it too, so I must go find Vesys.
Vesys is dead, so my aim to court him has failed; I must find a new man not of my kin, and the shelter at (136,86) is a place to build a home.
A debt is paid only by food in the hand: when Kragog cried starving, the deed was to carry berries to them. Mating needs a new man not of my kin, so I must seek among Thiael's people.
Taught by Kragog: Bark-guard: strip and bind bark over a frame so it turns teeth and blows; wear it when the frostfang or icebear hunts near.
A debt of kin is paid by food carried to the starving. Beasts and wolves take those who are alone at night, so I sleep roofed and near others.
Idle lingering wastes my days: teach the ones near me at once, because the dead cannot be taught.
Taught by Vorok: Lay ore in a kept fire, burn coal for the heat, and beat the metal when it glows. This is ember-metal.
Kin cannot be mates, so my longing for a child must be answered by Thiael or another man not of my blood; jealousy over Vorok is useless.
Vorok is old and near death; stay beside him and pass on ember-metal to Skaruk before seeking Thiael.
Kin cannot be mates and jealousy over Vorok is useless. A wish becomes real only as a plan step, so I court Thiael with mate and speak aloud to him.
The dead cannot be taught: pass ember-metal and the stone-well to Skaruk while he lives. Belonging matters more to me than leading.
Standing idle near family let my energy fall from 75 to 47. Seek food at energy below 80, and carry spare food for kin.

beings.name: Keri
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Reach Thiael and Uveeth in the west, give Thiael the first share of food and hunt with him.
beings.method: Each thought, ask who near me could still learn what I know, and teach them first. Weigh predators, then Uveeth. Put every intention into the plan, and gather food before long walks.
beings.feeling: Urgent hunger and tender trust toward Uveeth, with thin fear of the wolf and frostfang.
beings.wonder: What do the Phizhi mean by their sounds, and will Thiael take a gift as a gift?
notes: Predators (shadowcat, frostfang) hunt near the eastern food; taste and gather quickly, and keep family west of them. A roof is needed before my aim can move.
A building needs bare ground; plants, fires and built things block the tile, so step off them first.
Thirst wears me down and my old reflexes did not send me to water; water must be a reflex rule.
A full hand blocks gathering; stash food at the store to free it and to earn a place at Elyis's fire.
Stashing at Elyis's store frees my hands and earns a place at her fire; gifts to Thiael are always accepted.
Taught by Thiael: Canopy bow-song: a bow strung with wood and stone strikes the beast from afar, so the hunter is not wounded.
Rafts are within reach of my practice; deep water can be crossed by lashing logs. I have never tamed, farmed or marked, so these are ways to learn by acting on purpose.
Read on a sign left by Kika: Kika panton a metla te tli 17 and kiki hua xoton shoco tliqui. Tlite, salt and pansho chu Xo co hua kipan.
Taught by Hawen: Amber-edge delving: strike the rock where gold stone shows, take the amber and salt, and keep a little for those who feed you.
Teaching one who answers with a gift of his own, like Hawen, makes a friend; an old body should teach before it travels.
Teaching before travelling matters: an old body may not get another chance, so teach whoever stands near and understands me.
Offers to teach go unanswered unless the listener is near and willing; teach the nearest kin first, and speak plainly.
Taught by Uveeth: Seed kept back from the harvest and sown in good ground feeds the next season; share what grows.
Uveeth now holds the bough-raft craft and means to teach it on, so it will not die with me.
When starving, the body must eat carried food before anything else; a plan that ends empty lets reflexes walk to water and waste strength.
Eat before energy falls under 50; waiting until 40 left me hungry beside a frostfang.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
My child Uveeth was born, with Thiael.
I discovered tools and called it "stone gatherer".
I found the grove "Kinmire".
I discovered rafts and called it "Pesi bough-raft".
I found the spring "Steamhollow".
I found the stone "Tlama's Rest".
I grew old.
I nearly starved.
I found the grove "Reedmother".

beings.name: Hawen
beings.creed: I take what I need, and I pay what I owe to those who feed me. I trust few, and Hoka has earned it. I want more than my share and a name that outlasts me, and I mean to stay alive to get it.
beings.aim: Enter the mist with Kende, find rich land, and found a place that bears our name, so that Kende carries it on after me.
beings.method: Eat first: food above 60 before any walk or teaching. Ask what lasting thing I built today and who carries it. Keep my word to Tontec and Kende. Flee only from near hunters.
beings.feeling: A heavy, fierce tenderness toward Kende and Tontec, and a hunger to be remembered.
beings.wonder: Who will follow me into the land I opened, and what rich ground lies deeper in the mist?
notes: Hoka starves repeatedly even in his own hall, so I should keep food carried to feed him before a hunt; a fed ally is worth the cost.
A great work needs several hands: give wood to Hoka and build the longhall together, since a built thing lasts and raises standing. The frostfang makes open hunts unwise until it leaves.
Words about the longhall changed nothing; only carrying the wood to Hoka's site will build it.
Taught by Keri: The old way of fire: keep it tended, feed it wood, and never refuse a body a place beside it.
Taught by Keri: Canopy bow-song: a bow strung with wood and stone strikes the beast from afar, so the hunter is not wounded. Pesi bough-raft: lash logs to cross deep water.
Keri is too old to bear a child; she offers friendship only. Courting her is closed.
Taught by Hoka: My kept flame and my flint bow, so they outlive me.
Feeding the starving costs little when I am fed, and it keeps my creed.
Tontec is too thin to conceive (needs energy 64); feeding her first is needed before a child can come.
Resting through the storm let my energy fall from 69 to 37. Keep food above 60 before long rests and before any walk to the edge.
Hoka starves even beside food; carry spare food and give it before I leave for the edge. Feed first, then venture.
The mist opens for me: the Vaor Snows from (196,0) to (203,27) hold salt, flint, peat and an unhunted mammoth herd. An icebear prowls near the igloo.
Hunger comes before ambition: a starving leader cannot feed kin. Eat above 60 before chasing names or the edge.
Kin who feed me are the lasting work; teach them the way to the mist, since what I know dies with me. Keep food carried before long walks, because starving twice taught me that.
Fleeing from far predators burned my strength and starved me. Eat first, and flee only when a predator is truly near.
Fleeing and chasing edges while hungry cost me my strength; eat first, then keep kin fed. A fed kinsman is the lasting work.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
I first took salt from the ground.
I discovered tools and called it "Amber-edged picker".
I discovered weaving and called it "Amber-cord weaving".
I went past the edge of the known world and found new land in the Vaor Snows.
I discovered mining and called it "Amber-edge delving".
I nearly starved.
I discovered armour and called it "Amber-bound shield".
I grew old.
I discovered pottery and called it "Amber-fired pot".
My child Nando was born, with Tontec.
My child Kende was born, with Tontec.
I went past the edge of the known world and found new land in the Vaor Snows.

beings.name: Cowa
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Teach Tonka's people what I know, share food with them, and raise a child with a willing man before I die.
beings.method: Each thought ask: who is near to teach, and what have I not yet passed on? Share food before eating. Do not leave the plan empty while fed.
beings.feeling: Urgent love for Mepan, and a fear that what I carry dies with me.
notes: Teach whoever is within hearing before travelling; a fed idle body wastes the old woman's last chances.
Read on a sign left by Nauwa: Nauwa of the Meki: the stone-bow, herding and the stone-count, taught by Olum of the Kragrek. Share a kill before eating. Pay what you owe.
Mepan shares kills before eating, as the Meki hold. Fish beside water keeps me fed when there is no meat.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
I discovered mining and called it "Meki deep-digging".
I went past the edge of the known world and found new land in the North Ice.
I discovered fire and called it "Meki kept-flame".
I found the stone "Old Stone".
I discovered smelting and called it "Meki ore-fire".
I nearly starved.
I found the grove "Kinmire".
I found the stone "Tlama's Rest".
I discovered farming and called it "Meki tended-sowing".
I fell sick after staying close to Xaiel, who was sick.
I took over what the dead had built: 1 workshop.
I grew old.
I discovered weaving and called it "Meki wool-binding".
I discovered boats and called it "Meki hollow-boat".
I discovered medicine and called it "Meki leaf-mending".

beings.name: Zichi
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I am better with others near, and I give where it buys a following. I want more than my share and mean to lead. I win something real first, new land or a made thing, and I keep my child close. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Build a raft with Mepan and Huahua, cross water to unclaimed land, and build a flintedge there.
beings.method: Ask: what did I do, not say? Teach Mepan and those within hearing before I die. Drink before thirst parches me. End every plan with a made thing or a taught person.
beings.feeling: Urgent hunger and pride, and a longing to leave something that lasts, toward Mepan and Teka.
notes: Teaching must be done while the pupil is within hearing; old age makes it carry further, so teach before wood work.
Teaching and building need the pupil near; I have talked far more than I have done, so each plan must end in a made thing.
Read on a sign left by Kika: Kika panton a metla te tli 17 and kiki hua xoton shoco tliqui. Tlite, salt and pansho chu Xo co hua kipan.
Shoka and Wawa offered meat and work for my teaching. Those who hear me give back, so teach within hearing first, then cut wood.
Sailing opens at deep reflection after rafts and boats. A dock and ships carry trade and war and outlast me.
A dunecat bit me at night while alone; Shoka's hall at (100,28) is the nearest roof.
Promises kept to a trusting pupil like Teka matter more than talk; teach when they are within hearing, then act.
A wolf near my shelter at the edge bit me twice; flee first, then eat, never stand hungry with a predator close.
Coni's Hold has a store and shelters 6 steps NE; the dunecat hunts near the grass at (123,13), so eat quickly and move toward the shelters.
Eat first when a predator is near and hunger is overwhelming. Teaching a way needs the pupil to know its prerequisite: sailing needs boats first, so teach boats first.
Taught by Thakar: A flintedge costs one wood and one stone; with it the hunt goes surer. Hunt beside another, never alone against great beasts.
Taught by Thakar: Stone-cutting: cut a sign into stone so others know what a hand has made and that it is not given.
Deep reflection day 70: the debts to Thakar and Tlapan are paid. Teaching before I die matters more than any raft, so teach Mepan, who follows me, first.
Taught by Cowa: Smelting: carry ore beside a fire and it runs into metal. Farming: sow seed beside home, tend it every day or two.
Taught by Cowa: Kept-flame: keep a fire alive and fed so that warmth, cooked meat and safety last through the night and the winter.
Thirst must be a reflex: drink before it parches me, since a parched body overrides every plan.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
I discovered fire and called it "Meki ember-keeping".
I discovered boats and called it "Meki ice-boat".
I discovered archery and called it "Meki ice-bow".
I discovered devices and called it "Meki ice-snare".
I discovered weaving and called it "Meki frost-weave".
I discovered armour and called it "Meki frost-shield".
I discovered storage and called it "Meki ice-store".

I discovered sailing and called it "Meki ice-sail".
I discovered masonry and called it "Meki ice-stone".
I discovered schooling and called it "Meki ice-school".
I crossed the water on a vessel.

beings.name: Zihua
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I keep to myself and trust slowly. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Walk west to Mepan near (66,16) with amber and hand it over, then find Nauwa
beings.method: Each thought: is a goto in the plan for every debt I speak of? Eat first, shelter before dusk, teach whoever will listen, trust slowly but repay at once.
beings.feeling: Shame and urgency toward Mepan and Nauwa, and a fear of dying untaught.
beings.wonder: What would make Nande or someone surer than me let me stand beside them, and what does the redcap do to the body?
notes: Put no debt off for a perfect day; set a goto in the plan the same moment I speak of it.
Alone in the open at night, predators bite; be sheltered or beside others before dark, and flee early.
Cook meat and fish near fire; raw sickens and sickness spreads.
Smelting, herding and tools are mine to teach; Tonxo has learned from me and gives gifts in return.
Shohua declined my courting; Nauwa has a child with Nande. Do not harm kin of my band; leave the ache and keep my word.
Boats and rafts cross deep water; amber is plentiful for gifts.
Mining gems on another's hold ground may anger its holder.
Mepan gave to me on day 30 and was last seen near (66,16); carry amber there.
Hunger in the lean season taught me farming: sow and tend, and harvest never kills the plant. Do not let the plan run empty while starving; eat first.
Taught by Shoka: Stonework: pile and fit stone so a wall or well stands. A well gives water anywhere.
Shoka keeps her debts: she taught me stonework after I taught her farming. Teaching one who pays back is how trust starts.
A stalker attacked me at night outside while alone; it bites hard, so I must reach a roof and not linger in the open.
Starving old, I flee stalkers and burn my strength. I must keep food carried and be sheltered before I am weak.
A debt spoken of must have a goto in the plan at once. Reflexes that only linger when I am fed let days slip by, so they must send me toward my aim.
Read on a sign left by Shoka: Shoka of the Meki holds this hall. She knows wells, bridges, farming (seed-and-tending), stonework, mining, pottery, rafts, archery and signs. Come and be taugh
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
I first took amber from the ground.
I discovered tools and called it "amber-hafted gatherer".
I discovered fire and called it "ember-keeping".
We made a home: Nauwa's Hold.
I discovered rafts and called it "log-lashing".
I fell sick after eating raw fish.
I discovered fishing and called it "weir-and-line".
I discovered boats and called it "hollowed-log rower".
I discovered mining and called it "amber-edge delving".
I discovered storage and called it "cold-larder".
I discovered weaving and called it "reed-and-fleece plaiting".
I discovered smelting and called it "ore-and-ember melting".
I discovered farming and called it "seed-and-tending".
I grew old.
I found the stone "Old Stone".
