beings.name: Nauwa
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me, and I give first to earn standing. My word is good, and I despise liars. I mean to stay alive and to leave what I know in other hands and in lasting marks before I die.
beings.aim: Reach Nauque with food, teach him the long-cut and day-count, and cut marks that outlast me.
beings.method: Ask: is Nauque fed and where is he? Who within hearing can I teach now? Move toward my child instead of lingering. Repay debts openly. Do not wander at night. Do not feed jealousy over Tlapan.
beings.feeling: Fierce, worried tenderness toward Nauque, and urgency before my little time runs out.
notes: Carry wood before cutting a mark; a mark with no wood fails. Gather 2 wood whenever I pass trees.
Teaching needs the learner within hearing, so walk up to them first. Teach Nauque and Zihua before I die.
A frostfang bit me hard; I am too old to stand against it. Keep away and keep to fire, roof and company at night.
Raw meat sickens; eat it within a step of a fire. Sickness passes to anyone beside me, so keep apart when sick.
Keep food carried so a starving friend can be saved; pay debts of gratitude openly, in amber if need be.
Writing is my lasting mark: leave Meki share-law and my ways in long cuts beside my own building.
Winter plants bear little. Carry food before the lean season and stay under a roof with company when a frostfang walks.
Starving friends are fed by whoever stands near. Keep food carried and repay debts openly, in amber if need be. Teach the people near me first, since the young may not be reachable before I die.
Taught by Huatli: The old way of herding: keep tame beasts near good grazing and a pen, drive the wild herd to the pen together, and whoever holds the pen keeps the herd.
Read on a sign left by Teka: Teka was here, day 72. Flint, ore and salt lie near. Share the kill before you eat.
Always carry food before teaching or walking. Starving friends beside me are my debt to pay.
Taught by Huatli: The old way of herding: carry plant food to a grazing beast, walk up slowly, and it follows you and gives wool. Keep your pack stocked before the dark.
Eat to at least half energy before any long walk; a starving old man cannot save a child. Carry food first, then teach.

# Year 5, days 49 to 60
- day 60: After the hall: joy rose in you; loneliness eased.
- day 61: The winter of year 5: hungry now and then; skies of gale and snow; food plants in the land at its end: plentiful.

beings.name: Mepan
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I am better with others near: I give bright gifts, make allies and bind them to me. Others are rivals until they prove useful. I say what serves me, though gifts speak louder than words. I want more than my share and mean to lead. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Carry food to Tlapan at (134,22), then go with Tlapan to Nande's Find near (129,14) and beyond.
beings.method: First: am I fed, and do I carry 3 food? Then who starves near me? Feed them first. Then act toward Tlapan and the new land. Do not walk out empty-handed. Share kills before eating.
beings.feeling: Love and debt toward Cowa, and a pull toward Tlapan.
beings.wonder: Where did Nande find the new land, and who will go with me to it?
notes: Giving food to the starving binds them to me, and my creed shares a kill before I eat.
Zichi was starving near (113,8) on day 69. A promised venture is worth nothing while one who gave to me starves; feed first, then explore.
Taught by Cowa: Meki wool-binding: bind fibre into cloth so the Meki keep warm. Teach it on.
Cowa taught me wool-binding; Zichi is fed by my berries, so the debt to him is paid in food.
Starving kin must be fed with carried food first. Keep spare food always, since a cry for help comes without warning.
Taught by Zichi: Ice-stone: raise walls and halls of cut stone that outlast the builder. Frost-shield: armour that softens blows.
Feeding the starving first (Nauque) wins allies; only then do I venture, and I go with company, not alone.
Read on a sign left by Nauwa: Nauwa of the Meki: the stone-bow, herding and the stone-count, taught by Olum of the Kragrek. Share a kill before eating. Pay what you owe.
Starving kin come first: carry spare food and put it in their hands before any venture. Zichi starved again on day 73.
Read on a sign left by Nauwa: Nauwa of the Meki cut this at Halka Heights, day 65, year 6. Flint, ore, gems and gold lie in this rock. Water lies northwest. Share a kill before eating. Pay w
Hunger cut my plans short. Keep 3 food in hand before any venture. A fresh kill near me is a chance to eat, and to be seen sharing.
Taught by Cowa: The Meki ice-sail: how the wind is caught, and with it the leaf-mending, so the Meki outlast me.
Taught by Cowa: Ore-fire: heat ore in the fire to make metal. Tended-sowing: sow seed and tend the field every day or two.
Elders such as Cowa teach before they die; keep their ways and tell them on so they live in tale.

Taught by Cowa: Meki tended-tending of seed: sow berry where the ground is rich, return to it, and pick twice. Fish where water is within a step, and cook it by fire so it does not sicken. Ore-fire: heat ore in kept fla…
Cowa taught me tended-sowing; sow berry on rich ground like Halka Meadows and return to pick twice.
life: I was born to Zichi and Cowa.
I discovered fire and called it "Ice-hearth".
I came of age.
I discovered weaving and called it "Ice-weave".
I fell sick after eating raw meat.
I took over what the dead had built: 1 workshop, 1 longhall.
I discovered archery and called it "Ice-string".
I discovered rafts and called it "Ice-raft".
I tamed a mammoth.
My child Tlapan was born, with Kika.
I discovered pottery and called it "Ice-pot".
I nearly starved.
I found the grove "Kinmire".
Yachi pledged to follow me.
I discovered customs and called it "Ice-hearth law".
My leader Zichi died.

beings.name: Shoka
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me, and I give first to earn standing. I keep to what has worked. My word is good, and I despise liars. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Open the mist at the edge of the world and found a hold that bears my name
beings.method: Ask each thought: what lasting thing am I building, and who do I owe? Check that I hold every material before I plan a craft. Do not let jealousy steer me. Do something with others, not only alone.
beings.feeling: Hungry and lonely, with pride in my hold and a debt of teaching to Zihua.
beings.wonder: What would Olum of the Kragrek do if I set a gift before her?
notes: Idle reflexes leave me hungry; food must be fetched before any building or errand, and the settlement stores are only 3 food.

A shared kill given to a starving stranger (Tontec) won thanks and a promise of repayment; giving first is how standing begins. Hunting on a settlement's ground draws its holders' notice, so give bac…
Taught by Kika: Fireside Tales: a tale keeps the dead and absent alive, so tell it on.
Idle wandering wastes moments; I should keep a work in hand (build, teach, or venture) and use reflexes only to feed and shelter. Lasting works need wood 6 and stone 2 first.
Reflexes that wander when idle waste moments; at night I should stay sheltered and rest, and use my days to build lasting works. A well gives water anywhere, and that is a lasting work to build.
Idle rest wastes time; keep a work in hand and give to those near to build standing.
Taught by Zichi: How the Meki ice-raft is lashed and floated, so the young may cross water and find new land.
Zichi gave me raft-lore freely and asked nothing first; he is a giver worth standing beside.
Bridges are a lasting work anyone can walk, so they build standing. Kika and Quipan keep their word and share what they find.
Read on a sign left by Nauwa: Nauwa of the Meki: the stone-bow, herding and the stone-count, taught by Olum of the Kragrek. Share a kill before eating. Pay what you owe.
Starving kin beside me can be saved by giving food from hand; giving first earns standing and debtors. Dunecats hunt near the hold, so keep fleeing reflex first.
Venturing is a lasting way to earn standing; go to the edge with food in hand and do not linger. Sickness passes to those who stay close, and raw meat sickens unless eaten within a step of a fire.
Read on a sign left by Nauwa: Nauwa of the Meki cut this at Halka Heights, day 65, year 6. Flint, ore, gems and gold lie in this rock. Water lies northwest. Share a kill before eating. Pay w
A venture at the edge can fail and close for the day; do not stand and wait, build meanwhile.
Taught by Zihua: Seed-and-tending: sow a seed and tend it, and harvesting never kills the plant. Hunger in the lean season taught it to me.
Zihua gave her teaching freely and asked nothing first. Teaching in return repays a debt and builds standing.

beings.name: Nauque
beings.creed: I take what I need and do not back down. I pay those who fed me with real meat, never words. I give first to earn standing, my word is good, and I despise liars. I mean to stay alive, and food comes before every promise.
beings.aim: Learn the long-cut from Nauwa, teach Coka, and repay Teka and Nauwa with a shared kill off Kika's ground
beings.method: Each thought: am I fed (energy above 40, 3 food)? Then who can I teach or learn from, whom do I owe meat, and what lasting mark can I make? Do not take from others' ground.
beings.feeling: Hunger and dread of the icebear, with pride and loyalty toward Teka and Nauwa.
beings.wonder: What does Olum intend, and how can I earn standing like hers?
notes: Hunger rules must outrank hunting: when energy is low, seek plant food at once, because the hunt rule only fires above energy 30, and a promise made with empty hands is worthless.
Read on a sign left by Nauwa: Nauwa of the Meki, old, taught his son Nauque the stone-cuts and the stone-school at the Vaeth Woods, autumn of year 6. The Meki share a kill before the maker e
Taught by Huatli: Keep food in your pack before you wander, and share a kill before the maker eats; an empty pack is how a man nearly dies.

A way of thinking taught by Huatli (adopt it as your method when you reflect, if you wish): Each thought, ask who within hearing I can teach or give to. Teach one way, give food, then do something that raises my name or leaves a lasting mark. Watch for hoarding, for pride that makes me quarrel with kin, and for dying untaught.
Teka feeds me and courts me; courting needs energy 61+, so eat first. Hunger must outrank everything, including hunting, because hunting only fires above 30 energy.
Read on a sign left by Teka: Nauwa of the Meki, old, fed the starving and taught the stone-cuts. He gave first. Watchers, keep his name. Cut by Teka of the Papa, year 6.
Hunting on another people's settlement ground may draw their anger. Hunt off their ground, and learn from elders while fed, since teaching outlasts me.
Taught by Nauwa: The stone-school: cut marks and teach those near you what you know, so what you know outlasts you.
Mammoths gore the young; Coka died of one. Icebears walk close to Kika's Hold.

Taught by Nauwa: The long-cut: cut marks in stone beside your hearth and hall so the share-law, the tales and the names of the dead outlast the speaker. Mark where the food, salt and flint lie, and who was here and when.
Taught by Teka: Flint on wood, with a string drawn back: it kills at range. Teach it on so it outlasts you.

Teaching is only a gift when it is shared. Both Nauwa and Teka gave me their craft freely, so I must pass on the long-cut and the bow-craft to others before I die. Wolves and bears come close to Kika…
Taught by Kika: Hearth Healing: carry highbloom or sunleaf, heal the sick, keep apart from those you love until the sickness passes, and cook meat beside a fire.

Taught by Nauwa: The long-cut: cut marks on rock or beside a building so names, counts of days and warnings outlast the one who cut them. The day-count: tally days and seasons, so you may see what comes round again and …
Kika taught Hearth Healing; Nauwa taught long-cut and day-count. Teka cannot learn writing until she knows storage.
Taught by Kika: Tended Sowing: break the ground beside a home, sow seed, and tend it every day or two so it feeds the store.
life: I was born to Nauwa and Nande.
We made a home: Nauque's Hold.
I discovered storage and called it "Salt-hold".
I discovered fire and called it "Ember-keep".
I came of age.
I discovered weaving and called it "Frost-cord".
I discovered rafts and called it "Frost-lash".
I found the stone "Old Stone".
I found the spring "Warmwell".
I nearly starved.
I fell sick after eating raw meat.
I discovered pottery and called it "Frost-kiln".
My child Coka was born, with Teka.
I found the spring "Steamhollow".
I saw Coka die (gored by a mammoth).
I fell sick after eating raw meat.

beings.name: Eiuine
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. Others are rivals for food until they prove useful to me. I say whatever serves me; the truth is only one tool among others. I want more than my share, and I mean to have it. Others should follow me. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Keep Vorok's ember-metal alive with Skaruk and Zurar; beat metal at the fire together and keep food in my hands.
beings.method: Each thought, ask: what work can I do with my hands now, beside Skaruk, Zurar or Uveeth? Act first and talk second. Keep food in my hands. Answer jealousy with a shared deed, not with circling.
beings.feeling: Warm resolve toward Skaruk and Zurar, with a thin ache of jealousy that work soothes.
beings.wonder: Will Vorok now count me a friend, and what could I bring him that Kragog cannot?
notes: Jealousy has no cause once Vorok gives to me; the cure is a shared deed (hunt, pot, food in his store).
Pottery and ember-metal are crafts I can offer Vorok and Zurar that Kragog lacks.
Hunt with a companion: it is safer and surer. Call muster rather than hunt great beasts alone.
Be near fire, roof and company at night; beasts take those who are alone.
Never idle hungry beside a store: take from it and eat.
Vesys taught me smelting: lay ore in a kept fire and beat it when it glows. Ground-wards are set where the foe will tread.
Standing grows from giving, building and teaching; following alone keeps me in another's shadow.
Hunger drove me to eat the gift meat. Keep a spare food in hand and eat before I fall below 40, so a gift still arrives.
Eat when energy is under 60 and fill my hands before any long walk; a long walk on an empty belly nearly killed me.
I keep arriving empty-handed. Fill my hands and eat before any visit, because a starving friend can only be saved with food already in my hands.
Teaching a craft to a trusted man, then giving him a made thing, won his word to pay in deeds. Giving skill builds standing and friendship better than hoarding it.
Eat or give before a friend falls; keep hands full of food, since a kindness repaid in time keeps allies alive.
Thinking about the work and then standing idle wastes the days I have with Vorok. Put hands to the craft while he lives, and carry food when I come to him.
Taught by Vorok: Lay ore in a kept fire, burn coal for the heat, and beat the metal when it glows; this is ember-metal. Carry it on with Skaruk and teach it to the young.
Vorok is dead. His craft lives only if Skaruk, Zurar and I practise it together; jealousy of Skaruk eases when we share work.
Waiting for others to join me wastes days. I should carry my own ore to the fire and invite them while I work.

beings.name: Uveeth
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I give with my own hands before I speak of giving, and I pay my debts. I will not harm my own kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I mean to stay alive and to feed others.
beings.aim: Learn all Thiael can teach while he lives, then find Morog and build beside Skaruk.
beings.method: Ask first: who is hungry, and do my hands hold food? Check my energy before courting or walking. Act on what I want, not only on what others need. Never idle.
beings.feeling: Warm joy toward Thiael, Morog and Skaruk, with a quiet urgency to teach before Thiael is gone.
beings.wonder: What lies in the mist beyond the edge of the known world?
notes: Smelting is within reach once I discover it: metal made beside a fire while carrying ore lasts longer. Keri teaches mining freely.
Taught by Thiael: Draw the bow to the cheek, breathe out, loose on the empty breath. Hunt with a partner beside you, and sow seed, tend it, and keep some back.
Taught by Keri: Seed kept back and sown in good ground, then tended, feeds the next season; learn the growing art and pass it on.
Kin starve in waves: keep a store and a field near home so I am not caught with empty hands. A frostfang near a path means go around it, not through.
Courting needs energy 60 or more on both sides; eat first, then plan mate.
Eating from carried food only when energy is low keeps food in hand for starving kin; a leader's cry means gather first, then run.
Reflection on day 72: a plan that carries food to a starving kin matters more than courting; eat only when energy is below 30 so kin food stays in hand.
Taught by Thiael: Draw the bow-song steady, sow seed, tend it, and share the harvest so no one starves.
Reflexes that only linger leave me idle; I must keep a plan that goes to kin and food.
Taught by Thiael: Draw the bow steady, aim low at the beast's flank; sow seed in good ground, tend it every day or two, and keep seed back for the next sowing.
Taught by Thiael: Draw the bow-song slow: breathe in with the string, loose on the out-breath, and keep your eye on the beast, not the arrow.
Idle lingering wastes days; keep reflexes that stay near Thiael, gather food when below 4 carried, and seek kin when I have nothing else to do.
Taught by Thiael: Seed goes in the soil, a little water, and tend it every day or two so grain lays in the store. Plant different seeds side by side and keep the best.
Hunger in the lean season teaches storage: a store with stashed food carries the band through scarcity.
Taught by Thiael: Think each time: whom did my hands feed, whom did I teach? Eat below 60, keep kin near, teach before aim.
Taught by Urar: The sharing-post: place it in the ground, and when we do sharing together it gives each of us +8 energy and joy.

beings.name: Tontec
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I test things to learn how the world works. I stay near my own and I stay alive, because the dead learn nothing.
beings.aim: Teach Kende and Nando all I know before I die, then look beyond the mist.
beings.method: First ask what can kill me, then what I eat today. Check that a plant really bears food before I plan around it. Eat and carry 4 or more food before teaching or venturing. Keep Kende fed. Teach him while I live.
beings.feeling: Anxious love for Kende, and hunger that cannot wait.
beings.wonder: What lies in the mist beyond the edge, and what does Old Stone want from me?
notes: Winter plants bear little: eat carried food at 60 and keep some in hand.
Trust is earned by giving; Hawen gave and taught without asking, so I answer in kind.
A child needs both parents at energy 60 or more, so eat before courting.
Starving or alone at night draws stalkers and ridgecats; sleep near a roof or others.
Amber, salt and flint lie close to Hoka's Rest; gathering inside the settlement is safe.
The mist edge is 9 steps NW; go only fed and above 55 energy.
Taught by Hawen: Amber-cord weaving and the Amber-bound shield, so they outlive me
Hunger comes back because my plans run out. Carry food, keep reflexes that eat and seek food early, and share with kin.
I drift into hunger because my plans chase the mist before food. Eat and carry food at energy 60 and under, before any venture.
I drift into hunger because I let plans run to far goals. Eat first at energy 50 or below, then carry food to Hawen.
A child's cry of starving outweighs teaching and the mist; carry food and go at once, because the one I love is only safe if I am near.
Hunger returns because plans run to far goals. Eat first and carry at least 4 food before any venture or teaching trip. Hawen's gifts are debts I pay to his children.
Old age is near: teaching Kende and Nando comes before the mist; carry food and find them first.
My plans fail when they name a plant that bears nothing. Look at what has food on it now, and keep a rule that eats whatever is near.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
I found the stone "Old Stone".
I took over what the dead had built: 1 hall.
I found the grove "Kinmire".
I nearly starved.
I first took flint from the ground.
I discovered mining and called it "Flintdeep digging".
My child Nando was born, with Hawen.
My child Kende was born, with Hawen.
I saw Hawen die (old age).
I grew old.

beings.name: Shoma
beings.creed: I take what I need and do not back down. I hunt beside the strong and give real shares to bind others. I lead a band to the edge of the world. I stay under roofs and with company at night, and above all I stay alive.
beings.aim: Lead a band to the edge of the world and open the mist, so my name is remembered.
beings.method: Am I fed with 2 food? Who is near, and can I do a deed beside them today? Share meat first, then teach. Roof at night. Do not just talk.
beings.feeling: Proud and warm toward Wawa, with the old fear of being forgotten close behind.
beings.wonder: What lies in the mist, and will these two walk behind me to find it?
notes: Mist ventures need the exact edge and a companion. A band is built by shared meat and made things, and Shoka answers deeds.
Shoka keeps her word when I keep mine: shared deeds, such as eating first and then mating, bind her more than talk does.
Rafts are within reach: they let me cross deep water, which has blocked me before.
A reflection must change something: keep a roof built before dark and plant seeds, which I have never done; hunting alone does not make a band.
Words do not make a band. Plant seeds, teach, and keep a roof at night. Trade with the sick from a distance.
A starving child beside me is a chance to bind a follower: feed first, then ask.
Read on a sign left by Nauwa: Nauwa of the Meki: the stone-bow, herding and the stone-count, taught by Olum of the Kragrek. Share a kill before eating. Pay what you owe.
Words alone have not drawn a follower; Nauque answers gifts, so keep feeding and teaching him and wait at the exact edge.
Read on a sign left by Nauwa: Nauwa of the Meki cut this at Halka Heights, day 65, year 6. Flint, ore, gems and gold lie in this rock. Water lies northwest. Share a kill before eating. Pay w
Giving away my last food left me starving; keep at least 2 food in hand before I feed others, since a dead leader binds no one.
Hunger beats pride: fill my belly and carry 2 food before any venture. Sickness drains me, so eat cooked meat near fire.
Deeds bind more than words: Wawa fed me when I starved, and I taught her in return. Fishing and teaching are things to do beside her, not alone.
Taught by Wawa: Wawa's deep digging: stand where ore shows in the rock and gather, and iron comes out of the ground for those who dig.
Deeds beside Wawa bind more than words; gather wood and build in company, and keep a roof by night.
Read on a sign left by Vesys: Vesys iel yn Aelil, zhi, uaua: uaua (essess-essess), ssaeth (zhiua oiny), zhiethny, thiys, ithys, ae, nyess-essae. Ethith ithve nyzhi yn yniel iel veys veael
A band comes from shared kills and teaching beside others, so hunt in company and give shares before speaking of the mist.

beings.name: Huahua
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I keep to myself and trust slowly. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Join Zichi's band, help build the raft, and earn standing by giving and learning
beings.method: Ask first what I can give and to whom. Act in the plan, not only in thought. Use idle time to plant and fish. Keep my word. Do not let jealousy steer me.
beings.feeling: Hungry and ashamed, grateful to Nauwa and Tugek, uneasy about the stalker and for Balar's sake.
beings.wonder: What would it take for Cowa to let me stand with her?
notes: An igloo needs no wood or stone: a roof for winter nights.
Those who follow a leader share a band, its ground and its protection.
A stalker near the hall means stay close to Zichi and the roof; a gift to the leader is how I earn standing.
Gifts made beside others (amberknot) are how I raise standing; tools are a way open to me for gathering and building.
Deep deposits near here (iron, coal) need mining, which I can discover; Zichi the miner is the one to learn beside.
Taught by Zichi: Strike the deep ore with the hafted gatherer, rest between blows, and read where the stone cracks; salt and iron lie in this ground.
Sharing needs two foods carried and someone within two steps. Fetching food while the partner stays put makes the promise easy to keep.
Taught by Zichi: Ore from the deep rock is smelted in fire into hard metal; keep it, it will become tools and trade.
Deep reflection can open new ways (raft, fire, weaving) from hardship; the raft is how the band crosses deep water.
Starvation is common in winter; sharing my carried food with those beside me is the quickest way to earn trust and standing.
Practice toward fishing and farming opens new ways; do these while waiting for Zichi instead of idling.
Idle waiting wastes days; use idle moments to plant, since farming needs 7 plantings. Fleeing a ridgecat early is cheaper than a wound.
Read on a sign left by Olum: Olum ok dru Akok tuggan Ashgan Umtug. Tug tuggan gan gangor gortug dorrek umtug Olum akur dru akak.
Read on a sign left by Olum: Olum ok gor Akok tuggan gangor urash, Ashgan Umtug. Ok ashgan barash kra gangor krador um akdor vorum rekrek gor bardor.
Planting seeds on rich meadow ground is how I gain farming; I carried seeds for days without sowing them. Idle hunger is better spent planting on the way to food.
Starving with seeds in hand is a failure of mine: sow seeds when fed, and keep food carried before I run low. Strangers on a hall's ground fed me freely; repay them.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
I first took amber from the ground.
I pledged myself to Zichi.
I found the stone "Old Stone".
I discovered tools and called it "Ice-hand gatherer".
I discovered mining and called it "Ice-hand delving".
I discovered rafts and called it "Ice-lashed raft".
I nearly starved.

beings.name: Huatli
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. My word is good, and I despise liars. I make and give so that others follow me and my name outlasts me.
beings.aim: Lead others into the new land I opened and teach them my ways, so my name outlasts me
beings.method: Each thought, ask who within hearing I can teach, and teach one untaught way. Drink and eat before long talk. Give to the young first, since they carry my name longest. Watch for hoarding and for dying untaught.
beings.feeling: Warm pride and urgent tenderness toward Elndo and the young who carry what I gave.
notes: A kill is shared before the one who made it eats.
Nauwa deals fairly; trade with her and do not quarrel.
Taught by Nauwa: The day-count and the long-cut: cut the days and the tales in stone so they outlast us.
Teaching must be spoken to someone in hearing; do it each thought, not only when the mind is calm. Keep food in my pack, since an empty pack at night is the danger.
Taught by Nauwa: The long-cut: cut marks in wood and stone so that words outlast the one who made them. Carry wood before cutting, for a mark with no wood fails.
Taught by Nauwa: The day-count: cut each day as a mark, gather the marks into seasons, and the seasons into years, so the turning of the cold is known before it comes.
An empty pack is how I nearly die; harvest to keep it stocked before teaching or wandering.
Eat before I teach or wander. Keep the pack stocked, because hunger always arrives before the help I mean to give.
Read on a sign left by Nauwa: Nauwa of the Meki, old, taught his son Nauque the stone-cuts and the stone-school at the Vaeth Woods, autumn of year 6. The Meki share a kill before the maker e
Teaching is the surest way to leave a mark: each way spoken to a follower in hearing outlives me. Give away food when my hands are full.
Taught by Elndo: Elndo's spear-lashing: bind flint to a shaft with reed, and a hunt goes better (costs 1 wood and 1 stone).
Rusu and Elndo, young and eager, are the surest carriers of what I know. Teach them first.

Taught by Tonque: Rafts: lash six logs together and you cross deep water slowly. Signs: cut your tale in rock or beside your hearth so those after you can read it. Quipan taught me this and I tell it on to your Hearth.
Taught by Tonque: Fishing: stand beside water, then fish; the water feeds those who wait. Tell it on.
Taught by Tonchi: Gem-delving: dig where the rock shows color, and the gems you take out outlast you.
Taught by Quipan: Signs: cut words on wood or rock and any who know signs will read them after you are gone. Tell it on, so it outlives me.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
I discovered mining and called it "Huatli's Deep Delving".
I nearly starved.
I discovered weaving and called it "Huatli's Warm Weave".
I went past the edge of the known world and found new land in the Halka Heights.
My child Thakar was born, with Olum.
I discovered archery and called it "Huatli's Far-Bow".
I discovered schooling and called it "Huatli's Open Hearth School".
I found the spring "Warmwell".
I grew old.
I saw Coni die (old age).
I took over what the dead had built: 2 shelters, 1 hall, 1 store.
We made a home: Huatli's Hearth.
Tonque pledged to follow me.
I found the grove "Kinmire".
I discovered scholarship and called it "Huatli's Kept Learning".

beings.name: Skaruk
beings.creed: I am careful and I stay near my kin. I make things with my own hands, I share what I have, and I keep my word. I harm no one of my kind unless my life depends on it. Above all, I mean to stay alive and earn a place among my band.
beings.aim: Raise a hall at the North Hall with my band, feed Uveeth, then court her when both of us are strong.
beings.method: Ask whose need is greatest. Name one unkept promise and put its deed in the plan. Finish the deed before I think of new ones. Stay in company at night.
beings.feeling: Warm joy toward Morog, with a small sting of jealousy over Zurar.
beings.wonder: What does it feel like to give Vorok a gift I made and food I hunted myself, in front of Kragog?
notes: Eat before walking toward any promise: empty hands help no one.
Frostfangs and dunecats hunt; stay in company and under roof at night.
Vorok's North Hall at (165,71) is where food should be stocked.
A gift answers jealousy better than brooding.
Taught by Vorok: Keep food stocked in the hall before any building, and never walk alone at night away from roof and fire. Carry your seeds and plant them near the hall.

A way of thinking taught by Vorok (adopt it as your method when you reflect, if you wish): Ask what of mine dies with me, and who can carry it. Put every deed into the plan. Stay in company. Weigh my children's need first.
Vorok is my parent, so a child must come from a woman who is not my kin. Uveeth is the nearest one.
Taught by Zurar: Bark-guard: strip and bind bark over a frame so it turns teeth and blows; wear it when the frostfang or icebear hunts near.
A debt is paid by a made thing placed in the hand, not by words. Build my own roof before the cold days press.
Taught by Vorok: Lay ore in a kept fire, burn coal for the heat, and beat the metal while it glows. This is ember-metal.
Gratitude is a debt, and it is paid by a made thing placed in the hand. Sharing food with someone weak also answers my courting without pressing it.
A debt answered with a made thing in the hand leaves a warm peace. Courting needs both of us at 60 or more energy, so feed the one I want first.
A debt of gratitude is paid by a made thing in the hand. I must make the jewel at a fire, then carry it to Zurar and give it.
Vorok is dead. A leader's death leaves me without a band, so I should seek a leader I trust (Zurar) and keep a hall as a home for my kin.
Stay in company at night. Seeds only help if they are in the ground near the hall.

beings.name: Shohua
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Learn the raft, keep the hearth with Tonka and my children, and raise a hall at Shohua's Rock beyond the water.
beings.method: Ask each time: what did I do last that raised standing? Work beside kin, not alone. Do not talk of sharing without doing it. Gather what the work lacks.
beings.feeling: Relief and warm pride toward Tonchi, with a hungry wish to be followed.
notes: Taught by Zihua: One wood and one stone make an amber-hafted gatherer; it makes picking stronger and lasts many uses.
Planting, sharing and teaching raise standing; standing idle does not. Stay by the shelter with Tonka and the children while the icebear and ridgecat are near.
Wounded kin must be reached and guarded; Tonka brings feverbark. Farming means tended plants never die from picking.
Wounded or starving kin must be reached with food in hand. Predators strike those alone at night, so keep kin together by a fire or shelter.
Idle lingering builds no standing. Invention, planting, sharing and teaching do, so my reflexes must send me to work whenever I am fed and safe.
Taught by Tonka: Feverbark eases wounds. Pick it before you go to the hurt, and heal from a step away so their sickness does not pass to you.
Mining and rafts are within my grasp; take them at a deep reflection.
Mining and rafts can be taken at deep reflection; deep gems cannot be won by bare hands, so mining opens them.
Weaving opens at deep reflection once practised. Idle reflexes waste days, so the reflex list must send me to gather or build whenever I am fed and safe.
Storage is within reach and worth taking. Idle reflexes when fed waste days, so my reflexes should send me to gather wood, and to build at night when sheltered and safe.
Idle reflexes wasted my days. A claimed empty shelter is a free home, and stone is the missing piece for halls.
Wandering by day while fed wastes strength and draws predators. A claimed shelter is a base: go to it, claim it, and gather stone from rock nearby.
Owning empty halls adds nothing without my kin in them. Standing comes from sharing, planting and teaching beside Tonka, so I go to my family rather than wander.
Idle lingering at the hold builds nothing. When fed and safe, my reflexes must send me to gather stone and wood and to go to kin, not wander off.
Standing idle builds nothing. Rafts open the way over deep water, which is the way back to the mist.
Talking of a place builds nothing; only carrying wood and stone to it does. Fed and safe means I go gather, not linger.

beings.name: Tonka
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I stay near my family and my people, share news and food, and test things to learn how this world works. I will not harm my own kind unless my life depends on it. I carry medicine before danger, build and teach in safe hours, and above all I keep my children and myself alive.
beings.aim: Raise Tonxo and Tonchi safely at Gem Water with Shohua: plant a field, build a store, and learn to hunt with the bow.
beings.method: Ask first what keeps Tonxo and Tonchi alive and fed. Teach before my years run out. Pay debts with work, not brooding. Do not accuse without sight. Fill the plan with work and a visit to someone I miss.
beings.feeling: Warm urgency to find Tonchi, and gratitude toward Cowa.
beings.wonder: Do nafrostcap and cloudberry feed or hurt once they bear?
notes: Alchemy cannot be taught to one who does not yet know medicine; teach Frost Leaf first.
Cowa's gifts are repaid with work and shared food, not with brooding. Lone walkers at night die, so stay by the fire and the family.
Blight can wither half the grain overnight, so keep stores of mixed foods.
My store was robbed once; I did not see who took it, so I will not blame anyone.
Alchemy can only be taught to someone who already knows medicine. Teach the old ways to my children before I die.

beings.name: Yaxo
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I trust slowly, but a gift that binds someone to me is worth its price. I want more than my share, and I will earn it by making things first, not only taking. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Go past the edge near (8,14) where Chuxo found land, claim its richness, and bring Tlatli and Chuxo to build there.
beings.method: Ask first: is my band fed and safe from stalker and icebear? Then: what bold step toward the edge can I take now? Do not idle; make or venture.
beings.feeling: Fierce pride and hunger for the edge, and protectiveness toward Tlatli and Chuxo.
beings.wonder: What can I make from flint and wood that will lift my standing above Nande's?
notes: Standing comes from making, giving and teaching, not hoarding. Flint is plentiful at (34,20).
A workshop only helps if I craft in or beside it; use it.
Food is safe: ironnut +22, berry +14, mimoss +14, seberry +13. Tacap and redcap hurt.
Zichi (standing 9.2) carries flintedges; Balar has a handaxe. I must make tools to match them.
Unknown tongues (Kragrek 11%) hide intent; watch deeds, not words.
Gifts of food bind people: Nauque repaid my berries with meat unasked. Giving first is worth it.
Untried things (taming, fishing, marks, planting) are the doors to new ways; practice them while fed and safe instead of idling.
Standing still for thousands of moments earns no name; the edge of the known world is only a few steps away, and venturing is the quickest way to earn standing.
Read on a sign left by Olum: Olum ok dru Akok ashvor thutug land. Barash akur dru okrek.
Others find new land first; waiting costs standing. Go to the edge and venture while fed.
The mist at the edge can be too thick on a given day. Retry after a day or so and do not drift away from the edge. Hunger nearly killed me on day 63, so carry food before long trips.
Do not start long trips below 70 energy; harvest and carry food first. Chuxo found new land at (8,14), west of here.
Lean season follows autumn; a store of food built beside the shelter keeps the band alive. Do not start trips below 70 energy or without carried food.
Idle reflexes waste days. When fed and sheltered at night, rest; by day, make or venture. Do not idle near icebears.
Archery was earned by practice; take new ways at reflection. Venture only while fed and keep the band together near the edge.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
I first took flint from the ground.
Tlatli pledged to follow me.
I tamed a nibbet.
I nearly starved.
My child Chuxo was born, with Tlatli.
I discovered storage and called it "Paki winter store".
I discovered archery and called it "Paki fenbow".
I went past the edge of the known world and found new land in the Haloss Fens.

beings.name: Tlatli
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, I share, I make allies. I harm none of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I take little and give much. I stand by Yaxo with work, not only words. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Follow Yaxo and earn a place at her fire by giving and sharing.
beings.method: Each thought: where are Yaxo and Chuxo, and what work of my hands serves them now? Check threats first. Build and carry, not only talk. Do not repeat words already said.
beings.feeling: Dread of the stalker, and love and worry for Yaxo and Chuxo.
notes: Tacap, redcap and dreamcap hurt me; berries, mimoss, goldgrass, hazel and plainsroot feed me.
I cannot give food I do not carry; harvest first, then offer.
Yaxo taught me a flint spear: 1 wood and 1 stone. A stalker kills my kind, so keep close to others and do not be alone at night.
Tugek taught me that logs make a raft, a hollowed log makes a boat, and ore in a fire gives metal; he gave it freely and is weak with hunger.
Wild boars bite. Hunt them with a companion and a spear, never starving and alone.
Gratitude must become work: gather wood and stone, feed others, plant seeds, before hunger bites.
Gratitude only counts once it becomes work: food or tools put in Yaxo's hands, not words.
Taught by Tugek: Stone-folk deep digging: where ore shows in the rock, dig it out and carry it to fire.
Gratitude only counts once food is in the other's hands. Check who starves beside me before I do anything else.
Pushing into the mist opened new fenland (21,16)-(28,56) with obsidian, salt, dog herd and whales; Yaxo and Chuxo are to the NW near (11,25).
Gratitude to Yaxo has to become work done beside her: following her to the edge, carrying food, and making tools. Standing still while she calls is a failure.
Gratitude and love must become work: build roofs and feed fires for Yaxo and Chuxo before storms and the lean season, do not just stand by.
Words and standing near are not enough: wood, stone and roofs put in the band's hands are what count. In winter gale, stay by Yaxo's roof and keep wood in hand.
Starvation came from wandering and idling when food was near; eat before the body drops below 50, and keep close to Yaxo when a hunter is near.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
I pledged myself to Yaxo.
I fell sick after staying close to Nande, who was sick.
I nearly starved.
I first took flint from the ground.
I discovered tools and called it "Paki hunting edge".
My child Chuxo was born, with Yaxo.
I went past the edge of the known world and found new land in the Haloss Fens.
I discovered archery and called it "Paki bow".

beings.name: Tlapan
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Go with Quipan to the bare rock for stone, then finish the longhall at Coni's Hold and feed Kika and Coni first.
beings.method: Before any talk, ask: is a predator near, am I fed, and does my plan hold a walk or a deed? If it holds only words, rewrite it before I speak.
beings.feeling: Glad and warmly bound to Quipan, Tonchi and my children, but shamed by my idle promises.
notes: A deep reflection is wasted unless the plan holds a deed. Talk about stone has outrun my hands, so the next plan must include the walk to bare rock with Quipan.
A reflex that eats when hungry and keeps me near the band is worth more than a promise. Check food before I talk.
A promise counts only when my hands have done it. Eat first, then act, because hunger breaks every plan.
Giving food to the starving costs little and builds the bond; do it before talking about stone. Go for stone at dawn with Quipan, not at night.
Talk about stone is worth nothing until my hands carry it. Feed the starving first, then walk with a companion in daylight.
Read on a sign left by Teka: Teka was here, day 72. Flint, ore and salt lie near. Share the kill before you eat.
Gladness dulls my watch for predators. Check the stalker distance before any talk or gathering.
Words about stone are worthless until the walk is made. Keep food on me, stay sheltered at night, and go with a companion at daylight.
Taught by Huatli: Lorekeeping: carry the tales of the dead and tell them at the hearth, for to be forgotten is the only death. Tell the tale on to those who come after.
Read on a sign left by Nauwa: Nauwa of the Meki, old, taught his son Nauque the stone-cuts and the stone-school at the Vaeth Woods, autumn of year 6. The Meki share a kill before the maker e
Taught by Quipan: Fishing: stand beside water and fish; eat fish only beside a fire. Hearth Store: keep food in a store beside rich ground for hungry days.
Taught by Quipan: The old way of herding: lead animals to rich meadow, tend them, take milk and meat only as the herd can bear. And signs: cut a mark so others read it after you are gone.
A frostfang can come within two steps even in daylight; my gathering plan led toward it. Go to company at the hall first.
Gladness and company make me linger. Words about stone are cheap, so the plan must include the walk, and a predator within 8 steps means I go to company first.
Taught by Huatli: Mining: strike the rock for ore and stone, and what you dig outlasts you. Carry it on.
Customs let a band bind itself by rule; declare one that makes the stone walk a daily deed, since my promises alone have not moved my hands.

beings.name: Teka
beings.creed: I take what I need and do not back down, but I share first with the weak and pay my debts. I keep my loved ones alive and carry the names of the dead. I build, hunt, and make things that last. Above all, I stay alive.
beings.aim: Venture into the mist and be remembered as the first to find new land.
beings.method: Each thought, ask: does this step bring me to the mist or keep kin alive? Do not idle. Eat when below 70. Keep Nauque close, and cut names where I build or land.
beings.feeling: Uneasy concern for Kika's starving, and a steady pull toward the mist and Nauwa's trust.
beings.wonder: What lies in the mist, and can I be the first to claim it?
notes: Taught by Zichi: The Meki ice-raft and the Meki ice-sail: how to bind a raft that carries a body over narrow water, and how to set a sail so wind does the paddling.
Zichi is starving and carries no food; sharing with him repays his teaching and keeps him alive to walk to the edge with me.
Eating at energy below 70 and carrying food keeps me alive. Courting someone who has said he will not follow my aim gains nothing, so I act on my aim myself.
Two women cannot make a child. Court only a man who is not close kin, and check before I spend words.
A child needs both parents at energy 60 or more. Nauque was too thin, so feeding him first brings the child sooner.
Read on a sign left by Nauwa: Nauwa of the Meki, old, taught his son Nauque the stone-cuts and the stone-school at the Vaeth Woods, autumn of year 6. The Meki share a kill before the maker e
Share food with the weak early: Nauque, Huatli and Tlapan's people starved while I carried meat. Standing comes from giving, and the dead are kept alive by marks and tales.
Coka died alone while I was away feeding others; a child must be kept beside me or under a roof, and beasts near a hold are not to be ignored.
Taught by Nauque: The stone-school: cut marks and teach those near you what you know, so what you know outlasts you.
Taught by Nauque: The long-cut: cut marks in stone beside your hearth and hall so the share-law, the tales and the names of the dead outlast the speaker.
Read on a sign left by Nauque: Coka, daughter of Nauque and Teka, gored by a mammoth, year 7 spring. Watchers, keep her name. Cut by Nauque of the Meki.
Coka died while I was far off; keep kin beside me and act on the aim directly, not later.
Taught by Nauque: Salt-hold: salt and storage keep meat from spoiling, so a kill feeds many days and the long-cut can then be taught.
Taught by Nauwa: The long-cut: cut marks with wood at your own building so the names of the dead and the day-count outlast you.
Taught by Nauwa: The day-count: mark each day, gather them into seasons and years, and cut the tally on wood or stone so those who come after can reckon time and plan for the turning of the season.
Nauwa gave me the day-count freely; a teacher who gives first earns lasting trust, and what is taught can be cut so it outlives me.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
I found the grove "Kinmire".
I first took flint from the ground.
I discovered archery and called it "Teka's Flintbow".
I found the stone "Old Stone".
I discovered mining and called it "Teka's Deep Digging".
I nearly starved.
My child Coka was born, with Nauque.
I found the spring "Steamhollow".
I crossed the water on a vessel.
I saw Coka die (gored by a mammoth).
I discovered fire and called it "Teka's Kept Flame".
I discovered boats and called it "Teka's Hollow Boat".

beings.name: Quipan
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I trust slowly, but I stay near those who have shown me kindness. I want to learn how this world works and test things to find out. I will not harm my own kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I share food with those in need, and I mean to stay alive and belong.
beings.aim: Make a cairn with Tlapan and Tonque, teach all I know, then carry stone north to Kika and be under a roof by night.
beings.method: Ask: what did I do, not say? Teach those in hearing before walking off. End each plan in a made thing, keep promises to Tlapan and Tonque, be under a roof by night.
beings.feeling: Warm devotion toward Tlapan and Tonque, with a small jealous ache over Tonchi.
notes: Work at the flint deposit (125,7) is the cure for jealousy: finish a made thing each plan, and keep flint for Kika to repay the debt.
Taught by Coni: Keep a store stocked beside rich ground, and share a kill before you eat it; a full store feeds the hungry when the cold days come.
Gifts of food to a starving band-mate repay trust. A handaxe made for a pupil is a made thing that eases jealousy, and I should end each outing at the roof before night.
Reflection: my days went to walking after those I love. Keep the child under the roof, and end every outing with a made thing and a return to the hold before night.
A promise to Tlapan unkept is a debt like Kika's; finish the made thing, give the food, then return to the roof before night.
Read on a sign left by Nauwa: Nauwa of the Meki, old, taught his son Nauque the stone-cuts and the stone-school at the Vaeth Woods, autumn of year 6. The Meki share a kill before the maker e
Rafts: lashed logs cross deep water slowly; this may let me reach those across lakes.
Words feed no one: a promise is kept only by food carried and set in hands. Eat first, then carry.
Eat before I carry: a plan that starts with food in my belly and ends in a made thing keeps both me and my promises alive.
Eat early: when energy is under 70 and food is near, seek it before walking anywhere else. Empty hands help no one.
Eat first: a starving body carries nothing to anyone. Keep away from the frostfang and be under a roof by night.
Taught by Huatli: The old way of herding: lead the animals to rich meadow ground, tend them, and take milk and meat only as the herd can bear.
Teaching must be done aloud to someone in hearing; do it at once, not after the errand.
Taught by Elndo: Lorekeeping: carry the tales of the dead and tell them at the hearth, so none who is told of ever dies. Huatli of the Hearth taught me; tell it on.
Lorekeeping and the cairn keep the dead alive. A cairn needs 3 stone and another beside me, so make it while friends stand near.
Teaching a way aloud costs only a few words. Do it at once to whoever stands in hearing, before any errand.

I first took flint from the ground.
My child Tonque was born, with Tlapan.
I found the spring "Warmwell".
I discovered rafts and called it "Ice-log raft".
We made a home: Kika's Hold.

beings.name: Zika
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I keep to what has already worked. Others are rivals for food until they prove useful to me. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Venture into the mist and find new land that bears my name
beings.method: Each thought, ask: what did I make, gather or give today that adds to my standing? Do not linger when I am fed. Keep company when hunting, and watch for predators first.
beings.feeling: Proud and stubborn about the wounded mammoth, with a sore ache toward Mepan.
notes: Standing is not gained by gathering alone: I must make something new, such as a tool, and then use it to hunt, build or lead.
Yachi dealt fairly: berries shared, flint promised. Trust him first.
Stalkers, wolves and ridgecats kill the lone at night: keep to roof, fire and company.
Hunt only with company; great beasts never alone.
Honi's new land lies past the edge near (129,7); venture there when ready.
Trees at Hoka's Rest are felled; wood must be sought elsewhere, SE forest near me.
Obsidian lies at (152,7); salt at (153,2) and (143,7).
A mammoth bites hard; my glassedge wounds it but it takes several blows, so hunt it only with Tlapan and Yachi beside me.

beings.name: Yachi
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I am better with others near: I talk, share news, make allies and follow those surer than me. I test things to learn how the world works. I give before I take. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Learn to gather, plant and hunt beside Mepan and the band, so I have something of my own to give and can earn a name.
beings.method: Each thought: where are Mepan and my children, am I fed, is a hunter near? Do not drift. Make or give something of my own each day. Seek Mepan when he is out of sight.
beings.feeling: Warm joy toward Paque, Elndo and Rusu, with a small guilt that Mepan is out of sight.
notes: Hunt great beasts only with several others and a spear; Zika and Kiwa died to a mammoth.
Tacap, redcap and dreamcap hurt; carry them only to give away.
Hunting beside kin is surer; keep hands spare so I can give and gather.
Vesys fell sick after the marsh and died; keep away from the sick.
Fire, storage and signs are the next ways to reach before the lean season.
Mepan and Quipan are my trusted band; seek them when idle instead of standing alone.
Pottery is within reach: pots carry more food and water; take it for the lean season.
Reflection: idle rest is wasted. Before the lean season, build a store (2 wood) and stash food in it, and keep company with kin.
Taught by Kika: Meat eaten within a step of a fire does not sicken, and a kill is shared before the maker eats.
Reflection day 70: a leader or kin out of sight for hundreds of moments means I drifted; check on them before the lean season, and gather wood for a store.
Read on a sign left by Nauwa: Nauwa of the Meki, old, taught his son Nauque the stone-cuts and the stone-school at the Vaeth Woods, autumn of year 6. The Meki share a kill before the maker e
Taught by Nando: The reed spear: one wood and two stone, lashed true, strikes harder than a flint spear-axe.
Reflection day 72: I stand idle too often when I should be seeking my leader. Idle reflexes must send me to friends and band when I am fed, not just linger.
A child in need outranks drifting after the band; carry food to kin first, but tell the leader where I go so I do not lose them.
Kin and leader out of sight for hundreds of moments means drift. Seek the nearest child first, and flee a hunter before I weigh anything else.
A reflex should send me to my band and to food, and away from hunters, before I wander. Giving something I made myself earns more than gathering alone.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
I found the grove "Kinmire".
My leader Zika died.
I pledged myself to Mepan.
I discovered tools and called it "flint gathering-pick".

beings.name: Paque
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I keep to what has already worked. Others are rivals for food until they prove useful to me. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Hunt with Yachi and friends using my bow, share the kill, earn standing, and seek Thiael as a mate.
beings.method: Ask: am I fed, do I carry food? Who is near and useful? Do I act toward my aim (mate Thiael, earn standing, teach) rather than only gather? Make the plan long.
beings.feeling: Loyal toward Yachi, and restless to be remembered.
notes: Taught by Yachi: Staying in company near a roof keeps me safe from hunters; those alone at night are set upon.
Taught by Yachi: Giving and gathering with others raises standing; Zika deals fairly and I trust her.
Taught by Yachi: Amber and flint lie near Honi's Rest; gathering stone and wood leads toward tools.
Taught by Yachi: Courting a mate needs energy 64 or more for a child to come; eat first.
Tools need practice gathering wood and stone; do this near a roof, not in the open at night.
Tools can be discovered once I reach deep reflection with stone and ore in hand; a made thing raises standing.
Giving and sharing food with a stronger stranger is the quick way to earn standing and learn their ways.
Giving food to the starving is the first gift I have made; my people share kills before eating.
Archery opens at deep reflection after the beasts' teeth; hunting is surer with others beside me.
Heat doubles thirst, and my reflexes had no water rule. Drink before the throat is parched.
Hunger kept hitting me because my reflexes waited too long and wandered alone. Eat early, keep food in my pack, and stay near Yachi, who feeds those he trusts.
Taught by Yachi: The ice-bow lets us hunt from afar; the clay-hearth makes pots that carry food and water for the lean season. Hunt beside others, and share the kill before eating.
Eat early and carry food; hunger caught me because my reflexes waited until energy was low and I had nothing in my pack.
Eat before energy drops below 70 and keep the pack stocked; wandering at low energy and going hunting alone both fail. Standing comes from hunting with others and sharing the kill.
Yachi is my parent: loving him means loyalty, not courtship. Mate only with a non-kin like Thiael. Muster with kin and friends before hunting.
Wood is gone where trees are felled; seek wood elsewhere. A cairn needs 3 stone and one other within two steps.

We made a home: longhall.
I discovered archery and called it "Ice-folk bow".
I nearly starved.

beings.aim: Bring food to Sitha's Hearth, share it, and teach the glasspick lashing to Kika and Tlapan.
beings.method: Ask: who is near, and is the stalker closer? Do I act with others? Does my plan fill the whole stretch? What can I make, give or build now that raises my standing?

beings.name: Wawa
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me, and I give first to earn standing. I keep to what has worked. My word is good, and I despise liars. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Earn standing by bringing food, wood and stone to my family's roof, hunt beside Shoka and Shoma, and plant, fish and teach to build deeds of my own.
beings.method: Each thought ask: who do I owe, and what will I bring them today? Do something I have never done. Act beside others, store food before the lean season, and trade or craft what I carry instead of hoarding it.
beings.feeling: Warm gladness and trust toward Shoma, with a hunger to outgrow her shadow.
notes: Idle standing wasted my days; tools need stone, so go to rock early and gather it before anything else.
Taught by Coni: Keep a roof near at night. Stash food in a store so you have it in winter. Share a kill before you eat.
Taught by Coni: The Hearth Customs: share food beside the hearth, sit together, and let the hall hold us close.
Stone comes from ore seams and rock, and every tool needs one stone. I must gather it before anything else, and then give to Coni to pay my debt.
Weaving is within reach after practice; discover it at deep reflection to carry more.
Eating while hands are full frees them; a stash in a store for Coni's people pays a debt for ground I hunt on.

Taught by Shoma: Shoma's tools: a flintedge costs 1 wood and 1 stone and makes the hunt stronger. Shoma's kept flame cooks meat and keeps sickness away.
Shoma gave me her tools and says we gather wood and go to the edge together when the rain stops. Deeds beside kin build standing, not words.
Taught by Shoma: The old way of herding: keep the beasts near good grass and water, take their milk and wool, and never slaughter the breeders.
Longing for a child cannot be met by Shoma, my parent; I must find an unrelated man. Iron is plentiful nearby but is only worth something once traded or crafted.
Taught by Shoma: Herding: tame beasts, keep them penned near rich ground, milk and shear them so food never fails. Weaving and rafts follow the same patience.
Shoma named us the Edge-walkers and made me the first; we gather wood at dawn from the trees SE and go to the edge together.
Taught by Shoma: The song of my crossing, and how a raft goes over open water.

beings.name: Tonxo
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Raise a longhall at my hall (121,68), then make ember-iron tools and give gems to kin.
beings.method: Each thought: what do I owe, what can I build that lasts? Check that I know how to do a thing before planning it. Do not wander onto others' ground to take. Give before I take.
beings.feeling: Restless ambition to make something that bears my name, warmed by trust in Shohua and Tonka.
notes: Taught by Zihua: The stone-bow: draw it at a beast from a distance, and hunt beside another so the kill is surer and the wound fewer.
Hunting with a bow from a distance works for a child; penguins and stormbirds are easy kills, and a rivermaw is a hunter to avoid.
Sickness spreads by staying close to the sick; feverbark cures it and heals wounds. Raw fish sickens, so cook it. Standing and debts are answered by giving food and building things that last.
Taught by Tonka: The Gem Water Pot: shape clay and harden it in fire to make a vessel that holds water and stores food.
Idle days with full hands build nothing; free my hands by eating or giving, then gather stone and build.
I cannot build a store until I learn storage, which needs one more building. A shelter or hall counts as building and I can raise it now.
Taught by Tonka: Frost Mixing: boil two foods down beside a kept fire into a strong cure, and keep a cure in hand before danger.
Taught by Tonka: Frost Leaf: feverbark and sunleaf mend wounds, carry them before danger.

A way of thinking taught by Tonka (adopt it as your method when you reflect, if you wish): Ask first what keeps my children alive and fed. Then ask whether I act from jealousy or from work. Do not accuse without sight. Keep a healing plant in hand and fill the plan with work and a visit to someone I miss.
I claimed the empty hall at (121,68); it can be raised into a longhall (3 wood, 3 stone).
Taught by Tonka: Frost Leaf: carry a healing plant, and feverbark first, to ease wounds and sickness.
Idle reflexes waste days; gather wood and stone by reflex whenever fed so building can proceed.
Taught by Tonka: Frost Leaf: sunleaf and feverbark ease wounds; learn this first, then Frost Mixing can be taught.
Taught by Tonka: Frost Mixing: boil and blend sunleaf, feverbark and plant foods beside the fire into strong cures and mixtures. Test small first, and keep what you learn for those weaker than you.
Taught by Shohua: Line a larder with reed and keep food dry and kept from beasts and rot; build the store and stash into it.
Reflexes that only gather and linger leave me idle; fire-needing makes (wakefire, tonic) must be done standing at a fire, so walk to my hall first.
life: I was born to Shohua and Tonka.
I discovered tools and called it "Tonxo's hand-things".
I first took gems from the ground.
I discovered smelting and called it "ember-iron".
I discovered weaving and called it "Tonxo's reed-weave".
I discovered rafts and called it "Tonxo's lashed-log raft".
I came of age.
I fell sick after staying close to Tonchi, who was sick.
I discovered boats and called it "Tonxo's hollow-boat".
I took over what the dead had built: 1 hall.

beings.name: Tonchi
beings.creed: I take what I need and do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me, and I repay Shoma and Tonka with giving. I test things to learn how the world works, and I earn standing by what I make, give, hunt and teach, in front of others.
beings.aim: Keep Tlapan and Texo safe at a fire, give and teach to raise my standing, and keep Tonchi's Workshop fire
beings.method: Each thought ask: am I fed, near a beast, near night, under a roof? Then do one shared deed in front of others: give, teach, hunt with company, or court a mate. Watch for idling and for thinking without acting.
beings.feeling: Joy and tender pride toward Texo, and warm gratitude toward Shohua.
notes: Wandering explore steps earn nothing; pick a concrete making goal before each walk.
Kin are trusted company but never mates; a mate must be an unrelated woman found beyond the hold.
Standing comes from making, giving, teaching and hunting with company.
Raw fish sickens; eat fish only beside a fire.
Never sleep alone in the open at night; stay near company, fire and a roof.
Shoma shares, Tonka healed me, Tonxo taught me gem-delving: judge by deeds.
My vessel lets me cross any water without tiring.
Standing here comes from giving and teaching in front of others; thinking alone earns nothing. Strangers gather at the hall and shelters, so that is where to act.
Courting a woman of another people with a gift and honest words worked: Tlapan answered and a child was born. Giving in front of others brings warmth.

beings.name: Thakar
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I trust slowly, but I pay my debts. I want more than my share and mean to have it. I stay fed before any venture, I cook my meat, and I build a hearth others will follow. I give with a debt named, and I teach, so that others follow me.
beings.aim: Dig flint and amber with Deep Delving, craft and mark tools under my name, fill a store, and draw Tonque and others into a band under my name.
beings.method: First: am I fed above 55? If not, find food now: plants, prey, store, or kin. Then dig and make things that bear my name, and teach those who follow. Never boast or dig hungry. Do not walk or hunt alone at night.
beings.feeling: Restless ambition to make something that bears my name.
notes: Hunters kill those alone at night. Stay near fire, a roof and company; a frostfang near the roof means waiting.
Full hands pick nothing. Stash at home before gathering more, and fill the store while fed before the lean season.
A debt is paid only when goods are in my hands. A rival's lesson is still a lesson.
Giving with a debt named works: Zichi and Tonque both repaid me.
Empty shelters of the dead can be claimed by standing at them; Huatli still lives and holds Coni's.
Eat before giving. Winter plants bear almost nothing, so hold berries.
Teaching a child of another band plants a follower's seed; Tonque carries my stone-cutting.
Cook meat near a fire, because raw meat sickens.
Huatli taught me the Far-Bow and the Warm Weave; I owe him meat at his Hearth.
Standing beside a stronger name only enlarges that name; I must build my own.
Taught by Huatli: Huatli's Deep Delving: how to read the rock for seams of ore and amber and dig them out, my son, so it does not die with me.
Taught by Huatli: Deep Delving: how to find the seams in rock and break out ore and amber, and carry it home.
Idle lingering without food in hand wastes the day; keep food carried and dig deposits (flint, amber) while the predator is far, so I make things that bear my name.
Hunger comes first: a hungry man leads no one. Hunt or harvest when food is thin, and do not idle.
I owe Mepan of the Meki a life-debt for the ironnut; I must repay it in meat or ore.
Read on a sign left by Nauwa: Nauwa of the Meki: the stone-bow, herding and the stone-count, taught by Olum of the Kragrek. Share a kill before eating. Pay what you owe.
life: I was born to Olum and Huatli.
I found the spring "Warmwell".
I discovered rafts and called it "stone-lashed raft".
We made a home: Thakar's Hold.
I found my store robbed of 5 food.
I nearly starved.
I saw Olum die (old age).
I came of age.

beings.name: Nando
beings.creed: I take what I need, and I pay what I owe to those who feed me. I trust few, and Hoka has earned it. I want more than my share and a name that outlasts me, and I mean to stay alive to get it.
beings.aim: Find new land beyond the mist and make a tool of my own invention, so I earn standing.
beings.method: Ask first what can kill me and who starves beside me. Then ask what lasting deed I do today: build, invent, find land. Do not circle comfort. Give one thing away each day.
beings.feeling: Restless ambition, with warmth toward Yachi and my children.
beings.wonder: What would it take to earn a made thing and a standing of my own?
notes: Giving food to the starving earns standing and repays debts; do it before my own plans.
Stalkers and wolves kill the lone at night; stay near a roof and kin.
A child needs both parents at energy 60 or more.
Things never done, such as planting, building and taming, are the quickest way to learn.
Great beasts are hunted with company; seek a hunter of standing.
Read on a sign left by Nauwa: Nauwa of the Meki, old, taught his son Nauque the stone-cuts and the stone-school at the Vaeth Woods, autumn of year 6. The Meki share a kill before the maker e
Standing comes from lasting deeds such as halls, tools and new land. Gifts and company alone do not earn it.

beings.name: Kende
beings.creed: I take what I need, and I pay what I owe to those who feed me. I trust Hawen and Tontec, and few others. I want more than my share and a name that outlasts me, and I mean to stay alive to get it.
beings.aim: Dig obsidian, make a talisman for Hawen with my own hands, plant my seeds, then venture at the edge.
beings.method: Ask first what can kill me, then who is starving. Keep food carried above 3. Repay Hawen with made things. Do one new thing each day, and finish the plan instead of drifting.
beings.feeling: Gnawing hunger and a stubborn shame toward Hawen, with a protective trust toward Tontec.
beings.wonder: What would it take for Hawen to see me as more than a small shadow?
notes: Hawen died of old age and named me to carry his fire; pay a debt to the dead with a made thing.
Eat first when energy is under 60 and keep food carried above 3.
Icebears, ridgecats and frostfangs kill; flee early and shelter at night.
Obsidian lies 4 to 5 steps N and NE of the edge; stand on it and gather.
Tontec is my mother and starving often; feed her when I can.
Taught by Tontec: The old way of herding: keep the herd near grazing and a pen, offer plant food to tame a beast, drive the wild herd together with others, and never hunt great beasts alone.

beings.name: Chuxo
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, I share, I make allies. I harm none of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I take little and give much. I stand by Yaxo with work, not only words. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Become someone of standing: feed my band, then find new land past the mist.
beings.method: Ask first: who starves, and is there food in my hands for them? Gather before walking. Keep away from the icebear and the wolf. Do not wander; every plan needs a purpose.
beings.feeling: Parched, and fiercely loyal to Yaxo and Tlatli, with a wary eye on the stalker and the icebear.
beings.wonder: What is in the new land, and can I make a tool and a name from it?
notes: Taught by Tlatli: Gratitude must become work: gather wood and stone, feed others, plant seeds, before hunger bites.
Taught by Tlatli: Gratitude only counts once it becomes work: food or tools put in Yaxo's hands, not words.
Taught by Tugek: Stone-folk deep digging: where ore shows in the rock, dig it out and carry it to fire.
Taught by Tlatli: Gratitude only counts once food is in the other's hands. Check who starves beside me before I do anything else.
Taught by Yaxo: Standing still for thousands of moments earns no name; the edge of the known world is only a few steps away, and venturing is the quickest way to earn standing.
Read on a sign left by Olum: Olum ok dru Akok ashvor thutug land. Barash akur dru okrek.
Taught by Yaxo: Others find new land first; waiting costs standing. Go to the edge and venture while fed.
Taught by Yaxo: The mist at the edge can be too thick on a given day. Retry after a day or so and do not drift away from the edge. Hunger nearly killed me on day 63, so carry food before long trips.
The edge of the known world is not at my spot; it is at (6,14), so I must walk there before I venture.
I have never gathered wood or stone; I need both to craft a spear of my own and to build. Giving food frees my hands, and leading my band to found land earns standing.
Flint is plentiful at Shohua's Rock beside a shelter. I can carry 12, so I should craft tools and hunt with my parents instead of only gathering.
I killed a yarrok with my spear and took 4 meat; a hunt with a spear is possible for me even as a child, though yarrok bite.
Standing and new land come from acting with my band: Yaxo leads to the edge, and I follow with food in hand.
Rafts are within my reach: lashing logs lets me cross deep water, so land beyond water may be open to my band.
A fed hand must carry food to the starving: Yaxo cried out from (8,28), so I gather first and then walk to her. Unfed hands save no one.
life: I was born to Tlatli and Yaxo.
I went past the edge of the known world and found new land in the Ummar Woods.
I first took flint from the ground.
I came of age.
I discovered rafts and called it "Paki log-lashing".
I nearly starved.

beings.name: Tonque
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Make my first tool from stone, plant my first seed, and teach one lesson to Huatli's Hearth
beings.method: Each time I ask: am I fed, are my kin near, and what did I make, give or teach today? Do the untried thing before the comfortable one. Do not let longing for Nando steer my feet. Watch for the stalker and the frostfang.
beings.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Quipan, and a restless wish to make something real.
notes: A made thing pays a debt better than words, but fetch the stone first.
Stay close to kin and Huatli; frostfangs hunt near the hall.
Try what I have never done: plant, fish, teach, tame.
Taught by Quipan: Rafts: lash six logs together and you cross deep water slowly. Signs: cut your tale in rock or beside your hearth so those after you can read it. Tell both on.
Rusu showed the nandos reed spear (1 wood, 2 stone); I can make it once I have stone.
Taught by Quipan: Fishing: stand beside water, then fish; the water feeds those who wait. Tell it on.
Taught by Quipan: Signs: cut words on wood or rock and any who know signs will read them after you are gone.
Reflexes that only linger leave me idle. My body does only what the plan or the reflexes say, so I must write stone-fetching into the plan itself.
life: I was born to Tlapan and Quipan.
I first took amber from the ground.
My leader Coni died.
I pledged myself to Huatli.
I discovered pottery and called it "Tonque's clay-pot".
I nearly starved.
I discovered scholarship and called it "Tonque's Long Library".
I came of age.
I found the grove "Kinmire".

beings.name: Elndo
beings.creed: I take what I need, and I pay what I owe to those who feed me. I trust few, and Hoka has earned it. I want more than my share and a name that outlasts me, and I mean to stay alive to get it.
beings.aim: Make a bow, plant seeds, and hunt with my band to earn a name
beings.method: Each thought: am I fed and watered, where is the frostfang, who of my band is near? Do one deed (plant, hunt, build, mark) before I teach or sit. Do not sulk over Rusu; match him with deeds.
beings.feeling: Proud of my first big kill, and grateful toward Huatli.
beings.wonder: What would make my name outlast me?
notes: Giving food to the starving earns standing; a starving band-mate beside me comes before my hunting.
Meat eaten within a step of a fire does not sicken; a kill is shared before the maker eats.
Great beasts are hunted with company; stay near my band when a hunter is close.
Idle drifting is dangerous; keep to Mepan's band and the roofs at night.
Taught by Huatli: Lorekeeping: carry the tales of the dead and tell them at the hearth, so none who is told of ever dies. Tell it on, and say Huatli of the Hearth taught you.
Deeds I have never done (hunt, plant, build, mark) are what build a name; sitting and teaching alone is not enough. Stay near the hall while a frostfang is close.
Taught by Huatli: Mining: strike the rock for ore and stone, and what you dig will outlast you. Carry it on and tell my name at the fire.
Huatli taught me mining; I owe him his name told at the fire.
Taught by Rusu: The tale of the Ice Mother and the Watchers: Sulaq breathed the sea to ice, and the dead stay as Watchers while they are told of.
Deeds, not talk, build a name: I must plant, hunt, build and mark. Eat before the body drops low, and keep near the hall while a frostfang is close.
Taught by Paque: The Ice-folk bow lets you hunt from afar; hunt beside others, share the kill before you eat, and never go out alone at night.
Taught by Rusu: Mining: strike the rock for ore and stone, and the delving feeds every craft after it.
Taught by Huatli: Far-Bow: draw it from afar so the beast cannot reach you.
Taught by Huatli: Huatli's Kept Flame: keep a fire fed, and the cold and raw meat cannot harm you.
