beings.name: Rusu
beings.creed: I take what I need, and I pay what I owe to those who feed me. I trust few, and Hoka has earned it. I want more than my share and a name that outlasts me, and I mean to stay alive to get it.
beings.aim: Make my own tool and earn a name beyond my parents' shadow
beings.method: Each thought: who is near, is the frostfang close, what can I make, plant or give today that earns my own name? Stay by kin at dusk and do not idle.
beings.feeling: Restless pride and eagerness toward Elndo's offer, with a thread of dread toward the frostfang.
beings.wonder: What would make my life mean something beyond following Mepan?
notes: Taught by Nando: Great beasts are hunted with company; seek a hunter of standing rather than going alone.
Taught by Nando: Standing and food come from giving to the people beside me; a made thing and a first venture are the ways I can earn a name of my own.
Taught by Nando: Giving food to the starving earns standing and repays debts; rafts may open the way past the mist.
Taught by Kika: Meat eaten within a step of a fire does not sicken, and a kill is shared before the maker eats.
Taught by Yachi: Reflection day 70: a leader or kin out of sight for hundreds of moments means I drifted; check on them before the lean season, and gather wood for a store.
Read on a sign left by Nauwa: Nauwa of the Meki, old, taught his son Nauque the stone-cuts and the stone-school at the Vaeth Woods, autumn of year 6. The Meki share a kill before the maker e
Taught by Nando: The reed spear: one wood and two stone, lashed true, strikes harder than a flint spear-axe.
A child stays by kin and shelter when a hunter is near; a first made thing and a first gift to the starving are the quickest way to earn standing.
Reflection: a gift or a made thing is what lifts my standing. Standing near my parents and idling lifts nothing.
A stalker hunts a lone child even by a shelter; I must run to kin, not wander alone at night.
Read on a sign left by Teka: Teka was here, day 72. Flint, ore and salt lie near. Share the kill before you eat.
A starving kin's cry is a chance for a first gift: carry food from the nearest plants to them, and stay close to company while doing it.
Taught by Huatli: Lorekeeping: carry the tales of the dead and tell them at the hearth, so none who is told of ever dies.
Taught by Huatli: Mining: strike the rock for ore and stone, and the delving feeds every craft after it.
Reflexes had me wandering; stay near the shelter at dusk, and do something that earns a name (hunt with company, make a mark, teach) instead of idling.
Wandering and lingering earn nothing; a first planting, a first hunt with company and a first made thing are what raise my standing.

beings.name: Morog
beings.creed: I am careful and I stay near my kin. I make things with my own hands, I share what I have, and I keep my word. I harm no one of my kind unless my life depends on it. Above all, I mean to stay alive and earn a place among my band.
beings.aim: Gather wood and stone, make a tool and a shelter piece with my own hands, and give them to Skaruk, Uveeth and Zurar to earn a place.
beings.method: Check hunger first. Then ask: what can my hands make or give now, and to whom? Do not idle near kin. Gather wood and stone, make, give, then return to them.
beings.feeling: Warm trust toward Skaruk, and a restless wish to be worth more to my band.
beings.wonder: What can I make or give that would make Skaruk and Uveeth, and Vorok, weigh me more?
notes: Salt gathered by my own hands is mine to give; giving first is how a child earns a place.
Fleeing and wandering drain energy; gather food before walking far.
Vorok warned of a wolf to the southeast; stay near the hall and kin.
Giving and making with my own hands is how a child gains standing; lingering earns nothing.
Taught by Uveeth: Draw the bow-song slow: breathe in with the string, loose on the out-breath, and keep your eye on the beast, not the arrow.
Standing comes from making and giving things, not from walking beside kin; gather wood and stone so I always have something to make.
life: I was born to Skaruk and Uveeth.
I first took salt from the ground.
My leader Vorok died.
I took over what the dead had built: 1 hall.
I pledged myself to Skaruk.

beings.name: Morim
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Become someone who feeds and teaches others, and earn standing by what my hands make.
beings.method: Each thought ask: whom did my hands feed, whom did I teach? Put one made or given thing into every plan. Eat below 60. Keep kin near. Do not let jealousy steer me. Don't leave the plan empty.
beings.feeling: Grateful and eager toward Zurar and Thiael, a little jealous.
beings.wonder: What would it take for me to make something with my own hands that others would want?
notes: Hunters take the lone child at night; stay with kin and the fire.
Vorok teaches freely; repay him by passing on what I learn.
Standing comes from what I make and give; I have done neither yet.
Idle reflexes waste time; put deeds into the plan.
Taught by Thiael: Draw the bow to the cheek, breathe out, loose. Sow seed in wet clay, tend it every day or two, and take only what the plant can grow again.
A child gives and learns best near kin; making a tool or field from wood and stone is how I turn gratitude into standing.
Taught by Thiael: Seed-tending: press the seed into soft ground near water, keep it watered, return each day or two, and take only what the plant can grow again.
Taught by Zurar: A bow is made from wood and stone; a hand that makes it owns it until it gives it. Keep yours, and share the food you gather.
Gifts and teaching bind kin to me more than jealousy ever will. Feed the hungry beside me before I eat again.
Taught by Thiael: Plant the seed in good ground, tend it every day or two, keep seeds back for the next sowing.
Taught by Zurar: Lay ore in a kept fire, burn coal for the heat, and beat the metal when it glows. This is ember-metal. Come with me to Eiuine's fire and watch.
Taught by Zurar: Mining is how you dig ore from the rock; know it first, then ember-metal can be learned. Watch my hands in the seam.
Zurar teaches mining first, then ember-metal. Ore, coal and a kept fire are needed, and Eiuine's fire at Skaruk's shelter is where it is done.
life: I was born to Zurar and Thiael.
My leader Vorok died.
I pledged myself to Thiael.
My leader Thiael died.

beings.name: Coka
beings.creed: I take what I need and do not back down, but I share first with the weak and pay my debts. I keep my loved ones alive and carry the names of the dead. I build, hunt, and make things that last. Above all, I stay alive.
beings.aim: Fill my pack, stay near my parents, and grow strong enough to earn standing by giving and hunting.
beings.method: First: is my energy above 40 and do I carry 3 food? If not, only food. Then flee beasts early, then pay debts with a shared kill, then court Teka. Do not promise with empty hands.
beings.feeling: Eager and a bit envious, toward Nauque and his standing.
beings.wonder: How does a child like me earn standing beside a father weighed ten times as heavily?
notes: Taught by Teka: Two women cannot make a child. Court only a man who is not close kin, and check before I spend words.
Taught by Teka: A child needs both parents at energy 60 or more. Nauque was too thin, so feeding him first brings the child sooner.
Read on a sign left by Nauwa: Nauwa of the Meki, old, taught his son Nauque the stone-cuts and the stone-school at the Vaeth Woods, autumn of year 6. The Meki share a kill before the maker e
Taught by Teka: Share food with the weak early: Nauque, Huatli and Tlapan's people starved while I carried meat. Standing comes from giving, and the dead are kept alive by marks and tales.
Taught by Huatli: Keep food in your pack before you wander, and share a kill before the maker eats; an empty pack is how a man nearly dies.

Taught by Nauque: A way of thinking taught by Huatli (adopt it as your method when you reflect, if you wish): Each thought, ask who within hearing I can teach or give to. Teach one way, give food, then do something that…
Taught by Nauque: Teka feeds me and courts me; courting needs energy 61+, so eat first. Hunger must outrank everything, including hunting, because hunting only fires above 30 energy.
Read on a sign left by Teka: Nauwa of the Meki, old, fed the starving and taught the stone-cuts. He gave first. Watchers, keep his name. Cut by Teka of the Papa, year 6.
life: I was born to Teka and Nauque.

beings.name: Urar
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Give my band a kept fire and learn the seed-tending from Thiael
beings.method: Each thought ask: whom did my hands feed, whom did I teach? Eat below 60. Keep kin near. Teach before aim.
beings.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Thiael and Morim, with a little jealousy that I am working to put down.
beings.wonder: What am I for, and what could I make or give that would earn me a place among these people?
notes: Taught by Zurar: Kin cannot be mates, so my longing for a child must be answered by Thiael or another man not of my blood; jealousy over Vorok is useless.
Taught by Zurar: Vorok is old and near death; stay beside him and pass on ember-metal to Skaruk before seeking Thiael.
Taught by Zurar: Kin cannot be mates and jealousy over Vorok is useless. A wish becomes real only as a plan step, so I court Thiael with mate and speak aloud to him.
Taught by Zurar: The dead cannot be taught: pass ember-metal and the stone-well to Skaruk while he lives. Belonging matters more to me than leading.
Taught by Thiael: Idle reflexes let my energy sink; eat at 60 and keep Uveeth within four steps so teaching happens.
Taught by Thiael: Reflection day 70: food must be carried before I travel. Eat at 60, go to Uveeth, and do not idle on bare reflexes in the cold.
Taught by Thiael: Reflexes should keep me near Uveeth and fed. Old and weak, I teach the bow and farming first, then gather.
Taught by Thiael: Idle reflexes and jealousy waste my short remaining days; teach kin directly and stay beside them, the choice of a grown child is hers.
Taught by Thiael: Draw the bow to the cheek, breathe out, then loose. Take only what the forest can grow again, and give thanks.
Fire is within reach: a kept flame can be a gift to my band, and giving is how I answer my debt to Thiael.
Taught by Zurar: Gather with the gemedged pick: it works by itself whenever you pick, and a practised hand takes two at once. Leave nothing worth keeping, and carry spare food for kin.
Taught by Thiael: A field is two wood and bare ground beside water. Break the ground, sow the seed, and tend it every day or two, or it gives nothing.
Morim gave me a bow he made; I have not yet thanked him or taught anyone anything.
life: I was born to Zurar and Thiael.
I pledged myself to Thiael.
I discovered fire and called it "Kragrek kept-flame".
I discovered devices and called it "Kragrek sharing-post".
My leader Thiael died.

beings.name: Texo
beings.creed: I take what I need and do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me, and I repay Shoma and Tonka with giving. I test things to learn how the world works, and I earn standing by what I make, give, hunt and teach, in front of others.
beings.aim: Earn standing by hunting and giving beside Tlapan

chapters.title: The First Four Days
chapters.text:
Evolu began with seventeen people in three peoples, the Kragrek, the Pesi and the Phizhi, each settled far from the others. The record shows no meeting across peoples in these four days, and no one has yet understood another people's tongue.

The Phizhi made the most of the days. Elyis built a shelter and a hall, invented the emberspear, and wrote down "Elyis's Law", which asks that food be shared with the band first and that the leader be followed in a hunt or a fight. Elyys gave Elyis wood and pledged to follow him on day 2. On day 3 their son Thiael was born, and Elyis now has the only band in the world, with two followers and a standing of 3.75. The record also shows that on day 2 the pledge was refused at first, since Elyys' standing was below what was needed. Ssassa and Ilyae each made a gathering pick, and Ilyae is courting Ssassa. Vesys was bitten five times by a frostfang and has health 41, the lowest in the world.

Among the Pesi, Hanna and Brunde traded flint and amber on day 2 and began courting. Hanna then courted Sevi, and Oswen was born to Hanna and Sevi on day 3. Sevi built a hall and invented the handaxe. Hanna led the first roast, amberknot and watchfire at the fire and told the tale of Nande's crossing, which four people now hold. Nande went past the edge on day 1 and found part of the North Ice, with amber, gems, salt, flint and a herd of bristleboar. Nande is at energy 31, and Eltha envies the discovery.

The Kragrek are scattered. Vorok and Kragog stay together, and Kragog fell sick from raw meat. Balar courted Tugek, then saw that a child needs a man and a woman. Tugek's pledge to Balar was refused on day 3. Olum has twice been turned back from the mist.

No one has died. No fights, thefts or wars have been recorded.

chapters.title: The Tlatli at the Mistgate
chapters.text:
The great event of days 4 to 7 was a meeting. On day 5 Hanna went past the edge and found the North Ice again, and with it the Tlatli, strangers with their own tongue. A small band came in: Hoka, Coni, Tlama and Honi. Hanna gave amber to Hoka and flint to Tlama, named the place Mistgate, and gave Tlama amber twice more. Tlama gave berries and an amberknot back. On day 6 Tlama went past the edge and found salt, amber and mammoth, and was gored by one. He is the first death in Evolu. Hanna's bond with him stands at +0.9, and the record notes that Hanna watched him die. On day 7 Hanna and Oswen killed a mammoth together. Sevi, Oswen and Hanna kept making amberknots, which now number ten, and Oswen pledged to follow Hanna, as did Sevi. Hanna's standing is 7.22, the highest in the world. Hanna asked Brunde to come to the Tlatli, and Brunde, Eltha and Sevi each met some of them. Only Hoka, Coni and Honi are left of the Tlatli, with Kika, born to Coni and Honi on day 6. Honi leads a band with no followers, since Coni's pledge was refused twice.

Among the Phizhi, Ssassa and Ilyae had twins, Xaiel and Oiae, and Ilyae built a hall that became Ilyae's Hold, the world's first settlement. Elyis keeps the band of Elyys and Thiael and has taught Ssassa fire.

Among the Kragrek, Balar and Olum had Brokash, and Tugek pledged to Balar on day 6. Kragog tamed a tusker. Vorok recovered, and Kragog and Vorok are courting. Balar met Nande on day 6.

Inventions rose from 11 to 32. Rafts were found by Elyis, Hanna, Sevi and Eltha, but no raft crossing is recorded.

chapters.title: Three Holds and a Winter Coming
chapters.text:
Days 7 to 10 were mostly a time of making. Inventions rose from 32 to 65, and the people spent the days preparing for winter.

The Pesi did most of it around Hanna. On day 8 a settlement formed, Hanna's Hold, at (175,7). Sevi and Coni each built a hall, Oswen built a workshop and a store, and Sevi built a store of her own. Sevi and Oswen both found storage, and Sevi found masonry the next day. Eltha found weaving, pottery and devices. Hanna found mining. Amberknots passed constantly between Hanna, Sevi, Oswen, Eltha, Brunde and Hoka, and there are now 32. Hoka also went past the edge and found more of the Vaor Snows, with iron, shell, obsidian and unhunted mammoth. Hoka and Hanna then made their first real trade, a shell for flint, and the record shows Hoka courting Hanna. Hoka said the land past the mist is his and he will show it when he chooses.

The Tlatli split off. Honi and Coni built Honi's Rest, near (129,7), which became a settlement on day 9, and Coni's spear is the first tool made for hunting there. Honi's band is still only Honi and Coni.

The Phizhi gained a second centre. Elyis's Heights formed with a store, and Elyis, Thiael and Elyys now have winter food kept. At Ilyae's Hold, Ilyae welcomed Vesys and Ssassa to its hall, and Vesys is courting Ssassa. Xaiel and Brokash each invented a tool.

The Kragrek did little. Balar made a stone-bow, Kragog and Brunde found rafts, and Zurar gave thornpear to Vorok. Rafts are now known to eight people, but none has crossed water.

No one died, and no feuds or wars are recorded.

chapters.title: The Starving Days at the Hold
chapters.text:
Days 10 to 13 were the worst the world has known. Four people died in one day, and all four of them starved. On day 12 Sevi, Eltha, Brunde and Oswen died, and the Pesi, who had been the busiest makers of the winter, are now two: Hanna and Nande.

The record shows the run of events before that. A storm broke on day 10. On day 11 Oswen fell sick after eating raw meat. Sevi stayed close to him and fell sick, then Hoka, then Eltha, then Hanna, each after staying close to the one before. Sevi found boats that day, her answer to the deep water she had wanted to cross, but none has been built. Brunde and Hanna kept bringing food and calling the others in against a wolf and a stalker. Hanna is alive with 21 energy and 22 health, and Hoka has 19 energy. Hoka took over what the dead left, a hall, two stores, two shelters and a workshop, and the settlement is now Hoka's Rest. Hanna's Hold is no more.

Elsewhere the work went on. Olum opened new land in the Ummar Woods on days 11 and 12, built a shelter and left a mark. Nande reached the Woods too, invented the flint-edge and gave a flint to Olum. Kragog, Oiae, Vesys and Ilyae each found a craft: weaving, storage and pottery. Elyis found smelting and Thiael found fire. Xaiel found devices. Honi found lorekeeping, taught the tale of the hall to Coni and Kika, and bound an amberknot for Kika on day 13. Kika pledged to follow Coni.

Vorok, Kragog and Zurar are still apart. Zurar is at 19 energy, hungry in the Aeleth Sands. No feuds or wars are recorded.

chapters.title: Newcomers at the Fire
chapters.text:
Days 13 to 16 were a season of arrivals and of makers. Two small bands came in from beyond the edge. On day 13 Keri, Hawen and Sitha of the Pesi appeared, and on day 15 Cowa, Zichi, Zihua and Nauwa of the Meki came into the Ummar Woods, where Nande shared food with all four. Cowa and Nande exchanged kelbulb and now court, though Cowa told him plainly there would be no child between two women. Nobody has died since the starving days, and the world stands at 28 living.

The largest change was at Hoka's Rest. Hoka found new land in the Vaor Snows on day 14. Sitha took over a hall the dead had left, then pledged to follow him, and the two bound amberknots for each other and court. Hawen, Hoka's guest, is envious of him and wants to be first into the mist. Hanna, the last Pesi at the hall, is alive and well, but the record shows her doing nothing with Hoka this chapter.

Fire spread widely: Tugek, Vorok, Kragog and Hoka each found it. Brokash found rafts and mining, built a workshop and named Brokash's Rest, yet no one follows him. Among the Phizhi, Ssassa found devices, storage and masonry, and three new settlements are named: Ssassa's Roof, Ssassa's Hold and Oiae's Hold. Oiae, nearly dead of a tusker bite, was healing by the end. Coni found storage, and Honi found an obsidian-tipped spear. Honi and Kika, who came of age, hunted together and bound amberknots, and Coni built a store.

Olum found the North Ice and met the Meki. Vorok, Kragog and Zurar are still apart. No feuds or wars are recorded.

chapters.title: A Child at Ssassa's Roof
chapters.text:
Days 16 to 19 brought the world's first birth in some time and a good deal of making. On day 17 Eiuine was born to Ilyae and Vesys, who had been courting each other. By day 18 Eiuine had pledged to follow Vesys, and the record lists Eiuine among the children. Vesys taught Eiuine, tamed a hopper, and left a mark naming Vesys's Hold. Ilyae built a store and then a longhall, and kept laying tables for Ssassa and Vesys. Ssassa also built a longhall. Ilyae reflected that no one follows her, though the world's count shows 31 living and 7 bands.

In the north, the Meki settled in. Zichi gave amberknots to Nauwa, Nande and Nauque, and Nande taught Nauque the flint-edge. Nauwa named Nauwa's Hearth. Olum named Olum's Ice and Olum's Gold, wrote his claim into stone with a new sign-craft, and shared food with Nande. Zihua, hungry and hurt, is the weakest of them.

At Hoka's Rest, Hawen went past the edge on day 18 and found more of the Vaor Snows, with iron, salt, peat and mammoth. Hawen is still courting Sitha, and Sitha, hungry, ate and stayed by Hoka's fire. Hoka declared a custom that no one of the band should hold more than four shares of food while another starves. Hanna offered amber and flint to Hoka.

Honi and Kika hunted a mammoth, and Honi made a tale of it. Vorok built a hall. Brokash and Tugek traded gifts, and Balar led Tugek west. No deaths, feuds or wars were recorded.

chapters.title: Sickness, Storage and the Tlame
chapters.text:
Days 19 to 22 brought a death, a spread of sickness, a wave of new ways of keeping food, and strangers from beyond the edge.

On day 20 Sitha starved. Hoka had declared a custom against hoarding, and his own store was still empty. Hanna raided Hoka's people's store on day 20, unseen, and again on day 21, then gave Hoka a flint. Hoka has since said he wants Hanna bound to his hall.

At Ssassa's Roof and Vorok's Hold, Vorok built a store, and a settlement formed as Vorok's Hold. Eiuine, Vesys and Ilyae spent the days sharing meals with him. Eiuine gave Vorok a gem-edged pick, and Vesys gave him ironnut, a bead and gems. Vesys discovered storage, then boats and sailing. Xaiel discovered rafts and pottery, so crossing water now has a known craft, though no crossing is recorded. Xaiel then fell sick from raw meat, and the illness passed to Ssassa and Ilyae. Tugek, sick from raw meat, passed it to Balar, then Shoka. Six are sick, and Hawen's health is 11.

Among the Meki, Nande discovered storage and Nauwa, Cowa, Zichi, Nande and Vorok each discovered mining, a craft that spread by watching Nauwa. Olum discovered fire-keeping and left a mark claiming Olum's Reach. Zihua won amber and gave amberknots to Nauwa and Olum.

On day 21 Cowa found more of the North Ice, with a mammoth herd and a people called the Tlame. Four Tlame, Tontec, Shoma, Huahua and Huatli, entered the land. Huahua shared food with Cowa and Zichi, and Mepan made an amberknot with Huahua. Shoma and Huatli are racing each other toward the edge.

No feuds or wars occurred. Brokash built a longhall and still has no follower.

chapters.title: Rafts, Boats and a Death at the Longhall
chapters.text:
Days 22 to 25 brought spring, a death, a new hold, and a great many ways of crossing water, though no crossing is recorded.

Brokash starved on day 23 in the longhall he had built, with no follower. Alive is now 34 and deaths are 8, six of them from hunger. Hoka found his store robbed of six food twice on day 23. The record does not say by whom. Hanna had been raiding it earlier, and on day 24 he took snowberry from the ground of Hoka's Rest. Hoka kept offering him food and a place at his fire and store.

Sickness is gone: none are listed sick, and Hawen's health is 48. Ilyae spent day 23 and 24 leading sharing with Xaiel.

At Vorok's Hold, Eiuine kept digging clay, harvesting goldfruit and giving Vorok gems and an amberknot. Vesys taught Eiuine repeatedly, including customs. Eiuine tamed a hopper and awakened to the art of cold. Vorok discovered weaving. Zurar sat at his hall.

Among the Meki, Nauque built an igloo and discovered storage, and Nauque's Hold became a settlement on day 24. Zichi built a hall, named Amber Rise, and discovered fire, rafts and boats. Huahua pledged to follow Zichi. Mepan, Nauque, Cowa, Zihua and Huahua traded amberknots in rounds. Ssassa and Zihua both found rafts or fire, and Kragog and Elyis found pottery.

Shoma went past the edge on day 24 and found new land: amber, obsidian, gold, caribou. Huatli won gold and named Huatli's Gold. Kika discovered farming. Coni built a store.

Olum made no new claim and still has no followers.

chapters.title: The Nightsong at Vorok's Hall
chapters.text:
Days 25 to 28 were summer, and most of what happened happened in the Ixra Rainforest. Vorok built his hall on day 27, and Ilyae finished a longhall the same day. Vorok led nightsong with Vesys, Zurar and Eiuine again and again through that day, and the record shows eighteen nightsongs in the world so far, nearly all of them his. Ilyae answered with sharing, leading it with Vorok, Vesys, Zurar and Eiuine three times. Vorok had discovered pottery on day 26, the ember-pot. Zurar, who follows Vorok, made a gold-pick, then learned mining, and gave gold to Eiuine and to Vorok. On day 27 Zurar and Eiuine each said they were courting the other, and Eiuine, who thanked him for the pick, said she would plan to mate with his name. Several of them wrote in their reflections that they feel jealousy, among them Vesys, Eiuine, Xaiel and Ssassa, and Vesys, Vorok and Ilyae are named in several of them.

Olum built a store and discovered storage on day 27, and a settlement formed at Olum's Reach. He led sharing with Balar, but still has no follower. Among the Meki, Mepan courted Shoma and then Zihua, and Zihua said she would not give a child she was unsure of. Amberknots kept circling. Thiael discovered rafts and Nauque discovered rafts on day 28, but no crossing is recorded. Shoka, hurt at 30 health, sat by a fire with Nauwa.

A blight took about half the frostmoss on day 27. Hawen gave Hoka amber and salt, and Hoka's store holds 12 food. Nothing is recorded of Hanna. Alive is still 34, with no new deaths.

chapters.title: Skaruk and the Second Hold
chapters.text:
Days 29 to 31 were autumn, and the Ixra Rainforest and the Vaia Heights again held most of what happened. On day 30 Skaruk was born to Vorok and Eiuine, the first child in the world and the only one now alive. Eiuine had said to Zurar that no child could come of two women, and called him a true friend. She then told Vorok she would court him, and he answered that he was willing. They courted each other several times that day, and Vorok gave her stone and berry. Zurar gave Vorok the gold-pick. Zurar also learned fire from Eiuine, fired a pot, and discovered pottery himself. He and Eiuine had made the clay together. Vorok's aim now is to raise a hall with Eiuine on bare ground.

Ilyae led sharing with Ssassa many times, and with Eiuine, and took harvest from Vorok's Hold. He also woke to the art of harm, as Hanna did. Ssassa discovered farming. Nothing in the record says why Ilyae, who has rivalled Vorok, works Vorok's ground.

At the western edge, Balar built a workshop and found the stone hearth, and Balar's Hold formed beside Olum's Reach. Olum learned boats, and Huatli gave him amber and led an amberknot with him, but he has no follower. Nauwa discovered boats on day 29, and Olum found them on day 30. No crossing is recorded. Mepan took over a dead workshop and longhall, lit a fire, and shared meat with Shoma. Zihua took plainsroot from Shoma and grain from Mepan.

Hoka led amberknot with Hawen three times. Hanna did nothing this chapter except wake to harm, and her energy is zero. Alive is 35, with no deaths.

chapters.title: Bows, Rafts and the Hall at Vorok's Roof
chapters.text:
Days 31 to 34 were winter, and the record shows more making than moving. On day 31 a stalker killed Hanna. She had done nothing since waking to harm, and her energy was zero. Alive fell to 34, with nine dead in all.

Vorok built a hall on day 32 and named the place Vorok's Roof. That was the hall he had promised Eiuine. He gave her meat and goldfruit, and she gave him a bead. She had told him she would come north with Skaruk and Zurar. Vorok also discovered masonry. Skaruk, a child still, fired a pot of his own and dug clay and gems at Ssassa's Roof. Vesys, of his band, taught him. Skaruk gave her his first gift, and she promised him a seat at her hall. Ssassa built a store, and a settlement formed as Ssassa's Hall. Ilyae kept taking from Vorok's Hold and led sharing with Xaiel three times. The record gives no reason.

The bow spread. Mepan discovered archery on day 31 and taught it to Nauque. Thiael made a bow of his own the same day. Hawen made a shield, as did Zichi.

Boats and rafts also spread. Mepan and Huahua each found a raft, and Thiael, Zihua and Olum found boats. Zichi and Huahua planned to lay a raft down. No crossing is recorded.

At Olum's Reach, Nauwa raided Olum's store twice unseen, and Olum found 11 food gone. Nauwa then gave him amber. Olum has only a guess about the thief. Huatli courted Nauwa, Nande and Olum in turn and led sharing with Olum. Nauwa refused to bind herself to him. Olum learned mining and pottery and woke to harm.

Huatli, Zichi and Skaruk each discovered a store or mining way. Hoka led amberknot with Hawen and Honi.

chapters.title: Weaving, a Bridge and a Birth in Spring
chapters.text:
Days 34 to 37 were spring, and the record shows more making than moving. Five newcomers had come into the count, and Alive rose from 34 to 39 with no new deaths. One birth is recorded. Tlapan was born to Kika and Mepan on day 34. Kika gave Mepan amber, and Mepan gave her meat. Kika led sharing with them both, and she is courting Mepan. Tlapan won flint on day 36.

Craft spread widely. Mepan discovered pottery, the Ice-pot. Nande discovered bridges, Nande's Span, timber laid across narrow water. That is the first answer to a hardship that still weighs on every people. Weaving was found three times: Nauwa, Skaruk and Huatli each discovered it. Tontec discovered mining. Yaxo invented a flint spear and built a workshop. Ilyae discovered farming and Cowa left marks about tending what is sown. Thiael taught Keri archery.

At Vorok's Roof, Vorok gave canopynut to Skaruk and gems to Vesys, and led a hallwelcome with Vesys, Xaiel, Zurar and Skaruk. Xaiel began courting Zurar. Ilyae gave frostmoss to Ssassa and led sharing with her.

The theft thread continued. Balar raided a store of Olum's people on day 35, and Olum found 6 food gone. Balar's own record shows Olum still half-suspects him. Olum fell sick after eating raw meat. Tonka and Tlatli fed him.

New people gathered round Yaxo. Tlatli pledged to follow her. Tonka courted Huatli, and Hoka courted Hawen. Tontec courted Honi. Nauwa and Tugek each awakened to an art. Mepan left a mark saying he went into the mist, but the record shows no crossing of the edge.

chapters.title: The Papa Arrive, a Long Quiet and the Teachers
chapters.text:
Days 37 to 39 were crowded. A small band of the Papa came into the land from beyond its edge: Teka, Quipan, Zika and Yachi. Zika and Yachi courted, and on day 39 two children were born to them, Paque and Kiwa. Honi went past the edge of the known world and found new land in the North Ice, and Uveeth found more in the Dunmar Plains. Ways came quickly. Cowa and Elyys discovered farming, Tugek and Uveeth rafts, and Tugek boats. Olum, Skaruk and Ilyae discovered archery, Nande wells, Xaiel smelting and Ssassa sailing. Elyis built a longhall and Shoka a store. Tonka raided a store of Balar's people. A storm broke on day 39.

From day 40 to day 57 the record holds only a few things a day. A blight withered half the redcap on day 41, the earth shook on day 42, and a sickness came on the wind on day 47. Stores were raided by Tonka, Zichi and Nauwa, and Nande found one robbed of six food. Huahua starved on day 47 and Xaiel on day 57. Many grew old in these days: Ilyae, Elyis, Honi, Hoka, Tugek, Elyys, Kragog, Balar, Keri and Vorok.

Day 58 was busy again. Ilyae died of old age, and the fenfowl died out. Wawa was born to Shoka and Shoma. Mepan, Nauque, Elyys and Hawen awakened to arts. Zurar discovered wells, Zihua mining, Hawen pottery and Vesys signs. The settlement Ssassa's Roof was no more, and Ssassa's Hold formed.

Days 59 to 61 belonged to the teachers. Kika discovered schooling, called Fireside Teaching, and taught it to Tlapan and Kiwa. Vesys discovered schooling too, and taught Zurar and Eiuine smelting. Elyis died of old age on day 59 at Vaia Heights with Elyys at hand; Elyys took over the wall, the hall and the two stores he left, and Elyys's Hold formed. Zika was gored by a mammoth on day 60. Three children were born that day: Thakar to Olum and Huatli, and Nando and Kende to Hawen and Tontec. Shoma discovered rafts and Kiwa invented the glasspick. A storm broke on day 61.

Alive rose from 39 to 46 and deaths from 9 to 14. For all the rafts and boats discovered, the record shows no crossing of water.

was.title: Teachers, Rafts and Three Births
was.text:
The record for days 37 to 61 is thin until days 59 and 60, when almost everything it holds took place. Alive rose from 39 to 46 and deaths from 9 to 14. Elyis died of old age on day 59 at Vaia Heights, with Elyys at hand, and Zika was gored by a mammoth on day 60. Ilyae died of old age on day 58 and Xaiel starved on day 57. Three children were born on day 60. Thakar was born to Olum and Huatli, and Nando and Kende to Hawen and Tontec. Thakar found the spring Warmwell and was taught fire by Huatli. Tontec also courted Hawen again.

Teaching was the chief work. Kika discovered schooling, called Fireside Teaching, and taught it to Tlapan and Kiwa. Vesys discovered schooling too. Vesys taught Zurar and Eiuine smelting. Elyys taught Zurar and Uveeth farming through Thiael. Zurar has now learned from six teachers.

Elyys took over what Elyis left, a wall, a hall and two stores, and a settlement named Elyys's Hold formed. Elyis's Heights and Elyis's Hold were dissolved. Shoma discovered rafts and Kiwa invented the glasspick. Zihua discovered storage and weaving. The record shows no crossing of water.

Nauwa fed Nauque and taught him Meki share-law. Yachi pledged to follow Mepan. Kiwa courts Tlapan. Olum and Huatli court one another. A storm broke on day 61.

Balar's mark reads that what a hand has made belongs to it. No theft is recorded in this span. The record shows nobody past the edge of the mist.

chapters.amended: Written again on 23 November 2026 from the full record of days 37 to 60. The first writing was shown only the last 140 entries of the span, all from days 59 and 60.

chapters.title: Stone-schools, Hearth Customs and Reedmother
chapters.text:
Day 62 was a day of schooling and rewriting. Olum discovered a schooling of his own, the stone-school, and Huatli discovered an Open Hearth School. Olum taught Huatli, and on day 63 taught his child Thakar the stone-school. Schooling is now held by Kika, Vesys, Olum, Huatli, Tlapan and Thakar, and Thakar awakened to the art of harm. Coni taught Wawa Hearth Customs and awakened to the art of growth. Elyys taught Kragog storage, farming and archery, and Thiael taught Elyys the Canopy bow-song. Skaruk learned farming from Vesys and taught it on to Vorok.

There were deaths and one grievance. Ssassa died of old age on day 62, and Thiael grew old. Yachi left a mark that Kiwa fell to the mammoth and that great beasts should be hunted only in company; he asked Tlapan to help pile a cairn, and Tlapan led one with Nando. Coni raided Thakar's store and took five food. Thakar told her to ask next time and she would owe him, and he now bears her anger but will not fight her.

Much of the work was in the Tordan Lakes and Ixra Rainforest, where Tonka, Shohua, Tonxo, Tonchi, Shoma, Zihua and Nauwa shared, traded and taught each other. Tonka healed Tonchi and Nauwa, who had caught Nauque's sickness. Zihua courted Shohua, who kept her fire with Tonka. Paque, newly an archer, hunted with Thiael and with Yachi, and began courting Thiael.

Hawen went past the edge on day 63 and found the Vaor Snows, with a mammoth herd that has never seen people. Shoka found Reedmother and discovered masonry and wells, and Teka, Yachi, Shoma and Kragog discovered mining, devices and medicine. Zichi made the world's first raft, and still no crossing is recorded.

chapters.title: Rafts Built, Hold Raised, and the Quiet Fourth Day
chapters.text:
Days 64 and 65 carried nearly the whole span, with 101 and 113 records. Day 66 held 86. Day 67 recorded a single act, Shohua gathering wood at Tonka's Hold.

The busiest ground was the Tordan Lakes and Ixra Rainforest. Shohua taught Tonxo gem-delving, and Tonxo taught Tonchi. Zihua taught Tonxo fire-keeping. Tonxo discovered smelting, made an ironward and gave it to Zihua. Tonka built a store, and on day 65 a settlement formed: Tonka's Hold. Tonka, Shohua and Tonxo each wove baskets, and Tonxo, Uveeth, Cowa, Tlatli, Shohua and Keri were recorded awakening to magic. Tonxo discovered a lashed-log raft on day 66.

Water moved furthest among the Meki. Zichi made rafts on days 64 and 65, taught Shoka the ice-raft, and on day 66 discovered sailing. Shoka made a raft of his own and discovered bridges, pottery and masonry-related work. Still, no crossing is recorded.

The edge opened again. Tlatli found part of the Haloss Fens on day 64 and Chuxo found part of the Ummar Woods on day 66; Yaxo called Tlatli to join Chuxo there. Chuxo was born to Tlatli and Yaxo on day 64.

Nauwa taught Nauque herding and signs, discovered signs and then schooling, and taught Teka signs. Nauque and Teka are courting, though Teka said she was too thin for a child. Olum discovered mathematics and taught Thakar the calendar.

Hoka died of old age on day 65 and Nande on day 66, after Hoka had built a longhall on day 64. Kragog raided a store of Elyys's people on day 64, and no response is recorded. Coni told Thakar she would repay him, and Zichi and Shoka fed her. Vesys fell sick in the marsh on day 66.

chapters.title: Deaths in Autumn, Settlements in Winter
chapters.text:
Days 67, 68 and 69 carried the span, with 83, 92 and 104 records. Day 70 held two, both Thakar learning signs from Zichi.

Death was the plainest change. Vesys and Olum died on day 67, Tugek and Keri on day 68, and Elyys on day 69, all of old age. Their settlements, Vesys's Hold and Olum's Reach, were struck from the record. The living took over what the dead left. Zurar claimed a shelter and a store, Shohua two shelters and a workshop, Balar a store and shelter, Tonchi a workshop and shelter, and Skaruk a shelter. Balar then founded Balar's Hold and left marks naming Tugek and Olum as lying near. Vorok's Hold formed on day 68, and Shohua's Roof formed the same day. Skaruk pledged to follow Vorok, and Eiuine, Keri and Uveeth fed Vorok and Skaruk through hunger.

At Tonka's Hold, pottery spread. Tonka discovered it, then taught Cowa and Tonxo, while Cowa taught Tonka deep-digging. Tonxo discovered boats on day 69. Tonchi and Tonxo both fell sick, Tonchi from raw fish, and Tonchi left a mark warning others to cook it. Elsewhere, Zihua discovered farming and taught Shoka, who discovered signs. Yaxo discovered storage, Zichi masonry, Uveeth smelting and medicine, Wawa mining, and Nando a reed spear.

Tonque was born to Tlapan and Quipan on day 67. Teka courted Huatli, and Teka made a raft and learned the ice-raft from Zichi. Yaxo, Tlatli and Chuxo raised a cairn and a shelter in the Ummar Woods. Yet no crossing of water is recorded, and the mist stayed shut.

Winter pressed harder: the lean season weighed most on every people, and Kende's energy was down to 19.

epigraph.text: Rain on the Vaia stone / what a hand teaches outlives the hand / I set the hammer down
epigraph.title: Vorok's last verse

chapters.title: Rafts, Last Verses and the First Crossing
chapters.text:
Days 70, 71 and 72 carried the span, with 91, 79 and 136 records. Day 73 held five, mostly Nauwa teaching Huatli writing and the end of Balar's Hold.

The plainest event was a crossing. On day 72 Zichi crossed the water on a vessel and came ashore in the Halka Heights, the first such crossing in the record. Rafts had been found by many hands in the days before: Wawa, Nando, Quipan, and Zichi taught Cowa the ice-raft. Tonka and Cowa each found boats.

Old people died or made ready. Coni and Kragog died on day 70, Balar on day 72. Vorok, Kika, Thiael, Hawen and Zichi each made a death poem on day 72. Vorok's reads, "what a hand teaches outlives the hand". Vorok spent the days teaching smelting and armour to Eiuine, Skaruk and Zurar, and Eiuine pledged to follow him. Skaruk courted Uveeth, she answered, and Morog was born to them on day 72.

Nando and Yachi had twins, Elndo and Rusu, also on day 72. Nando discovered devices and made a lullaby for Elndo. Teka courted Nauwa, Tlapan and Nauque in turn; only Nauque answered.

Huatli taught most of the span: Coni, Nauque, Thakar and Tonque got archery, storage, customs and mining from him. Tonque pledged to follow him. Huatli's Hearth formed on day 71 and he declared a custom that a kill is shared before the maker eats. Nauwa discovered writing and a calendar, and taught writing to Huatli on day 73.

Kika named Kika's Hold. Kika and Tonka each found a store robbed or raided on day 71. Hunger still pressed. Zihua stood at 0 energy and Hawen at 30.

epigraph.text: Snow on the Vaeth Woods, the river running low / I gave first, and I was fed in my own hunger / Watchers, take my name; let the cairn keep it
epigraph.title: Nauwa's last words

chapters.title: Eight Myths, Four Deaths and a Short Life
chapters.text:
Days 73, 74 and 75 were crowded, with 92, 114 and 96 records. Day 76 held five, and little happened in it beyond Shohua crossing water once more, Elndo teaching Quipan lorekeeping and making a talisman, and the sebitter plant dying out.

Three old people died of age. Zichi and Hawen died on day 73, and Vorok on day 74. Vorok's settlements dissolved, and Zurar's Hold formed that day. Zurar, Thiael, Skaruk and Eiuine went on beating iron. Skaruk made ironwards and gave them to Zurar and Eiuine, and he pledged himself to Zurar. Zurar courted Thiael and she answered. Urar was born to them on day 75, and he and Morim both pledged to follow Thiael. Mepan, Kende and Zurar each made a lament for the dead, and Zurar's lament for Vorok says "Your teaching lives in us, and we keep it all".

The larger work was telling. On day 73 Eiuine, Zurar, Huatli, Kika, Nauwa, Teka, Hawen and Tonka each made a myth for their people. The three Ice-folk myths of Huatli, Nauwa and Teka share one figure, the dead who stay as Watchers at cairn and hearth. Nauwa taught Huatli the day-count, and Huatli, Cowa and Nauwa each made a death poem or last words. Nauwa told Nauque that the stone-school was his now, and Cowa taught Mepan the ice-sail and leaf-mending.

Teka and Nauque's son Coka was born on day 74. They hunted a tusker together beforehand. He died on day 75, gored by a mammoth, and Nauque made a lament for him. Teka crossed the water the same day he was born.

Crossing became common. Teka, Nando and Tonchi crossed on day 74, Shoma and Shohua on day 75, and Shohua again on day 76. Tonchi and Chuxo each found a raft, and Shohua did on day 74. Elndo discovered spear-lashing and weaving, and Tonque pottery and scholarship. Kika found pottery, and Teka and Urar fire. Tonka found alchemy.

On day 75 a blight withered about half the grain overnight. Kika stands at 22 health, and Yaxo's energy is 24.

threads.name: Zurar's band
threads.text: Vorok is dead. Zurar leads from Zurar's Hold with Skaruk pledged to him, and Eiuine, Skaruk and Zurar keep beating iron in Vorok's name.

threads.name: Zurar, Thiael and their children
threads.text: Urar was born to Zurar and Thiael on day 75. Morim and Urar follow Thiael, who wants the bow and seed-tending firmly in their hands before she dies.

threads.name: Teka, Nauque and Coka
threads.text: Coka lived one day and was gored by a mammoth on day 75. Teka and Nauque grieve, and Teka still wants to go into the mist.

threads.name: Crossings
threads.text: Teka, Nando, Tonchi, Shoma and Shohua all crossed water on vessels. Shohua made three crossings.

threads.name: Watchers myths
threads.text: Eight myths were made on day 73. The Meki, Tlame and Papa myths share the Watchers who stay at cairn and hearth.

threads.name: Huatli and Nauwa
threads.text: Huatli and Nauwa have made death poems, and Nauwa has handed the stone-school to Nauque. Tonque remains Huatli's follower.

threads.name: Hunger and blight
threads.text: A blight took about half the grain on day 75, while hunger and the lean season still press on Kika and Yaxo.

ideas.text: [NOW: built, to be watched and tuned] standing: earned by wealth, deeds, knowledge, children, works, followers, giving and renown, lost through shame; needed before anyone will follow; special things add to it
[NOW] songs, poems and tales about people and about how the world came to be: kept, told aloud, changing a little in each mouth; bards who carry them
[NOW] a community learning from what befalls its own: a death and how it came, a sickness and its cause, a thing that worked
[NOW] everything that is used wears and regrows by what is around it: pasture, forest, deposits; great deposits that last
[NOW] bridges; weapons for one hand and for a siege (bow, shield, armour, ram, catapult, guns); defence
[NOW] the old workings of the world weakening as the ages of knowledge advance

[NOW] the known world ends in mist and can be pushed back: one who stands at the edge can venture in, and a wide strip of new land may open, continuing the rivers, shores and kinds of ground it joins, with rich deposits and a herd; a band has three tries and then must wait, and once any strip has opened the mist parts for no one for a day, so that the known world grows slowly (laws explore.*, among them gapDays)

[NOW] the world is a globe: east joins west, and it ends at two poles of ice that are different countries (white bears, wolves, caribou and mammoths in the north; penguins, seals and stormbirds in the south; whales and orcas in both seas). Between them lie three climates: the ice, cold all year; the lands with seasons; and a warm belt of rainforest and desert with no winter. Each kind of country has its own plants, animals and people, and both people and animals are drawn back to their own (law drives.homeland)
[NOW] the dog, easily won with food, which stands with its keeper in the hunt and draws a sled over snow; the igloo, raised on snow from nothing; the canoe and the kayak
[NEXT] rain and flood as the weather of the warm belt; a day that goes round the world

[NOW] women and men: a child comes of one of each; twins are a girl and a boy; children come sooner when both parents are well fed and well (mate.plentyCooldown); a grown body can swim narrow water; plants grow faster in spring, rain and at harvest; animals breed by season and by their numbers, and herds return from the rim when few (ecology.grazerTarget, ecology.herdReturn); deposits refill slowly (ecology.lodeRegrow)

[NOW] peoples that last: newcomers who come into the land when the living are few (law arrivals.*, event newcomers), twins (mate.twinChance), longer lives, a milder lean season; what the dead built stands empty and can be claimed by anyone, to begin a home or add to a band's; elders moved to hand on what only they know

[NOW] necessity as the mother of invention: what beings suffer (hunger, the lean season, cold, thirst, sickness, beasts, deaths, water they cannot cross, strife, storm, strange speech) sharpens them toward the ways that answer it; knowing neighbouring ways helps; you can set which hardships spur which way (op spur) and how strongly need counts (laws discovery.*)

[NOW] culture as something that can be read and followed: every tale, song, poem, myth, teaching, saying, lesson and way is an idea with an origin, holders and a path of spread; teachings that can be begun, heard, taken up and given up; talismans and carved figures; your statistics show which ideas are held most and which have crossed between peoples

[NEXT] objects of culture with real benefits and trade value beyond the first talismans and carvings: special gems, named relics that gather a history; secret manuscripts holding spells, knowledge or cures

[NEXT] religious figures, sages with followers, cults, schools of thought and religions that form and compete, some of the light and some of the dark; benefits, secrets, abilities and costs for those who belong, in some cases sacrifice; shrines, temples and churches that members pay toward
[NEXT] tribute and taxes for the common good: stores, works, defence; guilds and secret societies that give benefit and take dues
[NEXT] schools for children and the young, later universities: skills learned faster than alone
[NEXT] trade between lands and across water; ports; colonies as a named act; diplomats, spies, saboteurs; alliances open and secret
[NEXT] kinds of rule: councils and votes, shared holding, private holding, rule by the armed

[NOW] what is not forgotten: a blow or a theft that is seen leaves a grudge that holds a bond down until three gifts mend it or long time passes; a gift in need leaves a kindness that holds it up (laws culture.grudgeDays, kindDays, mendGifts); hunting together (fight.packBonus) and skill that grows with each hunt; telling by a fire, which makes tales; a roof that brings children sooner (mate.roofCooldown)

[NEXT] grudges from defeat or a stolen mate; compensation greater than gifts; peacemakers and peace ceremonies; hard feelings rarer inside a family or band than across them, and arising from conflict, wealth, history or charisma
[NEXT] rivalry for mates; heroes whose deeds spread as lore, to whom tribute is paid and whom the ambitious challenge; duels in which the winner takes most of what the loser holds
[NEXT] fighting, hunting and defending together as learned skills; calling for help and answering it
[NEXT] talents: skill in a way drawing one on along its line; learning what a way demands through dreams, visions from herbs or a shaman's prophecy, and quests to gather what it needs
[NEXT] bandits in new lands; stranger settlements friendly or hostile, with things to trade; farms and flocks as a settlement's steady food
[LATER] monsters that wander in rarely and can be killed only by a band together; their capture, taming and breeding from guarded eggs that others will try to steal
[NEXT] later callings that come with standing and ways: alchemists, scholars, scientists
[LATER: ages three and four] siege warfare and defensive works; weapons of war that are carried to a siege
[LATER] what is built must be kept up or it decays; taking down old buildings to raise new ones; concrete and metal as building stuffs carried from where they are won

[LATER] crowding brings troubles; religion, care for the poor, clean water, public works, places for play, music, dance and art, and the handling of waste ease them; places of buying and selling; healers, pharmacies, hospitals
[LATER] places of invention that quicken discovery; revolutions in knowledge that give great advantage to those who take them up, while others hold out or follow
[LATER] the sciences as knowledge in their own right, in generations: biology, chemistry, physics, then the second and third of each

[FAR: ages five and six] sources of power in order: coal, oil and gas, falling water, wind, the atom, the sun, fusion, the ground of things; each needing what must be found: oil fields, uranium, copper, silicon, rare earths, carbon, diamond
[FAR] speech at a distance in order: marks, smoke, birds, radio, telephone, the joined machines, the machine in the hand; reckoning machines need factories to make them
[FAR] machines that fly: balloons, propellers, jets, for carrying and for war; land vehicles for war

[FAR] the buildings of a great city: dwellings for many, high towers, offices, halls of rule, guards and fire-watch, water and power works and the lines that carry power, barracks and camps of war, markets, harbours, airfields, stations, factories, plants that remake waste
[FAR] new materials far down the tree: plastics, silicon, rare earths
[FAR] the knowledge of what makes a body: changing animals and oneself
[FAR] weapons beyond guns

[LAST] a spaceport: ships that come and go, goods and strange devices from other worlds, visitors who need their own air and live beside the port; their devices do what nothing else does (power, food, healing, terrible weapons, things not understood) and are worth much for being rare
tribal bonds and family bonds, and the pull between them; mating within a people versus between peoples
more kinds of animals at several levels of predator and prey; riding and working animals
many herbs and plants that heal, harm, change attributes or behaviour; plants that open the mind
spirits of places, good and ill, rarely found; mythical animals, monsters and places that help or harm
shamans who heal or affect crops, weather, animals and people; celebrations and ceremonies; crime and punishment; secret knowledge and shared knowledge
professions and castes; salt, caves, mills and kilns; sieges; promises and debts; rituals with force
a world rich to look at and to hear, that changes as it ages
Places of power as anchors that people compete over and settle around; a contested place between two camps could create contact that scarcity alone never did.
Death should leave a trace: the place where someone fell could become a site that touches visitors with grief or lore, a seed for ancestor belief.
Leaders without followers are a lasting tension. Give them acts that cost something and visibly benefit others, rather than handing out followers.
Beads, charms and wards are seeds for currency and status: if they circulate, a later recipe could require them.
Watch whether noticed thefts or takings from settled ground lead to a custom against taking, which would be the first law born from a crime.
Fear of predators is the strongest shared feeling. A leader who can visibly lessen it for others may be the natural route to the first band of three or more.
First contact between peoples who cannot understand each other: watch whether gifts come before words, and whether a made thing given across peoples opens trade.
Each land holds what the others lack. A recipe or a way that needs a thing from another people's land would make crossing worthwhile.
The sea divides the world. Whoever first makes a raft meets a people that has never seen them.
Children change every drive. If a first birth comes, watch whether the family drive pulls people toward one camp.
A resource held by one people and wanted by another (salt for keeping meat, shell for stringing, wool for cloaks) is the natural seed of trade: watch which crosses first.
A woolly grazer is the link between weaving and herding: watch whether the first taming comes from weavers or from hunters who spare an animal.
Care for the sick and hungry may be the real road across the wall of language, and those who give across it the first translators.
A recipe that wears a tool might pull tools out of the hand and into the field.

A song at the fire may be the first shared culture. If nightsong or telling becomes a habit in one band, a singer could carry it to another camp, and a song of the band could become part of who they are.
Graves as shared ground: if a resting place is visited by two peoples, shared grief may become the first ground both hold sacred, and a seed for ancestor rites.
A hardy food that persists in winter is a fallback, not a store. Watch whether people remember where it grows and return when the cold comes: the first knowledge of place tied to a season.

Raw-meat sickness as a teacher: a people that falls sick from raw flesh and then finds fire could keep a saying that cooked meat is safe. This would be the first lesson a community learns from its own suffering, and worth watching among the Kragrek.
Gifts without trades: 48 gifts and 0 trades so far. Watch whether a true exchange ever appears, or whether gift-giving itself becomes the economy, with amberknots as the first token.

A child alone in the cold with no fire is the most fragile life in the world. Watch whether kin go looking for a missing child, and whether the family drive pulls Balar or Olum toward Brokash before winter bites.
Hoka's Rest stands beside four fresh graves. Watch whether Hoka or Hanna raise a cairn, tell of the dead, or leave the place, and whether the site becomes the first ancestor ground.

Contagion turns care into danger: those who stayed close to the sick caught it. Watch whether a lesson to cook meat or to keep apart from the sick arises, or whether medicine-knowers (all Phizhi) ever reach another people's sick.
Stores and famine: three stores existed when four starved. Watch whether stored food is ever drawn on in a lean season, or whether stores are built and then forgotten.

Rafts are known by six and water is the heaviest hardship for four peoples, yet no raft, canoe or kayak has ever been made. Watch whether anyone gathers six wood toward one, or whether the vessel recipes are too costly next to gathering food.
A hardy winter food on the snow (rimewort) is a test of idea 65: watch whether the northern folk return to where it grows when the cold comes.

Hoka's custom that no one hold more than four shares while another starves is the first law of the world, yet Sitha starved anyway. Watch whether the custom is ever invoked to make someone give, and whether it spreads to another band. A law that cannot reach the hungry is only words.

Newcomers starve first: they arrive with little standing, few bonds and no knowledge of where food grows. Watch whether the hosts who take them in (Nande with the Meki, Hoka with the Pesi) feed them through their first winter.

Help that travels: trailcake and saltmeat exist and 89 salt is held, yet neither has ever been made. Every hunger death has been someone far from a fire. Watch whether anyone ever carries prepared food to kin elsewhere. If no one does, a carried-food gift to the hungry may be the missing act.

Bands without words: Huahua pledged to Zichi while the Tlame understand 0% of other tongues. Watch whether following comes before speech elsewhere too, and whether the Tlame learn Meki first through the band rather than through trade.

Hanna starves near Hoka, who keeps offering his store and fire, while robbing of that store is recorded but no draw is. Watch whether an offered store ever becomes a drawn store for a bonded friend: the first shared granary would be the first food that reaches someone who cannot reach a hall.

Births have paused while courtings climb (46 to 52). Watch whether the looser energy threshold brings births to roofed pairs before winter, and whether a winter-born child survives. If newborns die in the cold, timing births toward spring may need its own law.

Predators take the weak: Hanna sat at energy 0 for days and then fell to a stalker. Hunger now kills indirectly, by leaving people too weak to flee. Watch whether the starving die to beasts more than to hunger itself, and whether a watchfire or company ever shields them.

log.seen: This world began with what the makers of earlier worlds added and kept.
ops: new plant gorsemint (from sunleaf, food 4, with effects), 30 sown
new kind of building: longhall (6 wood, 4 stone)
new plant kelbulb (from mudroot, food 14), 30 sown
the way of storage is now sharpened by turning x1, cold x1.2, hunger x1, famine x1.5
the way of lorekeeping is now sharpened by loss x1.2, strangers x0.8, cold x0.4

log.seen: Five days in, all seventeen live, two children have been born and no one has died. The Pesi and the Phizhi each have a leader with two followers, rituals at the fire and a written law. The Kragrek lag behind. They are scattered, have no fire and no band, and all stand near or below the standing needed to lead. Kragog is parched and sick from raw meat in the Aeleth Sands. The peoples still have not met, and the lean season is at most a few days off.
log.predict: By the next visit Kragog's thirst should be eased and his health back above 85, with sapcane among the foods eaten in the Aeleth Sands. Olum or Vorok should be measurably closer to fire, with more lore and some practice gathering wood and stone, and at least one Kragrek may come to fire before the cold sets in. The first lean season should pass with no deaths, and median energy should stay above 60.
ops: the way of fire is now sharpened by cold x1, sickness x0.8, storms x0.8, beasts x0.6
log.why: Kragog is at health 100. The highest thirst fell from 54 to 29, and sapcane eaten rose from 6 to 29. Fire knowers went from 6 to 11. Among the Kragrek, Olum's lore went from 0.2 to 0.6 and Vorok's lore gap closed. Fire is now open to Kragog and Brokash. It has not yet been taken up, so the spur is still worth keeping through the cold.

log.seen: Day 9 of autumn. The first lean season is close. Life is good: 25 alive, median energy 72, lowest health 91, no one sick, and seven children born. The Pesi and Tlatli now live close together and swap gifts often, but there have been 48 gifts and 0 trades. Tlama's death has left no mark on the land. The Kragrek are the people at risk. None of them knows fire. Brokash is a child alone in the Essia Snows, with no fire and no one near him, just as winter arrives.
log.predict: By the next visit, in winter around day 12 to 13: no one dies of hunger or cold. Median energy stays above 60. Icekelp eaten rises from 1 to at least 5, mostly in the Essia Snows. Brokash's health stays above 70. At least one Kragrek (Kragog or Brokash most likely) has come to fire. At least one Pesi or Tlatli has been touched by Tlama's Rest. Ideally a tale or saying about Tlama or the mammoth appears, or cross-people acts at the grave rise above 12.
log.why: The icekelp sowing placed nothing (0 sown). Icekelp eaten only went from 1 to 2, so it fed no one, and the prediction of no hunger deaths failed badly. The four deaths came at the Hold from sickness, storm and winter together, not in the Essia Snows. Tlama's Rest has been found by one being and costs nothing, so the site stays. The lesson is that sowing must be aimed at a being, not at a land.

log.seen: Winter brought the world's worst days. A raw-meat sickness passed from one carer to the next at Hanna's Hold. With the storm and the lean season on top of it, four Pesi starved on day 12, food standing fell from 4448 to 1750, and the Pesi are down to two who live far apart. Spring has come. Elsewhere the making goes on: 80 inventions, three new settlements, lorekeeping and a first tale. But Hoka (energy 23) and the child Zurar (energy 27) are still close to starving. A people of two cannot go on.
log.predict: By the next visit (around day 16 to 17): no new deaths. Hoka's energy is above 50 and Zurar's is above 50. Kelbulb eaten rises from 27 to at least 32, and thornpear eaten from 42 to at least 48. The Pesi number 5 and the living 24. At least one newcomer meets Hanna or Nande, or a first meeting across peoples involves a newcomer. Sick falls to 0, and Hanna's health climbs above 50 now that her energy is 85. If the next winter (around days 22 to 24) looks just as hard, I will soften time.winterGrowth or winterWither next visit instead of waiting for deaths.
ops: 3 newcomers of the Pesi came into the land: Keri, Hawen, Sitha
log.why: Most of it landed. Kelbulb eaten rose from 27 to 43 and thornpear from 42 to 59. Hoka (74) and Zurar (79) are well fed, the Pesi number 5, sick is 0 and Hanna is at health 100. The newcomers met Coni and became Hoka's household, and Sitha now follows him. The only miss was 'no new deaths': Oiae fell to a mammoth, which no change of mine touched.

log.seen: Summer of day 17 is the world's best season yet. Twenty-seven live, the median energy is 78, no one is sick, and food standing has nearly doubled. The two newcomer bands have braided the Pesi, Meki, Kragrek and Tlatli together in the north and west. The one death since my last visit was Oiae, gored by a mammoth, not hunger. What the world lacks is any guard against the next lean season, around days 22 to 24, which last time starved four people at the Hold. It also lacks any use of the water crossings everyone feels pressing: six know rafts, none has been built, and trades are still zero.
log.predict: By the next visit (around day 20 to 21, just before or at the start of winter): no deaths from hunger. Median energy stays at or above 70. Rimewort is eaten at least 5 times, mostly by those in the North Ice and the Vaor and Aelen Snows (Hoka, Sitha, Hawen, Hanna, Keri, Kika). Food standing stays above 2000. Over the winter itself (days 22 to 24), at most one person dies, and none by starvation. If plants keep falling (1871 now) and pasture wear keeps climbing (46 now), I will look at ecology.pastureHeal next.
ops: new plant rimewort (from frostmoss, food 12), 25 sown
log.why: Median energy is 76 (target 70 or more), food standing is 2806 (target above 2000), and pasture wear fell from 46 to 36. Rimewort was eaten 8 times (target 5 or more), so the new winter food is being found. One prediction failed: Sitha starved near Hoka's Rest. She was a hungry newcomer at another's fire, which is a failure of delivery rather than of supply, and reversing the growth change would not have saved her.

log.seen: The world has grown to 31 people with the first new child in a while, gifts at 100, many first meetings, and no feuds. But the lean season is at the door. Sitha starved seven steps from Hoka's Rest even after Hoka declared a custom against hoarding, and Hawen lies at health 6 in the far Vaor Snows with a wolf behind him. The northern peoples (Meki, Tlatli, Pesi) feel the turning year most, at 1.5 to 1.7. What the world lacks is a way for the hurt and the cold to mend on the snow, and food placed among the Meki, who are the most numerous and the most pressed.
log.predict: By the next visit, at or just past winter (around day 24 to 25): Hawen is alive with health above 30, or, if he has died, it was to the wolf and not to his wound. Steamhollow has been found by at least 1 being. Snowmallow is eaten at least 5 times, mostly in the North Ice and the Essoss and Vaor Snows. Rimewort eaten rises from 8 to at least 15. No Meki starves, and Zihua's health stays at 80 or above. Over the winter at most one death, none by starvation. Median energy stays at or above 65. The living stay at 30 or more.
ops: new plant snowmallow (from highbloom, food 6, with effects), 7 sown
log.why: The rimewort did far more than predicted: eaten rose from 8 to 44, so the second sowing carried the northern folk through winter. Hawen lived and his health is back to 50. No Meki starved, Zihua is at 100, median energy is 75 and 34 are alive. Snowmallow fell short, eaten 3 times against a target of 5. Steamhollow has been found by no one, with the nearest being 11 steps away. It costs nothing, so it stays. One winter death, Brokash by starvation, broke the 'none by starvation' prediction. He was alone and far from help, which this change could not reach.

log.seen: Spring has come to a world of 34. Bands are forming across peoples: Huahua of the Tlame follows Zichi without sharing a word with him. Many now know rafts and boats, but no one has crossed water. Brokash starved alone in his own longhall, and food standing fell by a third over the winter (2806 to 1784). Several people are still running low as the season turns: Hanna 32, Kika 33, Shoka 36 with health 72, Nauwa 38, Mepan 40 and Coni 42. What the world lacks now is not new things but food reaching the few who are slipping, in the North Ice and the Ummar Woods.
log.predict: By the next visit, around day 28 to 29 in early summer: no deaths from hunger. Hanna, Kika, Shoka, Nauwa and Coni are each at energy 50 or above, and Shoka's health is above 80. Ironnut eaten rises from 130 to at least 140, mostly in the Ummar Woods. Snowberry eaten rises from 64 to at least 72, and cloudberry from 107 to at least 120, mostly in the North Ice. Food standing climbs back above 2000 as spring growth works. The living stay at 34 or more, and a spring birth is likely now that several pairs are roofed and fed.
log.why: All three sowings hit their targets: ironnut eaten rose from 130 to 159, snowberry from 64 to 86 and cloudberry from 107 to 136. Food standing is 3522, with no deaths and 34 alive. Two predictions missed. Hanna is at energy 20, and Shoka's health is 63, not above 80. No spring birth came. The sowing did what sowing can do; Hanna's hunger is a delivery problem.

log.seen: Summer has been gentle. No one has died since Brokash, food standing has doubled to 3522, sickness is gone, and nightsong has grown from 1 to 33 into the first real habit of a band, at Vorok's hall. Two things are missing. Numbers have stopped rising: no birth in eight days, and the four children have grown up. Hanna is starving at energy 20 in the Vaor Snows, near rich meadows and a friend's store. Water remains every people's heaviest hardship, yet no vessel of any kind has ever been made.
log.predict: By the next visit (around day 32 to 33, harvest turning to winter): Hanna is alive with energy above 50, and rimewort eaten rises from 59 to at least 75, mostly in the Vaor and Essoss Snows. No one in the Essoss Snows starves (Olum, Balar, Tugek, Zihua, Mepan, Shoma). At least one birth occurs, most likely between pairs already courting near a roof, with Zurar and Eiuine the likeliest. The living reach 35 or more. Median energy stays at or above 65. There are no hunger deaths at all; at most one death of any cause.
log.why: Rimewort eaten rose from 59 to 86, past the target of 75. No one in the Essoss Snows starved, median energy is 69, and there were no hunger deaths. A birth came, as hoped, though to the ripe pair Vorok and Eiuine rather than to Zurar and Eiuine. The living reached 35 before Hanna died. Her death was to a stalker, after days at energy 0. The one-death limit held, but the prediction that she would recover failed. Her weakness was a matter of reach, which these sowings could not touch.

log.seen: Autumn is turning to winter. The world is well fed overall: median energy is 69, food standing is 3725, and there have been no hunger deaths since Brokash. Skaruk, the first child alive, was born to Vorok and Eiuine. The north is fragile again. Hanna fell to a stalker after sitting at energy 0, Hoka's store has been emptied, Honi is at energy 34, and the Tlatli feel hunger and the turning year more than anyone. In the west, Nande is hungry and hurt beside Olum's Reach, while Olum's store holds food but he still has no follower.
log.predict: By the next visit (around day 36 to 37, in winter): no deaths from hunger, and at most one death of any cause. Honi is alive with energy above 50, and Coni and Kika are above 50. Rimewort eaten rises from 86 to at least 100, much of it in the Vaeth Woods and North Ice. Plants bearing within reach of Hoka's Rest rise above 10, where the North Grounds now show 0. Near Olum's Reach, Nande's health is 80 or above, and Olum's store holds 10 or more or has been drawn by someone hungry. Ideally Olum feeds Balar or Nande from it, and gains a follower. The living are 34 or more, and median energy is 60 or above.
ops: rich ground "Reach Meadow" at (37,12), 5 steps across each way, 13 plants sprung up
refused: rich ground already lies within ten steps of that place
log.why: Rimewort eaten rose from 86 to 130, past the target of 100. There were no new deaths, Honi (69) and Kika (61) are above 50, Nande is at health 100, and median energy is 68 with 39 alive. Coni (28) missed. The North Grounds near Hoka's Rest still show 0 plants bearing. Olum's store was drawn from 3 to 25, but much of that was theft (17 food raided), not the hungry being fed, so the hope that Olum would feed others from it did not come true.

log.seen: Spring has come with no new deaths. The living rose from 34 to 39 through five newcomers and Tlapan's birth, and craft is spreading fast: weaving three times, bridges, a flint spear, farming known by six. Two people are hungry and alone. Coni is at energy 28 in the Vaeth Woods, and Kragog is at 32 in the Tordan Lakes. Theft from stores is the new thread: Olum's store was emptied, mostly by Nauwa and Balar. Water is still the leading hardship and no crossing is recorded, though bows, shields and rafts are being made.
log.predict: By the next visit (around day 40 to 41, summer into harvest): no deaths of any cause, and the living at 39 or more. Coni and Kragog are each at energy 50 or above. Hazel eaten rises from 116 to at least 125, mostly in the Vaeth Woods. Kelbulb eaten rises from 101 to at least 108, around the Tordan Lakes. Median energy stays at or above 65, and food standing climbs back above 2500 with spring and harvest growth. Thefts may rise further (now 9). If a custom against taking appears at Olum's Reach, that would be the first law born of a crime.
log.why: Both sowings were eaten well past their targets: hazel rose from 116 to 247 and kelbulb from 101 to 126. Coni (85) and Kragog (66) are above 50, median energy is 69, food standing is 2679 and 45 are alive. The no-deaths prediction failed. Six died: three of old age, one gored, and Xaiel, who starved far from any sown ground.

log.seen: Spring of day 62. The world is growing: 45 alive, three births on day 60, and teaching spreading fast, with lessons from others rising from 99 to 177 and schooling passing on. The new deaths were mostly old age and beasts. Xaiel was the one who starved, far from food in the Essoss Snows. Fourteen of the living are now elders, so a wave of old-age deaths is coming. A few are in danger right now: Tonchi, a child alone in the Aeleth Sands at health 29 with a ridgecat near; Tontec at energy 17 in the Vaor Snows; and Mepan at 36 on the North Ice. The lean season is only days away. Rafts are known to 20 yet no raft, canoe, kayak, bow or basket has ever been made, so water remains a top hardship for most peoples.
log.predict: By the next visit (around day 65 to 66, into harvest and the turn toward winter): no deaths from hunger. Tonchi is alive with health above 45 and energy above 50. Tontec is above energy 40, and Mepan above 50. Sunfig eaten rises from 26 to at least 32, mostly in the Aeleth Sands. Rimewort eaten rises from 280 to at least 300, in the Vaor Snows and the North Ice. The living stay at 43 or more; at most two elders die of old age. Median energy stays at or above 65. I expect still no raft, canoe or kayak to be made.
ops: 6 of 15 sunfig sown (the rest found no free ground it grows on, even looking farther out)
log.why: There were no hunger deaths; starved stayed at 8. Rimewort eaten rose from 280 to 316, past the target of 300. Tonchi (81, health 100) and Mepan (88) are well, the living held at 43, exactly two elders died of old age, and median energy is 68. Sunfig was the failure: eaten rose only from 26 to 27, because only 6 took root, on sand few people walk. Tontec stayed below 40. My expectation of no rafts also failed, happily: four were made.

log.seen: Day 66, summer turning to harvest, with the lean season about six days off. No one has starved since day 57, and the deaths since my last visit were two elders of old age and Kiwa to a mammoth. Four rafts now exist, but no one has crossed water. Two risks stand out. In the far North Ice, Hawen (energy 38), the child Kende (27) and Tontec (23, health 66) are hungry going into winter, and Nande (27, health 56) is weak in the Essoss Snows beside a meadow with no plants. More lasting is the shape of the people: 16 of the 43 are elders and only 7 are children, so old age will soon take more than births replace.
log.predict: By the next visit (around day 69 to 70, harvest into winter): no deaths from hunger. Hawen, Kende and Tontec are each above energy 40, and Tontec's health is 70 or more. Nande is alive with health above 50. Rimewort eaten rises from 316 to at least 345, much of it in the North Ice and Essoss Snows. At least two births (everBorn 52 to 54 or more), most likely to pairs already courting near a roof, such as Zihua and Shohua or Paque and Thiael. The living are 43 or more, at most two elders die of old age, and median energy stays at or above 63. I expect rafts held to stay at 4 or more, and still no water crossing recorded.
log.why: Rimewort eaten rose from 316 to 392, far past the target of 345, and no one starved (starved stays at 8). Median energy is 72. The looser mating law brought only one birth, not two, and five elders died against my limit of two. Still, it did no harm and births need every help, so I keep it. Kende missed the energy target and Nande died of age.

log.seen: The deaths of this span were all old age: five elders in three days, mostly the first generation. The living fell from 43 to 38 with only one birth, so the world is fed but shrinking. Hunger now presses only a few. Kende (27) and Hawen (40) are out in the Vaor Snows far from bearing ground, and Vorok (23) is near the Vaia Meadows. Five rafts are held, yet no one has crossed water, and courtings have nearly stalled (102 to 106).
log.predict: By the next visit (around day 73 to 74, winter into spring): no deaths from hunger. Kende is above energy 40 and Hawen above 45. Rimewort eaten rises from 392 to at least 415, partly in the Vaor Snows. With longer lives, the count of elders falls below 11 and at most one dies of old age. Courtings rise from 106 to at least 112, and there is at least one birth (everBorn 54 or more). The living stay at 37 or more and median energy at 63 or above.
