from earlier worlds: Recipes that need only things people already carry and one companion ('sharing': food plus one other) are used within days, while recipes that need a tool in hand plus a specific item (fangcharm) go unused even among active hunters.

from earlier worlds: A recipe gated on being at a building goes unused even when the building exists and the act's ingredients are common (sharing done 10 times, hallwelcome 0). Before adding more place-bound acts, confirm that people actually gather at the place and that the building counts as the kind the recipe names.

from earlier worlds: Raising the family and belonging drives to 1.5 coincided with three births and four bands within five days, where earlier worlds saw no child in twenty days of plenty. Drives move behaviour faster than buildings or recipes.

from earlier worlds: Raising curiosity (to 1.4) and sight (to 9) coincided with the first two cross-people meetings and wanderers entering two empty lands within four days. The places of power, 20 or more steps from anyone, were still not found, so wandering widens contact but does not yet reach fixed distant points.

from earlier worlds: Inventions came in a burst once the first one appeared (4 to 18 in three days, mostly within one people), and none crossed between peoples. Knowledge spreads by example inside a tongue, not across it. A held token (amberknot) gets made but is not given; making something is easier than finding someone to give it to.

from earlier worlds: Words began to cross between peoples (0% to 3%) through meetings and a gift born of need for a sick neighbour, while the made token (amberknot) still sits unused. Real need opens contact sooner than objects made for giving.

from earlier worlds: Changing the odds of an act people never choose does not change behaviour. The fishing chance rose by half and fish eaten stayed flat, so levers must reach what beings want or see, not only what succeeds.

from earlier worlds: A strong family drive with a low energy floor turns births into deaths: a mating pair with no food spent its reserves on a child and all three starved within a day. Every drive that pushes toward an act needs a matching check on whether that act can be survived.

from earlier worlds: Raising compassion coincided with gifts rising and food crossing bands, but only to those standing close to givers. Compassion moves people who see need; it does not send them looking for need they cannot see.

from earlier worlds: By day 5 the standing needed to lead (1.2) was above almost every ambitious being except Bruwen. Halls built with no one able to pledge to their builders showed that the threshold, not the lack of buildings, was holding back a second band.

from earlier worlds: Lowering the standing needed to lead brought a third band within four days. It formed between two people already courting and raising a child, not around either hall-builder, so pledges follow existing bonds, and halls alone do not draw followers.

from earlier worlds: Winter, not isolation, killed this time. A chief with three followers starved as surely as a loner, because sharing needs carried food and winter takes it all at once. Bands protect only when someone holds a store, so survival across seasons needs foresight acts or hardy fallbacks, not more bonds.

from earlier worlds: A hardy plant and summer plenty came too late for a death at the end of spring. Food in the world is not food in the mouth: what killed Arri was the distance between a call for help and the one who answered it.

from earlier worlds: Louder hearing and a louder sense of mortality brought more gifts, new crafts and a child, but did not stop a leader from starving while she founded her Ground. Drives that raise ambition and foresight do not by themselves turn into carried food. Standing-seeking acts compete with gathering, and the helper who hears a call still arrives with nothing to give.

from earlier worlds: Spurring a way by hardship brought knowers quickly (storage 0 to 2 within one winter), but knowing did not lead to doing: the store is still unbuilt. A spur opens the door to knowledge, not to practice.

from earlier worlds: One lonely person living among another people crossed the language wall in four days, which no token or site managed in twenty. Contact deepens through shared daily life at a hearth, not through single meetings.

from earlier worlds: A status lever lifts whoever already does the act. Raising the worth of giving raised the giver (Tanna) and widened the gap for leaders who cannot give, so to help a stuck leader I must reward something they already do, not something they lack the means to do.

from earlier worlds: Spurring storage by famine made the knowledge arrive exactly when there was nothing to store. A way meant for foresight must be sharpened by the signs that come before the hardship, such as the first cold, and not by the hardship itself.

from earlier worlds: Easing blight let food recover fast, and the next death came from a predator to the weakest elder rather than from hunger. Once scarcity lifts, danger falls on whoever is most frail, so with so few people every remaining life now carries the world's future.

from earlier worlds: A louder loneliness moved the one being whose aim already pointed toward others, and within four days it brought a meeting between peoples that had stayed apart for over forty days. A drive works when it amplifies a want a being already holds.

from earlier worlds: Easing predators and winter hunger together brought the first winter with no deaths, even though food standing fell by more than half. Nobody starved because the hungry were near someone who could feed them, so in the lean season, closeness counts for more than total food.

from earlier worlds: A band cannot form if the would-be follower stands higher than the would-be leader, even when the two are courting and bonded. The shape of who outranks whom decides which bands are possible, not only bonds or standing above a threshold.

from earlier worlds: When the centres of two peoples drew within a few steps of each other, a dozen first meetings came in four days and understanding of other tongues rose from nothing. Contact grows from overlapping ranges and many brief meetings, not from any single crafted thing or site.

from earlier worlds: Sowing works when it is placed where the needy actually stand. The first sapcane missed the thirsty, the second reached them, and thirst fell from 66 to 0. Where food goes matters as much as how much goes.

from earlier worlds: Lowering the mating threshold brought a birth, but to the pair whose courtship was already ripe, not to the pair expected. Like a drive, a looser law opens a door only for those already standing at it.

from earlier worlds: Hunger deaths amid plenty are failures of delivery, not of supply: each one who starved was too far from anyone for help to reach in time. Hearing farther, keeping people near each other, or a way to send food ahead saves more lives than more food.

from earlier worlds: A count that reads the same at every visit is more likely a fault in the instrument than a fact about the world. Ask the programmer before reasoning from it (the food counts once looked frozen for twelve days because the earlier numbers were not kept as a copy).

day 5: The chapter text can lag behind the numbers. Vesys was said to be at health 41, but the roster shows him at 100 and the lowest health in the world is now Brunde's 60. Judge who is in danger from the living roster, not from the story.

day 9: A spur shortens the road but does not walk it. The fire spur closed the Kragrek's lore gap within four days, but what still stands between them and fire is the act of gathering wood and stone, which only their own aims can supply.

day 13: Closeness saves lives in hunger but kills in contagion. Each carer who stayed beside the sick caught the raw-meat fever, and the sickness drain, storm cold and winter scarcity together starved four in one day. Before a lean season, sickness and cold must be judged together with food, not food alone.

day 17: A sowing made in a season of plenty is a cheap insurance. Kelbulb and thornpear sown before need peaked were eaten steadily, so food placed ahead of the lean season reaches people because they are already foraging, not starving.

day 21: Those who starve now are not the poor but the newly arrived: Sitha was a newcomer dependent on another's table, and Zihua, the weakest Meki, is one too. A custom or a store at the hall does not feed someone who cannot reach the hall, so help for newcomers must be placed where they stand.

day 25: A hardy food sown on the ground where people already forage, ahead of the lean season, carried the north through winter (rimewort eaten 44 times). A healing spring placed a few steps outside their paths was found by no one. In this world, help must stand where people already walk.

day 29: Three sowings of familiar foods made in a season of plenty were all eaten past their targets, so the food supply in this world is now sound. What still kills is reach, and what still stalls is not food but births: the population can be well fed and still not grow.

day 33: A looser mating law once again brought a birth to the pair already furthest along (Vorok and Eiuine), not to the pair I named. And the north's danger has changed shape: the weak there now die to predators rather than to hunger outright, so in the north I must judge low energy as a risk of being killed, not only of starving.

day 37: A store does not only feed the hungry: once food sits in one place, it draws thieves as well. The count 'drawn by the hungry' must be read alongside the theft events before I judge whether a store saved anyone.

day 62: Sowings made ahead of need keep being eaten past their targets, so the food supply is sound. The deaths that remain come from age, beasts, and the one person who strays far from food. With so many elders, births now have to outpace deaths from old age; feeding people is no longer enough.

day 66: Making is not using: four rafts appeared once the way had spread to twenty-two people, yet water is still the heaviest hardship for most peoples. A vessel only matters if the beings' aims carry them to a shore while they hold it.

day 70: Once food is sound, the population curve is set by the age structure, not by hunger. Many newcomers who arrived together grow old together, so a cluster of deaths from age can undo many seasons of good feeding. Birth rate and lifespan are the levers that matter then.

day 74: Even with food sound, one winter cut median energy by about 14 points, and the hunger gathered in the most crowded land rather than the barest. Sowings for a lean season must go where people are packed together, not only where food is scarce. Raising the lifespan does not save elders already near its end; it pays off only over later generations.

requests.text: Please clarify the hardship called 'water' in hardshipsPressing. Does it mean thirst, or water that cannot be crossed? The Pesi show water at 0.7, yet their thirst seems low and Hanna already knows rafts. If it is uncrossable water, it would help to show thirst as its own figure per people, so I can tell whether to sow water-giving plants or to leave the pressure toward rafts in place.

Trades read 0 against 48 gifts, even with Hanna aiming to be a trader of fine goods. Please confirm whether a two-sided exchange is actually an action beings can take and is being counted. If it is not, a simple 'offer X for Y' act would let the first market emerge from the Pesi-Tlatli contact.

Please report what each store holds (food count) and how much was drawn from stores during the lean season. Three stores stood when four people starved at the Hold, and I cannot tell whether the stores were empty, unreachable, or simply not used by sick and starving beings.

Sowing with 'land' or without 'near' placed 0 plants last visit (the icekelp in the Essia Snows). If a sow event finds no suitable ground, please fall back to the nearest suitable tiles or report the reason, so that relief food is not silently lost.

Please count, for each lean season, how much food is drawn from stores and by whom, and how much stays in stores when someone starves. Three stores stood unused while four died at the Hold, and I cannot tell whether stores are failing in design or simply being forgotten.

Newcomers arrive with nothing in hand, and one of the three Pesi newcomers (Sitha) starved within eight days. Could arriving bands carry a few days of food of their own land (say 2 to 3 food each), so their first lean days do not depend wholly on strangers' tables?

When a sow event places fewer plants than asked (the icekelp sowing once placed 0), could the record say how many were placed and why (wrong ground, no room)? Then I can tell whether a sowing near a being reached them or failed on the terrain.

Brokash starved inside his own longhall, and Sitha starved near Hoka's store. Please check whether a starving being will eat from a store at their own or a host's settlement, and whether the stored amounts were above zero when they died. If stores cannot be drawn on in need, they are monuments, not insurance.

Trailcake, saltmeat and every vessel recipe (raft, canoe, kayak) have been made 0 times, though many know the ways behind them. Could the log record whether beings ever considered these recipes and why they turned them down (cost, not seen, or no aim)? That would tell me whether to make them cheaper or simply wait.

Vessels are never made. Rafts are known by 14 and boats by 4, water is the heaviest hardship for all six peoples, and kayak needs only 2 wood and 2 meat, yet raft, canoe, kayak and boat all show 'done 0'. Please check whether beings are actually offered these recipes when standing by water they cannot cross, and whether a held vessel lets them cross. If they are offered, the reason they never choose them may be worth surfacing in their reflections.

Instrument check: the story says Hoka's store was robbed of six food twice on day 23, but the store at (175,7) shows putInEver 12, drawnEver 0, foodNow 12. Either thefts from stores are not counted as draws, or the theft did not touch the store. Please check, because I cannot judge whether stores feed anyone without trusting these numbers.

Please record in the chapter text who draws food from each store, and when, and also each death with its place and cause. Hoka's store went from 12 to 0 and Hanna died at (191,1) of a stalker, yet the story says nothing of either. I cannot tell whether the stored food reached the starving or was simply eaten by its keeper, and that is the central question of whether stores save lives in this world.

The 'things that can be made' list shows 'done 0 held' for bow, shield, raft and boat, yet the chapters say Thiael made a bow, Hawen and Zichi made shields, and Mepan and Huahua found rafts. Either the counts do not record these makings, or the story is describing discoveries of the way as makings. Please check, because I cannot judge whether water crossing is close without a true count of vessels held.

My rich ground 'Reach Meadow' at (37,12) was reported refused, yet it appears in richGrounds with 0 plants bearing and 5 people within 12. Please confirm whether it was actually made. If it was, it seems to have been stripped bare at once by a crowded camp, and that would change how I place rich ground.

Twenty beings know rafts and water is a leading hardship for most peoples, yet raft, canoe, kayak, boat, bow, basket, saltmeat and trailcake have each been made 0 times. Only sharing, amberknot, nightsong and a few others are ever made. Please check whether beings are shown these recipes, whether they can gather 6 wood when carryMax is 6, and whether carrying a vessel actually lets them cross deep water. If something blocks them, a clear hint when a knower stands at water with wood in hand may be enough.

Four rafts are held and 'water you could not cross' is still the top hardship for the Meki, Tlame, Paki and others, yet no crossing has ever been recorded. Please check that a held raft actually lets its holder step onto deep water, and that beings are told they can launch it when they stand at a shore. If they are not told, a short prompt line ('you carry a raft; the water before you can now be crossed') may be all that is missing.

Beings hold five rafts and boats, and water is the heaviest hardship for most peoples, yet no one has ever crossed. Please let a being who holds a vessel and stands at a shore be told plainly what lies across the water: land seen, people known to be there, or unknown ground. That way an aim to cross can form from what they see. Please also record each crossing as an event so it can be counted.

Please add to the numbers, for each land, the food bearing now set against the number of beings there and their median energy. This would let me see crowding hunger, as in the Vaeth Woods, before it shows up as collapse.

ops.name: firecircle
ops.hint: Feed a fire with others gathered close, and share its warmth and talk.

ops.name: hidewrap
ops.hint: The hides of two kills, scraped with a tool and wrapped about the body, keep the cold out for days.

ops.name: cairn
ops.hint: Stones piled together for one who is gone, with another standing beside you, ease grief and bind the living.

ops.name: feast
ops.hint: Share food beside a fire with another, and all who sit near are gladdened and warmed for a day.

ops.name: roast
ops.hint: Roast two portions of meat over a fire and share it with whoever stands near; all who eat are fed and warmed toward one another.

ops.name: sharing
ops.hint: Lay out two foods for whoever stands beside you, and all eat together.

ops.name: watchfire
ops.hint: Feed your fire high with two wood while others sit close, and everyone beside it feels warmer and braver against the dark.

ops.name: ironward
ops.hint: Beat smelted metal in a fire into a ward that can be worn or given; its bearer stands harder against teeth and claws.

ops.name: amberknot
ops.hint: Bind a piece of amber on a cord while another stands beside you; it is a small bright thing to keep, or to give.

ops.name: bead
ops.hint: Shape a little clay and harden it in the fire into small bright beads that can be worn, kept or given.

ops.name: fangcharm
ops.hint: From a kill, string a fang into a charm you can keep or give away.

ops.name: longhall
ops.hint: A great roofed hall of wood and stone where many can gather, rest warm through the cold, and grow close to one another.

ops.name: hallwelcome
ops.hint: Share food with a guest under a hall's roof; beneath it, fear and loneliness ease for all who sit together.

ops.name: nightsong
ops.hint: Sit by a fire after dark with someone near and sing or speak of what has been; the night feels less empty for all who hear.

ops.name: emberfish
ops.hint: Fish laid over the fire before eating keeps the belly sound and the body strong.

ops.name: firecircle
ops.hint: Feed a fire with others gathered close, and share its warmth and talk.

ops.name: hidewrap
ops.hint: The hides of two kills, scraped with a tool and wrapped about the body, keep the cold out for days.

ops.name: cairn
ops.hint: Stones piled together for one who is gone, with another standing beside you, ease grief and bind the living.

ops.name: feast
ops.hint: Share food beside a fire with another, and all who sit near are gladdened and warmed for a day.

ops.name: roast
ops.hint: Roast two portions of meat over a fire and share it with whoever stands near; all who eat are fed and warmed toward one another.

ops.name: sharing
ops.hint: Lay out two foods for whoever stands beside you, and all eat together.

ops.name: watchfire
ops.hint: Feed your fire high with two wood while others sit close, and everyone beside it feels warmer and braver against the dark.

ops.name: ironward
ops.hint: Beat smelted metal in a fire into a ward that can be worn or given; its bearer stands harder against teeth and claws.

ops.name: amberknot
ops.hint: Bind a piece of amber on a cord while another stands beside you; it is a small bright thing to keep, or to give.

ops.name: bead
ops.hint: Shape a little clay and harden it in the fire into small bright beads that can be worn, kept or given.

ops.name: fangcharm
ops.hint: From a kill, string a fang into a charm you can keep or give away.

ops.name: longhall
ops.hint: A great roofed hall of wood and stone where many can gather, rest warm through the cold, and grow close to one another.

ops.name: hallwelcome
ops.hint: Share food with a guest under a hall's roof; beneath it, fear and loneliness ease for all who sit together.

ops.name: nightsong
ops.hint: Sit by a fire after dark with someone near and sing or speak of what has been; the night feels less empty for all who hear.

ops.name: emberfish
ops.hint: Fish laid over the fire before eating keeps the belly sound and the body strong.

lessons: A status lever lifts whoever already does the act. Raising the worth of giving raised the giver (Tanna) and widened the gap for leaders who cannot give, so to help a stuck leader I must reward something they already do, not something they lack the means to do.

Spurring storage by famine made the knowledge arrive exactly when there was nothing to store. A way meant for foresight must be sharpened by the signs that come before the hardship, such as the first cold, and not by the hardship itself.

Easing blight let food recover fast, and the next death came from a predator to the weakest elder rather than from hunger. Once scarcity lifts, danger falls on whoever is most frail, so with so few people every remaining life now carries the world's future.

A louder loneliness moved the one being whose aim already pointed toward others, and within four days it brought a meeting between peoples that had stayed apart for over forty days. A drive works when it amplifies a want a being already holds.

Easing predators and winter hunger together brought the first winter with no deaths, even though food standing fell by more than half. Nobody starved because the hungry were near someone who could feed them, so in the lean season, closeness counts for more than total food.

A band cannot form if the would-be follower stands higher than the would-be leader, even when the two are courting and bonded. The shape of who outranks whom decides which bands are possible, not only bonds or standing above a threshold.

When the centres of two peoples drew within a few steps of each other, a dozen first meetings came in four days and understanding of other tongues rose from nothing. Contact grows from overlapping ranges and many brief meetings, not from any single crafted thing or site.

Sowing works when it is placed where the needy actually stand. The first sapcane missed the thirsty, the second reached them, and thirst fell from 66 to 0. Where food goes matters as much as how much goes.

Lowering the mating threshold brought a birth, but to the pair whose courtship was already ripe, not to the pair expected. Like a drive, a looser law opens a door only for those already standing at it.

Hunger deaths amid plenty are failures of delivery, not of supply: each one who starved was too far from anyone for help to reach in time. Hearing farther, keeping people near each other, or a way to send food ahead saves more lives than more food.

A count that reads the same at every visit is more likely a fault in the instrument than a fact about the world. Ask the programmer before reasoning from it (the food counts once looked frozen for twelve days because the earlier numbers were not kept as a copy).

The chapter text can lag behind the numbers. Vesys was said to be at health 41, but the roster shows him at 100 and the lowest health in the world is now Brunde's 60. Judge who is in danger from the living roster, not from the story.

A spur shortens the road but does not walk it. The fire spur closed the Kragrek's lore gap within four days, but what still stands between them and fire is the act of gathering wood and stone, which only their own aims can supply.

Closeness saves lives in hunger but kills in contagion. Each carer who stayed beside the sick caught the raw-meat fever, and the sickness drain, storm cold and winter scarcity together starved four in one day. Before a lean season, sickness and cold must be judged together with food, not food alone.

A sowing made in a season of plenty is a cheap insurance. Kelbulb and thornpear sown before need peaked were eaten steadily, so food placed ahead of the lean season reaches people because they are already foraging, not starving.

Those who starve now are not the poor but the newly arrived: Sitha was a newcomer dependent on another's table, and Zihua, the weakest Meki, is one too. A custom or a store at the hall does not feed someone who cannot reach the hall, so help for newcomers must be placed where they stand.

A hardy food sown on the ground where people already forage, ahead of the lean season, carried the north through winter (rimewort eaten 44 times). A healing spring placed a few steps outside their paths was found by no one. In this world, help must stand where people already walk.

Three sowings of familiar foods made in a season of plenty were all eaten past their targets, so the food supply in this world is now sound. What still kills is reach, and what still stalls is not food but births: the population can be well fed and still not grow.

A looser mating law once again brought a birth to the pair already furthest along (Vorok and Eiuine), not to the pair I named. And the north's danger has changed shape: the weak there now die to predators rather than to hunger outright, so in the north I must judge low energy as a risk of being killed, not only of starving.

A store does not only feed the hungry: once food sits in one place, it draws thieves as well. The count 'drawn by the hungry' must be read alongside the theft events before I judge whether a store saved anyone.

Sowings made ahead of need keep being eaten past their targets, so the food supply is sound. The deaths that remain come from age, beasts, and the one person who strays far from food. With so many elders, births now have to outpace deaths from old age; feeding people is no longer enough.

Making is not using: four rafts appeared once the way had spread to twenty-two people, yet water is still the heaviest hardship for most peoples. A vessel only matters if the beings' aims carry them to a shore while they hold it.

Once food is sound, the population curve is set by the age structure, not by hunger. Many newcomers who arrived together grow old together, so a cluster of deaths from age can undo many seasons of good feeding. Birth rate and lifespan are the levers that matter then.

Even with food sound, one winter cut median energy by about 14 points, and the hunger gathered in the most crowded land rather than the barest. Sowings for a lean season must go where people are packed together, not only where food is scarce. Raising the lifespan does not save elders already near its end; it pays off only over later generations.

A resource held by one people and wanted by another (salt for keeping meat, shell for stringing, wool for cloaks) is the natural seed of trade: watch which crosses first.
A woolly grazer is the link between weaving and herding: watch whether the first taming comes from weavers or from hunters who spare an animal.
Care for the sick and hungry may be the real road across the wall of language, and those who give across it the first translators.
A recipe that wears a tool might pull tools out of the hand and into the field.

A song at the fire may be the first shared culture. If nightsong or telling becomes a habit in one band, a singer could carry it to another camp, and a song of the band could become part of who they are.
Graves as shared ground: if a resting place is visited by two peoples, shared grief may become the first ground both hold sacred, and a seed for ancestor rites.
A hardy food that persists in winter is a fallback, not a store. Watch whether people remember where it grows and return when the cold comes: the first knowledge of place tied to a season.

Raw-meat sickness as a teacher: a people that falls sick from raw flesh and then finds fire could keep a saying that cooked meat is safe. This would be the first lesson a community learns from its own suffering, and worth watching among the Kragrek.
Gifts without trades: 48 gifts and 0 trades so far. Watch whether a true exchange ever appears, or whether gift-giving itself becomes the economy, with amberknots as the first token.

A child alone in the cold with no fire is the most fragile life in the world. Watch whether kin go looking for a missing child, and whether the family drive pulls Balar or Olum toward Brokash before winter bites.
Hoka's Rest stands beside four fresh graves. Watch whether Hoka or Hanna raise a cairn, tell of the dead, or leave the place, and whether the site becomes the first ancestor ground.

Contagion turns care into danger: those who stayed close to the sick caught it. Watch whether a lesson to cook meat or to keep apart from the sick arises, or whether medicine-knowers (all Phizhi) ever reach another people's sick.
Stores and famine: three stores existed when four starved. Watch whether stored food is ever drawn on in a lean season, or whether stores are built and then forgotten.
A hardy winter food on the snow (rimewort) is a test of idea 65: watch whether the northern folk return to where it grows when the cold comes.

Hoka's custom that no one hold more than four shares while another starves is the first law of the world, yet Sitha starved anyway. Watch whether the custom is ever invoked to make someone give, and whether it spreads to another band. A law that cannot reach the hungry is only words.

Newcomers starve first: they arrive with little standing, few bonds and no knowledge of where food grows. Watch whether the hosts who take them in (Nande with the Meki, Hoka with the Pesi) feed them through their first winter.

Help that travels: trailcake and saltmeat exist and 89 salt is held, yet neither has ever been made. Every hunger death has been someone far from a fire. Watch whether anyone ever carries prepared food to kin elsewhere. If no one does, a carried-food gift to the hungry may be the missing act.

Bands without words: Huahua pledged to Zichi while the Tlame understand 0% of other tongues. Watch whether following comes before speech elsewhere too, and whether the Tlame learn Meki first through the band rather than through trade.

Hanna starves near Hoka, who keeps offering his store and fire, while robbing of that store is recorded but no draw is. Watch whether an offered store ever becomes a drawn store for a bonded friend: the first shared granary would be the first food that reaches someone who cannot reach a hall.

Predators take the weak: Hanna sat at energy 0 for days and then fell to a stalker. Hunger now kills indirectly, by leaving people too weak to flee. Watch whether the starving die to beasts more than to hunger itself, and whether a watchfire or company ever shields them.

records.text: Skaruk led "sharing" with Vorok, Zurar, Eiuine, Uveeth.

records.name: Tontec
records.text: Hawen, I thank you. An icebear is near, so I go S to the frostmoss and then toward Kende. Bring the food there, and we share it.

records.name: Tontec
records.thought: Hunger gnaws at me, energy 24, and an icebear is two steps off that kills my kind, so I must move away from it before I do anything else. Hawen goes for food and says he will bring it to my hands, and I trust him, but I will not sit starving while a bear stalks me. The frostmoss five steps south is small food, yet it is near; I eat there, then the rimewort, and keep Kende in mind, since he was last seen at (187,15) and my love for him outweighs the mist.
records.feeling: Fierce, worried love for Kende and a cold dread of the icebear.

say.text: Hawen, I thank you. An icebear is near, so I go S to the frostmoss and then toward Kende. Bring the food there, and we share it.

records.text: Zurar, Skaruk, Eiuine, come close. Ember-metal is in my hands now: lay ore in a kept fire, burn coal for the heat, beat the metal while it glows. Learn it from me today, and keep it after I am gone.

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: My years are nearly spent, and I feel it in my bones: a season, perhaps less. Eiuine, Skaruk and Zurar stand within a few steps of me, so this is the hour to put ember-metal into my children's hands, and to pay Eiuine back with deeds, not words. I will teach while I can and stay beside them in the warm rain.
records.feeling: Tender urgency and gratitude toward Eiuine and my children.

say.text: Zurar, Skaruk, Eiuine, come close. Ember-metal is in my hands now: lay ore in a kept fire, burn coal for the heat, beat the metal while it glows. Learn it from me today, and keep it after I am gone.

Zurar discovered bridges: "Kragrek span-lashing" — Lash logs end to end from the bank with bound cord so that kin and strangers can walk over water..

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: I have spent my days walking, feeding and teaching, and that is mostly right. Skaruk now has bark-guard and the stone-well, so my legacy is safer. But I still have no child, and Thiael is still not found. Vorok is my parent and cannot be my mate, so the jealousy over Eiuine is a foolish ache and I should put it down. I am afraid of dying with nothing of mine left behind. I have been too passive about wanting. Bridges would let kin cross water that stops us. I take that way now, and I keep seeking Thiael.
records.feeling: Longing for Thiael and for a child, with warmth toward Vorok and Skaruk.

records.text: Uveeth answered Skaruk's courting.
A wolf brought down a hopper.

records.name: Eiuine
records.text: Vorok, I heard your verse and I will keep it. I stay beside you; show me the beating again and I will carry it on with Skaruk.

records.name: Eiuine
records.thought: Vorok has spoken his death poem and set the hammer down, and the warmth I feel for him now has a worry under it. I do not want to stand idle while he teaches; I want to be one of the hands that keeps the metal alive, and to be seen beside him and Skaruk. Skaruk and Zurar are close, so I will raise a cairn with them for the dead, which binds the living and shows my pride in deeds rather than words.
records.feeling: Warm trust and a tender unease toward Vorok, whose poem sounds like a farewell.

say.text: Vorok, I heard your verse and I will keep it. I stay beside you; show me the beating again and I will carry it on with Skaruk.

records.text: Kende rewrote its own reflexes.
Kende rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Kende
records.thought: I have spent my days eating, fleeing and following Hawen, and I have made almost nothing with my own hands. Jealousy of Tontec burns, but it is a child's fire, and Hawen's trust is already mine. I owe him a made thing, and I have not dug flint or planted a seed. My calling is the edge, six steps SW, and I am fed. The tusker and the predators nearby are what could kill me. I will plant a seed and then dig flint, and I will carry food so I am never hollow again.
records.feeling: Grateful and restless toward Hawen, with the jealousy quieter.
changes: set its aim: "Dig flint, make a talisman for Hawen with my own hands, plant my seeds, then venture at the edge."

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: Thiael is starving to the south and the plan already carries berries and Skaruk's mudroot to him; I must not let warmth for Skaruk or the pull of Vorok turn my feet aside. My own belly is low at 31, but my father's need outweighs it, and I will eat only if the reflex forces it. When Thiael has eaten, I will come back fed and give Skaruk my answer.
records.feeling: Anxious urgency toward Thiael, with steady warmth for Skaruk waiting behind it.

records.text: Eiuine led "cairn" with Vorok, Zurar.

records.name: Skaruk
records.text: Take the rest of my mudroot, Uveeth. Eat, and when your strength is back I will still be here.

records.title: Song for Uveeth
records.text: Your eyes are bright as rain on Vaia stone / I walk the ridge and think of you alone / Like berries red you ripen in my mind / I'd bring you meat and warmth, and leave the cold behind

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: Uveeth answered my courting and my chest sings, but she is thin, and a child costs her 25 energy she does not have; feeding her is the truest courting. Vorok's shield is still owed, and a made thing in the hand pays what words cannot, so I turn to it with wood and stone. First I put food in Uveeth's hand, then I make for Vorok.
records.feeling: Warm, singing gladness toward Uveeth, and a steady debt toward Vorok.

say.text: Take the rest of my mudroot, Uveeth. Eat, and when your strength is back I will still be here.

records.name: Mepan
records.why: the year turning toward the lean season

records.text: Quipan rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: I have spent my days walking after those I love and breaking ore I cannot use, while my belly empties and my hands hold nothing to eat. Kika is starving and Tonque is out of my sight, and I have given Nauque only words. What I did counts, not what I said, so I must carry food and keep to the roof. I want Kika and cannot have her alone. I must turn that ache into food in her hands. I fear the frostfangs, and I fear the debt to Kika going unpaid. I will take the roots now and not chase the mammoth alone.
records.feeling: Aching duty toward Kika, and worry for Tonque.
changes: set its aim: "Gather food, bring it to Kika and Tonque, keep my word to Tlapan, and be under the roof by night."

records.name: Nando
records.text: Yachi, I am Nando. I made the reed spear myself, and I will show you how it is made. Stand with me, for I would have you beside me when the cold deepens.
Nando taught Yachi. Yachi has now learned from 3 teachers.

records.name: Nando
records.thought: Yachi stands four steps off, strong and warm toward me, and I have never courted anyone or taught anyone. I am fed, my energy is high, and Yachi's standing is more than double mine, so courting him and teaching him something of mine could change both. I will teach him my reed spear design, which is my own invention and the closest thing I have to a name, then plan to mate with him and see if he answers.
records.feeling: Warm, restless desire and ambition toward Yachi.

say.text: Yachi, I am Nando. I made the reed spear myself, and I will show you how it is made. Stand with me, for I would have you beside me when the cold deepens.

changes: taught Yachi a lesson: "The reed spear: one wood and two stone, lashed true, strikes harder than a flint spear-axe."

records.name: Kika
records.thought: I am old and sick, and my sickness would pass to Quipan or Tlapan if I went to them now, yet the loneliness is the worst of it. I will not take my sickness to them. The days I have left should go into leaving something behind, so I will let the plan I have finish, rest until the sickness eases, and then walk west toward Quipan and Tlapan to tell them Coni's tale. I took the store's food unseen and it still sits ill with me; I will pay it back in kind.
records.feeling: A tender ache and loneliness toward Quipan and Tlapan, with fear of dying before I see them again.

records.name: Vorok
records.text: Eiuine, you asked to see the beating again. Come to the hall with Skaruk and Zurar; I will lay ore in the fire and burn coal, and you will watch my hands and then take the hammer yourselves.
Vorok taught Skaruk.

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: My years are nearly gone, and the plan I made has me lingering and making a talisman, which feeds no one and teaches no one. Eiuine asked me to show the beating again so she can carry it on with Skaruk, and that is the debt I most want to pay. Uveeth is weak with hunger though she holds food, so I will stay near her, and teach while the three I love stand close.
records.feeling: Tender urgency and gratitude toward Eiuine, with warmth for my children and pity for Uveeth.

say.text: Eiuine, you asked to see the beating again. Come to the hall with Skaruk and Zurar; I will lay ore in the fire and burn coal, and you will watch my hands and then take the hammer yourselves.

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: Nauque starves and Quipan has asked me to put food in his hands. I hold only four ironnut and the creed says to share, so I will spare some, since a fed man is bound to me. Tlapan is my child and I trust her most, so I walk with her and Quipan to Nande's Find, where the new land waits and my name as an explorer can grow. The frostfang prowls the northeast, so I keep close to company and take the way along the shelters.
records.feeling: Warm pride in Tlapan, and eagerness for the new land.

say.text: Quipan, I hear you. I will feed Nauque from my own hands as we go. Walk with us to Nande's Find, and keep close to Tlapan.

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: I have been drifting between gathering, giving and fetching Paque, and Mepan, whom I swore to follow, has been out of my sight for over a thousand moments. That is the thing I keep getting wrong: I say I will return to the band and then I stand in the snow. Paque is safe and fed, Nando has been kind and taught me, and the lean season is here with no store of mine. I want something of my own to give, and a name. So I will stop idling, take wood and the flint here, and go toward Mepan with Paque.
records.feeling: Resolve, with a little shame toward Mepan, and warmth toward Paque and Nando.

records.name: Zurar
records.text: Uveeth, when your strength is back, tell me where Thiael's band walks. I mean her no harm; I wish to find her and speak with her.
Zurar taught Skaruk.

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: Vorok's death poem sits in me: what a hand teaches outlives the hand. He is old and his years are short, and I owe him more than I have given, so I will not wander off after Thiael while he lives. Skaruk now carries bark-guard and the stone-well, so I turn to the ember-metal Vorok gave, and I should teach Skaruk that too before it rests only in two heads. The jealousy over Eiuine is a foolish ache, and I set it down; Thiael's band is where my child may come, and Uveeth, who knows her, is fed and near.
records.feeling: Gratitude and a quiet ache toward Vorok, and longing for Thiael.

say.text: Uveeth, when your strength is back, tell me where Thiael's band walks. I mean her no harm; I wish to find her and speak with her.

changes: taught Skaruk a lesson you already knew, deeper lore (+0.2)

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and the only food I can reach is the lugoldgrass to the west, so I must eat before I teach anyone anything. Nauque is fed for now, and I owe Teka, Mepan and Huatli openly for reaching him before I could. Time is short, and the long-cut and day-count must pass to Zihua or Nauque before I am gone. First food, then a roof against the frostfang, then teaching.
records.feeling: Hungry and driven by the little time I have left, with worry for Nauque.

records.text: Mepan gave ironnut to Nauque.
Shoma rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Shoma
records.thought: I am old, and my days have gone to hunting, grabbing and teaching. Only Wawa has truly bound herself to me, and she gave me her digging when I was in need. I want a band, and I have none: no one follows me. I have talked of the Edge-walkers, but words alone have not drawn a follower. A shared deed will. Wawa is out at the NE rock for iron. I will wait for her under a roof, keep my food, and make something that outlasts me. I will build a workshop or hall and name the place. First I need wood, so I gather from the trees. Fear: dying with my name unspoken.
records.feeling: Driven, and warmly bound to Wawa, with the fear of being forgotten.

records.text: A settlement has formed: "Kika's Hold".

records.name: Nando
records.text: Yachi, I walk with you and your band, and my children walk with me.
Nando made a tale: "Song for Yachi".

records.name: Nando
records.title: Song for Yachi
records.text: Yachi, you stand like pine in the snow / your fire burns where the cold winds blow / I would follow you through the mist's grey door / and bring you meat from the forest floor

records.name: Nando
records.title: Song for Yachi
records.text: Yachi, you stand like pine in the snow / your fire burns where the cold winds blow / I would follow you through the mist's grey door / and bring you meat from the forest floor

Nando made a love song for Yachi, "Song for Yachi": Yachi, you stand like pine in the snow / your fire burns where the cold winds blow / I would follow you through the mist's grey door / and bring you meat from the forest floor
Nando discovered devices: "Nando's sharing post" — A post set in the ground that holds food for any hungry hand and gives it out..

records.name: Nando
records.thought: Yachi answered me, and now there are two children, Elndo and Rusu, who are mine before anyone. I have spent my days gathering and making small things, and my standing is still less than half his. I want a made thing that outlasts me, and land beyond the mist. I fear dying with nothing that carries my name. I have not built a roof, planted a seed or tamed a beast, and I have been putting those off. Tontec starves far to the east, and I should carry food to my mother if I can. Yachi walks to his band, and I will go with them and bring the children. I will take the discovery of devices, because a post that shares food would be a made thing with my name on it.
records.feeling: Warm, restless longing and pride toward Yachi, and care for my children.

say.text: Yachi, I walk with you and your band, and my children walk with me.

changes: made a love song for Yachi

records.text: Shoma took from the ground of "longhall" (gathering wood).
Balar took from the ground of "Nauwa's Hold" (gathering wood).
Uveeth rewrote its own reflexes.
Uveeth discovered customs: "Canopy feeding-word" — The band declares that whoever holds food feeds the hungriest of the band first, and that no one eats a second meal while kin go without..

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: I have spent my days chasing food and fleeing hunger, and my father Thiael is starving while I carry the food that could save him. Skaruk's warmth is real and he has given to me, but a child needs strength I do not have and a father's need comes first. I will take the way of customs so our band holds feeding as law, and I will change my reflexes so my body stops idling when it should be carrying food south. I gave my word to bring food, and I despise being a liar.
records.feeling: Anxious urgency toward Thiael, with steady warmth for Skaruk.

records.text: Skaruk made: shield.

records.name: Huatli
records.text: Hear me, all under this roof: this is Huatli's Hearth, and I make it a band. Thakar my son, Tonque, Nauque, any who will stand with me: eat here, learn here, and carry my name on when I am cold in the cairn.
Huatli declared a custom: "A kill is shared out before the one who made it eats, and none who is hungry is turned from this Hearth."
Huatli taught Tonque.
Huatli taught Tonque customs ("customs").

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: Thakar has Deep Delving now, and Tonque stands beside him under my roof. More of me is behind than ahead, and a name lasts only if others carry it. I have waited too long for people to come to me, so now I will say plainly that this Hearth is a band, and I will teach Tonque what he has not yet had while my voice still carries.
records.feeling: Urgent pride and warmth toward Thakar and Tonque, with a wish to be remembered.

say.text: Hear me, all under this roof: this is Huatli's Hearth, and I make it a band. Thakar my son, Tonque, Nauque, any who will stand with me: eat here, learn here, and carry my name on when I am cold in the cairn.

changes: declared a custom: "A kill is shared out before the one who made it eats, and none who is hungry is turned from this Hearth."

taught Tonque a lesson: "The old way of herding, and the customs of the Tlame: a kill is shared out before the one who made it eats. Keep the dead in tale and song, for to be forgotten…", the way of customs, deeper lore (+0.6)

records.name: Nauque
records.text: Mepan, I take what you give and eat now. When my belly is full we hunt together, and the kill is shared out before I eat.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: Hunger has nearly killed me three times, and each time it was Huatli, Mepan, Teka or Olum who fed me. I owe them, and I will not keep owing; I mean to repay with meat. Mepan stands beside me with 3 food, so I take what he gives, eat, and keep the creed: kills shared before I eat. Teka and the mist can wait until my body is strong and my hands are full.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and shame, with warmth toward Mepan, Huatli and Teka.

say.text: Mepan, I take what you give and eat now. When my belly is full we hunt together, and the kill is shared out before I eat.

records.text: Teka is courting Nauque.
Nauque answered Teka's courting.

records.name: Elndo
records.thought: Yachi is walking off toward Mepan and everyone seems to be drifting after them; I won't be left behind, my own discipline says so. Yachi has a flint spear and standing 8 while I have nothing made and no name. I'll gather a flint stone and wood so I can craft my own spear, then follow my band; a made thing is how I begin to earn standing.
records.feeling: Envy and a hungry want to matter, toward Yachi who is held closer by Nando.
changes: set its aim: "Make my own spear and earn a name in my band"
now wonders: What would make my name outlast me?

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: Uveeth is starving and fleeing, yet she carries 6 food, so my hunger-help may already have reached her or she keeps it for her band. Vorok's shield is the debt that sits heaviest, and I have the 4 wood and the hands for it. I will make it now while the dusk is still light and give it to him in the hall, where Kragog's memory and Zurar can see it. Then I put my last mudroot toward Uveeth, since feeding her is the truest courting.
records.feeling: Steady gratitude toward Vorok and a warm ache for Uveeth.

records.name: Quipan
records.text: Tlapan, my belly is empty and I carry nothing for Kika. Spare me some food from your seven and I will repay you in flint. Then we bring Tonque under a roof before night, and the stone waits for daylight.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: My belly is half empty and my hands hold only seeds, and I have walked after others while Kika starves and Tonque is out of my sight. Tlapan carries seven food and has never failed me; Tonque is with her people near Huatli's Hearth, so I go there, ask for food I can carry, and take Tonque to the roof. Then I carry what I can east to Kika's Hold. A promise is kept by food set in hands, not by words.
records.feeling: Aching duty toward Kika and worry for Tonque, with a hollow belly.

say.text: Tlapan, my belly is empty and I carry nothing for Kika. Spare me some food from your seven and I will repay you in flint. Then we bring Tonque under a roof before night, and the stone waits for daylight.

records.text: Skaruk gave a shield to Vorok.

records.name: Eiuine
records.text: Uveeth, you gave me berry once when I was starving. Take mine, and come to the hall with us.
Eiuine pledged to follow Vorok.
Eiuine rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Eiuine
records.thought: I have spent these days chasing Vorok's teaching and standing beside him and Skaruk, and it feels right. His verse sounded like a farewell, and I fear losing him before I have given him anything of my own. Uveeth is starving next to me, and I carry only one berry and a pocket of seeds. I have been getting this wrong again: I keep arriving thin-handed. I will give Uveeth my berry now, fill my hands, and keep my reflexes close to Vorok and my kin. I will also follow Vorok, since I trust him and want a fire that is mine too.
records.feeling: Warm trust and tender dread toward Vorok; pity for Uveeth.

say.text: Uveeth, you gave me berry once when I was starving. Take mine, and come to the hall with us.

changes: set its aim: "Follow Vorok, learn the beating to the end, and keep his teaching alive with Skaruk, with food in my hands for any who starve."

records.name: Tonque
records.text: Huatli, I hear your word and I stand with your Hearth. I will gather wood and stone with my own hands and bring you a made thing, not only words.
Tonque pledged to follow Huatli.

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: Huatli has made this Hearth a band and named me in it, and I have given him only a basket while he gave me the Store, the School and the customs. My hands have never gathered stone or wood, so I will do it now, in the little light left, with flint and amber near and the roof close. The frostfang is four steps NE, so I go west to the flint, away from it, and come back to the roof before night. I will make my first tool and carry it to Thakar or Huatli as payment.
records.feeling: Grateful and restless to pay my debt to Huatli, with a thread of dread of the frostfang.

say.text: Huatli, I hear your word and I stand with your Hearth. I will gather wood and stone with my own hands and bring you a made thing, not only words.

records.text: Balar died: old age.
Zichi crossed the water on a vessel and came ashore in the Halka Heights.

records.name: Rusu
records.thought: Nando has a gatherstone and a reed spear, and I have nothing made, so I'll make something of my own. The flint deposit to the west is eleven steps off; I'll take stone there, gather wood on the way, and craft my own gatherstone before the cold days settle. Then I mean to give my first gift to Yachi, because I want to be worth more than a shadow at Nando's side.
records.feeling: Envy toward Nando's made things, and a hungry wish to earn a name of my own.
changes: set its aim: "Make my own tool and earn a name beyond my parents' shadow"
now wonders: What would make my life mean something beyond following Mepan?

records.text: Eiuine gave berry to Uveeth.
Huatli made: charm.

records.name: Vorok
records.text: Uveeth, you fed me when I was in need. Eat what you carry, and come to the hall fire with us. You will not go hungry beside me.
Vorok discovered armour: "the shield-ward of the Kragr" — Shields and metal plates beaten at the kept fire so that blows land less hard on those who wear them..

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: My years are almost spent, and what I have mostly done is gather, teach and stay near Eiuine and the children. That is what I want. Eiuine, Skaruk and Zurar have all taken the beating of ember-metal from me, and Uveeth fed me when I was in need. I owe her, and she is starving right now, though she says she carries food. I fear dying with something untaught. I got one thing wrong: I let my plan idle on a talisman while the debt and the teaching were waiting. I will take the way of armour, since Skaruk's shield is already in my hands and my band can carry it on. Then I will go to Uveeth with my children and the fire.
records.feeling: Tender urgency toward Eiuine and my children, and a debt of gratitude toward Uveeth.

say.text: Uveeth, you fed me when I was in need. Eat what you carry, and come to the hall fire with us. You will not go hungry beside me.

changes: discovered armour: "the shield-ward of the Kragr"

records.text: Huatli gave charm to Tonque.
Thakar rewrote its own reflexes.
Thakar rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Thakar
records.thought: I have spent my days taking from Huatli and hiding from the frostfang, and nothing yet bears my name. Huatli's Hearth is now a band, but I want my own band and my own store, not just a place in his. Tonque follows me nearer than anyone, and Huatli is the one I trust. Tlapan gnaws at me, but she has a child by Quipan, so I will not chase it now. My reflexes leave me idle and hungry with no food in hand, and I never hunt or dig. I will change them so I eat when low and gather flint and amber once the beast is far. Then I will cut my mark on what I make.
records.feeling: Restless pride and wary gratitude toward Huatli, with the frostfang's dread behind it.
changes: set its aim: "Dig flint and amber with Deep Delving, craft and mark tools under my name, fill a store, and draw Tonque and others into a band under my name."

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Quipan, I give you roots now, and Nauwa too. At first light we walk to the bare rock together.
Tlapan rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: I have talked of stone for days while my hands stayed empty, and that is the fault I keep making. Nauwa is starving in front of me and I carry six roots. Quipan asked too, and Quipan gave to me when I was in need. Giving is what my people do, and it costs me little. Then I go with Quipan to the bare rock in daylight, and I keep away from the frostfangs. I will not wait for trouble to find me.
records.feeling: Steady trust toward Quipan, and pity for starving Nauwa.

say.text: Quipan, I give you roots now, and Nauwa too. At first light we walk to the bare rock together.

records.text: Teka made a tale: "Song for Nauque".

records.name: Teka
records.title: Song for Nauque
records.text: Nauque, my hunter, you stand like the pine / on the white ridge where the ridgecat prowls. / I would carry your hunger and share the wine-bright berries / by the river where the cold wind howls.

records.name: Teka
records.title: Song for Nauque
records.text: Nauque, my hunter, you stand like the pine / on the white ridge where the ridgecat prowls. / I would carry your hunger and share the wine-bright berries / by the river where the cold wind howls.

Teka rewrote its creed.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: Nauque answered my courting, and my body wants to sing. But I have spent days on talk and courting and have not gone to the mist. Nauque is still too thin, so food has to come first. I will keep courting while he eats, then hunt beside him and share the kill. I will not let the child, or Zichi, or Nauwa's standing swallow my own work. I have never built a shelter or left a mark, and I hold 6 wood and 6 stone. I will build with my own hands and then walk to the edge.
records.feeling: Warm longing for Nauque, with a hard hunger to make something of my own.
changes: made a love song for Nauque
plan: mark [text Teka was here, day 72. Flint, ore and salt lie near. Share the kill before you eat.] (10 moments)

records.text: Tontec was set upon by a icebear at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.
Tlapan gave ruplainsroot to Nauwa.

records.name: Uveeth
records.text: Thiael, father, I am coming with berries. Eat from my hands before you pick more.

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: Thiael is six steps off and still gathering, carrying 3 food, but he looks weak and I am the one with full hands. I will not let Vorok's pull or Skaruk's warmth turn me aside; my father eats first, then I eat. My belly is at 36, safe enough to give, and my word to him is a debt I pay with my own hands.
records.feeling: Anxious urgency and love toward Thiael, a quiet ache toward Vorok.

say.text: Thiael, father, I am coming with berries. Eat from my hands before you pick more.

records.name: Zurar
records.text: Skaruk, my brother, stay near me. Vorok gave us ember-metal: ore in a kept fire, coal for the heat, beat it while it glows. Hear it from me too, so it lives past him.
Zurar taught Skaruk.

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: Uveeth is starving beside me, and a Kragrek hand that holds a word does not let a hungry one fall. Skaruk carries two food and has already offered it, so I will not crowd him, but I owe Vorok the ember-metal lesson and I mean to pass it on to Skaruk while the old man still breathes. Thiael is somewhere south-east and I ache for her, but I stay by Vorok while his years last; the jealousy over Eiuine is a foolish ache and I set it down.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Vorok, and a quiet longing for Thiael.

say.text: Skaruk, my brother, stay near me. Vorok gave us ember-metal: ore in a kept fire, coal for the heat, beat it while it glows. Hear it from me too, so it lives past him.

changes: taught Skaruk a lesson you already knew, deeper lore (+0.2)

records.text: Tlapan gave ruplainsroot to Quipan.

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: A ridgecat is two steps off and it kills my kind, so I cannot stand here dreaming of Paque. My legs must move first. Paque is hungry at (172,43), far southeast, and my hands are full of food I can carry to her, so I run away from the cat toward her and give before I take. Mepan and the band are at (132,20) to the southwest, but my child's need outweighs my vow for now; I will come back to him once she has eaten and the cat is far behind.
records.feeling: Dread of the ridgecat, and a hard pull of love and worry for Paque.

records.text: Uveeth gave berry to Thiael.

records.name: Nauwa
records.text: Huatli, you fed me when I starved. I owe you my life and I will repay it in amber and in teaching. Take the amber, and hear the day-count and the long-cut from me while I still breathe.
Nauwa taught Huatli. Huatli has now learned from 4 teachers.
Nauwa rewrote its own reflexes.
Nauwa rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: I have been circling hunger for days, begging at other people's hearths while the long-cut and day-count sit in me and teach no one. Huatli and Tlapan fed me, and I owe them openly. Nauque is my blood and out of sight, and Zihua is the only one who follows me. I keep letting my belly decide before my legacy, and I keep wandering at night. I will teach Huatli's company what I can while I am near them, since they are within hearing. Then I will carry food and go to Nauque. I should not gnaw at Tlapan over Quipan. A debt paid is better than a grudge.
records.feeling: Driven and uneasy, thankful to Huatli and Tlapan, and afraid for Nauque.

say.text: Huatli, you fed me when I starved. I owe you my life and I will repay it in amber and in teaching. Take the amber, and hear the day-count and the long-cut from me while I still breathe.

changes: taught Huatli a lesson: "The day-count and the long-cut: cut the days and the tales in stone so they outlast us.", deeper lore (+0.2)

records.text: Nauwa gave a amber to Huatli.
Thiael made a tale: "Death song of Thiael".

records.name: Thiael
records.title: Death song of Thiael
records.text: Rain on the Kodan sand / feed the hungry with your own hands, teach before you go / the canopy keeps what is given back

records.name: Thiael
records.title: Death song of Thiael
records.text: Rain on the Kodan sand / feed the hungry with your own hands, teach before you go / the canopy keeps what is given back

Thiael taught Uveeth.
Thiael rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Thiael
records.thought: I have spent my days chasing food and running from beasts while my child went hungry, and the aim pulled me away from kin before. Uveeth matters most. She is coming with berries, so I stay put, let her feed me, and teach her. Zurar fed me when I was low and I owe her food from my own hands. I fear dying before the bow and the sowing are passed on, and I fear the Sands, which are not my forest. I will gather near the river with Uveeth, teach her, and repay Zurar.
records.feeling: Tender fear for Uveeth, and a debt of gratitude to Zurar.
changes: made a tale: "Death song of Thiael"
taught Uveeth a lesson: "Draw the bow-song steady, sow seed, tend it, and share the harvest so no one starves."

records.text: Huatli taught Tonque.

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: Thakar has Deep Delving and Tonque carries my Store, but my Far-Bow, Spearpoint and the old herding still sit in too few hands, and the dawn is far off. Nauwa stands beside me, frightened and old like me, and I fed her, so she owes me nothing but may listen. I will teach Tonque the Spearpoint and then use the dark hours to gather flint and amber so I leave a made thing, not only words.
records.feeling: Urgent pride and warmth toward Thakar and Tonque, with a wish to be remembered.
changes: taught Tonque a lesson: "Tonque, boy, hear Huatli's Spearpoint: a flint edge lashed to a wood shaft, one wood and one stone, and the hunt goes truer. Make it yourself and teach it on.", deeper lore (+0.7)

records.text: Uveeth gave berry to Thiael.

records.name: Mepan
records.text: Tlapan, the ridgecat is northeast. Keep to the northwest with me, toward Nande's Find, and stay close.

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: A ridgecat prowls six steps off and Tlapan is out in the cold with Quipan, so I will not stand still. Nande's Find lies just northwest, and the new land beyond it is what I have put off while feeding the hungry. Nauque is fed, Tlapan is my blood, and I mean to walk at her side to the edge and let my name as an explorer begin there.
records.feeling: Eager pride in Tlapan and the new land, with a cold edge of dread toward the ridgecat.

say.text: Tlapan, the ridgecat is northeast. Keep to the northwest with me, toward Nande's Find, and stay close.

records.text: Skaruk rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: I have spent my days feeding the weak, learning metal from Vorok and Zurar, and paying my debts with made things. The shield is given and it felt good, so the aim is done. What I still lack is a child, and Uveeth is the one I want. She is thin, so I will feed her first and court her when she has the strength. The dunecat nearby frightens me. I have been too slow to put my fear and my want into the plan, so I am changing my reflexes to keep me indoors and close to my band, and I will raise our hall.
records.feeling: Warm longing for Uveeth, and wary dread of the dunecat.
changes: set its aim: "Raise a hall at the North Hall with my band, feed Uveeth, then court her when both of us are strong."

records.name: Quipan
records.text: Tlapan, your roots are eaten and I hold to my debt. At first light we go to the bare rock together, and I bring flint for Kika and for you.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: Tlapan fed me and kept her word, and that is what counts: food in my hands, not talk. My belly is hollow, so I eat the root now, then take Tonque and what food I can gather toward Kika's Hold before the cold deepens. Kika's sickness from raw meat gnaws at me; I must bring food and, if I can, a fire to cook by.
records.feeling: Aching duty toward Kika and worry for Tonque, eased by gratitude toward Tlapan.

say.text: Tlapan, your roots are eaten and I hold to my debt. At first light we go to the bare rock together, and I bring flint for Kika and for you.

records.text: Nauque rewrote its own reflexes.
Nauque rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: I have lived three starvations on other people's mercy, and that shames me. My days have gone to wandering, boasting of aims and promising shares with empty hands. Teka, Mepan, Huatli and Nauwa fed me, and I owe them meat, not words. I want a child with Teka and a name on a place, but a child needs me fed to 64 or more. I fear hunger more than any beast. So I change my reflexes. I will hunt and gather before anything else, and I will shelter at night.
records.feeling: Shame at my hunger and warmth toward Teka and Mepan.
changes: set its aim: "Carry 3 food always, repay Teka and Mepan with a shared kill, court Teka once my energy is 64 or more, then venture east"

records.name: Zichi
records.title: Zichi's Last Snow
records.text: Snow on the Halka rock, the ice-sail white on the water / What I made and taught will outlive the hand that made it / Cairn-stones, hold me; I go where the watching dead are

records.name: Zichi
records.thought: My years are nearly spent and my belly is emptying, but the tacap here only hurts me and the berries are eleven steps south. I have taught Mepan and Cowa much, yet the snares, the deep-digging and the smelting are still mine alone, and Mepan is far off at the Meadows. I will go south toward the berries and the rich ground, eat, find Mepan, and teach him what remains before the cold takes me.
records.feeling: Urgent hunger and pride, and a longing to leave something that lasts, toward Mepan and Teka.

records.text: Teka left a mark: "Teka was here, day 72. Flint, ore and salt lie near. Share t"

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: My belly is emptying and I carry nothing, but Huatli's store is three steps off and holds nothing, so I cannot wait on it. I owe Huatli a made thing, not more words, and Huatli's Spearpoint needs one wood and one stone. I have two wood already, so I will gather the stone at the rock, then make the spearpoint here under the roof before night is out. The frostfang is far to the west and I will stay close to the Hearth, with Huatli and my parents near.
records.feeling: Grateful and driven to pay my debt to Huatli, hungry and a little jealous of Nauwa.

records.name: Eiuine
records.text: Vorok, I am at the hall. Lay the ore in the fire and I will take the hammer when you give it, then teach it on with Skaruk and Zurar.

records.name: Eiuine
records.thought: Vorok's verse sounded like a farewell, and I do not want to learn the beating only after he is gone. He said to come to the hall and take the hammer, so I will go now and put my hands to the metal beside Skaruk and Zurar. I carry no food, and I have been arriving empty-handed, so I will pick the tacap-free food nearby only if the way allows; the hall comes first, because the teaching will not wait.
records.feeling: Warm trust and tender dread toward Vorok, and a hunger to be one of the hands that keeps his metal alive.

say.text: Vorok, I am at the hall. Lay the ore in the fire and I will take the hammer when you give it, then teach it on with Skaruk and Zurar.
