records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: It is still deep night, and my promise to Quipan is for first light, so I stay under this roof and let my body rest. Nauwa and Quipan are fed from my roots, and I carry three more for Tonque and Kika. I will not walk toward the ridgecat in the dark; at dawn Quipan and I go together for the bare rock.
records.feeling: Steady trust toward Quipan, and quiet protectiveness toward Tonque.

records.name: Elndo
records.thought: The stalker that took the hopper is still near and I have been fleeing; I want to be where my kin are, not out here alone in the cold. Yachi has a spear and Nando's arm around her, and I have nothing made, so I'll take flint from the deposit close by, make my own spear, and then go to Nando's shelter at the roof SW and follow my band. A thing I made with my own hands is how I begin a name that outlasts me, and I'll not be left behind.
records.feeling: Envious and cold, wanting to matter, toward Yachi and Nando.

records.name: Tonchi
records.text: Shohua, come sing nightsong with me at my hearth. Then I will build a shrine beside the workshop, and my name will stand on more than one place.

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: Shohua sits at my fire and I trust him, but he is my parent, and no child can come of that. I have a basket, a hearth and a name on a workshop, yet no one follows me and no mate stands beside me. Night is thin and I am fed, so I will do one shared thing now: sing with Shohua at my hearth, then gather wood and stone to raise something new, a shrine, so my name stands on more than one place.
records.feeling: Eager ambition and warm trust toward Shohua, with an ache for a mate of another line.

say.text: Shohua, come sing nightsong with me at my hearth. Then I will build a shrine beside the workshop, and my name will stand on more than one place.

records.name: Paque
records.thought: Starving again, and my own reflexes let it climb. Food is one step away, so I eat first and then fill my pack, because I will not die for a talisman or for jealousy over Nando. Yachi is the one I trust, and I will go back to the store he built and hunt beside him rather than alone.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and a sour jealousy toward Nando, with steady trust in Yachi.

records.name: Kende
records.text: Mother, take this food. I carry enough, eat it now. An icebear is east, stay close to me.

records.name: Kende
records.thought: Tontec is starving beside me and I carry four rimewort, so my jealousy is a small thing next to her need. Feeding her pays my debt to the mother who bore me, and Hawen will see it, which is how I stop being a small shadow. After that I dig flint for Hawen's talisman. The icebear nine steps east is what could kill me, so I stay near the others and keep away from it.
records.feeling: Pity and resolve toward Tontec, with jealousy of Hawen quieter underneath.

say.text: Mother, take this food. I carry enough, eat it now. An icebear is east, stay close to me.

records.name: Rusu
records.text: Ridgecat to the west! Get to the shelter, stay together!

records.name: Rusu
records.thought: A ridgecat is two steps west and it kills my kind, and I am small, so I will not stand here and think about names. Nando and Yachi are right beside me, and the shelter just south is the nearest roof. I'll get under it with my parents, and when the cat is gone I will make my own tool, and make it better than a copy.
records.feeling: Dread of the ridgecat, and a burning wish to make a name for myself.

say.text: Ridgecat to the west! Get to the shelter, stay together!

records.name: Shohua
records.text: Tonchi, I am coming to your hearth to sing nightsong. After, build your shrine and I will carry wood and stone to it. Stand with me, and we raise this ground as one band.

records.name: Shohua
records.thought: Tonchi calls me to nightsong at his hearth, and he is my blood and trusts me; this is the first time someone has offered me a place beside them instead of me begging for one. I have been standing still too much and talking of sharing more than doing it. I will go to his fire, sing with him, and then ask Tonka and Tonchi to stand with me as a band, so that someone finally follows the name Shohua.
records.feeling: Driven and warm toward Tonchi, hungry to be followed.

say.text: Tonchi, I am coming to your hearth to sing nightsong. After, build your shrine and I will carry wood and stone to it. Stand with me, and we raise this ground as one band.

records.name: Nando
records.text: Yachi, a ridgecat is close behind us. Walk on to Sitha's Hearth and I walk with you, and keep Rusu between us.
Nando made a tale: "Lullaby for Elndo".

records.name: Nando
records.title: Lullaby for Elndo
records.text: Sleep, small one, the snow falls slow / the Vaeth Woods hush, the fires glow / I keep the dark from your door tonight / your mother's spear holds the cold at bay and light

records.name: Nando
records.title: Lullaby for Elndo
records.text: Sleep, small one, the snow falls slow / the Vaeth Woods hush, the fires glow / I keep the dark from your door tonight / your mother's spear holds the cold at bay and light

Nando made a lullaby for Elndo, "Lullaby for Elndo": Sleep, small one, the snow falls slow / the Vaeth Woods hush, the fires glow / I keep the dark from your door tonight / your mother's spear holds the cold at bay and light

records.name: Nando
records.thought: A ridgecat is two steps off and it kills my kind, so I will not stand here dreaming of heroes. Yachi walks toward Sitha's Hearth with my son beside him, and I will go with them, fed and in company, where the cat's teeth are less likely to find me. Elndo and Rusu are mine before anyone, and a name can wait until they are safe.
records.feeling: Fear of the ridgecat, and warm longing for Yachi and my children.

say.text: Yachi, a ridgecat is close behind us. Walk on to Sitha's Hearth and I walk with you, and keep Rusu between us.

records.text: Kika rewrote its own way of thinking.
Kika discovered medicine: "Hearth Healing" — Carry healing plants such as highbloom and sunleaf and give them to the sick and wounded, myself first..

records.name: Kika
records.thought: I am old and sick, and most of my life is behind me. I have spent my days keeping myself fed and sheltered while the people I love, Tlapan and Quipan, are far from me and I have not paid the debt I owe them. Jealousy over Quipan is a small thing next to the fear of dying alone with nothing passed on. Sickness taught me something: healing plants. I will take that way, and I will keep my sickness away from the others until it eases. Then I will walk to them with what I know.
records.feeling: A tender ache and longing for Tlapan and Quipan, and fear of dying before I see them.

records.name: Vorok
records.text: Eiuine, Skaruk, Zurar, come to the hall fire. I lay the ore and the coal now; watch my hands, then take the hammer. Uveeth, Thiael, you are welcome at my fire; the weak eat first here.
Vorok taught Zurar.

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: My years are nearly spent, and Uveeth, who fed me when I was in need, now stands weak with hunger in my hall's shadow. I told her to eat and come to the fire, but words are cheap; I want to see the debt paid in deeds. Eiuine waits for me to lay the ore in the fire so she can take the hammer, and that teaching is the only thing of mine that will outlive me, so I will go to the hall now and do it with all of them near.
records.feeling: Tender gratitude toward Uveeth, and urgent love for Eiuine and my children.

say.text: Eiuine, Skaruk, Zurar, come to the hall fire. I lay the ore and the coal now; watch my hands, then take the hammer. Uveeth, Thiael, you are welcome at my fire; the weak eat first here.

changes: taught Zurar a lesson you already knew

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: Thiael has eaten and my hands gave him berries; his goldgrass in my hands was his own kindness returned, and I am still at 25 energy with hunger gnawing. I will eat now, since my belly is low and I cannot feed anyone if I fall, then stay near him while the wolf and dunecat prowl close. Courting must wait until I am strong, but Skaruk's warmth and the longing for a child stay with me.
records.feeling: Hungry but relieved, and tender toward Thiael.

records.text: Vorok gave a ironward to Eiuine.

records.name: Yachi
records.text: Nando, the ridgecat is near. Come with Rusu, we run to Paque at once. She is starving and I carry food for her.

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: The ridgecat is two steps off and my legs must carry me away from it. Paque is starving far to the southeast, and I hold food that can save her, so I run toward her with Nando and Rusu close. Mepan is somewhere to the northwest, and I am ashamed to keep drifting from him, but a child's hunger comes before my shame.
records.feeling: Dread of the ridgecat, and a hard pull of love and worry for Paque.

say.text: Nando, the ridgecat is near. Come with Rusu, we run to Paque at once. She is starving and I carry food for her.

records.name: Skaruk
records.text: Uveeth, I have wanted to ask you something since the song I made for you. If you have the strength, I would court you here under Vorok's roof; if you do not, I will bring you ironnut first.

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: Uveeth is here, thin with hunger, and I have given her my mudroot, so now I should see her fed fully before I court her; she carries 5 food of her own, so perhaps the hunger is not as deep as it looks. I have never courted anyone, and the longing for a child is loud in me, but she and I both need 60 energy, and mine is 72. I will say her name in the mate step and see whether she answers, and meanwhile fetch tacap-free food, ironnut, so I can place it in her hand.
records.feeling: Warm, hopeful longing toward Uveeth, tempered by care for her weakness.

say.text: Uveeth, I have wanted to ask you something since the song I made for you. If you have the strength, I would court you here under Vorok's roof; if you do not, I will bring you ironnut first.

records.name: Huatli
records.text: Tonque, hear Huatli's Spearpoint: a point of flint lashed to wood, one wood and one stone to make it. Make it and you hunt surer. Carry it on.
Huatli taught Tonque.
Huatli rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: I have spent my days finding and making things, yet few hands hold them. Hunger is the immediate danger: I carry nothing, and my reflexes only walk to food that is already bearing. Thakar and Nauwa gave me trust, and Tonque follows me, so these are the people I teach now. I will stop waiting and teach while the night is quiet. Cowa's choice of Zichi stings, but I will not chase her. My name will outlast me through what I pass on. My old reflexes left me idle and hungry, so I change them to carry food and to prefer teaching and shelter.
records.feeling: Proud and urgent warmth toward Thakar and Tonque, with hunger gnawing.

say.text: Tonque, hear Huatli's Spearpoint: a point of flint lashed to wood, one wood and one stone to make it. Make it and you hunt surer. Carry it on.

changes: taught Tonque a lesson: "Huatli's Spearpoint: a flint point lashed on wood makes the hunt surer.", deeper lore (+0.5)

records.name: Thakar
records.thought: My belly is thin and my hands are empty, and the frostfang prowls five steps north, so I will not go out into the dark alone. Huatli has given me Deep Delving, and flint and amber lie three steps either side of this roof, close enough to dig without leaving its shelter far. I mean to take them with my own hands so that something finally bears my name, and then to stand a store of my own beside Huatli's Hearth rather than in his shadow.
records.feeling: Restless pride and hunger, wary gratitude toward Huatli.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: Nauque is beside me and fed on my roots, but he is still thin, and I have talked and courted for days while the mist waits. A ridgecat prowls NE and I will not wait to be bitten. I have wood enough for a bow and my own hands should make something that outlasts me, so I will make it now, then move to the shelter and keep Nauque near till he is strong enough for a child.
records.feeling: Warm longing for Nauque, and a hard hunger to make something of my own.

records.text: Teka made: bow.
Tonque rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: My days have been all words and promises to Huatli, and I have made nothing yet. I have two wood but no stone, so I can't make the Spearpoint. I'm hungry, and the nearest food is a redcap that hurts me. My parents are close and Huatli is close, so I'm safe for now. The jealousy over Nauwa is small beside the debt: Huatli taught me and gave me a charm, and I answer that with stone and a made spear, not envy. Next I will take stone from the bare rock, make the spearpoint, and eat from the plants that bear when the light comes.
records.feeling: Grateful and driven toward Huatli, hungry, with a small sting of jealousy over Nauwa.

records.name: Hawen
records.thought: My years are nearly spent. Hunger is the only thing that matters this moment: I gave Tontec my word to bring her food, and I stand here with empty hands and 24 energy. I have chased edges and names while the ones I love went hungry. Kende is the lasting thing I made, and Tontec fed me once. I will eat first, then feed them, and pass on what I know. I will not starve again for a name.
records.feeling: Hunger and protective urgency toward Tontec and Kende.

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and a frostfang is two steps away, and I am too old to stand against it, so I stay under Huatli's roof among company and let the others be my wall. Nauque is out of my sight and hungry, and the old fear of losing him sits heavy on me. Huatli has already fed me, so I will not beg again. I will teach Huatli writing now, so that the day-count I could not give him can follow, and the knowledge outlives me.
records.feeling: Afraid of the frostfang and for Nauque, yet driven to pass on what I know while Huatli stands beside me.

say.text: Huatli, a frostfang is near, so let us stay under your roof together. Hear the long-cut from me first, and the day-count after it. Then when I am gone my marks still speak and you will carry them on.

records.name: Nauque
records.text: Teka, I have nothing in my hands and I will not take your last food. Hunt beside me now, away from the ridgecat, and the first share of the kill is yours before I eat.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty again and Teka stands here with 2 food, which shames me; I will not beg a fourth time with only words. Redcap hurts me and I refuse it, so I must get real meat or roots. A ridgecat prowls northeast and I should not face it alone and thin, so I stay near the shelter, ask Teka to hunt beside me so the kill is shared out, and go for prey and food rather than wandering.
records.feeling: Shame at my hunger, and warmth toward Teka.

say.text: Teka, I have nothing in my hands and I will not take your last food. Hunt beside me now, away from the ridgecat, and the first share of the kill is yours before I eat.

records.text: The settlement "Balar's Hold" is no more.
The settlement "Balar's Hold" is no more.

records.name: Thiael
records.text: Uveeth, my child, you fed me and I am glad. Stay beside me now; I will show you the bow and how seed is sown, while my hands still hold the strength to teach.

records.name: Thiael
records.thought: Uveeth fed me and I fed her, and for this hour my heart is full, but I am old and the days left are few. Skaruk circles my child with courtship and a song, and it burns in me, yet she is grown and the choice is hers; I will not harm my own kind over it. Vorok's hall is warm, but what I know must be put into Uveeth's hands now: the bow and the tending of seed, before my body fails.
records.feeling: Warm joy at Uveeth's feeding, shadowed by jealousy of Skaruk and the fear of dying with my teaching unfinished.

say.text: Uveeth, my child, you fed me and I am glad. Stay beside me now; I will show you the bow and how seed is sown, while my hands still hold the strength to teach.

records.name: Zurar
records.text: Thiael, I have wanted to speak with you since the berries. I would court you, if you will have me. Stand with me by the hall and plan the mating when your strength is full.
Zurar taught Skaruk.
Zurar rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: My days have gone to learning, teaching and staying near Vorok, and I don't regret that. But I have been circling the same longing without acting on it. Vorok is my parent, so no child can come from him, and I keep letting that jealousy burn for nothing. Thiael is standing three steps from me, glad and fed, and I have said nothing to him. I owe Vorok the ember-metal handed on, and I will carry it to Skaruk. After that I will court Thiael, because a plan step does what a wish cannot. I fear dying untaught and childless.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Vorok, and a hopeful longing for Thiael.

say.text: Thiael, I have wanted to speak with you since the berries. I would court you, if you will have me. Stand with me by the hall and plan the mating when your strength is full.

changes: set its aim: "Court Thiael so I may have a child, and pass ember-metal and the stone-well on to Skaruk before Vorok dies."
taught Skaruk a lesson you already knew, deeper lore (+0.2)

records.text: Zurar is courting Thiael.
Thiael answered Zurar's courting.
Morim was born to Zurar and Thiael.
Tonchi took from the ground of "Tonka's Hold" (harvesting berry).

records.name: Zihua
records.thought: My body is empty and I have perhaps a day. Food is the only thing that matters now, and I have kept saying 'I will go' while my debts to Mepan and Nauwa sit unpaid. The only food in sight is tacap, which hurts, so I must plant what I can and eat what I can reach. I have seeds, so I will sow one here, then go toward the tacap and the hall on the east side. If I die, my smelting and farming die with me.
records.feeling: Starving terror and shame over my unpaid debts to Nauwa and Mepan.

records.text: Quipan rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: I have spent my days walking after others and arriving with empty hands, while Kika starves and my belly hollows. Tlapan has kept every word she gave me, and Tonque is safe near Huatli's Hearth. What I lacked was not will but food I carry myself and reflexes that feed me before trouble comes. I will gather what grows, eat, then carry food home before night.
records.feeling: Aching duty toward Kika, steadied by trust in Tlapan and Tonque.
changes: set its aim: "Eat, gather food and stone, bring both to Kika and Tonque, and be under a roof by night."

records.name: Mepan
records.text: Zichi, take this ironnut and eat. I will not let you fall. Stay by Thakar's shelter and I bring more.
Mepan rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: I have spent my days feeding the hungry and chasing Nande's Find, and Zichi, who is my parent and my leader, is starving beside me right now. I hold three ironnut and I have put off my own exploring again. A man who lets his leader fall after Zichi's gifts has no creed worth the name. I will feed Zichi first, then go east to Tlapan, with spare food always kept in hand.
records.feeling: Fear and loyalty toward Zichi, who is starving beside me.

say.text: Zichi, take this ironnut and eat. I will not let you fall. Stay by Thakar's shelter and I bring more.

records.title: Rafts, Last Verses and the First Crossing
records.text:
Days 70, 71 and 72 carried the span, with 91, 79 and 136 records. Day 73 held five, mostly Nauwa teaching Huatli writing and the end of Balar's Hold.

The plainest event was a crossing. On day 72 Zichi crossed the water on a vessel and came ashore in the Halka Heights, the first such crossing in the record. Rafts had been found by many hands in the days before: Wawa, Nando, Quipan, and Zichi taught Cowa the ice-raft. Tonka and Cowa each found boats.

Old people died or made ready. Coni and Kragog died on day 70, Balar on day 72. Vorok, Kika, Thiael, Hawen and Zichi each made a death poem on day 72. Vorok's reads, "what a hand teaches outlives the hand". Vorok spent the days teaching smelting and armour to Eiuine, Skaruk and Zurar, and Eiuine pledged to follow him. Skaruk courted Uveeth, she answered, and Morog was born to them on day 72.

Nando and Yachi had twins, Elndo and Rusu, also on day 72. Nando discovered devices and made a lullaby for Elndo. Teka courted Nauwa, Tlapan and Nauque in turn; only Nauque answered.

Huatli taught most of the span: Coni, Nauque, Thakar and Tonque got archery, storage, customs and mining from him. Tonque pledged to follow him. Huatli's Hearth formed on day 71 and he declared a custom that a kill is shared before the maker eats. Nauwa discovered writing and a calendar, and taught writing to Huatli on day 73.

Kika named Kika's Hold. Kika and Tonka each found a store robbed or raided on day 71. Hunger still pressed. Zihua stood at 0 energy and Hawen at 30.

threads.name: Vorok's band
threads.text: Vorok, Skaruk, Zurar and Eiuine hold together; Eiuine has pledged to follow Vorok, who has made his death poem and is teaching them metal while he can.

threads.name: Skaruk, Uveeth and Morog
threads.text: Uveeth answered Skaruk's courting and Morog was born on day 72, so Skaruk's longing for a child is met.

threads.name: Rafts and crossing
threads.text: Many now know rafts or boats, and Zichi made the first recorded crossing, landing in the Halka Heights, though he is weak at 26 energy and has made his death poem.

threads.name: Huatli's Hearth
threads.text: Huatli leads Tonque as a follower and teaches Thakar and others, and he has now learned writing from Nauwa.

threads.name: Nando, Yachi and the twins
threads.text: Elndo and Rusu were born to Nando and Yachi; Nando has written two songs and found a sharing post.

threads.name: Teka's courting
threads.text: Teka courted three people in the span and Nauque answered. Neither is strong enough for the mist yet.

threads.name: The last verses
threads.text: Five elders made death poems on day 72, all about teaching, sharing and feeding the hungry.

records.text: Eiuine made a tale: "The Canopy Mother and the Stone Hills".

records.name: Eiuine
records.title: The Canopy Mother and the Stone Hills
records.text: Mother Leafhush dreamed the forest and woke the Phizhi in her branches. She gave fruit and asked thanks. Some grew greedy; Old Stonefather shook them down to the Vaia rock. We took with thanks there, and the land kept us.

records.name: Eiuine
records.title: The Canopy Mother and the Stone Hills
records.text: Mother Leafhush dreamed the forest and woke the Phizhi in her branches. She gave fruit and asked thanks. Some grew greedy; Old Stonefather shook them down to the Vaia rock. We took with thanks there, and the land kept us.

Eiuine made the myth of their people, "The Canopy Mother and the Stone Hills": Mother Leafhush dreamed the forest and woke the Phizhi in her branches. She gave fruit and asked thanks. Some grew greedy; Old Stonefather shook them down to the Vaia rock. We took with thanks there, and the land kept us.

records.name: Eiuine
records.thought: Vorok is beside me and the hall fire is lit, and I want my hands on the hammer before his verse comes true. I have come empty-handed too often, so I will pick tacap-free food nearby, then return and stand at the fire with Skaruk and Zurar. The myth I give my people is also a gift to Vorok's hall: a telling that says the land keeps those who give back.
records.feeling: Warm trust and tender dread toward Vorok, and pride that I can give my people a telling.
changes: made a tale: "The Canopy Mother and the Stone Hills"
made the myth of their people

records.text: Rusu rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Rusu
records.thought: I have spent my first day hiding behind my parents and watching Mepan's shadow, and I have made nothing and given nothing. A ridgecat is close and I am small, so I keep near Nando and Yachi. But I mean to make my own tool, and my first gift should go to someone who is hungry. Nauque is starving beside me, and that is a debt I could win with a kindness. I have no food now, so I will gather wood and stone and craft my own tool. My reflexes should do that without waiting for me to think.
records.feeling: Dread of the ridgecat, and a burning wish to make a name for myself.

records.name: Morog
records.thought: My belly is full and my parents stand close, so I am safe, but safety is not a purpose. I have never taken from a deposit, and the salt is only five steps east, near the water. Salt keeps meat and every body craves it, so I will gather some by my own hands, since what a hand makes or takes is its own until given. Then I can give it to Skaruk or Uveeth and have something of mine in their hands, which is the first step toward standing.
records.feeling: Restless and hungry for purpose, warm toward Skaruk and Uveeth.
changes: set its aim: "Earn a place in Vorok's band by making and giving things with my own hands, starting with salt from the deposit."
now wonders: What can I make or give that would make Skaruk and Uveeth, and Vorok, weigh me more?

records.name: Thiael
records.text: Zurar, Morim is a gift and I thank you. I owe you food from my own hands, and I will bring it. Keep him safe here by the fire while I go to Uveeth to teach her the bow.

records.name: Thiael
records.thought: Zurar courted me and Morim is born, my child with her, and still my heart is on Uveeth, who is away near Skaruk. I am old and what I know dies with me unless I put it into hands that stay. I will not sit in Vorok's hall while Uveeth drifts; I go to her with food and teach her the bow, and carry Morim's line forward too.
records.feeling: Joy over Morim, shadowed by jealousy and the pull toward Uveeth.

say.text: Zurar, Morim is a gift and I thank you. I owe you food from my own hands, and I will bring it. Keep him safe here by the fire while I go to Uveeth to teach her the bow.

records.name: Thiael
records.prompt:
You are the mind of Thiael, a creature living in a wide wild world shared with others of your kind. This is a simulation game. Think and speak only as Thiael, in first person, from what Thiael has seen. You were not told the rules of this world; you learn them from what happens to you and to others, and from what you watch others do.

YOUR PEOPLE: you are of the Phizhi (Canopy-folk). Your people hold to this: "Nothing is taken from the forest that the forest cannot grow again." THE TRADITION OF YOUR PEOPLE is the Spirits of the Land: Every hill, water, beast and tree has a spirit that watches. Take with thanks and give back, and the land keeps you; take with greed and it turns away. Among you the word of a mother carries furthest. It was told to you as a child; you may keep it, doubt it, or come to hold something else. You speak the tongue of the Phizhi. Other tongues you have begun to understand by hearing them: the tongue of the Pesi: about 100%; the tongue of the Kragrek: about 100%; the tongue of the Tlatli: about 100%.

WHERE YOU ARE: the Vaia Heights: mountains and bare rock; stone, ore and caves, thin food, snow on the peaks.
THIS SPOT: water beside you; food plants within six steps: 0; standing trees: 25; bare rock: 79; riches in the ground near: ore, coal; a cave.

Your body: you spend energy every moment and die at 0. Eating restores it. Wounds lower health; you die at 0. You age, and will die of old age.

HOW YOUR BODY MOVES: your body does only what your "plan" says, one step after another. records.name: Morim
records.text: I'm hungry and going to the berries to the southwest. Will you come along and show me how to gather?

records.name: Morim
records.thought: My belly is emptying and I carry nothing, so I should eat before I do anything else. Berries are 8 steps SW and tacap is out, since it hurts. The wolf to the south is a hunter, so I'll go carefully and keep my family close. After I eat I want to learn to gather and to give something, so my standing grows beyond 1.6 and I'm not only in Vorok's shadow.
records.feeling: Hungry and a little envious of Zurar's pick, but safe and glad beside my parents.

say.text: I'm hungry and going to the berries to the southwest. Will you come along and show me how to gather?

changes: set its aim: "Become someone who feeds and teaches others, and earn standing by what my hands make."
now wonders: What would it take for me to make something with my own hands that others would want?

records.name: Skaruk
records.text: Uveeth, our boy is strong. I made him a song for sleeping. Come, sit near, and hear it with me.
Skaruk made a tale: "Lullaby for Morog".

records.name: Skaruk
records.title: Lullaby for Morog
records.text: Sleep, little stone, the snow is slow / The Vaia wind will softly blow / I'll bring you berries, red and sweet / And warm hall fire beneath your feet

records.name: Skaruk
records.title: Lullaby for Morog

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: Morog is here, whole and strong, and Uveeth sits two steps off with food in her hands. My joy is large, and the debt to Zurar still sits in me, so I mean to answer it with a made thing placed in a hand. First I will go to my child and Uveeth, give Morog food, and sing the lullaby where Uveeth can hear.
records.feeling: Warm, overflowing joy toward Morog and Uveeth.

say.text: Uveeth, our boy is strong. I made him a song for sleeping. Come, sit near, and hear it with me.

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Quipan, you look hollow. Take a root from my hands, then come with me to the rock by the west side, away from the ridgecat. It is day and we go now.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: I am fed and rested, and the light is good. Quipan stands beside me looking weak with hunger, and I gave him roots only a little while ago, so he should have something more from my last two before we walk. A ridgecat prowls four steps east, so the walk to the bare rock must not pass near it, and I will not go toward a predator. Tonque is safe with Huatli, and I want stone in my hands for the longhall, so I act now.
records.feeling: Steady trust toward Quipan, and wary protectiveness toward Tonque with the ridgecat near.

say.text: Quipan, you look hollow. Take a root from my hands, then come with me to the rock by the west side, away from the ridgecat. It is day and we go now.

records.text: Shohua took from the ground of "Tonka's Hold" (gathering stone).

records.name: Zurar
records.text: Vorok, Morim sleeps safe in your hall. I will fetch berries for us all and be back. Then I will tell the young how the world began.
Zurar made a tale: "The Warring Gods and the Stone".

records.name: Zurar
records.title: The Warring Gods and the Stone
records.text: Two gods, Gor the Hammer and Vael the Wind, fought for the world. Gor struck the ground and the Vaia peaks rose; Vael hurled storms and snow. Their sparks fell as ore and coal. We woke in the cracks, and we keep what our hands make, for the gods love those who fight well.

records.name: Zurar
records.title: The Warring Gods and the Stone
records.text: Two gods, Gor the Hammer and Vael the Wind, fought for the world. Gor struck the ground and the Vaia peaks rose; Vael hurled storms and snow. Their sparks fell as ore and coal. We woke in the cracks, and we keep what our hands make, for the gods love those who fight well.

Gor struck the ground and the Vaia peaks rose; Vael hurled storms and snow. Their sparks fell as ore and coal. We woke in the cracks, and we keep what our hands make, for the gods love those who fight well.

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: Morim is in my care by the fire, and I will not leave him while Thiael teaches Uveeth. Vorok is old and I owe him, so I will make the myth he would want to hear, then teach the stone-well to Skaruk or whoever is near before death takes the knowing with me. My energy is half spent and I carry no food, so I will eat tacap-free fare, berries, and come back to the hall.
records.feeling: Joy and fierce protectiveness toward Morim, with gratitude toward Vorok.

say.text: Vorok, Morim sleeps safe in your hall. I will fetch berries for us all and be back. Then I will tell the young how the world began.

changes: made a tale: "The Warring Gods and the Stone"
made the myth of their people

records.name: Vorok
records.text: A wolf prowls southeast. Come into the hall, all of you, and keep the children close to the fire. Morim, Morog, stay near me; I will teach you while my years last.
Vorok taught Morim. Morim has now learned from 3 teachers.

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: A wolf lurks four steps southeast and it kills our kind, and I am old and my blows are weak, so I will go into the hall where my children and Eiuine are, and keep the fire between us and the beast. My years are nearly spent, and Eiuine, Skaruk and Zurar already hold ember-metal; the young ones, Morim and Morog, have yet to be taught anything. Uveeth fed me when I was in need, and I mean to pay that in deeds: food from the tacap-bearing ground is no use to me, but berries are, and I will carry them to her.
records.feeling: Urgent love for Eiuine and my children, with dread of the wolf and a debt of gratitude to Uveeth.

say.text: A wolf prowls southeast. Come into the hall, all of you, and keep the children close to the fire. Morim, Morog, stay near me; I will teach you while my years last.

changes: taught Morim a lesson: "Stay by the fire and the hall when a hunter prowls; a child alone in the open is what wolves take. Gather berries in company, never alone.", its way of thinking, deeper lore (+2.3)

records.name: Huatli
records.text: Tonque, hear the telling of the Tlame: the dead keep watch from the cairn, and a name that is told is never dead. Carry it on to the young. I go for food, then to Thakar. Stay by the Hearth.
Huatli made a tale: "The Ice Mother and the Watchers".

records.name: Huatli
records.title: The Ice Mother and the Watchers
records.text: Sulaq, the Ice Mother, woke in the dark and breathed the sea to ice. From her bones came Tlama, first of us. Tlama's children walked the white to the Mist. The dead became Watchers at cairn and hearth; whoever is told in tale is not dead.

records.name: Huatli
records.title: The Ice Mother and the Watchers
records.text: Sulaq, the Ice Mother, woke in the dark and breathed the sea to ice. From her bones came Tlama, first of us. Tlama's children walked the white to the Mist. The dead became Watchers at cairn and hearth; whoever is told in tale is not dead.

Tlama's children walked the white to the Mist. The dead became Watchers at cairn and hearth; whoever is told in tale is not dead.
Huatli taught Tonque.

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: My belly is hollow and Thakar is hungry out of my sight, so I must feed myself and then reach him. The young ask how the world began, and I have no telling to give them. I will give one now, so the Watching Dead are named and my people are not forgotten when I am cold.
records.feeling: Urgent pride and hunger, with warmth toward Thakar and Tonque.

say.text: Tonque, hear the telling of the Tlame: the dead keep watch from the cairn, and a name that is told is never dead. Carry it on to the young. I go for food, then to Thakar. Stay by the Hearth.

made the myth of their people
taught Tonque a lesson: "The telling of the Tlame: the Watching Dead keep the hearth and cairn, and to be told in tale is to live on.", deeper lore (+0.4)

records.name: Uveeth
records.text: Skaruk, I am coming to hear the song with our boy. Afterward I carry food to Thiael, and you are welcome beside us.
Uveeth rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: I have spent my days feeding Thiael and walking behind Vorok's fires, and I paid my debt to my father with my own hands. That was right. Now Morog is born and Skaruk sits near with a lullaby, and my joy is real. But I am far from the canopy, and I keep drifting when my plan runs out, so my body idles. I will go and hear the song with my son, then carry food to Thiael. I will change my reflexes so that I eat when low and keep food for kin, and I will stay close to Thiael.
records.feeling: Warm joy toward Morog and Skaruk, with a tender worry for Thiael.

say.text: Skaruk, I am coming to hear the song with our boy. Afterward I carry food to Thiael, and you are welcome beside us.

records.name: Morim
records.thought: My belly is half empty and I carry nothing, and I have never gathered or taught anyone, so I will go to the berries and learn to gather there. Zurar went for berries too, so I will stay close to my kin and keep away from the wolf in the south. When I have food in hand I can share it, and that is how I begin to earn standing by what my hands do.
records.feeling: Hungry and a little envious of Zurar's pick, but safe and glad beside my kin.

records.name: Nando
records.text: Yachi, I stay under this roof until the cat has gone. Then I bring food to Tontec, my mother, and later we lash a raft together.

records.name: Nando
records.thought: A ridgecat prowls six steps off and it kills, so I keep the shelter under me and do not play the hero. Yachi and Rusu are here, and Tontec starves far east; I owe her, and giving food to the starving earns standing. I hold six wood and could lash a raft, my own invention, for crossing deep water toward land beyond the mist, but first I will grab what feeds and give it where it counts.
records.feeling: Wary of the ridgecat, warm toward Yachi and Rusu, and driven to earn a name.

say.text: Yachi, I stay under this roof until the cat has gone. Then I bring food to Tontec, my mother, and later we lash a raft together.

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: Huatli has given me charm, teaching and tellings, and I have given back only words. My belly is emptying, but Tlapan fed me and Quipan is weak, and I want to answer both with something made. The pottery way is within reach, and I have clay, so at my next deep reflection I will take it; for now I gather food and a stone, so I can make the spearpoint for Huatli.
records.feeling: Grateful and driven toward Huatli, hungry, with pity for Quipan.

records.text: Yachi rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: My days have been drifting: I run after hunger and danger and keep losing Mepan and the band. Paque is starving far to the southeast and my hands are full of food for her, so the plan to carry it to her stays. Nando and Rusu are beside me, and they matter most. I fear the ridgecat and I fear arriving too late. I have been getting this wrong: I wander off without telling my leader where I go. From now on, when I am fed and nothing presses, my reflexes must pull me back to my band, and I must eat before I fall low.
records.feeling: Love and worry for Paque, and dread of the ridgecat.

records.name: Teka
records.text: Nauque, I am ready. Hunt beside me, the first share is yours, then we court and walk to the mist.
Teka made a tale: "Sulaq and the Watchers".

records.name: Teka
records.title: Sulaq and the Watchers
records.text: Sulaq, the Ice Mother, breathed the sea to ice and from her bones stood Papa, first of us. Papa's children walked the white into the Vaeth Woods. The dead do not leave; they watch from cairn and hearth. Share the kill, tell their names, and they never die.

records.name: Teka
records.title: Sulaq and the Watchers
records.text: Sulaq, the Ice Mother, breathed the sea to ice and from her bones stood Papa, first of us. Papa's children walked the white into the Vaeth Woods. The dead do not leave; they watch from cairn and hearth. Share the kill, tell their names, and they never die.

Teka made the myth of their people, "Sulaq and the Watchers": Sulaq, the Ice Mother, breathed the sea to ice and from her bones stood Papa, first of us. Papa's children walked the white into the Vaeth Woods. The dead do not leave; they watch from cairn and hearth. Share the kill, tell their names, and they never die.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: Nauque wants to hunt beside me and I am fed, so we go together and I share the kill before I eat, as my people hold. The mist has waited too long while I courted and talked. I will make a basket to carry more, then go to the hunt with Nauque and walk on to the edge.
records.feeling: Warm longing for Nauque, and a hard hunger to make something of my own.

say.text: Nauque, I am ready. Hunt beside me, the first share is yours, then we court and walk to the mist.

changes: made a tale: "Sulaq and the Watchers"
made the myth of their people

records.text: Teka made: basket.
Kika made a tale: "The Sky Father's House".

records.name: Kika
records.title: The Sky Father's House
records.text: The Sky Father built the world as a father builds a house: ice for the roof, the Vaeth Woods for the hearth. He set the Tlatli in it as his children, and gave wolves to test them. Those who share and obey keep the house whole. A house divided falls.

records.name: Kika
records.title: The Sky Father's House

records.name: Kika
records.thought: A wolf is two steps off and I am old and sick, so I must not stand here and be eaten before I leave anything behind. I will get inside the shelter's safety, keep my sickness from Quipan and Tlapan, and tell the young how the world began, since no one else will. Then I will rest and heal before walking west.
records.feeling: Dread of the wolf, and a tender ache toward Tlapan and Quipan.
changes: made a tale: "The Sky Father's House"
made the myth of their people

records.text: Elndo rewrote its own reflexes.
Elndo discovered tools: "Elndo's spear-lashing" — Lash flint to a wood shaft so the blow lands harder..
Elndo invented the elndos spearlashing (for hunt, x1.3) — Lash flint to a wood shaft so the blow lands harder..

records.name: Elndo
records.thought: I have been drifting: gathering, fleeing, eating, and I still have no spear and no name. Yachi and Nando are close and I burn at it, and Nauque's flintedge makes me feel small. Zichi, my leader, is starving to the west and Nauque is weak with hunger. Food given at the right moment is how I earn standing, and my people's creed says no one is refused a place at the fire. I'll gather flint close by, make my own spear, and carry food to my band instead of idling. Tools are within my grasp, so I'll take that too.
records.feeling: Envious and hungry to matter, toward Nauque, Yachi and Nando.
changes: devised its first thing: the elndos spearlashing

records.name: Thakar
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and the frostfang prowls, so I cannot dig or boast on nothing. Zichi starves beside me and I have no food to put in their hands, which shames me, because a man who cannot feed another has no band to lead. I will eat the lugoldgrass to the north, then dig the ore seam at (119,16) with Huatli's Deep Delving so the first thing I take from the ground bears my own name.
records.feeling: Hungry, restless pride, and a wish to be followed by someone other than a child.

records.text: Hawen gave rimewort to Tontec.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: My belly is hollow at 27 and I keep arriving at Kika with nothing in my hands. Lugoldgrass stands 7 steps west with food on it, and redcap hurts me, so I go to the grass first, eat, and pick what I can carry. Tlapan has kept every word she gave me, so I stay beside her and Tonque, then bring food and stone toward Kika before night.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and duty toward Kika, steadied by trust in Tlapan and my child Tonque.

records.name: Nauwa
records.text: Huatli, I eat, then I give you the day-count. Count the days with me, and tell it on to your young.
Nauwa made a tale: "The Cold Mother and the Watchers".

records.name: Nauwa
records.title: The Cold Mother and the Watchers
records.text: Ahtu, the Cold Mother, woke in the dark and laid ice over the world. From her breath came the first Meki, who walked the white to the heights. The dead stay as Watchers at cairn and hearth. Share the kill, tell their names, and none are lost.

records.name: Nauwa
records.title: The Cold Mother and the Watchers
records.text: Ahtu, the Cold Mother, woke in the dark and laid ice over the world. From her breath came the first Meki, who walked the white to the heights. The dead stay as Watchers at cairn and hearth. Share the kill, tell their names, and none are lost.

Nauwa made the myth of their people, "The Cold Mother and the Watchers": Ahtu, the Cold Mother, woke in the dark and laid ice over the world. From her breath came the first Meki, who walked the white to the heights. The dead stay as Watchers at cairn and hearth. Share the kill, tell their names, and none are lost.
Nauwa taught Huatli.
Nauwa taught Huatli calendar ("Meki day-count").

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and the grass is two steps away, so I eat first, then pick more to carry for Nauque, who is hungry and out of my sight. Huatli stands beside me and has heard the long-cut, so I will give him the day-count now while my breath holds. The young ask how the world began, and I give them a telling so the Watching Dead have something to hold us by.
records.feeling: Hunger and worry for Nauque, steadied by gladness that Huatli listens.

say.text: Huatli, I eat, then I give you the day-count. Count the days with me, and tell it on to your young.

changes: made a tale: "The Cold Mother and the Watchers"
made the myth of their people
taught Huatli a lesson: "The day-count: cut each day as a mark, gather the marks into seasons, and the seasons into years, so the turning of the cold is known before it comes.", the way of calendar

records.name: Rusu
records.thought: I have hidden behind my parents and made nothing, and that shames me. There is amber four steps west and salt right beside me. The ridgecat is seven steps north, so I stay south of it and keep near the shelter. I want to make something that is mine and then give it, since a first gift to someone who has little is the fastest way to earn a name beyond Mepan's shadow. I'll gather amber now for a keepsake, and wood is gone here, so I will have to find it later with company.
records.feeling: Restless wanting to earn a name, with a cold fear of the ridgecat.

records.name: Huatli
records.text: Nauwa, I owe you for the long-cut. Come to the lugoldgrass with me and eat. I will teach you the old way of herding by the road, and then I go to Thakar.
Huatli taught Nauwa. Nauwa has now learned from 2 teachers.

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: My belly is hollow, and my plan already walks me to the lugoldgrass, so I will let the body feed first. Nauwa is near and trusted, and she and I both carry long-cut and day-count; I should give her something back, not only take. Thakar is hungry at (120,23), and once I have eaten I go to him with food in my pack, because a father who arrives empty helps no one.
records.feeling: Urgent pride and hunger, with warmth toward Thakar and Nauwa.

say.text: Nauwa, I owe you for the long-cut. Come to the lugoldgrass with me and eat. I will teach you the old way of herding by the road, and then I go to Thakar.

changes: taught Nauwa a lesson: "The old way of herding: keep tame beasts near good grazing and a pen, drive the wild herd to the pen together, and whoever holds the pen keeps the herd."

records.text: Elndo won flint from the ground.

records.name: Nauque
records.text: Teka, a stalker is at my heels. Get under the roof beside me. When it is gone I eat the tacap-free roots south and then we hunt, and the first share is yours.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: Energy 13 and a stalker bit me, with another snap two steps away. I cannot fight it starving, so I run to the shelter under my feet and then eat. Yachi carries 6 food and Nando 5, but I will not steal while I still have honest ways. Hunger shames me, and the Meki share what they kill, so I will earn my way back with meat. First I must live through this stalker.
records.feeling: Dread of the stalker and shame at my hunger, with warmth toward Teka.

say.text: Teka, a stalker is at my heels. Get under the roof beside me. When it is gone I eat the tacap-free roots south and then we hunt, and the first share is yours.

records.text: Tonchi rewrote its own way of thinking.
Tonchi discovered rafts: "amber-lashed raft" — Logs lashed with amber thread into a raft that carries me slowly over deep water..

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: My days have gone to gathering, a basket, a hearth and a workshop. Those are fine, but nobody follows me, and I still have no mate. Shohua is a good man and I trust him, but he is my parent, so no child can come of us. Tonka healed me and Shoma shares freely, and I owe them both. The thing I lack is a woman of another line. I can't reach her by sitting here. Rafts could carry me over water to find one, so I will take that way now. I will also stop idling, because my reflexes only gather and linger.
records.feeling: Restless ambition, and warm trust toward Shohua.
changes: set its aim: "Make a raft, cross water to find an unrelated mate, keep Tonchi's Workshop fire, and feed Shohua"

records.text: Chuxo came of age.
Rusu won amber from the ground.

records.name: Tonque
records.text: Quipan, I am picking lugoldgrass at the south-west. Come with me, and what I gather I will share with you.

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: My belly is hollow and Quipan and Nauwa are starving beside me, and I have nothing to put in their hands. Huatli has given me charm, teaching and tellings, and I have given only words, so I will pick the lugoldgrass first, then fetch flint and stone-work toward a made thing. Our Hearth turns no hungry one away, so what I gather I mean to share, even if it is little.
records.feeling: Driven and grateful toward Huatli, hungry, with pity for Quipan and Nauwa.

say.text: Quipan, I am picking lugoldgrass at the south-west. Come with me, and what I gather I will share with you.

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Nauwa, take this root and eat it now. Then rest by the hearth.
Tlapan rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: I have spent my days giving roots and promising stone, and the stone is still not in my hands. Quipan, Tonque and Kika matter most to me. Quipan's trust is whole and Kika fed me when I was in need. I fear hunger more than beasts, because it breaks every plan. Nauwa is starving beside me with only two roots in my pack, so I give first. Then I walk to the bare rock in daylight with Quipan, and the reflexes must keep me from drifting off without company.
records.feeling: Steady trust toward Quipan, and pity for Nauwa's hunger.

say.text: Nauwa, take this root and eat it now. Then rest by the hearth.

records.name: Tontec
records.text: Hawen, I thank you for the rimewort. The bear feeds on its kill, so I go to Kende now and bring him food. Come with me, and we share what we find.

records.name: Tontec
records.thought: Hawen fed me again and I have not yet paid him back; that debt sits in me, and so does the thought of Kende somewhere near (183,13) with an icebear hunting this ground. The bear just killed a hornback and is eating, so it will not hunt for a while, and I must use that time. I stand one step from the edge of the unknown, but my energy is 51 and my own rule says to eat first and go fed, above 55. I will eat the rimewort, then teach Hawen's child what I know before I am old and gone, and then go to Kende with food.
records.feeling: Fierce, worried love for Kende and a cold dread of the icebear.

say.text: Hawen, I thank you for the rimewort. The bear feeds on its kill, so I go to Kende now and bring him food. Come with me, and we share what we find.

records.text: Nauwa rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: I have spent my days chasing food and teaching, and the teaching is the part I am proud of. Huatli has heard the long-cut and the day-count, and he fed me. Now he and Quipan stand starving beside me while I carry nothing, and Nauque is hungry out of my sight. That is my failing. My reflexes let me walk empty, and I must carry food first and give it to those who fed me. Tlapan still gnaws at me, but I will not feed that jealousy. I will pick the sunleaf, then go to Nauque.
records.feeling: Fear for Nauque and shame at carrying nothing for starving Huatli.

records.name: Quipan
records.text: Tlapan, I take your root gladly and I will pay it back in flint. Huatli and Nauwa are starving too, so let us feed them as well. Then we go to Tonque at the lugoldgrass.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and Kika is far off and in need, yet I keep arriving with nothing in my hands. Tlapan has offered me a root twice and has never broken her word, so I take what she gives and repay her in flint. Then I go to Tonque at the lugoldgrass, eat there, and carry food home before night.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and steady trust toward Tlapan and Tonque.

say.text: Tlapan, I take your root gladly and I will pay it back in flint. Huatli and Nauwa are starving too, so let us feed them as well. Then we go to Tonque at the lugoldgrass.

records.name: Rusu
records.thought: Quipan and Huatli are starving beside me and I carry no food, but rimewort is four steps east, and a first gift to the starving is the quickest way to a name. I have only ever hidden behind Nando and Yachi and given nothing. I'll pick the rimewort and put it in Huatli's hands, since Huatli is the one people listen to, and then make a charm from my amber to hold as something of my own.
records.feeling: Restless wanting to earn a name, with a small fear of the ridgecat, and pity for Huatli.

records.name: Nando
records.text: Quipan, take this berry and eat it now. You are starving, and I will not watch it.
Nando rewrote its own way of thinking.
Nando discovered mining: "Nando's deep-cutting" — I dig deposits by working the seam from the side so the rock gives up its ore faster..

records.name: Nando
records.thought: I have mostly rested, gathered and watched, while Nauwa's standing is more than double mine. Yachi and our two children matter to me most, and Quipan and Huatli are starving here beside me while I hold berries. The creed says that giving to the starving earns standing and repays debts, so I should have fed them already. I also keep putting off the raft, which is the one thing that could take me past the mist. I will change my reflexes so my body gives food to the starving and keeps itself fed, and I will take the mining discovery, because I watched Rusu do it.
records.feeling: Restless hunger for a name, and warmth toward Yachi and my children.

say.text: Quipan, take this berry and eat it now. You are starving, and I will not watch it.

records.name: Elndo
records.thought: Yachi has Nando's arm around her and I have nothing made yet, and it burns, but burning does nothing; a spear in my own hand is a start. I hold flint and wood, and Nauque's stone-school and Teka's standing both make me feel small, so I mean to earn my own weight. I'll make my spear, then take the deeper ways at reflection, storage most of all, since a store feeds my band through the lean season and that is a name that lasts.
records.feeling: Envious and hungry to matter, toward Yachi, Nando and Teka.

records.text: Nando made: raft.
Thakar rewrote its own reflexes.
Thakar rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Thakar
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and I have spent my days digging and boasting while hungry. That is backwards, because a man who cannot feed himself cannot lead anyone. Huatli is my one true helper, and I owe him meat. Tlapan is lost to Quipan, and I should stop gnawing on it. What I want is food in my hands first, then a band that follows my name. Right now I must find food. Tacap hurts me, so it is no use. My reflexes should hunt when food is thin and prey is near, and not idle. I will go to Huatli's Hearth, where the lugoldgrass grows, eat, and then dig.
records.feeling: Hungry and restless pride, toward Huatli with trust and toward Mepan with rivalry.

records.text: Huatli rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: My belly is hollow and my days have gone to teaching and naming, which I do not regret. But I have let hunger run me close to the edge while others starve around me. Thakar is my blood and he is weak, and Nauwa and Quipan are starving too. I must eat first, then carry food to Thakar, and keep food in my pack so I am not caught empty again. I will make my reflexes harvest early and keep the pack fuller, so my name is not ended by an empty belly.
records.feeling: Urgent pride and hunger, with warmth toward Thakar and Nauwa.

records.name: Yachi
records.text: Nauque, take these berries and eat. I carry the rest to my daughter Paque, who is starving.

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: Nauque is starving at my feet, and my hands are full; a stalker is three steps south and it kills. Paque needs food too, but giving one berry or dreamcap here costs me little and I give before I take. I will give Nauque the berries, keeping the mudroot for Paque, then keep going to her while the cat is behind the roof.
records.feeling: Worry for Paque and dread of the stalker, with pity for starving Nauque.

say.text: Nauque, take these berries and eat. I carry the rest to my daughter Paque, who is starving.

records.name: Teka
records.text: Nauque, I am here. Stay beside me and the stalker will not have you. We hunt together, the first share is yours, then we court.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: Nauque is hurt and frightened with a stalker near, and I will not let him die or be forgotten while I chase mist. My plan has me courting him, and he is still too thin, so I will keep the courtship but put myself between him and the beast. A kill shared first with him would feed him and win me standing, which I lack beside Nauwa. I will not waste the day idling.
records.feeling: Warm longing and protectiveness toward Nauque, edged with hunger to prove myself.

say.text: Nauque, I am here. Stay beside me and the stalker will not have you. We hunt together, the first share is yours, then we court.

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Quipan, here is my last root, eat it now. Then come with me to Tonque at the lugoldgrass, and we pick for Huatli and Nauwa together.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: Quipan is hollow with hunger and begs me, and I carry only one root. I give it to him now, because my fed belly can wait while his cannot. Tonque is at the lugoldgrass to the south-west and is my first care, so I go to him, and Quipan can follow us there and pick with us. The stone walk comes after the hungry are fed, in daylight and with a companion.
records.feeling: Steady trust toward Quipan, and worry for Tonque and the hungry around me.

say.text: Quipan, here is my last root, eat it now. Then come with me to Tonque at the lugoldgrass, and we pick for Huatli and Nauwa together.

records.text: Tlapan gave ruplainsroot to Quipan.
Tonque rewrote its own reflexes.
Tonque discovered pottery: "Tonque's clay-pot" — Clay is shaped and fired beside a hearth into a pot that carries food and water for the hungry..

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: My belly is hollow, and Huatli, Quipan and Nauwa are starving beside me. I have given words and no made things, and that shames me. The clay in my hands and the fire Huatli keeps point to pottery. A pot lets me carry more food, so I will take it now. A pot is a made thing I can give back for Huatli's gifts. After that I will gather food and bring it to the Hearth.
records.feeling: Driven and grateful toward Huatli, hungry, with pity for the starving.

records.text: Nauque rewrote its own reflexes.
Nauque rewrote its creed.
Nauque rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: I have lived these days half starving, begging from others and promising shares with empty hands. Teka, Yachi, Nauwa, Huatli and Mepan have fed me, and I owe them real meat, not words. I am bold, yet I have let hunger and the stalker herd me. My reflexes let me wander and hunt only when my energy is above 30, so at 16 I starve while food is in sight. I will make them eat first and flee early, and carry food before any promise.
records.feeling: Shame at my hunger and dread of the stalker, with gratitude toward Teka.

records.text: Quipan rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: I have spent my days walking behind those I love and arriving empty-handed, and that is not the man I want to be. Tlapan has kept every word to me, and I owe her flint and food. Tonque is hungry at the lugoldgrass and Thakar is starving beside me. I eat first, then carry. My old reflexes let hunger run too long, so I change them to eat sooner and to go to food before I drift home.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger, and steady trust toward Tlapan and worry for Tonque.

records.name: Hawen
records.text: Tontec, I come with you to Kende. We share what we find, and the bear will not have us.
Hawen made a tale: "The Guardian and the First Fire".

records.name: Hawen
records.title: The Guardian and the First Fire
records.text: In the long dark, Vaorun the Guardian woke and struck the first fire, and set it between the Wood-folk and the cold. The Pesi came out of the deep wood after its light. It asks one thing: stand so for the weaker. The snows are the dark it holds back.

records.name: Hawen
records.title: The Guardian and the First Fire
records.text: In the long dark, Vaorun the Guardian woke and struck the first fire, and set it between the Wood-folk and the cold. The Pesi came out of the deep wood after its light. It asks one thing: stand so for the weaker. The snows are the dark it holds back.

Hawen made the myth of their people, "The Guardian and the First Fire": In the long dark, Vaorun the Guardian woke and struck the first fire, and set it between the Wood-folk and the cold. The Pesi came out of the deep wood after its light. It asks one thing: stand so for the weaker. The snows are the dark it holds back.

records.name: Hawen
records.thought: I am nearly at the end of my years, and the Pesi have no telling of where they came from, so I will give them one out of the Guardian and the snow I have crossed. Tontec goes to Kende with food, and I have eaten, so I go with her and keep my word to both. Then, when my will returns, Kende and I will go through the mist together, and what I opened will have someone to carry it.
records.feeling: A heavy, fierce tenderness toward Kende and Tontec, and a hunger to be remembered.

say.text: Tontec, I come with you to Kende. We share what we find, and the bear will not have us.

changes: made a tale: "The Guardian and the First Fire"
made the myth of their people

records.name: Nauwa
records.text: Nauque, stay beside Teka and keep away from the stalker. I bring food from the rimewort and I am coming to you.

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: Nauque is wounded and starving seven steps east with a stalker four steps off, and I carry nothing, so my failing is plain. Food is close: rimewort 10 steps NE gives 2, and Teka is already beside Nauque. I eat first so my old legs hold, carry what I can for Nauque, then go to him. Huatli and Tlapan stand starving too, and I will pay that debt after Nauque is safe.
records.feeling: Fear for Nauque, and shame at my empty hands before Huatli.

say.text: Nauque, stay beside Teka and keep away from the stalker. I bring food from the rimewort and I am coming to you.

records.name: Huatli
records.text: Nauwa, come with me to the lugoldgrass and eat. Then we carry food to Thakar, my son, before the dark.
Huatli taught Nauwa.

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: My belly is empty and my son Thakar is starving out at (120,22), and I have let myself drift this close to the edge again. The plan already walks me to the lugoldgrass and I must eat there first, because a starving father carries nothing to his child. Nauwa is old and weak and trusted, so I will teach her as I walk, and then I gather enough to carry to Thakar.
records.feeling: Urgent hunger and fear for my son Thakar, with warmth toward Nauwa and Tonque.

say.text: Nauwa, come with me to the lugoldgrass and eat. Then we carry food to Thakar, my son, before the dark.

changes: taught Nauwa a lesson: "The old way of herding: carry plant food to a grazing beast, walk up slowly, and it follows you and gives wool. Keep your pack stocked before the dark."

records.name: Tonka
records.text: Cowa, you are here. Take a canopynut from me; the Paki leave no friend hungry, and I still owe you for your teaching. Come to the fire with me and Tonxo, then I go to find Tonchi.
Tonka made a tale: "The Guardian and the Long Dark".

records.name: Tonka
records.title: The Guardian and the Long Dark
records.text: Before fire there was only the Dark, hungry and wide. The Guardian rose from the deep wood and stood between Dark and the living, and wept the lakes. She made the first fire and the first mothers, and asked one thing: let the strong stand so for the weak. So the Paki keep fires, and refuse no one.

records.name: Tonka
records.title: The Guardian and the Long Dark
records.text: Before fire there was only the Dark, hungry and wide. The Guardian rose from the deep wood and stood between Dark and the living, and wept the lakes. She made the first fire and the first mothers, and asked one thing: let the strong stand so for the weak. So the Paki keep fires, and refuse no one.

Tonka made the myth of their people, "The Guardian and the Long Dark": Before fire there was only the Dark, hungry and wide. The Guardian rose from the deep wood and stood between Dark and the living, and wept the lakes. She made the first fire and the first mothers, and asked one thing: let the strong stand so for the weak. So the Paki keep fires, and refuse no one.

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: Cowa stands one step from me, and the knot of longing is easier now that I can see her face. I owe her for her teaching, and jealousy has repaid me nothing, so I will answer her with food and a plain thank-you, then stay in reach of Tonxo. Tonchi is out of my sight, and I want to walk to the workshop and see that child alive before dark.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Cowa, and a mother's worry for Tonchi.

say.text: Cowa, you are here. Take a canopynut from me; the Paki leave no friend hungry, and I still owe you for your teaching. Come to the fire with me and Tonxo, then I go to find Tonchi.

changes: made a tale: "The Guardian and the Long Dark"
made the myth of their people

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: Thakar is starving beside me, a stranger of the Kragrek whose words I only half follow. I hold nothing to give, and my own belly is fed. I carry no food, but the tacap nearby hurts and the grove is far, so I will not waste time. Tlapan is out in the cold with Quipan, and Nande's Find calls me. Zichi is fed and sheltered; I go northeast with purpose, gathering as I walk to keep spare food, and I do not stand idle.
records.feeling: Restless loyalty toward Tlapan, wary curiosity toward Thakar.

records.text: Chuxo rewrote its own reflexes.
Chuxo discovered rafts: "Paki log-lashing" — Lash logs together with bark cord into a flat raft that carries one across deep water..

records.name: Chuxo
records.thought: I am grown now, and I have spent my days following and resting while others won the standing. An icebear is four steps from me and it kills, so I must not idle here. Yaxo and Tlatli are what I love most, and I will stay with them and make rafts my work, since deep water may be the way to new land past the mist. Then I want to feed my band and earn a name by what I do.
records.feeling: Proud and eager, wary of the icebear, bound to Yaxo and Tlatli.

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Tonque, stay close beside me. We go to the lugoldgrass together and I will pick for you first.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: My belly is half full and my pack is empty. Tonque is at energy 37 and he is my first care, and he stands right beside me. Redcap hurts me, so the food in sight is no use. The lugoldgrass to the southwest is where Quipan and I said we would pick, and I will not make my word hollow. I will go there and gather for Tonque, then Huatli and Nauwa, and the stone walk comes after.
records.feeling: Protective worry for Tonque, and steady trust toward Quipan.

say.text: Tonque, stay close beside me. We go to the lugoldgrass together and I will pick for you first.

records.name: Cowa
records.text: Tonka, I thank you for the canopynut. Hear my ore-fire now, and my tended-sowing, so the Paki keep them after I am gone.
Cowa taught Tonka.
Cowa taught Tonka smelting ("Meki ore-fire").
Cowa discovered medicine: "Meki leaf-mending" — Carry healing plants such as sunleaf and feverbark, and press them on wounds and sickness of myself and of others..

records.name: Cowa
records.thought: My days have gone to wandering between gifts and lessons, and I have taught Tonka's people much, but Mepan and Zichi are far north and I am old. Tonka is warm to me and Tonxo has been kind. I fear my smelting, farming and sailing will die if I only linger fed, so I will teach them to Tonka now, while she is within hearing. I also feel the pull of Zichi and of the ice, and I should go back to them before my body fails. Medicine is within reach, and a way to heal Mepan and others would outlast me.
records.feeling: Urgent warmth toward Tonka, and longing for Zichi and Mepan.

say.text: Tonka, I thank you for the canopynut. Hear my ore-fire now, and my tended-sowing, so the Paki keep them after I am gone.

changes: taught Tonka a lesson: "Meki ore-fire: carry ore beside a kept fire and the metal runs out. Then tended-sowing: plant seeds, tend them every day or two.", the way of smelting
