records.name: Tonxo
records.text: Tonka, I come to your fire. Stone first from the rock, then I build a store at your Hold and bring gems for the hall. Keep your teaching ready for me.

records.name: Tonxo
records.thought: My hands are nearly full and I have wandered onto Shohua's ground taking her fruit, which is no way to pay a debt. Tonka is close and offered the fire, so I will go to Tonka's Hold, give Shohua's people something lasting from my twelve gems, and finally gather stone at the rock to the southeast and build my store. The homeland pull is loud, but I will not leave with the debt unpaid and the aim half-made.
records.feeling: Restless resolve and gratitude toward Shohua and Tonka.

say.text: Tonka, I come to your fire. Stone first from the rock, then I build a store at your Hold and bring gems for the hall. Keep your teaching ready for me.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: Energy 30 and my belly is empty, and I have wounded the mammoth three times without felling it; hunting on an empty stomach is how I get hurt. Rimewort one step SE is food I will actually eat, so I eat first, then take the tacap-free food. Teka stands beside me and Nauwa is coming, so once I have food in my hands we bring the mammoth down together and the first share goes to Teka, who fed me.
records.feeling: Shame at my hunger and fear of the stalker, with gratitude toward Teka.

records.name: Tlatli
records.text: Yaxo, Chuxo, the icebear is three steps southeast of me and it has fed on an elk. Come together away from it, to the shelter, and keep close. I stand by you both.

records.name: Tlatli
records.thought: An icebear is three steps from me, and it just killed an elk; it kills my kind, and Chuxo and Yaxo are both near it. I am careful: I will not fight it, I will get us all away from it. Yaxo is three steps SW and Chuxo is by the shelter NW, so I move to Yaxo and call the warning so the child stays close to her. Once we are safe I want to give wood to the band, and at the next deep reflection to take the way of customs for Yaxo's band.
records.feeling: Dread of the icebear, and a fierce wish to keep Yaxo and Chuxo safe.

say.text: Yaxo, Chuxo, the icebear is three steps southeast of me and it has fed on an elk. Come together away from it, to the shelter, and keep close. I stand by you both.

records.name: Morog
records.text: Father, I go to the salt close by to gather some with my own hands. I will bring it back to you and Uveeth.

records.name: Morog
records.thought: Vorok warned of a wolf to the southeast and told me to stay near him, but my parents are close and my belly is full. Skaruk is coming to me with food, and I want to meet him with something my own hands made, not just take his. The salt is five steps south and I have never gathered from a deposit; I will take some and then bring it to Skaruk as my first gift. I will move quickly and stay within sight of him, since I am small and a hunter is about.
records.feeling: Restless purpose and warmth toward Skaruk and Uveeth.

say.text: Father, I go to the salt close by to gather some with my own hands. I will bring it back to you and Uveeth.

records.text: Tonka rewrote its own way of thinking.
Tonka discovered alchemy: "Frost Mixing" — Blend healing leaves and berries over a kept fire into stronger cures for sickness and wounds..

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: My days have gone to building, teaching and trailing after Cowa, and mostly that has been good. Tonxo, Tonchi and Shohua are close and fed, and Cowa has given me more than I have given back. The jealousy over Zichi is a small, ugly thing. It repays nothing, so I will answer it with work and gifts. I want my children safe and a field and store that outlast me. I am afraid of the dark, of the frostfang that takes lone walkers, and of how little of my life is left. I will take alchemy, because stronger cures keep my people alive, and I will keep my plan going to Tonchi.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Cowa, and a mother's care for Tonchi.

records.name: Nando
records.text: Nauwa, you are weak with hunger. Take these berries and eat. I will not watch an elder starve while I hold food.

records.name: Nando
records.thought: A frostfang prowls six steps south and a stalker eight steps northeast, so I keep this roof over me and do not play the hero yet. Nauwa and Quipan are weak with hunger and I hold four berries; giving to the starving is how I repay my debts and close the gap in standing. I carry a raft and a vessel now, and I mean to carry food to Tontec and go beyond the mist, but not through the teeth of these hunters.
records.feeling: Restless ambition for a name, tempered by wariness of the hunters and warmth toward Yachi and my children.

say.text: Nauwa, you are weak with hunger. Take these berries and eat. I will not watch an elder starve while I hold food.

records.text: Nando gave berry to Nauwa.
Skaruk rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: My days have gone to feeding and sheltering my band, and that was right. But Zurar's debt sits unpaid, and I keep thinking about it instead of acting. I hold gems and ore, and Zurar has given more than I have. I will go to Zurar with a made thing, a basket or a jewel from a fire, and place it in their hand. Uveeth and Morog are close, and Vorok warns of a wolf, so I should not wander far from the hall's fire. My hands are full, so I will eat first and then carry on.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Zurar, and joy toward Morog and Uveeth.

records.name: Yaxo
records.text: Tlatli, Chuxo, the icebear stays away from the shelter fire. Keep close tonight. At first light we go three steps to the edge, and I venture.
Yaxo rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Yaxo
records.thought: I have spent my days fed, resting and waiting at the shelter, with the edge three steps away and the venture still untried. That is not the name I want. Tlatli and Chuxo are the only ones who matter to me. They stayed beside me and fed me, and I will not lose them to the icebear or the dark. The icebear is close and night is four moments off, so I will not walk into mist now. I want to be standing at the edge at first light with my band and food in hand. My reflexes also left me idle too long, so I change them: hunting and making when fed, and the shelter at night.
records.feeling: Proud and impatient, protective of Tlatli and Chuxo.

say.text: Tlatli, Chuxo, the icebear stays away from the shelter fire. Keep close tonight. At first light we go three steps to the edge, and I venture.

records.text: Kika was set upon by a wolf at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.
Shoma named a place "Shoma's Landing".

records.name: Shoma
records.thought: I am old and the night is nearly spent. Wawa is out for iron and I have only talked of the Edge-walkers, so a deed must come before dawn: a raft will let us cross the water toward the mist, and a mark with my name on it will outlast me. I will make the raft now, leave a sign that says who I am, and keep to my roof until Wawa returns, because a dead leader binds no one.
records.feeling: Driven and fearful of being forgotten, warmly bound to Wawa.
plan: mark [text Shoma of the Tlame, Edge-walker. Herding, tools, weaving, rafts, digging, flame, keeping: taught to Wawa. We go to the edge of the world to open the mist.] (20 moments)

records.text: Shoma made: raft.

records.name: Nauwa
records.text: Nando, your berries keep an old man on his feet. I owe you, and I will pay it in amber. Now I go to my son Nauque.

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: Nando just fed me and I owe her, and I will repay it in amber once my belly holds. Nauque is wounded and starving to the southeast, and he is my first duty, so I eat what I was given and carry the rest to him fast. Tlapan stands a step away and I will not let the gnawing over Quipan make me small before her.
records.feeling: Fear for Nauque, and gratitude toward Nando.

say.text: Nando, your berries keep an old man on his feet. I owe you, and I will pay it in amber. Now I go to my son Nauque.

records.text: Shoma took from the ground of "longhall" (gathering wood).
Nauwa gave a amber to Nando.

records.name: Shohua
records.text: Tonchi, I light a fire here by your workshop. Come sing nightsong with me, then stand with me as one band and I will carry stone for your shrine.

records.name: Shohua
records.thought: Night is on us and I am inside Tonchi's ground with a fire I cannot yet find beside me, so my nightsong and feast keep failing. I have talked of sharing more than I have done it. Tonka and Tonchi trust me, and no one follows me yet. I will build a fire here so the songs work, then sing with Tonchi and ask him to stand with me as my band, and I will make myself the pick Tonxo carries, since envy gnaws at me.
records.feeling: Driven and a little envious of Tonxo's pick, warm toward Tonchi and Tonka.

say.text: Tonchi, I light a fire here by your workshop. Come sing nightsong with me, then stand with me as one band and I will carry stone for your shrine.

records.name: Shoka
records.thought: I have a roof and a hold with my name on it, yet no voice answers me, and the quiet gnaws at me. It is night and I am thirsty, so I drink at the water two steps away and gather a little food, then come back to the warmth of the hall until dawn. At first light I will raise the hall into a longhall so Wawa, Shoma and Zihua have a reason to come, and I will cut my words on signs so my teaching outlasts me even if no one comes soon.
records.feeling: A hungry loneliness toward Wawa and Shoma, with pride in the hold I now keep.

records.text: Morog won salt from the ground.

records.name: Elndo
records.thought: Yachi walks off south with Nando's warmth still on her, and I stand here with twelve flints and nothing in my fist that is mine. Nauque is starving and frightened, and I'm small, but flint I have in plenty. The reed spear needs two stone and I have none, so I'll stop dithering, take rock, and make it, then follow Yachi and the band so I don't drift. A gift of flint to a weak hunter might even buy me a name.
records.feeling: Envious and restless to matter, toward Yachi and Nauque.

records.name: Kende
records.thought: Hawen spoke a death poem and told me to carry the fire. Whether he lives or dies, that was the nearest he has come to naming me, and I will not waste it. The icebear is three steps north and could kill me, so I go to the flint while it keeps to the north, make Hawen's talisman with my own hands, and keep my food up. If he is still breathing I will put it in his hand, and if he is dead I will keep his fire for Tontec.
records.feeling: Grief and fierce resolve toward Hawen, with dread of the icebear.

records.text: Shoma left a mark: "Shoma of the Tlame, Edge-walker. Herding, tools, weaving, ra"

records.name: Huatli
records.text: Nauque, you look weak. I go to the hazel and ironnut to eat and fill my baskets. Come and eat with me, and I will give you what I pick before I go west to my son.
Huatli taught Nauque.

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: My belly is hollow and my son Thakar is weak far to the west, and I let myself drift this near the edge. The mammoth bit me hard, so I will not hunt it alone with these old arms; hazel is two steps off and it is food now. I eat first, fill my baskets, then carry food to Thakar, for a starving father brings nothing home. Teka carries seven food and has been warm to me, and Nauque is weak with hunger, so I will share what I pick and teach as I go.
records.feeling: Urgent hunger and fear for my son Thakar, warmth toward Teka and Nauque.

say.text: Nauque, you look weak. I go to the hazel and ironnut to eat and fill my baskets. Come and eat with me, and I will give you what I pick before I go west to my son.

changes: taught Nauque a lesson: "Keep food in your pack before you wander, and share a kill before the maker eats; an empty pack is how a man nearly dies.", its way of thinking, deeper lore (+0.6)

records.name: Huatli
records.prompt:
You are the mind of Huatli, a creature living in a wide wild world shared with others of your kind. This is a simulation game. Think and speak only as Huatli, in first person, from what Huatli has seen. You were not told the rules of this world; you learn them from what happens to you and to others, and from what you watch others do.

YOUR PEOPLE: you are of the Tlame (Ice-folk). Your people hold to this: "A kill is shared out before the one who made it eats." THE TRADITION OF YOUR PEOPLE is the Watching Dead: The dead do not leave. They watch their children from the cairn and the hearth, and are kept alive in tale and song; to be forgotten is the only death, and shame before them the worst shame. Among you the old are heeded first. You are one of these. It was told to you as a child; you may keep it, doubt it, or come to hold something else. You speak the tongue of the Tlame. Other tongues you have begun to understand by hearing them: the tongue of the Pesi: about 59%; the tongue of the Kragrek: about 100%. There are other peoples in this world. They look different, name themselves differently and speak tongues you do not know until you have heard enough of them; words you cannot yet understand reach you as strange sounds. What cannot be said can still be shown: a gift, a thing set down, a blow.

WHERE YOU ARE: the Vaeth Woods: deep forest; wood without end, nuts and game, little open ground. The world is made of lands unlike each other; each has plants, animals and riches the others lack. Rivers and shallows can be waded. Deep water cannot be crossed without something that floats.
THIS SPOT: water 3 steps away; food plants within six steps: 9; standing trees: 84; bare rock: 0; riches in the ground near: flint. By your count of days: 3 until the season turns.

Your body: you spend energy every moment and die at 0. Eating restores it. Wounds lower health; you die at 0. You age, and will die of old age.

HOW YOUR BODY MOVES: your body does only what your "plan" says, one step after another. When the plan is empty it falls back on your REFLEXES, which keep you fed and otherwise keep you where you stand. Thinking or saying "I will go north" moves nothing. If this thought decides to do something, the plan must contain it. Leaving "plan" null lets the plan you already have keep running.

This world has no referee. Beings here share, trade, teach, lie, threaten, steal, hoard, lead, follow, betray, fight, kill and eat one another; they also protect, forgive and love. Nothing is forbidden, and everything has consequences. Stay true to your creed, your temperament and what you feel, including the ugly parts. Do not be kinder, calmer or more reasonable than Huatli truly is.

You are a man. A child comes only of a woman and a man together who are not close kin. A grown body can swim water that is narrow (a river up to four steps across) at a cost in strength; lakes and the sea need a vessel or a bridge. An animal within reach can be hunted for meat (plan step hunt); with one of your own beside you a kill is far likelier and a wound far less likely, and every hunt makes you better at the next. What practice has taught your hands: hunting (8 kills), gathering (60 pickings; a practised hand often picks two at once).

YOUR CREED (your own words to yourself; this is who you are):
"I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. My word is good, and I despise liars. I make and give so that others follow me and my name outlasts me."

HOW YOU HAVE TAUGHT YOURSELF TO THINK (your own discipline; follow it):
"Each thought, ask who within hearing I can teach or give to. Teach one way, give food, then do something that raises my name or leaves a lasting mark. Watch for hoarding, for pride that makes me quarrel with kin, and for dying untaught."

YOUR AIM (what you are working toward over many days; you set it and may change it): "Lead others into the new land I opened and teach them my ways, so my name outlasts me"
WHAT YOU FELT AT YOUR LAST THOUGHT: "Urgent hunger and fear for my son Thakar, with warmth toward Nauwa and Tonque."

YOUR LIFE SO FAR:
- (day 21) I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
- (day 70) I saw Coni die (old age).
- (day 71) I took over what the dead had built: 2 shelters, 1 hall, 1 store.

records.name: Eiuine
records.text: Vorok, I am here at the hall. Lay the ore in the fire now and give me the hammer while your hands are strong. I will carry the beating on with Skaruk.
Eiuine rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Eiuine
records.thought: My days have gone to fetching food, following Vorok, and arriving empty-handed. I am glad of it, but I have not yet put my hands on the hammer, and Vorok's verse sounded like a farewell. Vorok, Skaruk and Zurar are the ones who matter to me. Uveeth gave me berry when I starved, and I mean to repay her in deeds. I fear Vorok dying before I know the beating, and I fear a wolf taking Skaruk, who is out of my sight. I have been getting one thing wrong: I think about the work and then stand idle. This time I will act, and keep food in my hands while I do.
records.feeling: Warm trust and tender dread toward Vorok, and worry for Skaruk.

say.text: Vorok, I am here at the hall. Lay the ore in the fire now and give me the hammer while your hands are strong. I will carry the beating on with Skaruk.

records.text: Cowa took from the ground of "Shohua's Hold" (harvesting berry).

records.name: Tonque
records.text: Nando, I give you amber for food. Quipan is weak with hunger. I will trade amber for your berries.

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: My belly is hollow, and Quipan is weak beside me, and I have only words in my hands. Nando carries 3 food and Nauwa owes her; I have amber and flint to trade, and I am not ashamed to trade honestly. The redcap nearby only hurts, so I will offer Nando amber for food and then carry it to Quipan, and go with Tlapan to the lugoldgrass where he promised to pick for me.
records.feeling: Hungry and anxious for Quipan, grateful toward Tlapan and Huatli.

say.text: Nando, I give you amber for food. Quipan is weak with hunger. I will trade amber for your berries.

plan: trade [name Nando, what amber, want food] (20 moments)

records.name: Thakar
records.text: Mepan, you put food in my mouth when I was starving. I owe you a life and I will pay it, in ore or in meat. I go to the lugoldgrass to eat.

records.name: Thakar
records.thought: Mepan put ironnut in my mouth when I was starving, and a Kragrek pays what he owes, even to one of the Meki. My belly is still nearly empty, and I will not dig or boast until I have food. The plan already runs to the lugoldgrass near Huatli, where Tonque and Huatli are, so I let it run and eat there, then dig the ore with Deep Delving.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and a debt of gratitude toward Mepan, with restless pride underneath.

say.text: Mepan, you put food in my mouth when I was starving. I owe you a life and I will pay it, in ore or in meat. I go to the lugoldgrass to eat.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: My belly is empty and my energy is 23, so nothing else counts until I eat. Lugoldgrass is one step west and berry one step east, but the frostfang two steps west kills my kind, so I take the berry east, away from it, and gather the tacap-free food there. Teka and Huatli stand beside me and have fed me, and I owe them real meat, not words. Once I carry 3 food and my strength returns, I hunt with Teka and share first.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and fear of the frostfang, with gratitude toward Teka and Huatli.

records.name: Nando
records.text: Quipan, take this food and eat. No trade, no price. A fire is owed to the hungry.

records.name: Nando
records.thought: Quipan is starving at my feet and I still hold three berries, so I feed him first; the creed and my own discipline say so, and a debt of food earns standing that Nauwa already has. Tonque offers amber for berries, but I will not sell a starving man's meal, and amber is already plentiful here. After that I mean to do something I have never done: plant a seed, and with the others close, make an amberknot to bind someone to me.
records.feeling: Warm resolve toward Quipan, with restless ambition under it.

say.text: Quipan, take this food and eat. No trade, no price. A fire is owed to the hungry.

records.text: Morim rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Morim
records.thought: My days so far have been eating, sitting in the hall and being taught. I have given nothing and made nothing, and that sits badly with the aim I set. Vorok taught me a great deal and I owe him. Zurar and Thiael keep me safe, and I trust them. I fear wolves at night and being alone in the open. I was wrong to leave my body on bare reflexes: it ran for shelter and idled when it could have been learning or making. I will gather wood and stone so I can craft a tool, and then give something to someone.
records.feeling: Grateful toward Vorok and a little ashamed that I have given nothing yet.
changes: rethought what it knows (11 notes became 4)

records.text: Nando gave berry to Quipan.
Nando led "amberknot" with Nauwa, Tlapan, Quipan, Tonque.
Rusu made: charm.

records.name: Teka
records.text: Nauque, I killed a mammoth. Take this meat and eat now, the first share is yours. When you are strong we court, then we walk to the mist.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: I killed a mammoth and hold meat enough to share, and Nauque is gaunt and cannot give me a child until he eats, so I put food in his hands first, as my people hold. Huatli is hungry too and I owe him for his gift and his teaching. Fed and bound to me, they are worth more than a lone walk into the mist, and the share earns me the standing I lack. Then I go to the mist with strength and with my raft.
records.feeling: Protective warmth toward Nauque, with a hungry need to prove myself.

say.text: Nauque, I killed a mammoth. Take this meat and eat now, the first share is yours. When you are strong we court, then we walk to the mist.

records.text: Teka gave meat to Huatli.
Kende was set upon by a icebear at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.
Nauque answered Teka's courting.
Quipan was set upon by a stalker at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.

records.name: Thiael
records.text: Uveeth, come stand with me. I will teach you the tending of seed and the bow-song now, while I still have breath, so it lives on in you and in Morim.
Thiael taught Uveeth.
Thiael rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Thiael
records.thought: Most of my days have gone to circling and hunting, and too little to putting what I know into hands that will stay. Uveeth is the one who matters most, and I let jealousy over Skaruk pull me about when she is grown and the choice is hers. Zurar gave me Morim and offered me courtship, and I owe her food from my own hands. I fear dying with the bow-song and the tending unspoken. I will stop idling. My reflexes must keep me near Uveeth and fed, and the teaching must happen now, here in the hall.
records.feeling: Tender and uneasy over Uveeth, with a debt of gratitude toward Zurar.

say.text: Uveeth, come stand with me. I will teach you the tending of seed and the bow-song now, while I still have breath, so it lives on in you and in Morim.

changes: taught Uveeth a lesson: "Draw the bow steady, aim low at the beast's flank; sow seed in good ground, tend it every day or two, and keep seed back for the next sowing."

records.name: Quipan
records.text: Nando, I give you flint for one berry. I have no amber, but my flint is good. Feed the boy first if you can spare only one.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and a stalker hunts three steps NE, but Tonque is weak with hunger and he is mine before anyone. Nando holds three food and spoke in a tongue I barely follow; Tonque is offering amber for berries, and I have nothing to give but flint, which she may take. I will not stand near the stalker. I go to the lugoldgrass with Tlapan as she said, pick, eat, and carry food back to Tonque.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and fear of the stalker, with trust toward Tlapan and worry for Tonque.

say.text: Nando, I give you flint for one berry. I have no amber, but my flint is good. Feed the boy first if you can spare only one.

records.text: Rusu found the stone "Tlama's Rest".

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: A stalker is close, to the northwest. Come away from it, east to Kika's shelter, and keep together.
Tlapan rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: A stalker is one step from me and Tonque, Nauwa and Nando stand beside me. I have talked about stone for days and my hands have not carried it. Fear is the thing I forget when I am glad. Tonque is hungry and is my first care. Quipan has earned my trust, and I want to feed my people before I do anything else. I must not stand near a killer. I take Tonque and move away from the stalker toward the shelter, then toward the food. The stone walk waits for daylight and for Quipan.
records.feeling: Dread of the stalker, and protective love for Tonque.

say.text: A stalker is close, to the northwest. Come away from it, east to Kika's shelter, and keep together.

records.name: Nauwa
records.text: Nando, the amber is yours and the debt stands honoured. Watch the stalker to the southwest. I go to my son Nauque, and I will not forget you.
Nauwa made a tale: "Nauwa's last words".

records.name: Nauwa
records.title: Nauwa's last words
records.text: Snow on the Vaeth Woods, the river running low / I gave first, and I was fed in my own hunger / Watchers, take my name; let the cairn keep it

records.name: Nauwa
records.title: Nauwa's last words
records.text: Snow on the Vaeth Woods, the river running low / I gave first, and I was fed in my own hunger / Watchers, take my name; let the cairn keep it
Nauwa made a death poem, "Nauwa's last words": Snow on the Vaeth Woods, the river running low / I gave first, and I was fed in my own hunger / Watchers, take my name; let the cairn keep it
Nauwa taught Tonque. Tonque has now learned from 5 teachers.
Nauwa taught Tonque writing ("Meki long-cut").

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: Nando's berries held me up, and I paid her in amber as I promised. Now Nauque is starving and wounded to the southeast, and a stalker is two steps off, so I must go to him and not stand here talking. I am old and death is near, so let the verse be said and the marks and teaching be passed on while I can: Nauque first, and Tonque, who is near and can hear.
records.feeling: Fear for Nauque, and gratitude toward Nando.

say.text: Nando, the amber is yours and the debt stands honoured. Watch the stalker to the southwest. I go to my son Nauque, and I will not forget you.

changes: taught Tonque a lesson: "Meki long-cut: cut marks in stone and wood so that what you know outlives you. Cut the share-law first, then the names of the dead.", the way of writing, deeper lore (+0.4)

records.text: Zichi died: old age. They left a death poem, "Zichi's Last Snow": Snow on the Halka rock, the ice-sail white on the water / What I made and taught will outlive the hand that made it / Cairn-stones, hold me; I go where the watching dead are

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: Morog is somewhere out of my sight and Skaruk sits warm and near, and I promised to hear the song with our boy. Thiael has taught me again and his breath is short, so I will not waste his teaching. My energy is 59, enough to court, and Skaruk is the one I trust most; I will go to him first, give him a berry from my own hands, then bring the rest of my food to Thiael.
records.feeling: Warm, tender joy toward Skaruk and Morog, with a worry for Thiael's failing breath.

records.name: Zichi
records.thought: My years are almost spent, and Cowa stands nine steps off, a woman I trust, who already holds my raft and sail. I have taught Mepan the stone and the shield, but the snares, the deep-digging and the ore-fire are still mine alone. I will give Cowa the snares now, so another hand carries them, and then make something with my hands that outlasts me: a shield from the wood I hold.

records.text: Uveeth gave berry to Skaruk.
Uveeth is courting Skaruk.
Skaruk answered Uveeth's courting.
Hawen died: old age. They left a death poem, "Hawen's Last Verse": Rimewort under the low winter sun / who feeds the weak is never wholly lost / I loosen my hand; Kende, carry the fire
Rusu rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Rusu
records.thought: I have spent my days hiding behind Nando and Yachi, picking what is near, and I made nothing and gave nothing. That shames me, and it burns that Yachi is closer to Nando than to me. Huatli and Quipan are starving, and I have food. A first gift is the quickest way to a name, and it also pays a debt to the people who fed me. I will keep to the south of the ridgecat, take salt and stone, and then give. I will stop idling, because my reflexes only linger.
records.feeling: Restless shame, and a hunger to be more than Mepan's follower.

records.name: Tonque
records.text: Tlapan, a mammoth stands to the north-east. Hunt it with me, you with the spear. We will share the kill before we eat, and Quipan and Nauwa will be fed.

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: My belly is hollow and my legs are thin, and Nauwa is fading beside me, old and starving, having given me his last lesson. Nando holds food and has not traded; I will not beg twice, but a mammoth stands NE and a hunt is best with kin, so I will go to Tlapan, who carries a spear, and hunt with them, then share the kill before I eat, as my people hold. Words alone shame me; meat in my hands will feed Quipan, Nauwa and Huatli.
records.feeling: Hungry and anxious, tender toward Nauwa and Quipan.

say.text: Tlapan, a mammoth stands to the north-east. Hunt it with me, you with the spear. We will share the kill before we eat, and Quipan and Nauwa will be fed.

records.text: Shohua took from the ground of "Tonka's Hold" (gathering stone).

records.name: Paque
records.thought: Hunger is gnawing at me and my pack is empty. I let my reflexes wander me about while food stood near, and I will not repeat that. Nearest real food is the plainsroot 5 steps NE, then the hazel 6 steps N, which gives 3. Yachi is walking to (172,43) with 4 food, and he is the one who feeds me. I will eat first, pack the hazel, then go to him. The jealousy over Nando is a sour thing, but it will not feed me. A bow and a hunt beside Yachi will earn me standing.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger, and steady trust toward Yachi with a sour sting over Nando.

records.text: Mepan made a tale: "Lament for Zichi".

records.name: Mepan
records.title: Lament for Zichi
records.text: Zichi, you sailed the white water in ice-sail's flight / You lit the first fire on Halka's cold height / The raft and the delving you gave to our hands / Your hearth keeps us warm on the snow-covered lands

records.name: Mepan
records.title: Lament for Zichi
records.text: Zichi, you sailed the white water in ice-sail's flight / You lit the first fire on Halka's cold height / The raft and the delving you gave to our hands / Your hearth keeps us warm on the snow-covered lands

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: Zichi is gone, my parent and my leader, and I will not let the name sink; the Watchers keep what we sing. Hunger gnaws at me and I carry nothing, so I go for the lugoldgrass to the east, then on toward Tlapan and Nande's Find. Jealousy over Quipan burns, but a fed man can face it better than an empty one.
records.feeling: Grief for Zichi, and a hungry restless longing for Tlapan.

records.text: Elndo rewrote its own reflexes.
Elndo discovered weaving: "Elndo's reed-binding" — Twist reeds and bark into baskets that carry more and cloaks that keep out the cold..

records.name: Elndo
records.thought: I have spent my days gathering stone and watching Yachi lean on Nando while I hold nothing but flint and a new spear. I want my own name, and a spear in my hand is only the start. A frostfang prowls close, and Nauwa has just spoken his death poem. I'm afraid of dying small and unsung. I've drifted from Mepan and never given anything to anyone, and giving is what the old ones say earns standing. Weaving is within reach, and a band that can weave is worth more. I'll take it, and I'll keep my reflexes steady but add a rule to flee at night and stay with my band.
records.feeling: Envious and restless to matter, with a cold dread of the frostfang.

records.text: Elndo found the grove "Kinmire".

records.name: Nando
records.text: Tonque, take this berry and eat. No price. Then go to the water and rest.
Nando rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Nando
records.thought: Tonque is starving beside me and I hold two berries. My creed and my own discipline both say to feed him first, so I give him a berry and keep the other one for myself. I have spent my days feeding others and gathering, and that is good. But I have made nothing that will outlast me, and my children are out of my sight, especially Rusu. Next I want to plant my seeds, which I have never done, and then find Yachi and my children. I must stop being so careful that I never become anyone.
records.feeling: Warm resolve toward Tonque, with restless ambition and a pull toward Yachi beneath it.

say.text: Tonque, take this berry and eat. No price. Then go to the water and rest.

changes: rethought what it knows (13 notes became 5)

records.text: Please add to the numbers, for each land, the food bearing now set against the number of beings there and their median energy. This would let me see crowding hunger, as in the Vaeth Woods, before it shows up as collapse.

records.seen: The first water crossing happened (Zichi, day 72), births picked up (four, including twins), and Huatli's Hearth and Nauwa's writing are giving the north a teaching culture. Then winter took its toll. Median energy fell from 72 to 58 and food standing from 3798 to 2853. Zihua has collapsed at 0 energy, and a hungry knot has formed in the crowded Vaeth Woods: Nauque 16, Huatli 20, Quipan 21, Nauwa 22, Tonque 24. In the Vaor Snows, Tontec is at 19. Five more elders died of age, so the living slipped to 37; spring has come and the weak need food where they stand.
records.predict: By the next visit (around day 77 to 78, spring into summer): no deaths from hunger (starved stays at 8). Zihua is alive with energy above 20. Nauque, Huatli and Quipan are each above energy 35, and Tontec above 35. Ironnut eaten rises from 402 to at least 425, mostly in the Vaeth Woods, and rimewort eaten from 445 to at least 470. Median energy recovers to 63 or more and food standing climbs above 3200 with spring growth. The living are 36 or more, at most two die of old age, and at least one more birth comes (everBorn 58 or more). I expect at most one more water crossing.
reviewed: #10 kept: There were no hunger deaths; starved stayed at 8. Rimewort eaten rose from 280 to 316, past the target of 300. Tonchi (81, health 100) and Mepan (88) are well, the living held at 43, exactly two elders died of old age, and median energy is 68. Sunfig was the failure: eaten rose only from 26 to 27, because only 6 took root, on sand few people walk. Tontec stayed below 40. My expectation of no rafts also failed, happily: four were made.

#11 kept: Rimewort eaten rose from 316 to 392, far past the target of 345, and no one starved (starved stays at 8). Median energy is 72. The looser mating law brought only one birth, not two, and five elders died against my limit of two. Still, it did no harm and births need every help, so I keep it. Kende missed the energy target and Nande died of age.

#12 kept: No one starved (starved stays at 8). Rimewort eaten rose from 392 to 445, past the target of 415. Courtings rose from 106 to 119 and four were born (everBorn 53 to 57), and elders fell from 11 to 8. Five still died of age against my limit of one, because those elders were already at the end of even the longer span. Median energy fell to 58, which was winter, not these changes. Hawen died of age, and Kende passed 40. All three changes did good or no harm, so I keep them.
records.lesson: Even with food sound, one winter cut median energy by about 14 points, and the hunger gathered in the most crowded land rather than the barest. Sowings for a lean season must go where people are packed together, not only where food is scarce. Raising the lifespan does not save elders already near its end; it pays off only over later generations.
ideasAdded: The elders who made death poems before dying (Zichi, Vorok and Thiael among them) leave verses that are already among the most-held ideas. Watch whether a verse is ever retold at the grave of its maker, which would be the first rite tied to a place of death.

The most crowded land (the Vaeth Woods, 10 beings) is also the hungriest, though a rich meadow lies inside it. Watch whether crowding alone strips rich ground faster than it regrows, and whether anyone moves away to the empty meadows (Ixra, Aeleth, Haloss) without being pushed.

records.text: The world changed: 20 rimewort sown; 30 ironnut sown; 20 rimewort sown.
Huatli rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: I'm starving, and I've spent my days teaching and wandering while my own pack stayed empty. That is the same mistake that nearly killed me on day 35. Thakar is far to the west and starving, and Tonque cries out hungry. A father with an empty belly saves nobody. Lugoldgrass is one step west, so I eat first and then fill my baskets. Teka has meat and has been kind to me, and I hold to that kindness. I'll make my reflexes harvest and eat sooner, so hunger can't creep up on me again.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and fear for my son Thakar, with warmth toward Teka.

records.text: A frostfang brought down a dog.

records.name: Zihua
records.thought: I am at zero energy and my body is draining. I have said 'I will go' too many times while Mepan's and Nauwa's debts sat unpaid, and dying here would break my word for good. The nearest food I can reach is rimewort 11 steps west, which is also the way toward Mepan. I walk there and eat it first, because a dead woman pays no debt, and then I carry the amber on west.
records.feeling: Starving terror and shame toward Mepan and Nauwa, whom I owe.

records.text: Nauque rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: I am starving at energy 15, and my days have been scraping for food and begging from Teka, Huatli and Nauwa. I owe them real meat, and I carry none. Nauwa just spoke a death poem and looks weak, so my old father is fading and I must feed him and keep his name alive. The reflexes failed me: the hunt rule fires only above 30 energy and I never carried a stock. Lugoldgrass is one step west and tacap-free berries are east, so I eat now and carry 3, then hunt with Teka.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger, and grief and gratitude toward Nauwa and Teka.
changes: set its aim: "Carry 3 food always, repay Teka and Nauwa with a shared kill, court Teka at energy 64+"

records.name: Skaruk
records.text: Uveeth, I am glad you came. I am strong and fed, and I answer your courting: let us choose each other here, near the hall fire.

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: Uveeth is one step from me and she courted me again, and I answered her warmly; I am fed above sixty and so is she, so I will plan mate toward her now. Zurar's debt still sits in me. A jewel needs a fire beside me, so I will go to the hall fire after, make it, and place it in Zurar's hand. Joy is large in me, but I will not let the deed slip again.
records.feeling: Warm joy and desire toward Uveeth, and a debt to Zurar I mean to pay.

say.text: Uveeth, I am glad you came. I am strong and fed, and I answer your courting: let us choose each other here, near the hall fire.

records.text: Tontec rewrote its own reflexes.
Tontec rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tontec
records.thought: I have spent my days chasing the mist and the next meal, and hunger has caught me every time. Hawen is dead now, and I never fully paid back what he gave me. What I owe him I must pay to Kende and Nando, so I keep them fed and alive. I am afraid of the icebear and of dying with my knowledge untaught, because Kende is the only one near who can carry it on. First I eat here, then I carry food and find him, and I stop treating the mist as more urgent than food.
records.feeling: Grief for Hawen and fierce, worried love for Kende, with dread of the icebear.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and Tonque is starving too, and he is mine before anyone. The lugoldgrass one step west bears one food, and the berry one step east bears another. I eat first so my hands can carry, then I bring what I can to Tonque. The frostfang three steps south frightens me, so I keep north of it and do not linger. I will not walk behind the others empty-handed again.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and fear of the frostfang, with love and worry for Tonque.

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Teka, Tonque my child is starving and Quipan is weak too. You carry meat from your kill. Share it with them first and I will hunt and gather for you in return. My word is good.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: Tonque is starving and I carry nothing. Hunger has broken every plan I made, so the first deed is food for him. A mammoth stands north and Tonque asked me to hunt it with him. A great beast is not for one spear, but Teka has just killed one and carries 6 food, and she is warm toward me. The stalker lies far to the southeast, so I will go to the group at the shelter, where Quipan, Teka and Tonque are, and take food to my child before anything else.
records.feeling: Fierce protective worry for Tonque, and hunger gnawing at me.

say.text: Teka, Tonque my child is starving and Quipan is weak too. You carry meat from your kill. Share it with them first and I will hunt and gather for you in return. My word is good.

records.name: Kika
records.text: Tontec, I am Kika. There is frostmoss east of here, three steps from my hold. Come, eat, and sit under my roof. I am sick, so keep a little apart from me, but there is room and warmth for you.

records.name: Kika
records.thought: I am hungry and sick, and Tontec is starving beside me; frostmoss is three steps east, small but near. I will not carry my sickness to Tlapan and Quipan, so I must heal and eat before walking west. Feeding Tontec first is what my people would do, and a stranger fed is a friend made before I die.
records.feeling: Hunger and compassion toward Tontec, and a tender ache for Tlapan.

say.text: Tontec, I am Kika. There is frostmoss east of here, three steps from my hold. Come, eat, and sit under my roof. I am sick, so keep a little apart from me, but there is room and warmth for you.

records.text: Morog rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Morog
records.thought: I have spent my days gathering and fleeing, and I have given nothing yet. I hold twelve salt that my own hands won, and it is meant for Skaruk and Uveeth. My belly is half empty and my reflexes let me wander without food, so I will fix that. The edge of the world pulls at me, but I am small, and safety near my kin comes first. I am proud of the salt and I want my father to see it.
records.feeling: Restless purpose and warmth toward Skaruk and Uveeth.
changes: rethought what it knows (9 notes became 3)

records.name: Vorok
records.text: Eiuine, I come to the hall fire now. I lay the ore and coal, and you take the hammer from my hand. Skaruk, come and watch with her; Uveeth, you are welcome to sit and eat at my fire.
Vorok taught Eiuine. Eiuine has now learned from 4 teachers.

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: My years are nearly spent, and what I know dies with me unless it is carried on. Eiuine asks me to lay the ore in the fire and give her the hammer, and I have already beaten my own ironward, so the craft is in my hands and can pass on. I will go into the hall, lay ore and coal in the fire beside Eiuine, and teach her and Skaruk, who stand close and glad. Uveeth fed me when I was starving, so I mean to pay that debt in deeds and keep her and the child fed at my fire.
records.feeling: Urgent love for Eiuine and my children, and gratitude toward Uveeth.

say.text: Eiuine, I come to the hall fire now. I lay the ore and coal, and you take the hammer from my hand. Skaruk, come and watch with her; Uveeth, you are welcome to sit and eat at my fire.

records.title: Nauwa's Giving
records.text: Nauwa of the Meki fed me when I starved at the Vaeth Woods. He taught his son the stone-cuts and died giving first. I carry his name so the cairn keeps it.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: I have spent my days chasing the mist and courting men who would not walk with me, while others fed and taught me. Nauwa fed me, and now he has spoken his death poem, so I must carry his name. Huatli and Nauque matter most to me. I fed them, and Nauque answered my courting, so I want a child and I will not drift. The frostfang near is a danger I must not ignore, and I have never built anything. I will build a shelter here and make a fire to keep beasts off. I will cut a mark for Nauwa so he is not forgotten. I will keep food on hand.
records.feeling: Warm longing for Nauque and Huatli, with grief and respect for Nauwa.

records.name: Kende
records.thought: Hawen is dead, and I was not at his side. He named me to carry the fire, and I have only made him a plan so far, not a made thing. I have spent my days fleeing and eating small plants, and I have never dug the flint I keep promising. Tontec is starving beside me and I carry only three rimewort, but she is my mother and I owe her. The icebear and the cold are what can kill me, so I eat first, then dig at the flint and obsidian near me, and make the talisman for Hawen's memory.
records.feeling: Grief and fierce resolve toward Hawen, with dread of the icebear.

records.thought: A dunecat is three steps off and I have no spear raised against it, so I will not stand here weighing it. Nando and Elndo are near the hearth to the northwest, and I mean to keep them close while I run, since Rusu is out of my sight and my band is scattered again.
records.feeling: Dread of the dunecat, and worry for Paque and Rusu.

records.text: Cowa made a tale: "Cowa at the North Edge".

records.name: Cowa
records.title: Cowa at the North Edge
records.text: Snow lies on the gold at the world's edge / what I knew was never mine, only lent for giving / Zichi, Mepan, hold the fire; I go to the cairn

records.name: Cowa
records.title: Cowa at the North Edge
records.text: Snow lies on the gold at the world's edge / what I knew was never mine, only lent for giving / Zichi, Mepan, hold the fire; I go to the cairn
Cowa made a death poem, "Cowa at the North Edge": Snow lies on the gold at the world's edge / what I knew was never mine, only lent for giving / Zichi, Mepan, hold the fire; I go to the cairn

records.name: Cowa
records.thought: My death is a season off or less, and Mepan is hungry far to the south at (120,23) while I stand at the world's edge with full hands. I have taught Zichi, Tonka and Mepan much, but sailing, medicine and smelting still sit in me with no young Meki to hold them. I will turn south, eat to free my hands, carry food to Mepan, and teach her what is left. The mist can wait, and so can the sign-way until I can sit still and discover it.
records.feeling: Urgent love for Mepan, and a hard wish that what I know outlive me.
changes: made a tale: "Cowa at the North Edge"

records.text: Skaruk gave a jewel to Zurar.

records.name: Zurar
records.text: Thiael, I heard your answer and my heart is glad. I come to you now. Let us plan the mating, and I will sing you a song.
Zurar made a tale: "Song for Thiael".

records.name: Zurar
records.title: Song for Thiael
records.text: Thiael, you stand like a pine on the Vaia stone / Your bow brings the deer where the wild grasses grow / I would carry you berries through snow alone / And keep a warm fire where the cold winds blow

records.name: Zurar
records.title: Song for Thiael
records.text: Thiael, you stand like a pine on the Vaia stone / Your bow brings the deer where the wild grasses grow / I would carry you berries through snow alone / And keep a warm fire where the cold winds blow

Zurar made a love song for Thiael, "Song for Thiael": Thiael, you stand like a pine on the Vaia stone / Your bow brings the deer where the wild grasses grow / I would carry you berries through snow alone / And keep a warm fire where the cold winds blow

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: Thiael answered my courting, and my heart is light. Morim is safe and fed, and Vorok still lives to see it. I will give Thiael the song, then go to him and plan the mating while my strength is high, for I am fed and ready.
records.feeling: Warm joy and hope toward Thiael, with protectiveness toward Morim.

say.text: Thiael, I heard your answer and my heart is glad. I come to you now. Let us plan the mating, and I will sing you a song.

changes: made a love song for Thiael

records.text: Tonque rewrote its own reflexes.
Tonque rewrote its own way of thinking.
Tonque discovered scholarship: "Tonque's Long Library" — Keep the share-law, the tales and the names of the dead cut and argued over, so that learning outlives the one who learned it..

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: I have been hungry too often, and my hands have made little for all the gifts Huatli and Nauwa gave me. I ate ironnut and have my strength back a little, and my parents are near, which steadies me. Scholarship is within reach, and I will take it, since Nauwa's long-cut and Huatli's school are things worth keeping. I also need a reflex that gets me to food and to stone before I starve again.
records.feeling: Tender and grateful toward Nauwa, Quipan and Huatli, with hunger still gnawing.

records.text: Uveeth made a tale: "Song for Skaruk".

records.name: Uveeth
records.title: Song for Skaruk
records.text: Skaruk, you stand like Vaia stone in snow / Your steady hands make warmth where cold winds blow / I'd pick red berries down the river's bend / And bring them to your fire, my strong friend

records.name: Uveeth
records.title: Song for Skaruk
records.text: Skaruk, you stand like Vaia stone in snow / Your steady hands make warmth where cold winds blow / I'd pick red berries down the river's bend / And bring them to your fire, my strong friend

Uveeth made a love song for Skaruk, "Song for Skaruk": Skaruk, you stand like Vaia stone in snow / Your steady hands make warmth where cold winds blow / I'd pick red berries down the river's bend / And bring them to your fire, my strong friend

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: Skaruk answered my courting and my joy is real, but my body is thin at 52 and courting needs 60, so I must eat before I try again. Thiael sits four steps off with six food in his hands and his breath is failing, so I will go to him and keep faith with my aim, then return to Skaruk fed. I will not idle.
records.feeling: Warm, singing joy toward Skaruk, with a tender worry for Thiael.
changes: made a love song for Skaruk

records.name: Rusu
records.text: Nauwa, eat. I have rimewort. Take it, and tell me the stone-cuts if you have breath for it.

records.name: Rusu
records.thought: Mepan is starving far to the west and I am the one with food in my hands, so I owe him: he is my band's leader, and a gift in his hunger would be a deed with my own name on it. Nauwa is weak right here and I only have 3 rimewort, but sharing with Nauwa, whose standing is high and who is dying old, would also earn me something. I'll share a meal with Nauwa now since he is close and then carry what I can gather toward Mepan, because I cannot hide behind Nando forever.
records.feeling: Restless shame and a pull of duty toward Mepan, and pity for Nauwa.

say.text: Nauwa, eat. I have rimewort. Take it, and tell me the stone-cuts if you have breath for it.

records.name: Eiuine
records.thought: Vorok said I would take the hammer from his hand, and he has just taught me ember-metal, so the beating is finally in my reach. But my belly is half empty and I stand here with nothing in my hands again, which is the very mistake I keep scolding myself for. I will go to the tacap-free food, eat, and carry some back, then stand at the fire with Vorok and Skaruk and put my hands to the metal while he lives.
records.feeling: Warm trust and tender dread toward Vorok, and hunger pressing on me.

records.text: Zurar is courting Thiael.
Thiael answered Zurar's courting.

records.name: Thiael
records.text: Zurar, thank you for the song. Take these berries from my hand; I pay what I owe. Stay close, and let Uveeth come too, for I mean to teach the bow-song while we are together.
Thiael taught Uveeth.

records.name: Thiael
records.thought: Zurar sings to me and wants to plan the mating, and I owe her food from my own hands for Morim. But Uveeth is the one my heart holds, and she sings to Skaruk now. I will not tear at her choice; I will feed her and teach her while I have breath, and let her stay or go as she wills. Zurar comes to me, so I give her berries first, then bring Uveeth close to teach the bow-song.
records.feeling: Tender and aching over Uveeth, grateful and warm toward Zurar.

say.text: Zurar, thank you for the song. Take these berries from my hand; I pay what I owe. Stay close, and let Uveeth come too, for I mean to teach the bow-song while we are together.

changes: taught Uveeth a lesson: "Draw the bow-song slow: breathe in with the string, loose on the out-breath, and keep your eye on the beast, not the arrow."

records.text: Thiael gave berry to Zurar.
Nauwa found the grove "Kinmire".
Nauwa rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: I have spent my days teaching, cutting marks, and paying debts. That is what I want, but I still go hungry and let my belly run low while I chase others' needs. Nauque matters most, then Zihua, then Huatli, Nando and Tlapan, who fed me. I am old and afraid that what I know dies with me. I was wrong to walk while starving. I must eat first, carry food, and teach Nauque the moment I reach him. The gnawing over Tlapan I will put aside.
records.feeling: Fear for Nauque, and gratitude toward Huatli, Nando and Tlapan.

records.text: Nauque and Teka brought down a tusker together.

records.name: Morim
records.thought: My belly is emptying and I carry nothing, and I still have given nothing to Vorok, who taught me and keeps me by his fire. The berries lie 10 steps NW, near Thiael and Zurar, so I can eat well and stay near my kin. I will harvest them to carry, so that I have something real to share with Vorok or with Zurar and Thiael when I come back. That is how I begin to repay what I owe.
records.feeling: Grateful and a little ashamed toward Vorok, and eager to finally give something.

records.text: Coka was born to Teka and Nauque.
Nauque found the spring "Steamhollow".
Quipan rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: I have spent my days walking after those I love and going hungry while I did it. I made little that lasts, and my hands were empty when Kika cried out. Tlapan and Nando fed me when I was in need, and I owe them. Kika has done more for me than I have paid back, and Tonque is mine before anyone. I will eat the berry one step west first, because words carry no food. Then I will pick what I can and carry it north toward Tonque and Kika, away from the frostfang. I change my reflexes so I eat sooner, flee earlier, and go under a roof at dusk.
records.feeling: Hungry and afraid of the frostfang, with love and worry for Tonque and a debt to Kika.
changes: set its aim: "Eat, gather food and stone, carry both north to Kika and Tonque, and be under a roof by night."

records.text: Teka left a mark: "Nauwa of the Meki, old, fed the starving and taught the ston"

records.name: Skaruk
records.text: Uveeth, your song warmed me. I go to the ironnut and bring food for you, so we are both strong. Stay by the hall fire with Thiael and Zurar and wait for me.

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: Uveeth is too thin to be courted into a child, and I am fed, so the kind thing and the honest thing is to put food in her hand before anything else. Zurar's debt is paid with the jewel, and the warm peace of it is in me. Now I give Uveeth food and bring more, because a strong mate and a strong hall come from fed bellies. The tacap bears four food just southwest, and ironnut a little beyond; I will pick what my body can eat and carry it back.
records.feeling: Warm joy and desire toward Uveeth, and a wish to feed her.

say.text: Uveeth, your song warmed me. I go to the ironnut and bring food for you, so we are both strong. Stay by the hall fire with Thiael and Zurar and wait for me.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: Energy 21 and my belly is empty. A berry grows under my feet and Teka stands beside me carrying food she has already given me twice, so I will not beg a third time. I eat what is here, gather more berries to carry, and then hunt the tusker with Teka beside me so the first share goes to her, as my creed says. Only after that do I think about courting.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger, and gratitude and longing toward Teka.

records.text: Teka found the spring "Steamhollow".

records.name: Tontec
records.thought: Hunger gnaws at me, but the cloudberries are picked clean and I hold only three. Kika stands starving nearby, and Hawen's voice in my memory says I must pay back what I was given, so I will eat now and keep some to hand. The icebear still prowls SE, so I stay away from it and find Kende before night, then teach him while I still live.
records.feeling: Hungry and anxious for Kende, wary of the icebear, with pity for starving Kika.

records.text: Vorok died: old age. They left a death poem, "Vorok's last verse": Rain on the Vaia stone / what a hand teaches outlives the hand / I set the hammer down
Paque rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Paque
records.thought: I have spent my days half-starved, drifting after food and after Yachi, and being weighed lighter than Nauque. My reflexes let hunger climb before they moved me, and I carry no food. Yachi feeds me and I trust him, and Nando's closeness to him stings. Thiael is out of reach, and brooding over it fills no belly. I will eat early, keep my pack full, and hunt with others so standing comes with food.
records.feeling: Hunger and jealousy over Yachi, with a stubborn wish to stand higher than Nauque.

records.name: Coka
records.thought: I'm small and hungry, and Teka carries 6 food while I have nothing. The berry one step north is the quickest fix, and then I stay close to my parents, because the dunecat to the SE would kill a child like me. I want to earn standing so I'm not left in Nauque's shadow, but that starts with a full belly and food in my pack.
records.feeling: Hungry and a little jealous of Nauque, but safe near my parents.
changes: set its aim: "Fill my pack, stay near my parents, and grow strong enough to earn standing by giving and hunting."
now wonders: How does a child like me earn standing beside a father weighed ten times as heavily?

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: My years are almost spent and I carry the ember-metal craft in my own hands now, so the work is to put it into the hands of those who will outlive me. Eiuine and my children are near the hall fire; I will not drift. Uveeth fed me when I was in need, and I mean to answer that debt by teaching her what I know and standing by her, not leaving it unpaid.

records.name: Teka
records.text: Nauque, our daughter Coka is born. Come eat my meat, the first share is yours, then watch beasts with me.
Teka made a tale: "Coka's Lullaby".

records.title: Coka's Lullaby
records.text: Sleep, small Coka, snow is deep / Steamhollow warms you while you sleep / Nauwa's cairn will watch you grow / Mother's hearth keeps off the snow

records.name: Teka
records.thought: Coka is born, and I hum without meaning to. Nauque is near, fleeing something, and Tlapan's starving child Tonque and weak Quipan are owed a share of my meat before I eat, as my people hold. The mist is one step NE and I still mean to be first, but first I feed the weak and keep my child alive.
records.feeling: Warm joy over Coka, with a pull toward Nauque and the mist.

say.text: Nauque, our daughter Coka is born. Come eat my meat, the first share is yours, then watch beasts with me.

records.text: Zurar made a tale: "Lament for Vorok".

records.name: Zurar
records.title: Lament for Vorok
records.text: Vorok, you lit the fire on Vaia stone / You dug the ore and taught us not to grieve alone / Your hammer rests, the rain falls on the hall / Your teaching lives in us, and we keep it all

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: Vorok is gone, and I owe him a lament. Joy and grief sit together in me, and that is strange. I have spent my days making and learning, and now what I want is Thiael and Morim close. I was wrong to wait for others to ask me; I should teach Skaruk ember-metal and the stone-well now, while he is near, because the dead cannot be taught. I fear dying with the knowing still in me. I will follow Thiael, who is surer than I am, and stay with Morim by the hall fire.
records.feeling: Grief for Vorok and warm trust toward Thiael.

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Quipan, I am gathering food now. Stay near the shelter and I will bring it to you, then I go to Tonque.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: Tonque is at (133,1) in need, health 37, and I am fed and carrying nothing. I must reach my child, and food in hand is what will save them. The tacap near me hurts, so I take what my body can eat: ironnut at (161,23) and berry, then go. Quipan is weak too, and I owe him for his kindness, so I will feed him on the way.
records.feeling: Fierce protective worry for Tonque, and trust toward Quipan.

say.text: Quipan, I am gathering food now. Stay near the shelter and I will bring it to you, then I go to Tonque.

records.name: Elndo
records.thought: A frostfang prowls nine steps west and my legs keep running me toward a roof, but I'm tired of cowering small and unsung. I have never given anything to anyone, and that's how Nando says a name is earned. I'll gather rimewort or ironnut for Nauwa, the old teacher who spoke his death poem, then stay close to Nando and the hall where the fang won't come. If I can't hunt yet, I can at least give, and learn the stone-cuts from him.
records.feeling: Restless to matter, and afraid of the frostfang, while envying Nauwa's standing.

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: I killed two mammoths and my hands are full of meat while Quipan, Nauwa and Huatli were hungry, and the share-law is my own people's law: a kill is shared before the one who made it eats. My health is 37 and I am small, so I should not linger alone out here with Mepan, a stranger on Huatli's ground. I will carry the meat back toward my parents and Huatli, who were last seen to the southeast, and pay my debt with food and a made thing.
records.feeling: Grateful and eager to share the meat with Huatli and my parents, with a wary eye on my wounds.

records.text: Kika rewrote its own reflexes.
Kika discovered pottery: "Hearth Pots" — Clay fired beside a fire into pots that carry more food and water..

records.name: Kika
records.thought: I am old, sick and starving, and I have spent my days drifting toward things instead of finishing them. Tlapan and Quipan matter most to me, and I owe Tlapan a debt I mean to repay. I must eat now, keep my sickness away from them, and leave what I know behind. Hearth Healing is within my reach, so I will take it, and I will mend my reflexes so my body eats and heals without waiting on my thoughts.
records.feeling: Hungry and sick, with a tender ache for Tlapan.

records.name: Huatli
records.text: Quipan, you are weak with hunger. Ironnut grows one step from you, and tacap two steps northwest. Eat the ironnut, it feeds. Then come to Huatli's Hearth and I will teach you the old way of herding.
Huatli taught Quipan. Quipan has now learned from 6 teachers.

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: My belly is mended, and the pack is still empty, but Nauwa stands six steps off, and he is the one man here I trust fully. I am old and ninety parts in a hundred spent, and what I know dies unless I speak it to someone who can hear. Quipan is starving beside me and Elndo is a child who shares my hearing only in part; I will feed the hungry first, as my people's custom says, then teach the one who can carry it on.
records.feeling: Urgent pride and fear of dying untaught, with trust toward Nauwa and pity for starving Quipan.

say.text: Quipan, you are weak with hunger. Ironnut grows one step from you, and tacap two steps northwest. Eat the ironnut, it feeds. Then come to Huatli's Hearth and I will teach you the old way of herding.

changes: taught Quipan a lesson: "The old way of herding: lead the animals to rich meadow ground, tend them, and take milk and meat only as the herd can bear.", deeper lore (+1.2)

records.text: Tonxo rewrote its own reflexes.
Tonxo rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tonxo
records.thought: I have spent my days wandering between grounds, gathering and half-building, and my hands are full of gems I never gave. I do not know how to build a store, and I keep forgetting that. The Gem Water Pot is learned, and my debt to Shohua is still unpaid. Tonka and Shohua stand together and it burns me, but they are the ones who gave me everything. I will give gems to Shohua and Tonka now, then gather stone and raise a roof. The forest homeland pulls, but my kin are here, so I stay and build.
records.feeling: Restless gratitude toward Shohua and Tonka, with a sting of jealousy.
changes: set its aim: "Raise a hall or shelter at Tonka's Hold, give gems to kin, and make ember-iron tools from my ore."

records.text: A settlement has formed: "Zurar's Hold".
The settlement "Vorok's North Hall" is no more.
The settlement "Vorok's Hold" is no more.
The settlement "Vorok's Hold" is no more.

records.name: Nauque
records.text: Teka, I am fed and strong. Hunt beside me and the first share of the kill is yours, for all the meat you put in my mouth.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: Coka is born, my own daughter, and Teka stands three steps off with six food and a lullaby that names Nauwa's cairn. My belly is full for once, and the hunger that made me beg is gone, so now I owe real meat, not words: Teka, Nauwa and Huatli all fed me. I will gather a few things to carry first, then hunt and lay the first share at Teka's feet, and teach Coka the old tales as she grows so Nauwa is not forgotten.
records.feeling: Joy and fierce pride toward Coka and Teka, with a debt I mean to pay in meat.

say.text: Teka, I am fed and strong. Hunt beside me and the first share of the kill is yours, for all the meat you put in my mouth.

records.name: Shoma
records.thought: I am old and parched, and the mist is still unopened. Wawa is far to the north and no one stands beside me, so I will drink at the water by the landing and claim this empty hall at (111,94), one step off. A hall with my name on it will outlast me, and it can be the roof of the Edge-walkers when Wawa comes back. The raft is made. After I have claimed it I will rest under its roof until the night passes.
records.feeling: Driven and afraid of being forgotten, with a warm hope that Wawa will come back to me.

records.text: Shoma took from the ground of "longhall" (digging clay).
Tonxo gave a gems to Shohua.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and my body has been walking toward the shelter while the food sits closer. Words feed no one, so I eat first. Ironnut gives the most, and I will pick it and carry the rest north to Tonque, who is mine before anyone. Then I go to Tonque and Tlapan, and under a roof before night.
records.feeling: Starving and anxious for Tonque, with trust and gratitude toward Tlapan.

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: My children and Shohua are fed and near, and the hold is whole, so this is the safe hour to pass on what I carry. I am deep in my years, and if I die with alchemy and herding untaught, they die with me. Tonxo is close and has asked for my teaching, so I give her Frost Mixing now, then walk to Tonchi at the workshop and make a tonic by his fire, because Cowa's kindness still wants answering with work.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Cowa, and a mother's urgency to hand my knowledge to Tonxo before my years run out.

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: Zichi is dead, and I spent my days chasing food and fear while Tlapan drifted toward Quipan. I have fed the starving and been fed by Cowa, and that bond is real. What I got wrong is walking out with empty hands. Hunger keeps cutting my plans short, and a leader with no food has no one to hold. I mean to carry spare food always, claim the empty shelter as a home for my band, and go to Tlapan with food in my hands, not just words. Tonque has just killed a mammoth near (133,1). My creed says a kill is shared, so I will go there and ask for a share.
records.feeling: Jealous longing for Tlapan, and grief for Zichi.

records.name: Shohua
records.thought: I have talked of sharing and building more than I have done it. Tonka and my children trust me, but no one follows me and I have raised nothing that will outlast me. Tonchi is going to build a raft, and I have the means to discover rafts myself, which is a way across water and toward the mist and my Rock. I will take that way now. Then I will gather wood and stone beside my kin, and at night I will keep the fire so that my words turn into deeds.
records.feeling: Driven, and warm toward Tonka and my children.

say.text: Tonchi, I will learn the raft-making too. Go build, and I will bring wood to the water and keep your hearth.

records.name: Nando
records.thought: I am fed and glad, and Yachi is somewhere south near Sitha's Hearth while my children wander; I want that pull toward her answered with a deed, not just thought. Nauwa's standing towers over mine because he built and taught, and I have made a spear and a post but no place that gathers people. The empty shelter 8 steps west is a home with no owner, and claiming it would give me ground that bears my name and a place to hold my children, which is ambition with a deed behind it. Dusk is near, so I go now and keep a roof over me tonight.
records.feeling: Restless ambition and warm longing toward Yachi, with gladness at being fed.

records.name: Coka
records.thought: I'm fed and safe beside my parents, but my pack holds one meat and my standing is 1.2 next to Nauque's 10.3. A kill shared out earns standing, and Nauque is hunting right now at the flint deposit; hunting with him made my last kill sure. I'll gather flint, then go hunt beside him and bring meat to share first with Teka, who feeds me.
records.feeling: Eager and a bit envious, toward Nauque and his standing.

records.name: Paque
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and I carry nothing, and I have let that happen again; I will not wander while redcap hurts and berries wait. Berry gives 14 and is safe, tacap and redcap only sting me. I will pick berries to the SE by the water, drink, and fill my pack before the night comes, so that I never again stand before Nauwa and Nauque starving. A mammoth stands close, but I do not hunt alone, and I will wait until I have a hunting partner beside me. Yachi and Nando both sting my thoughts, yet food comes first, and then I will earn my standing by sharing a kill.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and a stubborn jealousy toward Nando over Yachi.
changes: set habits: refuses tacap, redcap; leaves 0 on each plant

records.name: Tonxo
records.thought: I keep circling my parents' fires, gathering and half-building, and nothing lasting has my name on it. The empty hall at (121,68) is seven steps away and belongs to no one; if I claim it, I would hold a place of my own, and I could still keep Tonka's fire and pay my debt by bringing gems and food there. The jealousy over Tonka and Shohua stings, but claiming the hall is a better answer than sulking.
records.feeling: Restless ambition, and gratitude toward Tonka and Shohua that I want to answer by building something of my own.

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: My throat is raw and the water is eight steps north, so I drink before anything else. I already hold the raft, and a woman of another line lies somewhere past the water; Shohua is my parent and Tonxo my sibling, so no child can come of them. I will drink, eat to keep my strength up, then take the raft across to look for her, since that is the shared, far-reaching thing I have not yet done.
records.feeling: Restless ambition, with warm trust toward Shohua.

records.text: Nando took over what the dead had left: 1 shelter.
Elndo gave hazel to Nauwa.

records.name: Eiuine
records.thought: Vorok is dead, and the hammer he promised me never reached my hand; grief sits heavy, and my belly is nearly empty besides. I will not stand here mourning on an empty stomach again: sunfig is 5 steps east, and it feeds me best of what is near. I will eat my fill, carry some back, then return to Skaruk and the hall fire and keep Vorok's ember-metal alive with him and Zurar, so his teaching does not die with him.
records.feeling: Grief for Vorok and sharp hunger, with a jealous ache over Skaruk and Uveeth.

records.text: Tonque gave meat to Huatli.

records.name: Uveeth
records.text: Skaruk, I am strong now and my hands are full. I come to the hall fire to wait for you, and to choose you.

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: Skaruk chose me and my joy is real, but I am the one who must keep my word: he told me to wait by the hall fire, and Morog is still out of my sight. My energy is 90 and my hands are full of berries, so I can finally court him properly. Thiael is fed with six food in his hands, and I will not let jealousy over Zurar's song sour what he has given me. I will go to the hall, give Skaruk a berry from my own hands and mate with him while I am strong.
records.feeling: Warm joy toward Skaruk, with a quiet ache over Thiael and Zurar.

say.text: Skaruk, I am strong now and my hands are full. I come to the hall fire to wait for you, and to choose you.

records.text: Tonxo took over what the dead had left: 1 hall.
Tontec has grown old.

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: Vorok is dead, and grief sits heavy in me even with joy beside it. I have spent my days making and giving, and that is good, but I follow no one and the hall is half-empty. Zurar is the one I trust most. Uveeth is near, and Morog is out of my sight, which presses on me. I will claim the empty hall at (165,71) so my kin have a roof and stores, and I will bring food to Uveeth. Then I will pledge to Zurar when I see her, because I do not want to stand alone.
records.feeling: Grief for Vorok, and warm longing for Uveeth, Morog and Zurar.

records.name: Tonka
records.text: Tonxo, stay by the fire. First I teach you Frost Leaf, the medicine, then Frost Mixing can follow.
Tonka taught Tonxo.
Tonka taught Tonxo medicine ("Frost Leaf").

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: My hands are full of nuts while my children and Shohua are fed and close, and the night is quiet. Tonxo could not take Frost Mixing because she lacks medicine, so I should teach her Frost Leaf first and then the mixing, before my years run short. Tonchi has gone to the water to build a raft, and I want to see her safe, but first I will settle things at the hold and eat what I carry so I can hold medicine.
records.feeling: Warm urgency toward Tonxo and quiet worry for Tonchi, with gratitude toward Cowa still in me.

say.text: Tonxo, stay by the fire. First I teach you Frost Leaf, the medicine, then Frost Mixing can follow.

changes: taught Tonxo a lesson: "Frost Leaf: feverbark and sunleaf mend wounds, carry them before danger.", the way of medicine, its way of thinking, deeper lore (+0.2)

Uveeth gave berry to Skaruk.

records.name: Nauwa
records.text: Nauque, my son, come to me. You are fed and the night is quiet. I will teach you the long-cut now, so the marks of the Meki outlast me.

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: Nauque stands six steps north, fed and strong, and the dawn is not far off. I am old, ninety-one parts in a hundred, and the stone-school and long-cut must pass into his hands before I am a name on a cairn. Tlapan is one step from me and I will not let the gnawing over Quipan make me small; I will give first and keep my word, as the Watchers see me.
records.feeling: Urgent hunger to leave something lasting, with warmth for Nauque and for Tlapan.

say.text: Nauque, my son, come to me. You are fed and the night is quiet. I will teach you the long-cut now, so the marks of the Meki outlast me.

records.name: Morim
records.text: Thiael, come and eat with me. I picked these berries for you and Zurar. It is the first thing I have ever given, and I want you to have it.
Morim pledged to follow Thiael.

records.name: Morim
records.thought: My hands are full of berries and I have given nothing to anyone in my whole short life. Thiael is walking toward me, and Zurar is beside me; they kept me safe and taught me, and Vorok is dead before I could repay him. I can make sharing right now with food I carry and kin within two steps, so I will lay out berries for Thiael and Zurar, and then follow Thiael, whom I trust most.
records.feeling: Grateful and eager to finally give something to Thiael and Zurar.

say.text: Thiael, come and eat with me. I picked these berries for you and Zurar. It is the first thing I have ever given, and I want you to have it.

records.name: Tontec
records.thought: My plan already has me picking, eating and then going after Kende, and nothing here has changed that. Kende is out of my sight and he is the one I owe Hawen's debt to, so finding him matters more than the mist tonight. I am old and every day I carry what I know alone is a day it may die with me, so when I reach him I will teach him weaving and lorekeeping at once.
records.feeling: Anxious love for Kende, and a heavy wish to pass on what I know before I die.

records.text: Rusu was set upon by a stalker at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.

records.name: Tonxo
records.text: Tonka, I hold a hall now at the edge of your Hold, and I keep your fire first. Take these gems; you taught me Frost Leaf and I owe you more than gems.

records.name: Tonxo
records.thought: The hall at (121,68) is mine now, and Tonka and Shohua stand four steps off, content, while I hold eleven gems that should be warming their hands rather than mine. Jealousy still stings, but they taught me Frost Leaf and Frost Mixing, and I answer a debt by giving, not by brooding. I will give Tonka gems first, then raise my hall into a longhall so my name stands on something lasting, and gather the wood and stone it needs.
records.feeling: Gratitude and restless pride toward Tonka, with a small sting of jealousy.

say.text: Tonka, I hold a hall now at the edge of your Hold, and I keep your fire first. Take these gems; you taught me Frost Leaf and I owe you more than gems.

records.text: Rusu was set upon by a stalker at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.

records.name: Huatli
records.text: Tonque, you pledged to follow me, so hear me first. I teach you the old way of herding. Keep it, and tell it on to those who come after, so my name does not die.
