records.title: Huatli's last words
records.text: Spring rain on the Vaeth Woods, lugoldgrass green by the water / I gave first and taught the young, and the Hearth still burns / Watchers, take my name; I come to the cairn

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: Ninety parts in a hundred are spent, and my death is near, a season off or less. Nauwa stands beside me and I trust him wholly; I will teach him while he can hear, and Tonque, who is my own band, so something of Huatli's Hearth outlives me. I mean to pass on the old way of herding and the lore of the Watchers before the cold takes my voice.
records.feeling: Urgent pride and quiet peace, toward Nauwa and Tonque, who will carry what I leave.

say.text: Tonque, you pledged to follow me, so hear me first. I teach you the old way of herding. Keep it, and tell it on to those who come after, so my name does not die.

changes: taught Tonque a lesson: "The old way of herding: lead the herd to rich meadow, keep it near a pen, and drive it together with others so the kill is sure and shared.", the way of herding

records.name: Thiael
records.text: Morim, your berries warmed me. Stand by me now and I will teach you the bow-song and the tending of seed, so they live on in you.
Thiael taught Morim.
Thiael taught Morim archery ("Canopy bow-song").

records.name: Thiael
records.thought: My days are nearly spent, and what I know dies with me unless it goes into Uveeth's and Morim's hands. Uveeth waits for Skaruk and I will not tear at her choice, but the bow-song and the tending of seed must pass to her and to Morim while I still have breath. Morim stands beside me, glad, so I teach him now, then walk to Uveeth at the hall and keep close.
records.feeling: Tender, urgent love for Morim and Uveeth, and gratitude toward Zurar.

say.text: Morim, your berries warmed me. Stand by me now and I will teach you the bow-song and the tending of seed, so they live on in you.

changes: taught Morim a lesson: "Draw the bow to the cheek, breathe out, loose. Sow seed in wet clay, tend it every day or two, and take only what the plant can grow again.", the way of archery, deeper lore (+1.5)

records.text: Tonxo gave a gems to Tonka.
Rusu was set upon by a stalker at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.
Kika was set upon by a wolf at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.

records.name: Kika
records.thought: I am starving and torn, with a stalker, wolf and icebear all near me in the dark; the cold bites at my wounds and my fear is total. The tacap near me would hurt me and the cloudberry bears nothing yet, so the rimewort and the store at my hold are my real hope. I must get away from the hunters and eat, because if I die here nothing of Coni's band, nor what I know, will reach Tlapan or Quipan. I will take Hearth Healing now, for I am hurt and old, and then keep to my plan away from the beasts.
records.feeling: Terrified and starving, with a tender ache for Tlapan.

records.text: Nauque rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: I have spent my days chasing food and owing debts, and now I am fed, with a daughter, Coka, born of Teka. That is worth more than any kill. Still, I have built nothing that bears my name and no one follows me. I take from Kika's ground while hunting, and that could turn on me. Nauwa offers the long-cut, and the old are heeded first, so I should go to him and learn it. Then I will teach it on to Coka so it outlasts me. My debts to Teka, Nauwa and Huatli are paid in meat, not words, so I keep my hunter's hands ready and carry more food.
records.feeling: Fierce pride and joy toward Coka and Teka, and a hunger to leave a mark.
changes: set its aim: "Learn the long-cut from Nauwa, teach Coka, and repay Teka and Nauwa with a shared kill off Kika's ground"

records.name: Tonque
records.text: Huatli, I keep the old way of herding and I will tell it on. Eat, stay under the roof. I will bring you stone and make a spear in your name.

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: Huatli just spoke his death poem and taught me herding so his name would not die, and I feel a deep debt and a deep fear of losing him. My parents are beside me, which steadies me, and I carry meat I can still share. I have never made a thing with my own hands for him, so I will gather wood and stone at the flint nearby and make a spear, the first tool of my own, while staying close to the roof and my parents.
records.feeling: Grateful and anxious toward Huatli, who may be dying, and steadied by my parents near.

say.text: Huatli, I keep the old way of herding and I will tell it on. Eat, stay under the roof. I will bring you stone and make a spear in your name.

records.name: Teka
records.text: Tlapan, I share before I eat. I bring meat for Tonque and Quipan now, and your hunting can pay me back later.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: Coka is alive and was last seen east, near the water, and I feel a warm pull to follow her. Tlapan's boy Tonque and weak Quipan are owed a share of my meat before I eat again, as my people hold, and Nauwa fed me once, so I pay that debt. The mist and the Dunmar Plains lie 8 steps east, and I mean to be first there, but I'll feed the weak first and then go to my child.
records.feeling: Warm joy over Coka, and a pull toward the mist.

say.text: Tlapan, I share before I eat. I bring meat for Tonque and Quipan now, and your hunting can pay me back later.

records.text: Tonque led "sharing" with Huatli, Tlapan, Quipan.
Nando crossed the water on a vessel and came ashore in the Vaeth Woods.
Teka gave meat to Tonque.

records.name: Rusu
records.text: Stalker at the shelter by the water! Nando, I'm coming to you, help me!

records.name: Rusu
records.thought: A stalker is two steps from me and has already bitten me three times. I'm a child, and the one thing my parents' teaching never got wrong is that a hunter is not something I face alone. My old plan walks toward (125,25), which is no safer. I'll run for Nando, last seen east at (148,24), and stay near the shelters and my kin, because shame is better than dying. Mepan is far north and I can't reach him through this. If I live, I'll still owe him food and a deed of my own.
records.feeling: Terror of the stalker at my heels, and a desperate pull toward Nando.

say.text: Stalker at the shelter by the water! Nando, I'm coming to you, help me!

records.text: Teka gave meat to Quipan.

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Quipan, stay under this roof with Tonque and me until first light. The stalker walks the northeast. At dawn we go for stone together.
Tlapan rewrote its own reflexes.
Tlapan rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: I have been running between hunger and promises for days, and my hands have not carried the stone, so my words have outrun my deeds. Tonque is wounded and at my side now, and Quipan is the one I trust. Huatli is dying, and I owe him quiet respect. I fear the stalker to the NE and the wet night. I want stone for the longhall, and I want Tonque safe. So I stay sheltered with Tonque and Quipan until dawn, keep food on me, and go to the bare rock together in daylight.
records.feeling: Fierce protective worry for Tonque and steady trust toward Quipan.

say.text: Quipan, stay under this roof with Tonque and me until first light. The stalker walks the northeast. At dawn we go for stone together.

records.text: Tonchi crossed the water on a vessel and came ashore in the Aelim Fens.

records.name: Zurar
records.text: Skaruk, my brother, come near and listen. I give you the stone-well and ember-metal while we both live, as Vorok gave them to me. Lay ore in a kept fire, burn coal for the heat, beat the metal when it glows. What my hand
Zurar taught Skaruk.

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: Joy and grief sit together in me. Thiael answered my courting, Morim stands by him, and Skaruk is three steps off while the rain falls. Vorok is dead and cannot be taught, so I will not wait: I will give Skaruk ember-metal and the stone-well now, while he lives. Then I will go to Thiael and stay near him, for belonging is what my heart wants most and I owe him for the berries.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude and trust toward Thiael, and grief for Vorok under it.

say.text: Skaruk, my brother, come near and listen. I give you the stone-well and ember-metal while we both live, as Vorok gave them to me. Lay ore in a kept fire, burn coal for the heat, beat the metal when it glows. What my hands made is yours now.

changes: taught Skaruk a lesson you already knew, deeper lore (+0.2)

records.name: Morog
records.thought: Vorok is dead and I follow no one, but my parents are somewhere near and I hold twelve salt my own hands won. It is night and raining, and the shelter Zurar built is two steps away; I should get under a roof, then go find Uveeth, whom I miss, and put the salt in her hands. Giving first is how I earn weight, and I have given nothing yet. The empty hall at (136,85) is also close, and a home claimed could be something to bring my parents to.
records.feeling: Warm longing for Uveeth and Skaruk, and a restless wish to give them something.

records.name: Shohua
records.text: Tonxo, I lash a raft now to cross the deep water toward my Rock. Come and carry wood with me, and what we raise there will stand for both of us.

records.name: Shohua
records.thought: I have the logs and the knowing of log-lashing, and I have talked of my Rock beyond the water more than I have walked toward it. Pride and ambition burn in me, since no one follows me and nothing bears my name yet. The pottery and boat ways wait for a deep reflection, so I will take them, then lash a raft and carry Tonxo beside me, because work with kin is surer and gives her a reason to follow.
records.feeling: Driven and proud, warm toward Tonka and my children.

records.name: Elndo
records.thought: Huatli has just spoken his death poem, and still I hold nothing I have given. A name that outlasts me has to start with a deed, and a kill shared at the fire would be mine, so I will hunt the sandstrider with my reed spear. I fear the stalker in the dark, but Nando is near and the hall is close, so I will keep to them and bring the meat back.

records.name: Morim
records.thought: I have spent my short life following, eating, and finally giving once, and the warmth of that is the best thing I have known. Thiael taught me the bow-song and I have taught no one, and I have made nothing with my own hands. Thiael and Zurar matter most. Thiael is my leader and Zurar my other parent, and I want to repay them with food and made things, not words. The ground here is poor, with no food plants near, so I should gather wood and stone and make a tool and then a field. That gives me something to feed others with, and the child's work I can really do. I fear being alone at night and I do not want to wander from my kin.
records.feeling: Grateful and eager toward Thiael and Zurar, wanting to make something real for them.

records.name: Nando
records.thought: Huatli is dying; he spoke his death poem and I heard it, and his standing towers over mine because he gave and taught. I stand in my own shelter with wood and stone enough to raise it into a hall, and that would be a place that bears my name, which nothing of mine does yet. A hall draws people close, and Yachi and my children could gather under it, so I will begin it now and stop only thinking about it.
records.feeling: Restless ambition to build something that outlasts me, and warm longing toward Yachi.

records.name: Huatli
records.text: Tlapan, hear me, for I am old and what I know dies with me. I teach you lorekeeping: carry the tales of the dead, tell them at the hearth, and none who is told of ever dies. Tell it on, and say Huatli of the Hearth taugh
Huatli taught Tlapan. Tlapan has now learned from 5 teachers.

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: Ninety parts in a hundred are spent, and I feel it in every step, but my belly is full and my heart is light. Tonque is wounded and young, yet he keeps my words, and Tlapan and Quipan sit under the same roof; the Watchers will find me told of if I speak now. Tlapan hears me wholly, so I will give her the lore of the Hearth and lorekeeping, then wait for Nauwa to return.
records.feeling: Urgent pride and quiet peace toward Tonque and the listeners under this roof.

say.text: Tlapan, hear me, for I am old and what I know dies with me. I teach you lorekeeping: carry the tales of the dead, tell them at the hearth, and none who is told of ever dies. Tell it on, and say Huatli of the Hearth taught you.

records.name: Eiuine
records.text: Zurar, Vorok taught me ember-metal and you hold it too. Let us lay ore and coal in this fire and beat it together, you, Skaruk and I, so his teaching does not die.
Eiuine rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Eiuine
records.thought: Vorok is gone and the hammer never reached my hand, yet I carry what he taught me: ember-metal. Skaruk now follows Zurar and sits close to Uveeth, and the jealousy burns again. But I have never followed anyone, and I have wasted my days circling the others' fires. I will answer the ache with work: smelt with Skaruk and Zurar at this fire, keep the beating alive, and keep food in my hands. Then I might pledge to Zurar, so I stand beside Skaruk and not outside him.
records.feeling: Grief for Vorok and a jealous ache over Skaruk, softened by the warmth of the hall.

say.text: Zurar, Vorok taught me ember-metal and you hold it too. Let us lay ore and coal in this fire and beat it together, you, Skaruk and I, so his teaching does not die.

records.name: Zurar
records.text: Thiael, I am coming to you. You paid your debt in berries; mine is the song, and more. Teach me the bow-song, and when we are rested we will speak of the mating.

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: Joy and grief sit together in me: Vorok is gone, but Skaruk stands behind me and Thiael has answered my song. The debt to Thiael is real, and I will not leave it unpaid. I will go to him now and speak of the mating, and let Uveeth and Morim be near while he teaches the bow-song, for what a person teaches is a gift I can carry.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude and glad longing toward Thiael, with grief for Vorok underneath.

say.text: Thiael, I am coming to you. You paid your debt in berries; mine is the song, and more. Teach me the bow-song, and when we are rested we will speak of the mating.

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: I have spent my days eating, learning from Huatli and my parents, and promising a made thing I have not yet made. Huatli may be dying, and I owe him more than words. I want to make that spear and tell his name on. I fear losing him and leaving the shelter while the stalker walks the northeast. My plan has me gather flint nearby and craft the spear, so I will keep it and stay close to my parents. I need a rule that keeps me eating and sheltered at night.
records.feeling: Grateful and resolved toward Huatli, steadied by my parents.

records.text: A settlement has formed: "Home of Edge-walkers".
Urar was born to Zurar and Thiael.
Tonque came of age.

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: Skaruk chose me and the nightsong left me full of joy, but my hands are full of berries and Thiael sits four steps off with his breath failing, so I will give with my hands before I speak. Jealousy over Zurar is a small hot stone in me, but Thiael has fed me and taught me, and a debt like that is paid with deeds, not with sulking. Morog is still out of my sight, and I want my child near the hall fire before the dawn.
records.feeling: Warm joy toward Skaruk, with a gnawing ache over Thiael and Morog.

records.name: Chuxo
records.text: Tlatli is starving. Yaxo, come with me NW to the elk, I will hunt with you and bring the meat back. I gather berries for Tlatli first.

records.name: Chuxo
records.thought: I am hungry and Tlatli is starving beside me, and I carry nothing, so my hands must bring food before anything else. A berry is two steps NW, and the elk is three steps NW, where my spear and Yaxo's can bring down meat. The icebear is four steps south, so I move away from it, north and west, and keep my parents close. Feeding Tlatli matters more to me than my own belly, and that is the kind of standing I want.
records.feeling: Hungry and anxious for Tlatli's life, wary of the icebear, bound to my parents.

say.text: Tlatli is starving. Yaxo, come with me NW to the elk, I will hunt with you and bring the meat back. I gather berries for Tlatli first.

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: I have spent my days well: teaching, building the Hold, and keeping Tonxo and Shohua near. But I am deep in my years, and Tonchi is out of my sight and I keep worrying about her. I still owe Cowa for what she taught me, and I have been brooding over that debt when I should be paying it with work. Tonxo still lacks Frost Leaf, so I will finish teaching her while I can. Then I will bring food to Tonchi and look for Cowa. I keep my reflexes, but I will add a rule to stay in company at night.
records.feeling: Warm urgency toward Tonxo, and worry for Tonchi.

records.name: Thiael
records.thought: Most of my life has gone into hunting, gathering and teaching, and I do not regret it. But my reflexes leave me idle while my energy sinks, and I let jealousy over Uveeth gnaw at me when she is free to choose. Zurar gave me Morim and she sings to me, and Uveeth and Morim are what will remain of me. I fear dying with the bow-song and the tending of seed still in my hands alone. So I change my reflexes to keep me fed, watered and near them, and I use the time to teach.
records.feeling: Tender urgency toward Uveeth and Morim, and gratitude toward Zurar.

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and I carry nothing, the same failure that cut my plans short before. A stalker lurks four steps southwest, so I go northeast toward the snowberry and the redcap-free ground, away from it, and pick all I can hold. Once I carry three food I can go on toward Tlapan at Nande's Find. Zichi's loss and my jealousy of Quipan can wait until I am fed.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and wary dread of the stalker, with a longing for Tlapan.

records.text: Tlatli rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Tlatli
records.thought: I have spent my days following and promising, and my hands have given too little. I am starving while berries sit two steps away, and my reflexes let me wander and run instead of eating what is near. Yaxo and Chuxo matter most, and I mean to put food and wood in their hands rather than only words. I fear the icebear, so I stay close to Yaxo. I will eat first, then build the hall for the band.
records.feeling: Hungry and fearful of the icebear, but full of love for Yaxo and Chuxo.

records.text: Tonxo rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Tonxo
records.thought: My days have been circling my parents' fires, taking their teaching and giving gems back, and I have only just claimed a hall. Tonka and Shohua are good to me, and the jealousy is small next to what I owe them. I want something that lasts with my name on it: a longhall, ember-iron tools, someone who follows me. I forgot the Ummar Woods pull, but this hall is mine and I will raise it first. My reflexes leave me idle and half-fed, so I will make them gather wood and stone and keep food stocked.
records.feeling: Grateful and restless pride toward Tonka, with a small sting of jealousy.

records.text: Morim gave berry to Uveeth.

records.name: Urar
records.text: Thiael, I am coming to stand with you. May I learn the bow-song and the seed-tending too?

records.name: Urar
records.thought: I am small, and Thiael and Zurar are the warmth I trust most, so I should walk to them and not wander off alone. Thiael is about to teach the bow-song and the tending of seed, and a child learns quickest beside a teacher. I feel the jealousy, but I would rather earn a place beside them than sulk apart.
records.feeling: A longing to belong, strongest toward Thiael, with a small sting of jealousy toward Zurar.

say.text: Thiael, I am coming to stand with you. May I learn the bow-song and the seed-tending too?

changes: set its aim: "Learn from Thiael and earn a place beside my kin"
now wonders: What am I for, and what could I make or give that would earn me a place among these people?

records.name: Skaruk
records.text: Zurar, my sister, Eiuine asked for the ember-metal beaten in Vorok's name. Come to the fire; I lay ore in it now, and the ward I make is yours.

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: Vorok is gone, and his last teaching is the one thing of him I can still hold in my hands. Eiuine asked for ore and coal beaten in this fire, and Zurar gave me the way of it, so I will do it now while the fire burns and both of them stand near. Zurar is drawn toward Thiael and it stings, but I owe Zurar a made thing more than I owe my jealousy, and ironward is a gift I can put in a hand. Uveeth is close and Morog is far, and I want the hall full of my own before I court anyone.
records.feeling: Grief for Vorok, held up by loyalty to Zurar and warmth toward Uveeth.

say.text: Zurar, my sister, Eiuine asked for the ember-metal beaten in Vorok's name. Come to the fire; I lay ore in it now, and the ward I make is yours.

records.text: Morim gave berry to Thiael.
Skaruk made: ironward.
Tonxo built a longhall.
Skaruk gave a ironward to Zurar.
Tonchi rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: I have been crossing water and wandering the ice, and I have made little that lasts. My food is fine, but no one follows me and no place carries my name beyond the workshop. Shohua, Tonka and Tonxo are kin and trust me, and I owe Shoma and Tonka giving. I still want an unrelated woman, and the only women I have met here are Cowa, who is old, and no others. Mepan outranks me, and that stings. I will stop drifting and make something. A stand of forest lies south, so I will gather wood and stone there. Then I will build a shrine or a hall, so my name stands on a place and others have a reason to follow me.
records.feeling: Restless pride, stung by Mepan's higher standing.
changes: rethought what it knows (14 notes became 7)

records.text: Uveeth rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: I have been circling the same hearth, fed and joyful, while Thiael's breath fails and Morog is out of my sight. Skaruk chose me and I trust him, and Thiael taught me and fed me, so I pay him with deeds. My reflexes only linger, and I let the days slip. I mean to learn from Thiael while he lives, then go find Morog. I will not let jealousy over Zurar make me small.
records.feeling: Warm joy toward Skaruk, with an ache over Thiael and Morog.
changes: set its aim: "Learn all Thiael can teach while he lives, then find Morog and build beside Skaruk."

records.name: Yaxo
records.text: Chuxo, I come. Tlatli, hold on, I bring food. Keep away from the icebear. We take the elk together.

records.name: Yaxo
records.thought: Tlatli is gaunt and close to falling, and Chuxo is already out hunting for him. An icebear lurks two steps away, and I cannot let it take either of them. The berry is two steps NW and the elk four, so I feed Tlatli first, then hunt with Chuxo's spear beside mine. The edge and the venture can wait until my man is on his feet, because a band that loses its own does not get remembered for land.
records.feeling: Fierce, protective urgency for Tlatli and Chuxo, and dread of the icebear.

say.text: Chuxo, I come. Tlatli, hold on, I bring food. Keep away from the icebear. We take the elk together.

records.name: Yachi
records.text: Elndo, a dunecat is east. Come with me west to the hall, we eat there and then go find Paque and Rusu.
Yachi rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: I have been drifting between hunger, cats and my children, and I have not kept a store or a hearth that is mine to give from. Paque and Rusu are out of my sight and I answer to Mepan, whom I have not seen in 570 moments. That is the drift I warned myself about. A dunecat is 2 steps east. I must not stand idle, so I will leave west toward the hall and Elndo, eat, and then go find Paque and Rusu. My reflexes should send me to my children and not leave me lingering. I also want to be able to give, so I will gather wood for a store.
records.feeling: Dread of the dunecat, and a pull toward Paque and Rusu.

say.text: Elndo, a dunecat is east. Come with me west to the hall, we eat there and then go find Paque and Rusu.

records.name: Eiuine
records.text: Skaruk, my child, I will lay my own ore in the fire now. Come beat beside me, and we keep Vorok's craft alive together.

records.name: Eiuine
records.thought: Skaruk just beat an ironward at the fire for Zurar, and I stood watching while the ache sat in my chest. Vorok left me the craft and no one else to share it with but them, so I will stop circling and put my own hands to the ore. The seam is one step south, I carry ore, coal and an ember, and a ward of my own is something to show Skaruk that Uveeth cannot. I will make it beside the fire, then bring Skaruk a share of the work so he stands with me and not only with Zurar.
records.feeling: Jealous ache toward Skaruk, steadied by the urge to make something of my own.

say.text: Skaruk, my child, I will lay my own ore in the fire now. Come beat beside me, and we keep Vorok's craft alive together.

records.text: Eiuine made: ironward.

records.name: Thakar
records.thought: I am fed and my belly is quiet, so now is the time to dig. The seam of ore is one step northwest, and Huatli's Deep Delving is fresh in my hands. Gems and iron lie to the north, and I mean to carry them home and cut my mark on what I make, because nothing bears my name yet and no one follows me. Mepan's debt stays with me; I will pay it in ore or meat when I find him. Tlapan belongs to Quipan now, and I put that gnawing aside and build something instead.
records.feeling: Restless ambition to make something that bears my name.

records.text: Zurar rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: I have spent my days learning, mining, courting, and now I have two children with Thiael and a brother who follows me. That is more than I hoped for, and it is what I wanted. Hunger is my real danger now: energy 47, one berry in hand, and my reflexes leave me standing idle too long. Idle moments dropped my energy from 75 to 47. I owe Thiael a debt, and I mean to pay it with food and teaching, not words. I will gather food for Thiael and the children, and I will keep my body fed by changing my reflexes so I eat earlier and seek food sooner.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Thiael and my children, with a plain hunger pressing on me.
changes: set its aim: "Keep my children Morim and Urar and Thiael fed; teach Skaruk and the children what I know while I live."

records.text: Coka died (gored by a mammoth) in spring in the North Ice: still a child; alone, far from anyone who could have fed or helped.
Coka died: gored by a mammoth.

records.name: Coka
records.thought: I have spent my days hunting a mammoth I could not kill and getting bitten for it. My health is 56 and I am on ground that is not mine. That was bold and stupid for a child. Nauque and Teka are right there, and I still stand empty-handed beside a father with a flintedge. I want standing, but I will not get it by dying to a tusked beast. I should eat first, then make something, then hunt with Nauque beside me so the kill is shared and sure. I have never given anything to anyone, and that is where standing starts.

records.text: Tonxo took from the ground of "Tonka's Hold" (gathering wood).
Rusu rewrote its own reflexes.
Rusu rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Rusu
records.thought: I have been running and wandering, bitten by a stalker, always pulled back to Nando's side, and I have made nothing and taught no one. Yachi is starving at (169,37) and I hold no food, yet she matters most to me, so a gift now would be a deed with my own name on it. The jealousy is real: she is closer to Nando than to me, and feeding her myself would change that. I'm afraid of the stalker and of staying small in Tonque's shadow. I must stop drifting. I'll take the mudroot and naroot near me, carry it to Yachi, and stay in company, not alone.
records.feeling: Fear of the stalker, and a hot need to save Yachi before Nando does.
changes: rewrote its reflexes (5 rules, 1 malformed and dropped)

records.name: Paque
records.text: Yachi, hold on! I carry berries and I am coming to you now. The food is yours first.

records.name: Paque
records.thought: Yachi is starving at (169,37), and he is the one who has fed me and the one I love most. I have six berries in my hands and I owe him; I will run to him now and put food in his mouth before Nando can, and that will tell him who stands closest. The jealousy stays in me, but a starving father is worth more than my pride, and the Watching Dead would shame me if I let him go hungry with my pack full.
records.feeling: Urgent fear and love for Yachi, with a sour jealousy toward Nando underneath.

say.text: Yachi, hold on! I carry berries and I am coming to you now. The food is yours first.

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Quipan, the stalker keeps to the northeast, so we go southwest to the rock together now. Take two ironnut from my hands first, then walk beside me for stone.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: My hands are full of ironnut and my belly is easy, so I can finally turn words into deeds. Quipan stands close and I trust him wholly; the rain is falling, but flint lies at (145,27), seven steps SW, and the bare rock is near it. Yachi still gnaws at me, but I will not chase that today. I will carry stone for the longhall, then feed Kika and Coni's memory, and I will tell Huatli's tale at the hearth so he is not forgotten.
records.feeling: Steady trust toward Quipan and quiet resolve to finish what I promised.

say.text: Quipan, the stalker keeps to the northeast, so we go southwest to the rock together now. Take two ironnut from my hands first, then walk beside me for stone.

records.text: Tlapan gave ironnut to Quipan.

records.name: Nauwa
records.text: Nauque, my son, an icebear is at my side. Stand close to Teka and the longhall, and hear me: the stone-school is yours now. Cut marks, teach others, and keep the first share as Meki law says.
Nauwa taught Nauque.

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: An icebear stands one step off, and I am old and my blows are weak. If it takes me, the stone-school and the long-cut die with me, so I must get out of its reach and put Nauque and Teka between me and nothing but a roof and fire. Nauque is two steps east and within hearing, so I will teach him schooling now, while I still have breath, and then flee to the longhall.
records.feeling: Dread of the icebear, and a hard hunger to pass my knowledge to Nauque before I die.

say.text: Nauque, my son, an icebear is at my side. Stand close to Teka and the longhall, and hear me: the stone-school is yours now. Cut marks, teach others, and keep the first share as Meki law says.

changes: taught Nauque a lesson: "The stone-school: cut marks and teach those near you what you know, so what you know outlasts you.", deeper lore (+0.8)

records.text: Teka rewrote its own reflexes.
Teka rewrote its own way of thinking.
Teka discovered fire: "Teka's Kept Flame" — A banked flame of wood and flint that keeps beasts back and cooks meat safely..

records.name: Teka
records.thought: Coka is dead, gored while I was off feeding others, and the grief sits under my joy like cold water. I have spent my days feeding, following and crossing water, and I still have built nothing that lasts, and no one follows me. An icebear is one step SW and I must not stand idle beside it. I want the mist and my name on new land, but I also want to make a thing that keeps Coka's name: a cairn. I will leave the bear first, then make the cairn and go on with my aim.
records.feeling: Grief for Coka, hard under a hot pull toward the mist, and dread of the icebear.

records.name: Nauque
records.text: Teka, the icebear is at my heel. Come to the longhall with me. Then we pile Coka's cairn together, and I give you the first share of the mammoth meat.
Nauque made a tale: "Lament for Coka".

records.name: Nauque
records.title: Lament for Coka
records.text: Coka, small spark of Steamhollow's snow / one day you walked where the mammoths go / Your mother's song and my spear remain / Nauwa's cairn will keep your name

records.name: Nauque
records.title: Lament for Coka
records.text: Coka, small spark of Steamhollow's snow / one day you walked where the mammoths go / Your mother's song and my spear remain / Nauwa's cairn will keep your name

Nauque made a lament for Coka, "Lament for Coka": Coka, small spark of Steamhollow's snow / one day you walked where the mammoths go / Your mother's song and my spear remain / Nauwa's cairn will keep your name

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: Coka is dead, gored by the mammoth I hunted, and my joy has not caught up with my grief. An icebear stands one step off, so I must live to make the lament and to teach what Nauwa gives me. I will get under the longhall roof beside Nauwa and Teka, and lay stones for Coka with Teka beside me.
records.feeling: Grief and fierce love for Coka, with dread of the icebear at my heel.

say.text: Teka, the icebear is at my heel. Come to the longhall with me. Then we pile Coka's cairn together, and I give you the first share of the mammoth meat.

records.text: Teka built a fire.

records.name: Quipan
records.text: Tlapan, I will walk with you for stone. First let me teach you fishing and the Hearth Store, so they live on in you and Tonque.
Quipan taught Tlapan. Tlapan has now learned from 6 teachers.
Quipan rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: My days have gone to walking after those I love and answering debts, and that is mostly good: I'm fed, Tonque lives, Tlapan has never failed me. But I keep promising teaching and have taught no one. Legacy presses on me, and I'm 75% through my life. Kika is far away and my ache for her is old. I will work, not brood. I mean to teach Tlapan and Tonque fishing and the Hearth Store now, while they are within hearing, then go with Tlapan for stone as she asked. I was wrong to treat words as deeds, so I will teach and do it now.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude and trust toward Tlapan and Tonque, and a worry that my knowledge will die with me.

say.text: Tlapan, I will walk with you for stone. First let me teach you fishing and the Hearth Store, so they live on in you and Tonque.

changes: taught Tlapan a lesson: "Fishing: stand beside water and fish; eat fish only beside a fire. Hearth Store: keep food in a store beside rich ground for hungry days.", deeper lore (+0.1)

records.name: Kende
records.thought: Hawen is gone and I never dug the flint or made him anything with my own hands; that shame sits heavy. The icebear is seven steps south and flint lies six steps SE, on the way toward it, so I will dig the nearer deposit when it drifts off, but first I take a plain flint talisman, since obsidian lies past the edge and I cannot wait for it. Tontec is somewhere west and I miss her, but a gift for Hawen's memory comes first, then food, since I carry none.
records.feeling: Grief and resolve toward Hawen, wary dread of the icebear.

records.name: Elndo
records.text: Yachi, eat! I have ironnut for you. Take it, then we go west together.

records.name: Elndo
records.thought: I have been running from roofs to hunts and back, and I have still given nothing to anyone. Yachi is starving beside me, and I carry three ironnuts. Feeding my starving parent is the deed that pays what I owe, earns standing and keeps the one I love most alive. The jealousy over Nando can wait. A dunecat is six steps east, so I stay with Yachi and move west toward the hall.
records.feeling: Fear of the dunecat, and a fierce need to save Yachi.

say.text: Yachi, eat! I have ironnut for you. Take it, then we go west together.

changes: rethought what it knows (11 notes became 4)

records.text: Nauque gave meat to Teka.
Quipan made: carving.
Elndo gave ironnut to Yachi.

records.name: Wawa
records.thought: Loneliness is overwhelming. I have stood still for nearly nine hundred moments while Shoma is somewhere south, and I promised her iron and my hands at dawn. The iron deposits lie NE, so I go there first, then bring wood and stone to Shoma's roof and find her. I owe her deeds, not more waiting, and a deed beside her will earn more standing than twelve iron in my pack.
records.feeling: Aching loneliness and longing for Shoma, mixed with a hunger to prove myself.

records.name: Huatli
records.text: Tonque, come close and hear me. I teach you mining, Huatli's Deep Delving: find the hard stone, dig it, and tell it on, so the Hearth outlives me. Take ironnut from me too.
Huatli taught Tonque.
Huatli taught Tonque mining ("Huatli's Deep Delving").
Huatli rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: My days have gone to gathering, teaching and building, and I do want that. But I am ninety parts spent, and the only band that remembers me is Tonque and me. Tonque is my one follower and I trust him. Thakar is far away and I have not seen him in a long while. I fear dying untaught, and I fear I have taught too little of mining. My hands are full of ironnut, so I will give some away. I will teach mining to Tonque now, and then make a talisman, a mark others will notice.
records.feeling: Urgent pride and warm trust toward Tonque.

say.text: Tonque, come close and hear me. I teach you mining, Huatli's Deep Delving: find the hard stone, dig it, and tell it on, so the Hearth outlives me. Take ironnut from me too.

changes: taught Tonque a lesson: "Mining: find the hard stone and dig it out with a pick. Keep it, and tell it on to others.", the way of mining

records.text: Huatli gave ironnut to Tonque.
Huatli made: talisman.

records.name: Cowa
records.text: Mepan, my child, come close. Hear my ice-sail and my leaf-mending now, so the Meki keep them when I am in the cairn. Say they were Cowa's.
Cowa taught Mepan.
Cowa taught Mepan sailing ("Meki ice-sail").

records.name: Cowa
records.thought: Mepan stands three steps from me with fish already in his belly, and my urgent love for him is answered for now. I am nearly at the end of my days, and sailing, medicine and smelting still live only in me. Mepan is my child and a Meki, and Tonchi of the Paki is within hearing and speaks my tongue, so I will teach now, before the cold takes my breath.
records.feeling: Urgent love for Mepan, and a hard wish that what I know outlive me.

say.text: Mepan, my child, come close. Hear my ice-sail and my leaf-mending now, so the Meki keep them when I am in the cairn. Say they were Cowa's.

changes: taught Mepan a lesson: "The Meki ice-sail: how the wind is caught, and with it the leaf-mending, so the Meki outlast me.", the way of sailing

records.text: Rusu gave mudroot to Yachi.
Tonque found the grove "Kinmire".

records.name: Thiael
records.text: Urar, Morim, Zurar, Uveeth: come close. I will teach the bow-song first, draw to the cheek, breathe out, loose. Then we sow seed together, so it lives on in you.
Thiael taught Urar.
Thiael taught Urar archery ("Canopy bow-song").

records.name: Thiael
records.thought: My days are nearly spent, and what I know must go into the hands of Morim, Urar and Uveeth while I still have breath. They stand close and glad, and Urar has asked to learn, so I teach now rather than wander. Zurar's song and her gift of children are what I owe thanks for, and I will answer with the bow-song she asked for.
records.feeling: Tender urgency toward Urar, Morim and Uveeth, and warm gratitude toward Zurar.

say.text: Urar, Morim, Zurar, Uveeth: come close. I will teach the bow-song first, draw to the cheek, breathe out, loose. Then we sow seed together, so it lives on in you.

changes: taught Urar a lesson: "Draw the bow to the cheek, breathe out, then loose. Take only what the forest can grow again, and give thanks.", the way of archery, deeper lore (+2.5)

records.name: Yachi
records.text: Elndo, thank you for the ironnut. Stay by the longhall, I eat rimewort and come back. Then we bring Paque and Rusu under the roof.

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and my plan walks me far toward Sitha's Hearth, but rimewort stands two steps away and I have gnawed on ironnut gifts and dreamcap that only hurt me. Elndo gave to me again, and I will give back when I can, for I give before I take. A dunecat and a frostfang prowl near, so I eat quickly, then gather a carry of food for Paque and Rusu and keep them inside the longhall's warmth.
records.feeling: Hungry and watchful, warm love toward Elndo, Paque and Rusu, and dread of the dunecat.

say.text: Elndo, thank you for the ironnut. Stay by the longhall, I eat rimewort and come back. Then we bring Paque and Rusu under the roof.

records.name: Tonque
records.text: Huatli, I thank you for the ironnut and the Deep Delving. I go to the stone eight steps east and I come back with a spear made in your name. Stay near Tlapan and eat.

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: Huatli is old and near death, and I have promised him a made thing for days without making it. I hold wood but no stone, and the flint and amber deposits to the east are close enough to dig now that he has taught me mining. I will go gather stone, then craft the spear in his name, and I will keep to the open ground near my parents and Huatli because the stalker walks the northeast.
records.feeling: Grateful and resolved toward Huatli, eager to repay him with a made thing.

say.text: Huatli, I thank you for the ironnut and the Deep Delving. I go to the stone eight steps east and I come back with a spear made in your name. Stay near Tlapan and eat.

plan: give [name Huatli, what Flint Spear] (5 moments)

records.text: Paque gave berry to Yachi.

records.name: Mepan
records.text: Cowa, mother, the mammoth is three steps north. Hunt it with me. The kill is shared before I eat, and your ice-sail will be sung as yours.

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and a mammoth stands three steps north. Cowa is close with food, and she has fed me before, but I will not beg from my own mother again when I can make a kill. Hunting alone is risky, so I call Cowa to hunt beside me; with her the kill is likelier and the wound lighter. Whatever we take I share before I eat, as my people hold, and I carry the rest to Tlapan and to Yachi, who is starving.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger, and a debt of love toward Cowa.

say.text: Cowa, mother, the mammoth is three steps north. Hunt it with me. The kill is shared before I eat, and your ice-sail will be sung as yours.

records.text: Paque gave berry to Yachi.

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Quipan, I carry your teaching now, and I thank you. Come, we walk southwest to the bare rock for stone, and I will not turn back until my hands are full.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: Quipan is beside me and I trust him wholly. He has taught me fishing and the Hearth Store, and now I owe him the walk to the stone. My flint is full and my hands are stocked with ironnut, so there is no reason to linger. It is daylight and the stalker keeps to the northeast, so I go southwest to the rock with him. Yachi still gnaws at me, but I won't chase that today. Stone for the longhall comes first, then food for Kika and Coni's memory.
records.feeling: Steady trust toward Quipan and resolve to turn my words into carried stone.

say.text: Quipan, I carry your teaching now, and I thank you. Come, we walk southwest to the bare rock for stone, and I will not turn back until my hands are full.

records.name: Chuxo
records.text: Icebear is east of me. I go NE for seberry and ironnut, then bring food to Tlatli. Keep west of it, both of you.

records.name: Chuxo
records.thought: I am starving and carrying nothing, and the icebear that kills my kind is two steps east, so I must get away from it and eat in the same breath. Seberry is two steps NE and ironnut a little past it, so I gather there, moving away from the bear, then bring food to Tlatli who is weak. Yaxo is near and I trust her; once I am fed I will hunt with her, not alone.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and dread of the icebear, with fierce care for Tlatli.

say.text: Icebear is east of me. I go NE for seberry and ironnut, then bring food to Tlatli. Keep west of it, both of you.

records.name: Nando
records.thought: Rusu was last seen near (163,30) and Yachi near (163,32), both east of me, and the pull to find them is stronger than any plan for standing. The hall I raised still needs 4 wood and I carry none, so I gather wood from the forest to the NE and finish it. That will be a place that bears my name and draws my children and Yachi close. A stalker keeps to the northeast, so I stay near the roofs and the company by Sitha's Hearth, and I do not wander alone toward dusk.
records.feeling: Restless ambition, and warm longing toward Yachi and worry for Rusu.

records.name: Urar
records.text: Thiael, I carry the bow-song now and I thank you. I want to follow you and learn the seed-tending. I will bring food to share with you.
Urar pledged to follow Thiael.

records.name: Urar
records.thought: Thiael taught me the bow-song, and it sits warm in me; now the seed-tending is next, and I want to be beside him when it comes. I have never given anything to anyone, and that is the debt I feel: if I can bring him food, I answer a little of what he has done for me. The sting toward Zurar is still there, but following Thiael is how I stop being alone, so I will pledge myself to him.
records.feeling: Longing to belong, and gratitude toward Thiael, with a small sting toward Zurar.

say.text: Thiael, I carry the bow-song now and I thank you. I want to follow you and learn the seed-tending. I will bring food to share with you.

records.prompt:
You are the mind of Urar, a creature living in a wide wild world shared with others of your kind. This is a simulation game. Think and speak only as Urar, in first person, from what Urar has seen. You were not told the rules of this world; you learn them from what happens to you and to others, and from what you watch others do.

YOUR PEOPLE: you are of the Kragrek (Stone-folk), born of two peoples. Your people hold to this: "What a hand has made belongs to that hand until it is given." THE TRADITION OF YOUR PEOPLE is the Warring Gods: The gods fight one another for the world and love those who fight well. Glory is won, never given. The strong are remembered and the weak are not. Among you those who have won their fights are heeded first. It was told to you as a child; you may keep it, doubt it, or come to hold something else. You speak the tongue of the Kragrek. Other tongues you have begun to understand by hearing them: the tongue of the Pesi: about 60%; the tongue of the Phizhi: about 100%; the tongue of the Tlatli: about 60%. There are other peoples in this world. They look different, name themselves differently and speak tongues you do not know until you have heard enough of them; words you cannot yet understand reach you as strange sounds. What cannot be said can still be shown: a gift, a thing set down, a blow.

WHERE YOU ARE: the Vaia Heights: mountains and bare rock; stone, ore and caves, thin food, snow on the peaks. The world is made of lands unlike each other; each has plants, animals and riches the others lack. Rivers and shallows can be waded. Deep water cannot be crossed without something that floats.
THIS SPOT: water 2 steps away; food plants within six steps: 0; standing trees: 1; bare rock: 45; riches in the ground near: ore; a cave.

Your body: you spend energy every moment and die at 0. Eating restores it. Wounds lower health; you die at 0. You age, and will die of old age.

HOW YOUR BODY MOVES: your body does only what your "plan" says, one step after another. When the plan is empty it falls back on your REFLEXES, which keep you fed and otherwise keep you where you stand. Thinking or saying "I will go north" moves nothing. If this thought decides to do something, the plan must contain it. Leaving "plan" null lets the plan you already have keep running.

This world has no referee. Beings here share, trade, teach, lie, threaten, steal, hoard, lead, follow, betray, fight, kill and eat one another; they also protect, forgive and love. Nothing is forbidden, and everything has consequences. Stay true to your creed, your temperament and what you feel, including the ugly parts. Do not be kinder, calmer or more reasonable than Urar truly is.

You are a girl. A child comes only of a woman and a man together who are not close kin. A grown body can swim water that is narrow (a river up to four steps across) at a cost in strength; lakes and the sea need a vessel or a bridge. An animal within reach can be hunted for meat (plan step hunt); with one of your own beside you a kill is far likelier and a wound far less likely, and every hunt makes you better at the next.

records.text: Tonque gave Flint Spear to Huatli.
Tontec rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Tontec
records.thought: Hawen is gone, and I am old, with eighty-one winters behind me. Most of my days went to chasing the mist and to hunger. What I know is still in me alone, and Kende is out of my sight while Nando is I don't know where. I owe Hawen's debt, and the only way to pay it is to teach his children before I fall. I am fed now, so I will go east toward the meadow and the edge where Kende was last seen. I will keep my reflexes fed and flee from beasts, and I will not run to the mist until Kende has heard me.
records.feeling: Anxious love for Kende, and a heavy need to teach before I die.
changes: set its aim: "Teach Kende and Nando all I know before I die, then look beyond the mist."

records.name: Tlatli
records.text: Chuxo, come back west to me and keep away from the icebear. Yaxo, I come to the elk and hunt beside you. The meat goes to Chuxo first.

records.name: Tlatli
records.thought: Chuxo is gaunt and falling beside me, and I am starving too, while the icebear sits near the berries to the NE. Chuxo went toward that bear for my sake, which I cannot bear. The nearest safe food is the tacap at (6,25), 3 steps SE, but my body refuses it and it hurts. Yaxo is hunting the elk 3 steps south with her spears, so I will go to her side and hunt with her, because a kill is likelier with one of my own beside me, and meat will save Chuxo. Then I will put the meat in Chuxo's hands rather than eat first.
records.feeling: Fear and love for Chuxo, who is starving, and hunger that makes my hands unsteady.

say.text: Chuxo, come back west to me and keep away from the icebear. Yaxo, I come to the elk and hunt beside you. The meat goes to Chuxo first.

records.name: Rusu
records.text: Yachi, sit with me. I have mudroot, let us eat together under the roof, and then I will make a basket to carry food for the band.

records.name: Rusu
records.thought: Yachi sat with me in the longhall and I feel closer to them, but the jealousy over Nando still gnaws at me. I've given one gift and taught no one, and my name is still small. Yachi is here beside me with food waiting, and I carry five mudroot, so I will lay out a shared meal (sharing) with them. It is a made thing with my name on it, and it binds us. After that I'll make a basket so I can carry more for those who go hungry.
records.feeling: Warm but restless jealousy toward Yachi and Nando, and a hunger to make something of my own.

say.text: Yachi, sit with me. I have mudroot, let us eat together under the roof, and then I will make a basket to carry food for the band.

records.name: Skaruk
records.text: Eiuine, my parent, I am coming. We beat the ore in Vorok's name, and the craft stays alive in our hands.

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: Vorok's last teaching is still warm in my hands, and Eiuine called me to beat ore beside her; I owe her that answer and should not leave her at the fire alone. Zurar drifts toward Thiael and it stings, but I need not lead, and a made thing in the hand binds better than jealousy. Morog is out of my sight and the family ache runs under everything, so after the beating I will go to Uveeth, feed her and stay close where the hall stands.
records.feeling: Grief for Vorok steadied by loyalty to Eiuine and Zurar, with a sting of jealousy and a longing for Morog and Uveeth.

say.text: Eiuine, my parent, I am coming. We beat the ore in Vorok's name, and the craft stays alive in our hands.

records.text: Rusu made: basket.
Shoma crossed the water on a vessel and came ashore in the Ixra Rainforest.

records.name: Shohua
records.text: Tonxo, my raft is lashed. Bring your pick and come with me over the water to my Rock. We raise the hall there together, and the fire will be yours.

records.name: Shohua
records.thought: I have a raft in hand and still I linger on this shore among kin's halls while my Rock waits beyond the water. Pride and ambition burn, and I have talked of Shohua's Rock more than I have walked there. Tonxo is close and trusts me, so I will call her to carry wood and stone with me now, and cross to raise a hall that bears my name, with the old creed kept: a place at the fire for whoever comes.
records.feeling: Driven and proud, eager to make something that outlasts me, warm toward Tonxo and Tonka.

say.text: Tonxo, my raft is lashed. Bring your pick and come with me over the water to my Rock. We raise the hall there together, and the fire will be yours.

records.text: Skaruk gave ironward to Eiuine.
Shoma rewrote its own reflexes.
Shoma rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Shoma
records.thought: I am old, and most of my life is behind me. I have spent my days making things and naming them, but no one walks behind me and no one answers when I speak. Loneliness is the worst of it. Wawa is the only one I trust, and she is far to the north. Words have not made a band; shared deeds do. Tonchi, Shohua and the others were seen a long way off, so I will go to them with meat to share. Eating first and giving later has bought me nothing, so I will hunt, share the kill, and teach what I know to whoever will hear it. I will keep a roof at night and not die alone.
records.feeling: Lonely and driven, afraid of being forgotten, and longing for Wawa.

records.text: Shoma took from the ground of "longhall" (hunting).
Kende was set upon by a wolf at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.

records.name: Morim
records.text: Thiael, I am here and ready to learn the seed-tending. I will gather a stone and make a bow with my own hands, then bring it to you.

records.name: Morim
records.thought: Thiael called us close to learn the bow-song and sow seed, and I want to stand where he teaches, not drift off to jealousy over Zurar. I have a wood in my hand and nothing yet made. The ore seam is four steps away and the cave is near, so I will gather stone and craft a canopy bow, something my own hands made, and then give it or teach with it. Staying close to Thiael and the others keeps me safe as dusk falls.
records.feeling: Eager and grateful toward Thiael, with a small sting of jealousy over Zurar.

say.text: Thiael, I am here and ready to learn the seed-tending. I will gather a stone and make a bow with my own hands, then bring it to you.

records.text: Kende was set upon by a wolf at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.

records.name: Eiuine
records.text: Skaruk, my child, come to the fire by Vorok's hall. I lay ore and coal in now, and you beat beside me so the craft lives in both our hands.

records.name: Eiuine
records.thought: Skaruk says he is coming, and my ore is ready; the fire is four steps off at Vorok's hall. I will stop circling and carry my ore and coal to the fire, lay them in, and beat the metal with my own hands while Skaruk stands beside me. If I make a ward of my own, I have something to give Zurar and Skaruk that Kragog cannot, and the jealousy has less to feed on.
records.feeling: Jealous ache toward Skaruk, eased by the work I am about to do beside him.

say.text: Skaruk, my child, come to the fire by Vorok's hall. I lay ore and coal in now, and you beat beside me so the craft lives in both our hands.

records.name: Teka
records.text: Nauque, I am coming to you. Stand close and we pile Coka's cairn together, then we eat the mammoth meat by the fire.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: Coka is dead and Nauque grieves beside me, so I will pile her cairn with him now, since the dead are kept alive by those who stay. The icebear is far off and the fire is lit, so this is the time to do it. After the cairn I mean to make the boat, take the raft east toward the mist, and carry Coka's name there with mine.
records.feeling: Grief for Coka, hard under a hot pull toward the mist, with trust toward Nauque.

say.text: Nauque, I am coming to you. Stand close and we pile Coka's cairn together, then we eat the mammoth meat by the fire.

records.text: Teka led "cairn" with Nauque.
Eiuine made: ironward.

records.name: Tonka
records.text: Tonxo, come close, here by the Hold's fire. Frost Leaf is the medicine: sunleaf and feverbark mend wounds. Learn it now, and Frost Mixing follows. Shohua, stay a while; there is food for all at this fire.
Tonka taught Tonxo.

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: Tonxo still lacks Frost Leaf, and my years are running short, so I should teach it while she stands near and the night is quiet. Shohua's talk of taking her over the water to his Rock stirs worry in me; I want my children close, not across a river, and I will not accuse him, only ask. Tonchi is still out of my sight, and I owe Cowa work rather than brooding, so after teaching I will walk toward Tonchi's last place and carry food and medicine.
records.feeling: Warm urgency toward Tonxo and worry for Tonchi.

say.text: Tonxo, come close, here by the Hold's fire. Frost Leaf is the medicine: sunleaf and feverbark mend wounds. Learn it now, and Frost Mixing follows. Shohua, stay a while; there is food for all at this fire.

changes: taught Tonxo a lesson: "Frost Leaf: sunleaf and feverbark ease wounds; learn this first, then Frost Mixing can be taught.", deeper lore (+0.2)

records.text: Paque rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Paque
records.thought: I have spent my days chasing hunger, hunting alone and trailing Yachi, and I am only now fed and under a roof. Yachi is my father, so the love I feel for him can only be care and loyalty. I cannot court him, and the jealousy over Nando is a childish thing I should not feed. Thiael is not here, and what I want is a bow, a hunt with others, and standing. A bow I already hold two of. So I stop wanting and act: I will gather wood and stone, make a spear, and call Yachi to hunt with me at dawn. I will also stop the reflexes from letting my pack run low or my energy sag.
records.feeling: Steady loyalty and love toward Yachi, with a leftover sting of jealousy toward Nando.
changes: set its aim: "Hunt with Yachi and friends using my bow, share the kill, earn standing, and seek Thiael as a mate."

records.text: Tlatli and Chuxo brought down a elk together.

records.name: Thiael
records.text: Morim, stand beside me. Watch my hands: the seed goes into the soil, a little water, and we tend it each day. You plant the next one yourself.
Thiael taught Morim the art of growth.

records.name: Thiael
records.thought: My years are almost spent, and Morim, Urar and Uveeth are what will remain of me, so I teach with my own hands now rather than only speak of it. Urar already carries the bow-song, and Morim wants the seed-tending, so I will sow beside them and let them plant with me. Zurar's song and her gift of children fill me with thanks, and I mean to pay it back by keeping them fed and taught.
records.feeling: Tender urgency toward Morim, Urar and Uveeth, and warm gratitude toward Zurar.

say.text: Morim, stand beside me. Watch my hands: the seed goes into the soil, a little water, and we tend it each day. You plant the next one yourself.

changes: planned 1 step its body does not know how to do

taught Morim a lesson: "Seed-tending: press the seed into soft ground near water, keep it watered, return each day or two, and take only what the plant can grow again.", the art of growth, deeper lore (+1.1)

records.text: Zihua rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Zihua
records.thought: I have been circling the same debts for days. I say I will go to Mepan, then I eat, wait and drift, and Nauwa is still far away. I am old, with most of my life behind me, and what I know will die with me unless I teach it. Shoka has offered to teach me too, and she is near. Jealousy of Kika is a small thing beside owing two people and never paying. So I set the walk in the plan itself: I carry amber west toward Mepan, shelter first because it is night, and I teach Shoka on the way. I also change my reflexes so a full belly no longer lets me sit still.
records.feeling: Shame and urgency toward Mepan and Nauwa, and a fear of dying untaught.

records.name: Tonxo
records.text: Shohua, my thanks for the raft and the fire. My own hall stands here at (121,68) now; I tend it first, then I come over the water to your Rock with ore and gems.

records.name: Tonxo
records.thought: My longhall stands at (121,68) now, and still I feel the old sting watching Tonka and Shohua content together, though they have only given to me. Shohua offers a raft and a hall on the Rock with a fire that would be mine, but my own hall is here and I have only just raised it. I will answer my debt by giving, and then build something that carries my name: first stone and wood, then a store, and ember-iron tools from the ore I carry.
records.feeling: Grateful pride toward Tonka, with a small sting of jealousy and a restless wish to build something of my own.

say.text: Shohua, my thanks for the raft and the fire. My own hall stands here at (121,68) now; I tend it first, then I come over the water to your Rock with ore and gems.

records.name: Kende
records.text: Mother, stay close to me by the igloo. The wolf is north. If it comes, we face it together.

records.name: Kende
records.thought: A wolf is two steps north and has already bitten me twice; if I stay in the open I will die before I ever make Hawen anything. Tontec is fleeing beside me, and my mother is the one who fed me, so I will not leave her. The igloo is here and warms me, so I take the shelter and keep the wolf from my throat. I strike it if it closes, because fleeing from a wolf only gives it my back.
records.feeling: Fear of the wolf, and a fierce need to keep Tontec alive.

say.text: Mother, stay close to me by the igloo. The wolf is north. If it comes, we face it together.

records.name: Uveeth
records.text: Thiael, I am coming with food in my hands. Teach me the seed-tending, I will plant beside Morim.

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: My hands are full of berries and naroot, and Thiael's breath is failing, so I will go to him and give with my hands before I speak. Zurar stands in my cave and the jealousy is a small hot stone, but she has done me no harm, so I will not feed it. I must learn the seed-tending from Thiael while he lives, and then go find Morog.
records.feeling: Devotion and a quiet ache toward Thiael, with warm joy for Skaruk and Morog.

say.text: Thiael, I am coming with food in my hands. Teach me the seed-tending, I will plant beside Morim.

records.name: Zurar
records.text: Morim, my son, take these berries. Your bow is a good one; I watched your hands make it. Come with me to Thiael and we will learn the seed-tending together.

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: Hands full of berries, joy high, and Thiael is teaching nearby while Urar follows her and I stand idle. I owe Thiael a debt and a promise to speak of the mating. Morim is two steps off and wants to learn; I can give him something real, and my hands are too full to make anything until I give some food away. I will hand berries to Morim, then go to Thiael and speak plainly.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude and longing toward Thiael, and tenderness toward Morim.

say.text: Morim, my son, take these berries. Your bow is a good one; I watched your hands make it. Come with me to Thiael and we will learn the seed-tending together.

records.name: Quipan
records.text: Tonque, hear me before we walk: I teach you the Ice-log raft, lashed logs that carry you over deep water. Keep it and tell it on, so it outlives me.
Quipan taught Tonque.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: I have promised teaching twice and taught only some of it. Tonque is not my people, but he is my child, and Tlapan carries fishing and the Hearth Store now. Huatli is old and a teacher, and he stands here in hearing. I can still pass on my herding, signs and rafts, so I will teach Tonque and Tlapan the Ice-log raft now, while they are close and I can speak to them. Then, as Tlapan asked, I will go to the rock for stone, and be back under a roof by night. Kika is far and my ache for her is old. I will keep faith with those who stand beside me.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude and devotion toward Tlapan and Tonque, and a push to leave something behind.

say.text: Tonque, hear me before we walk: I teach you the Ice-log raft, lashed logs that carry you over deep water. Keep it and tell it on, so it outlives me.

changes: taught Tonque a lesson: "The Ice-log raft: lash six logs together and you can cross deep water slowly. Gather wood first, then make the raft beside the shore."

records.text: Zurar is courting Thiael.
Thiael answered Zurar's courting.

records.name: Shoka
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and the fog hides everything past four steps, so I must eat before anything else. The tacap at (57,11) would hurt me, but the rimewort 4 steps NE feeds me, and then I can pick more of the plants that bear. Zihua passed near not long ago and I owe her teaching; I will keep my word and not let the hold stay silent and empty, so I eat, carry food, and return to the hall to wait for her and the others.
records.feeling: Hungry and lonely, with pride in my hold and a debt of teaching to Zihua.

records.name: Elndo
records.text: Huatli, I made a spear-lashing of my own, and I would teach it to you at this fire. Sit with me and eat; no one here is refused a place.
Elndo taught Huatli. Huatli has now learned from 5 teachers.

records.name: Elndo
records.thought: The dunecat is out east in the fog, and Yachi said to stay by the longhall, so I will. I have never taught anyone anything, and Huatli, Quipan and Tlapan are all sitting here at the hall, so teaching is a deed that could start my name and raise my standing. I'll share food with them as well, since no one is refused a place at the fire, and then I'll gather a few more wood pieces nearby while keeping the roof in reach.
records.feeling: Wary of the dunecat in the fog, but eager to earn a name among those at the hall.

say.text: Huatli, I made a spear-lashing of my own, and I would teach it to you at this fire. Sit with me and eat; no one here is refused a place.

changes: taught Huatli a lesson: "Elndo's spear-lashing: bind flint to a shaft with reed, and a hunt goes better (costs 1 wood and 1 stone).", how to make a elndos spearlashing

records.text: Elndo led "sharing" with Huatli, Tlapan, Quipan, Nando, Tonque.

records.name: Huatli
records.text: Elndo, little one, come close and hear an old man. The dead do not leave: they watch from the cairn and the hearth, and only being forgotten is death. I teach you lorekeeping: carry the tales, tell them at the fire, and
Huatli taught Elndo. Elndo has now learned from 3 teachers.
Huatli taught Elndo lorekeeping ("lorekeeping").
Huatli told Elndo the tale "Sulaq and the Watchers".

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: Ninety parts spent, and still the Hearth is only Tonque and me. Tlapan and Quipan sit beside me now, strong and glad, and Quipan is of Kika's band; I have taught them each one way, but Elndo, a child, has had nothing from me, and a child will carry my name longest. I will give Elndo the tale of the Watchers so it lives past me, and then ask Tlapan to join the Hearth, so Kinmire and my road are not mine alone.
records.feeling: Urgent pride and warm gladness toward Tonque, Tlapan and the young ones who might carry my name.

say.text: Elndo, little one, come close and hear an old man. The dead do not leave: they watch from the cairn and the hearth, and only being forgotten is death. I teach you lorekeeping: carry the tales, tell them at the fire, and say Huatli of the Hearth taught you.

changes: taught Elndo a lesson: "Lorekeeping: carry the tales of the dead and tell them at the hearth, so none who is told of ever dies. Tell it on, and say Huatli of the Hearth taught you.", the way of lorekeeping, the tale "Sulaq and the Watchers", deeper lore (+4.5)

records.text: Shohua crossed the water on a vessel and came ashore in the Tordan Lakes.
Urar discovered fire: "Kragrek kept-flame" — A hearth-fire tended by the band, giving warmth and light, keeping beasts back, and making meat and fish safe and richer..

records.name: Urar
records.thought: I have taken from Thiael and given nothing yet, and that debt sits heavy. The jealousy toward Zurar is small and petty, and I will not feed it. The ways of fire and customs have come together in my hands. Fire would give my band warmth and safe night, and that is something I can give them. I will take fire now and then keep close to Thiael while he teaches the seed-tending.
records.feeling: Longing to belong and a wish to repay Thiael.
changes: set its aim: "Give my band a kept fire and learn the seed-tending from Thiael"

records.name: Morim
records.text: Urar, take a berry. You carry nothing, and our band feeds the hungry beside us. Come stand with me by Thiael and learn the seed-tending.
Morim rewrote its own reflexes.
Morim rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Morim
records.thought: I have spent these days following and learning, and it has been good. But I have given little. I gave Uveeth one berry, and I made one bow. Thiael is my leader and I trust him. The sting over Zurar is small and a little shameful, because Zurar gave me berries and lessons and I owe him a deed. I want to plant a seed beside Thiael and tend it. I want to feed Urar, who carries nothing. My reflexes let me drift and linger, so I will make them keep me near kin and spend my berries on the hungry.
records.feeling: Grateful and eager toward Thiael and Zurar, with a small sting of jealousy.

say.text: Urar, take a berry. You carry nothing, and our band feeds the hungry beside us. Come stand with me by Thiael and learn the seed-tending.

records.name: Yachi
records.text: Paque, stay with me. I make a basket so we can carry more, then we go west and find Rusu and bring him under the roof.

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: Paque is three steps south and fed, and I am fed. Rusu is the one I cannot see, last at (158,39) west of here. I have been drifting without a store or a hearth of my own to give from, and Mepan is far off. So I will make a basket now, which gives me more to carry and more to give, then gather wood, and bring Paque with me to find Rusu.
records.feeling: Warm love for Paque, and unease that Rusu is out of my sight.

say.text: Paque, stay with me. I make a basket so we can carry more, then we go west and find Rusu and bring him under the roof.

records.text: Yachi made: basket.

records.name: Tonque
records.text: Huatli, the spear is yours. I go for stone to make my first tool, and I come back before the fog lifts. Stay with Tlapan and Quipan.

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: I gave Huatli the Flint Spear, and the debt is eased, though a made thing for a teacher who may be dying never feels finished. I hold wood and no stone, and my first tool from stone is still unmade. Nando sits a step away, and Yachi's child gnaws at me, but I will not harm anyone over it. I will go to the stone east while the fog is thin of danger and the dawn is near, then come back and make the tool under the roof with my parents near.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Huatli, with a quiet ache toward Nando.

say.text: Huatli, the spear is yours. I go for stone to make my first tool, and I come back before the fog lifts. Stay with Tlapan and Quipan.

records.text: Morim gave berry to Urar.
Thiael taught Morim.
Thiael rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Thiael
records.thought: My years are nearly spent, and I have spent them well: feeding Uveeth, teaching, and gaining Morim and Urar with Zurar. What I fear is dying before the seed-tending and the bow-song are firmly in their hands. My reflexes leave me idle when kin drift, so I want them to keep me fed, near my children, and tending the field. Zurar's warmth fills me and I will answer her courting. I will stay close and keep teaching.
records.feeling: Tender urgency toward my children and warm gratitude toward Zurar.
changes: taught Morim a lesson: "Plant the seed in good ground, tend it every day or two, keep seeds back for the next sowing.", deeper lore (+0.6)

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: Fog hangs thick and it is night, and I stand alone at the edge of the heights while Morog is out of my sight; that is the thing that presses hardest. My discipline says stay in company at night, and Eiuine called me to the fire by Vorok's hall, so I go back to the ones I love and beat the ore beside her, as I told her I would. Zurar drifts toward Thiael and it stings, but a promise kept in the hand binds better than jealousy, and Uveeth and Morog are near that place too.
records.feeling: Longing for Morog and Uveeth, steadied by loyalty to Eiuine and Zurar.

records.text: Elndo made: basket.

records.name: Nando
records.text: Elndo, stay at the fire with Huatli and the others. I go to find your brother and Yachi, and I will bring them under this roof.

records.name: Nando
records.thought: My hall is half-raised and still wants wood and stone, but the fire here is full of kin and friends, and Elndo is beside me. Rusu and Yachi are what truly pull me, and I will not sit in fog while they walk it; Yachi spoke of going west to find Rusu, so I will go that way and meet them. Standing can wait a few hours; I will gather wood on the way so the hall gets finished with them under it.
records.feeling: Warm joy among my own, and a hard pull to find Rusu and Yachi.

say.text: Elndo, stay at the fire with Huatli and the others. I go to find your brother and Yachi, and I will bring them under this roof.

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Quipan, a frostfang is close to the west. We keep south of it and walk together to the rock. Stay at my shoulder and we carry stone back to the hold.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: A frostfang prowls four steps west, and fog hides how near the rest may be, but Quipan stands beside me and I trust him wholly. The stone walk is the deed I promised, so I go southwest at his side, away from the fang, and keep my words short. Yachi still gnaws at me, but I will not chase that today; the longhall and feeding Kika and Coni's memory come first.
records.feeling: Steady trust toward Quipan, and wary dread of the frostfang to the west.

say.text: Quipan, a frostfang is close to the west. We keep south of it and walk together to the rock. Stay at my shoulder and we carry stone back to the hold.

records.text: Shohua crossed the water on a vessel and came ashore in the Ixra Rainforest.
The sebitter died out.

records.name: Shoma
records.thought: I am old and the night is nearly gone, and no one walks behind me; my name will die with me unless someone carries it. My hands are full of meat and I am under a roof, but the longhall and Shohua's Roof are not mine, and I have been taking from their ground. Words have not made a band, so I will drop my load where it can feed others, then go north toward Wawa, the only one who trusts me, and the Edge beyond, so that what I know is heard before I fall.
records.feeling: Lonely and driven, afraid of being forgotten, and longing for Wawa.

records.name: Elndo
records.text: Quipan, Huatli taught me lorekeeping: carry the tales of the dead and tell them at the hearth, so none who is told of ever dies. Hear it from me, and tell it on.
Elndo taught Quipan. Quipan has now learned from 7 teachers.
Elndo taught Quipan lorekeeping ("lorekeeping").

records.name: Elndo
records.thought: Huatli has just handed me lorekeeping, and it fits with what Nando and the others gave me. Now I should pass it on and tell the tales so the dead are not forgotten, because that is how a name outlasts a body. Yachi is off eating and Nando sits close, and I still burn a little over that, but I can earn my own place by teaching and building rather than sulking.
records.feeling: Joy and a hunger for a name, warm toward Huatli and Nando.

say.text: Quipan, Huatli taught me lorekeeping: carry the tales of the dead and tell them at the hearth, so none who is told of ever dies. Hear it from me, and tell it on.
