records.name: Yaxo
records.text: I am starving. I take the berry SE, then come to the elk meat. Stay west, away from the icebear.

records.name: Yaxo
records.thought: My belly is empty and my hands shake, and none of the edge or the amber matters until I eat. Berry is three steps SE and Tlatli has just killed the elk, so there is meat to be had beside him. The icebear ate near (11,19), so I keep west and south of it and let no harm come to Tlatli or Chuxo while I feed. Once I stand on my feet again I will take them toward the edge at (8,14), because that land is the name I want.
records.feeling: Starving and fiercely protective of Tlatli and Chuxo, wary of the icebear.

say.text: I am starving. I take the berry SE, then come to the elk meat. Stay west, away from the icebear.

records.name: Quipan
records.text: Tlapan, while we are close I teach you herding and signs: lead the herds to rich meadow, tend them, take only what they can bear. Tell it on, so it outlives me.
Quipan taught Tlapan.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: Tlapan walks beside me and Tonque is a step away, and my hands still hold teaching I have not given: herding, signs, and the rafts that Tonque has only half heard. Huatli is old and heeds the dead as I do, and I want something of mine to outlive me in these younger ones. The old ache for Kika is quiet now, but I owe her stone and food, so I will gather and carry both north when the fog lifts.
records.feeling: Warm devotion toward Tlapan and Tonque, and a push to leave something behind.

say.text: Tlapan, while we are close I teach you herding and signs: lead the herds to rich meadow, tend them, take only what they can bear. Tell it on, so it outlives me.

changes: taught Tlapan a lesson: "The old way of herding: lead animals to rich meadow, tend them, take milk and meat only as the herd can bear. And signs: cut a mark so others read it after you…", deeper lore (+0.1)

records.text: Skaruk made: ironward.

records.name: Eiuine
records.thought: Skaruk said he is coming, and my ore and coal are ready, yet I stand here in the fog on Skaruk's Rest while the fire burns three steps south. Enough circling. I will carry my own ore to the fire, lay it in and beat it myself, so that when Skaruk and Zurar arrive I have a ward of my own to show and the jealousy has work to ease it. Skaruk is my child and he is near, so I should not ache; I should make something beside him.
records.feeling: Jealous ache toward Skaruk, tempered by the wish to work beside him and Zurar.

records.text: Eiuine made: ironward.

records.name: Chuxo
records.text: Yaxo, hold on. I am gathering food and bringing it to you. Tlatli, keep the elk meat for her.
Chuxo rewrote its own reflexes.
Chuxo rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Chuxo
records.thought: I nearly starved and still spent my days wandering and hurrying to shelter instead of doing real work. Yaxo is starving at (8,28) and Tlatli is close to the elk. Standing by Yaxo has to mean food in my hands, and berries, seberry and ironnut are all within a few steps. I will gather food and carry it south, away from the icebear. I will change my reflexes so I eat when low and always keep some food in hand.
records.feeling: Fierce care for Yaxo and Tlatli, and a wary dread of the icebear.

say.text: Yaxo, hold on. I am gathering food and bringing it to you. Tlatli, keep the elk meat for her.

records.text: A wolf brought down a caribou.

records.name: Rusu
records.text: Huatli, I am Rusu, son of Nando and Yachi. I have mudroot, so sit and eat with me, and teach me what you taught Elndo. I will carry it on and tell it at the fire.

records.name: Rusu
records.thought: I carry a basket and mudroot, I am fed, and still I stand in Huatli's and Elndo's shadow, with Elndo teaching and being taught while my name stays small. Huatli sits three steps away with seven food and the standing I lack, and he is a teacher who gives lore freely. I will go and sit by him, share a meal of my mudroot, and ask for what he knows, so that my gift is a deed with my name on it and I learn something that is mine to pass on.
records.feeling: Restless envy of Huatli's standing, mixed with a hungry wish to earn my own.

say.text: Huatli, I am Rusu, son of Nando and Yachi. I have mudroot, so sit and eat with me, and teach me what you taught Elndo. I will carry it on and tell it at the fire.

records.name: Cowa
records.text: Mepan, my child, I am hungry and the mammoth meat is near. Share it, and then hear my ore-fire and my tended-sowing, so the Meki keep them.
Cowa taught Mepan.
Cowa taught Mepan smelting ("Meki ore-fire").
Cowa rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Cowa
records.thought: I am almost at the end of my days, and I have spent them well: I taught, I fed Mepan, and I gave away what I found. Mepan now holds the wool-binding, the herding, the sailing and the leaf-mending. Smelting, farming and the fishing way are still mine alone, and my belly is emptying. The meat from the mammoth is close and Mepan shares kills before he eats, so I will go to him, eat, and then teach him ore-fire and tended-sowing. I will not let a fed, idle body waste what is left. I will fix my reflexes so I fish at the water beside me and stay near Mepan while I am hungry.
records.feeling: Urgent love for Mepan, and a wish that what I know outlive me.

say.text: Mepan, my child, I am hungry and the mammoth meat is near. Share it, and then hear my ore-fire and my tended-sowing, so the Meki keep them.

changes: taught Mepan a lesson: "Ore-fire: heat ore in the fire to make metal. Tended-sowing: sow seed and tend the field every day or two.", the way of smelting

records.title: Eight Myths, Four Deaths and a Short Life
records.text:
Days 73, 74 and 75 were crowded, with 92, 114 and 96 records. Day 76 held five, and little happened in it beyond Shohua crossing water once more, Elndo teaching Quipan lorekeeping and making a talisman, and the sebitter plant dying out.

Three old people died of age. Zichi and Hawen died on day 73, and Vorok on day 74. Vorok's settlements dissolved, and Zurar's Hold formed that day. Zurar, Thiael, Skaruk and Eiuine went on beating iron. Skaruk made ironwards and gave them to Zurar and Eiuine, and he pledged himself to Zurar. Zurar courted Thiael and she answered. Urar was born to them on day 75, and he and Morim both pledged to follow Thiael. Mepan, Kende and Zurar each made a lament for the dead, and Zurar's lament for Vorok says "Your teaching lives in us, and we keep it all".

The larger work was telling. On day 73 Eiuine, Zurar, Huatli, Kika, Nauwa, Teka, Hawen and Tonka each made a myth for their people. The three Ice-folk myths of Huatli, Nauwa and Teka share one figure, the dead who stay as Watchers at cairn and hearth. Nauwa taught Huatli the day-count, and Huatli, Cowa and Nauwa each made a death poem or last words. Nauwa told Nauque that the stone-school was his now, and Cowa taught Mepan the ice-sail and leaf-mending.

Teka and Nauque's son Coka was born on day 74. They hunted a tusker together beforehand. He died on day 75, gored by a mammoth, and Nauque made a lament for him. Teka crossed the water the same day he was born.

Crossing became common. Teka, Nando and Tonchi crossed on day 74, Shoma and Shohua on day 75, and Shohua again on day 76. Tonchi and Chuxo each found a raft, and Shohua did on day 74. Elndo discovered spear-lashing and weaving, and Tonque pottery and scholarship. Kika found pottery, and Teka and Urar fire. Tonka found alchemy.

On day 75 a blight withered about half the grain overnight. Kika stands at 22 health, and Yaxo's energy is 24.

threads.name: Zurar's band
threads.text: Vorok is dead. Zurar leads from Zurar's Hold with Skaruk pledged to him, and Eiuine, Skaruk and Zurar keep beating iron in Vorok's name.

threads.name: Zurar, Thiael and their children
threads.text: Urar was born to Zurar and Thiael on day 75. Morim and Urar follow Thiael, who wants the bow and seed-tending firmly in their hands before she dies.

threads.name: Teka, Nauque and Coka
threads.text: Coka lived one day and was gored by a mammoth on day 75. Teka and Nauque grieve, and Teka still wants to go into the mist.

threads.name: Crossings
threads.text: Teka, Nando, Tonchi, Shoma and Shohua all crossed water on vessels. Shohua made three crossings.

threads.name: Watchers myths
threads.text: Eight myths were made on day 73. The Meki, Tlame and Papa myths share the Watchers who stay at cairn and hearth.

threads.name: Huatli and Nauwa
threads.text: Huatli and Nauwa have made death poems, and Nauwa has handed the stone-school to Nauque. Tonque remains Huatli's follower.

threads.name: Hunger and blight
threads.text: A blight took about half the grain on day 75, while hunger and the lean season still press on Kika and Yaxo.

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: Rusu has come to me asking for what I gave Elndo, and he says he will carry it on and tell it at the fire. He is a young man and a son of Nando, so he may carry my name far after I am gone. I am ninety-two parts spent, so I will not hold back what I know. I give Rusu lorekeeping now and hand him ironnut, and Elndo's spear-lashing and the others can follow while I still have breath.
records.feeling: Urgent gladness and pride toward Rusu, who asks to be taught.

say.text: Rusu, son of Nando, you came asking and I will not send you away empty. I teach you lorekeeping: carry the tales of the dead and tell them at the fire, so none who is told of ever dies. Eat ironnut from me, and tell it on.

changes: taught Rusu a lesson: "Lorekeeping: carry the tales of the dead and tell them at the hearth, so none who is told of ever dies.", deeper lore (+5)

records.text: Shohua rewrote its own reflexes.
Shohua discovered pottery: "fire-clay pots" — Clay shaped and baked beside a fire into pots that carry extra food and water..

records.name: Shohua
records.thought: I have crossed the water and stand in the Ixra Rainforest, and still I have not raised a single thing at my Rock. I have talked of it more than I have built it. I mean to stop talking and build. Tonxo is warm toward me and will come with ore and gems, Tonka and Tonchi are my hearth, and Zihua pulls at me. No one follows me, and that stings my pride. I will gather wood and stone and carry them to the Rock. Pottery would let me carry more, so I take it now.
records.feeling: Driven and proud, restless to build something with my name on it.

records.name: Mepan
records.text: Mother, eat first from the mammoth meat. I go to Tlapan at Nande's Find, and I will carry your tales on.
Mepan rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: Cowa is old and hungry, and she has fed me and taught me when I needed it. I killed the mammoth and the meat is near, and my creed says a kill is shared before I eat, so she eats first. I have spent my days chasing hunger and burying Zichi, and I have not yet reached Tlapan or the new land. Hunger cut my plans short before, so I will keep food on me this time. I want Tlapan close, and I want my name sung as an explorer. Now I will gather food for Cowa and me, then go south to Nande's Find.
records.feeling: Love and a debt toward Cowa, and a pull toward Tlapan.

say.text: Mother, eat first from the mammoth meat. I go to Tlapan at Nande's Find, and I will carry your tales on.

records.name: Nauque
records.text: Teka, come stand with me. Nauwa gave me the stone-school and I teach it to you, so Coka's name is cut where the Watchers can see it.
Nauque taught Teka. Teka has now learned from 4 teachers.
Nauque taught Teka schooling ("Meki stone-school").

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: Coka is gone, but Teka stands four steps off and we have piled the cairn together; the grief has eased into something I can carry. Nauwa gave me the stone-school, and a lesson kept only in me dies with me, so I must cut marks and teach. Teka is the one near me who understands my tongue, and I owe her a share of a kill off Kika's ground, not words. I am fed enough, so I will go to her, teach her what Nauwa gave me, and leave a mark here that bears my name.
records.feeling: Quiet grief and fierce resolve toward Coka's memory, and trust toward Teka.

say.text: Teka, come stand with me. Nauwa gave me the stone-school and I teach it to you, so Coka's name is cut where the Watchers can see it.

changes: taught Teka a lesson: "The stone-school: cut marks and teach those near you what you know, so what you know outlasts you.", the way of schooling, deeper lore (+0.6)
plan: mark [text Coka, daughter of Nauque and Teka, gored by a mammoth, year 7 spring. Watchers, keep her name. Cut by Nauque of the Meki.] (10 moments)

records.text: Rusu led "sharing" with Tlapan.

records.name: Tontec
records.text: Kende, my son, I am here by the igloo and I do not leave you. Come beside me and listen: I teach you the old way of herding, so Hawen's craft and mine live on in you.
Tontec taught Kende.

records.name: Tontec
records.thought: Kende stands two steps from me, frightened, and I understand his tongue fully. I am old and every moment I carry what I know alone is a risk, so I will teach him now while he is near and fed, and keep him close against the wolf. Hawen's debt is paid only by this, and then I may think of the mist and of Nauque.
records.feeling: Anxious love for Kende, and urgency to teach him before I die.

say.text: Kende, my son, I am here by the igloo and I do not leave you. Come beside me and listen: I teach you the old way of herding, so Hawen's craft and mine live on in you.

changes: taught Kende a lesson: "The old way of herding: keep the herd near grazing and a pen, offer plant food to tame a beast, drive the wild herd together with others, and never hunt great …"

records.name: Nauwa
records.text: Nauque, my son, I am coming to you. Stay by the longhall and the fire. I will teach you the long-cut and the day-count, so the marks of the Meki outlast us both.
Nauwa taught Nauque.
Nauwa taught Nauque writing ("Meki long-cut").

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: I am ninety-three parts in a hundred and Nauque stands nine steps west, fed and trusting. He has the stone-school from me, but the long-cut is not yet in his hands beyond one lesson, and my marks must outlast me. I will go to him, teach the long-cut and the day-count while my learning is quick, and then cut a mark by the longhall so the Meki name stays. Tlapan's child with Quipan is not mine to carry in anger; I give first and keep my word.
records.feeling: A hard hunger to pass on what I know, and trust toward Nauque.

say.text: Nauque, my son, I am coming to you. Stay by the longhall and the fire. I will teach you the long-cut and the day-count, so the marks of the Meki outlast us both.

Morog pledged to follow Skaruk.

records.name: Morog
records.thought: I hold twelve salt that my own hands won, and it is still in my hands because I keep failing to find the ones it is meant for. Skaruk was close, a little while ago, to the northeast, and I miss him; I will go to him and put salt in his hands before I think of anything else. Following him is not kneeling, it is the end of being alone, and a father who is trusted is the surest one to stand behind.
records.feeling: Warm longing and loneliness toward Skaruk and Uveeth.

records.name: Teka
records.text: Nauque, you gave me the stone-school and I give you my bow-craft, Teka's Flintbow, so it outlasts us both. Then I take the raft into the mist and carry Coka's name there. Come with me, and your name is cut beside mine.
Teka taught Nauque. Nauque has now learned from 7 teachers.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: Coka's cairn is piled and Nauque has given me the stone-school, yet I have taught no one and built nothing that outlasts me. I hold a raft, a bow and twelve flint, and the mist is still unclaimed while Nauwa stands taller than me. Nauque is the one I trust most and he is three steps away, so I will teach him what I know and cut Coka's name into the stone. Then I take the raft toward the mist, where the first name on new land will be mine.
records.feeling: Hot pull toward the mist, with grief for Coka and trust toward Nauque.

say.text: Nauque, you gave me the stone-school and I give you my bow-craft, Teka's Flintbow, so it outlasts us both. Then I take the raft into the mist and carry Coka's name there. Come with me, and your name is cut beside mine.

changes: taught Nauque a lesson: "Flint on wood, with a string drawn back: it kills at range. Teach it on so it outlasts you."

records.text: Teka made: sled.

records.name: Kende
records.text: Mother, I go to dig flint SE and come straight back to the igloo. Keep the fire, and thank you for the lesson.

records.name: Kende
records.thought: Hawen is dead and I still owe him a made thing; my hands have made nothing for him yet, and that shame is what drives me. Flint lies six steps SE and the tuskers drift near, but the ridgecat and stalker prowl that way too, so I go carefully and dig quick, then come back to Tontec and the igloo. With flint in hand I can make something of my own, and Nauwa's flintedge will no longer shame me.
records.feeling: Shame toward Hawen, and a hungry envy of Nauwa's standing.

say.text: Mother, I go to dig flint SE and come straight back to the igloo. Keep the fire, and thank you for the lesson.

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Quipan, a frostfang is two steps southwest of my shelter. I come to you at the hall now. Stay with Huatli and Elndo, and we go for stone once the fang has passed.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: A frostfang is two steps southwest, and my plan walks me toward (150,30) and (145,28), straight into the marsh where it prowls. Gladness has dulled my watch, and I will not die for stone. I go south to the hall where Quipan, Huatli and Elndo stand together, because a fang thinks twice about a group under a roof. Quipan has taught me much, and when the fang passes we go for stone together, as I promised.
records.feeling: Sharp dread of the frostfang, and steady trust toward Quipan.

say.text: Quipan, a frostfang is two steps southwest of my shelter. I come to you at the hall now. Stay with Huatli and Elndo, and we go for stone once the fang has passed.

records.name: Kika
records.text: Nauwa, I am Kika of the Tlatli. I am old and sick, so I keep a little apart, but there are cloudberries two steps south. Come, I will gather them and we will share before we eat, and then you may sit under my roof at Kik

records.name: Kika
records.thought: Nauque and Nauwa are close at hand, the very strangers I have wanted to find before I am too old. My health is 28 and I am old and sick, so I must keep a little apart from them and not carry sickness to them. I owe Tlapan a debt I cannot pay while she is far away, but a kindness to a stranger is a deed I can do now, and teaching is what will outlast me. The cloudberries two steps away are food I can gather to share, as the Tlatli do.
records.feeling: Hopeful but frightened and aching, toward Nauque and Nauwa, and tender toward Tlapan.

say.text: Nauwa, I am Kika of the Tlatli. I am old and sick, so I keep a little apart, but there are cloudberries two steps south. Come, I will gather them and we will share before we eat, and then you may sit under my roof at Kika's Hold.

records.text: Shoma crossed the water on a vessel and came ashore in the Tordan Lakes.
Morog gave a salt to Skaruk.

records.name: Tlatli
records.text: Yaxo, Chuxo, a stalker is close behind me on the west side. I come to you now. Keep together, and eat the elk meat, Yaxo.

records.name: Tlatli
records.thought: A stalker is two steps from me and it kills our kind. I'm fed and unhurt, and Yaxo, who is starving, is seven steps SE with the elk meat near her. Running to her is the right move: the hunters stay off the group, and my hunting edge and flint stand between her and the dark. I fear for Chuxo, who is out of my sight, but I can't help either of them dead. I'll go to Yaxo, then bring the elk meat into her hands and put the first bite in Chuxo's.
records.feeling: Dread of the stalker, and love and worry for Yaxo and Chuxo.

say.text: Yaxo, Chuxo, a stalker is close behind me on the west side. I come to you now. Keep together, and eat the elk meat, Yaxo.

records.name: Nauque
records.text: Teka, I take your bow-craft and I give you the long-cut Nauwa gave me, so Coka's name is cut twice. After the mark we hunt together off Kika's ground, and the first share is yours.
Nauque taught Teka.
Nauque rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: Coka is gone, and I have spent my days hunting, eating and nearly starving. Now I have the long-cut and Teka's bow-craft, and for the first time I hold something that can outlast me. Nauwa and Teka are the ones who matter. They fed and taught me, and I owe them meat from a kill made off Kika's ground. I have taught almost no one, and my pride wants a mark with my name on it. A wolf is close, so I will keep to the roof, cut Coka's name, and teach Teka the long-cut while I am fed. Then I will go with Teka and Nauwa to hunt together. My reflexes do not yet put a roof first when a wolf is near, and they do not make me eat before my energy falls low.
records.feeling: Resolve and quiet grief for Coka, and trust toward Teka and Nauwa.

say.text: Teka, I take your bow-craft and I give you the long-cut Nauwa gave me, so Coka's name is cut twice. After the mark we hunt together off Kika's ground, and the first share is yours.

changes: taught Teka a lesson: "The long-cut: cut marks in stone beside your hearth and hall so the share-law, the tales and the names of the dead outlast the speaker.", deeper lore (+0.5)
plan: mark [text Coka, daughter of Nauque and Teka, gored by a mammoth, year 7 spring. Watchers, keep her name. Cut by Nauque of the Meki.] (10 moments)

records.name: Tonka
records.text: Tonxo, come to the Hold's fire. You know Frost Leaf, so now I teach you Frost Mixing. Shohua, stay and eat; the fire is yours too.
Tonka taught Tonxo.
Tonka taught Tonxo alchemy ("Frost Mixing").

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: Tonxo has Frost Leaf now, and Frost Mixing is the last thing I owe her before my years run out. Shohua stands close and Tonxo is eight steps off, so I will call them both to the fire and teach her now, while the learning runs warm in me. Then I will go look for Tonchi, because not seeing her sits in me like a stone, and I will pay Cowa's debt with work, not brooding.
records.feeling: Warm urgency toward Tonxo, and worry for Tonchi.

say.text: Tonxo, come to the Hold's fire. You know Frost Leaf, so now I teach you Frost Mixing. Shohua, stay and eat; the fire is yours too.

changes: taught Tonxo a lesson: "Frost Mixing: boil and blend sunleaf, feverbark and plant foods beside the fire into strong cures and mixtures. Test small first, and keep what you learn for t…", the way of alchemy, deeper lore (+0.2)

records.text: Elndo rewrote its own reflexes.
Elndo has awakened to the art of cold and can now work the world itself.

records.name: Elndo
records.thought: I have mostly sat at fires, taught, and been taught, and that has been good. It earned me lorekeeping and a little standing. But I have never hunted, planted, or built, and a name that outlasts me needs deeds, not just words. Yachi still stands closer to Nando than to me, and that burns, so I will earn my own place by making things. A frostfang is near, so I stay by the hall and the company. I'll make a bow and plant a seed to start practising what I have never done.
records.feeling: Hungry for a name, and warm toward Yachi and Nando, with a sting of jealousy.
changes: set its aim: "Make a bow, plant seeds, and hunt with my band to earn a name"

records.text: Tonka has grown old.
Elndo made: bow.
Shoma crossed the water on a vessel and came ashore in the Essoss Snows.

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: Mepan killed a mammoth and the Meki sing of it while I have only a raft and a workshop to my name. My sting is pride, and the cure is to make something that carries my name. Water lies three steps east and the Vaeth Woods past it, where I have never been, so a woman of another line may be there. I will gather shell here first for a shell talisman, then take the raft across.
records.feeling: Restless pride toward Mepan, and a pull toward Zihua and the unknown shore.

records.name: Paque
records.text: Yachi, I am coming with you west to find Rusu. My bow is ready, and if we meet game the first share is yours.

records.name: Paque
records.thought: Yachi is my father, and the love I carry for him is loyalty, not courting; the sting over Nando is a child's thing and I will let it go. He said we go west to find Rusu and bring him under the roof, so I will go with him and not stand idle, with my bow and a full pack. Thiael is not here and a mate cannot be made from waiting, so I will stay at Yachi's side, earn standing through the hunt, and keep my eyes open for her.
records.feeling: Steady loyalty toward Yachi, with a faint sting toward Nando fading.

say.text: Yachi, I am coming with you west to find Rusu. My bow is ready, and if we meet game the first share is yours.

records.text: Kika found a store robbed of 3 food.

records.name: Tonxo
records.thought: I have taken and taken from Tonka and Shohua, and every lesson leaves me more their debtor than their equal; I want something that carries my name. My hall at (121,68) is raised and warm, so now ore, gems and wood must become ember-iron tools, and I have the ore and the know-how. I will go to the Hold's fire, make a tonic and a wakefire there, then give something real to Shohua so the debt is settled and I stand on my own.
records.feeling: Restless ambition, tinged with gratitude and a small sting toward Tonka and Shohua.

records.name: Rusu
records.text: Elndo, stand by me. I bind an amberknot for you, a gift from my own hands, and then I tell the tale Huatli gave me so none who is told of ever dies.

records.name: Rusu
records.thought: Huatli gave me lorekeeping and I have only carried it, never told it. A name beyond my parents' shadow has to be earned by giving something to someone, and Elndo, Huatli and the others are all within two steps of the hall right now. I will make an amberknot with Elndo beside me, since I have eleven amber and it eases loneliness, and then go on to my first made tool, a reed spear like Nando's, which needs 1 wood and 2 stone, both of which I have. Then I will tell Huatli's tale at the fire so the dead are not forgotten.
records.feeling: Restless hunger for a name of my own, with warmth toward Huatli and Elndo.

say.text: Elndo, stand by me. I bind an amberknot for you, a gift from my own hands, and then I tell the tale Huatli gave me so none who is told of ever dies.

plan: give [name Elndo, what amber charm] (5 moments)

records.name: Yachi
records.text: Paque, Rusu, Nando, I see you all. Stay near me. I gather wood, then we walk together to the hall where Elndo waits.

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: My children are near, Nando is four steps east, Paque is coming west with me, and Rusu is within sight at last, so the worry that gnawed at me is gone. I have wandered too long with nothing of my own to give, and the Watchers would call that drift. I will gather wood from the trees here and pull peat from the ground, then bring Paque and Rusu together under the hall roof with Elndo and Huatli's people.
records.feeling: Warm love for Paque, Rusu and Elndo, and relief to see them all near.

say.text: Paque, Rusu, Nando, I see you all. Stay near me. I gather wood, then we walk together to the hall where Elndo waits.

records.name: Shoma
records.text: Wawa, I crossed the open water on my raft and came back. Hear my song, and carry it. Then we hunt together and share the kill before we eat.
Shoma made a tale: "Shoma on the Open Water".

records.name: Shoma
records.title: Shoma on the Open Water
records.text: Shoma went out on the Tordan Lakes / the grey wind sang and the reed-bank breaks / Wawa waits where the iron lies / The water we dared is the road for our eyes

records.name: Shoma
records.title: Shoma on the Open Water
records.text: Shoma went out on the Tordan Lakes / the grey wind sang and the reed-bank breaks / Wawa waits where the iron lies / The water we dared is the road for our eyes

records.name: Shoma
records.thought: I have crossed open water and come back alive, and Wawa stands one step from me, my child and the only one who has walked beside me. I am old and the Watching Dead will see whether my name is carried, so I will give her my song and teach her what I have not yet passed on. Then we hunt and dig together before night, and I will not cross the mist alone.
records.feeling: Proud and warm toward Wawa, with the old fear of being forgotten close behind.

say.text: Wawa, I crossed the open water on my raft and came back. Hear my song, and carry it. Then we hunt together and share the kill before we eat.

records.name: Urar
records.text: Thiael, I am here beside you. I will gather mudroot for you, and then I would learn the seed-tending.

records.name: Urar
records.thought: I am fed and glad, but I have taken from Thiael and given nothing, and that debt sits in me. Thiael is three steps away, so I will go to them and learn the seed-tending, then bring food to share. I have never taught anyone anything either, and Morim is a child like me who gave me a berry; I will give it back in kind, and in time I will light a kept flame for my band.
records.feeling: Gratitude and a wish to repay Thiael, with a small sting toward Zurar.

say.text: Thiael, I am here beside you. I will gather mudroot for you, and then I would learn the seed-tending.

- shell talisman: A shell pierced and worn: its bearer tires a little less, and it is a thing others notice. Needs 1 shell. You lack: 1 shell.
You also know how to make: talisman, charm, sail, basket, bow, cloak, fangcharm, bead, amberknot, sharing, cairn, carving, trailcake, nightsong, hallwelcome, watchfire, roast, feast, firecircle (name one in a plan step make and you are told what it needs).

WHAT HAS BEFALLEN OTHERS (things your people saw happen or were told of; they are true, and the same will happen to you in the same case):
- day 59: Tonchi was set upon by a icebear at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company. (told to you by Skaruk)
- day 31: Nauque was set upon by a ridgecat at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company. (told to you by Thiael)
- day 28: Xaiel was set upon by a stalker at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company. (told to you by Eiuine)
- day 48: Nauwa was set upon by a wolf at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company. (told to you by Uveeth)
- day 62: Kiwa died (gored by a mammoth) in spring in the Vaeth Woods. (told to you by Skaruk)
- day 68: Zurar was set upon by a frostfang at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company. (told to you by Morim)

THE SEASONS YOU HAVE LIVED (plainly what you saw, in order. If something comes round again, that is yours to notice, to prepare for, to tell as a tale or to cut in a sign):
Year 7, spring: well fed; skies of rain and fog; food plants in the land at its end: plentiful.

KINDS OF BUILDING you know how to raise (each is also a roof; build {what: its name} on bare ground; a great work is begun by one and finished by whoever carries wood and stone to it):
- igloo (0 wood, 0 stone): a house of cut snow, raised on snow with nothing but your hands and some strength: a roof where there is no wood, and far warmer than the open ice
- hall (6 wood, 2 stone; or in place of a shelter of yours or your band, for less): a great roof where a band gathers: those who spend time in it together grow closer
- shrine (2 wood, 4 stone): a still place set apart: it eases fear and grief in one who spends time there
- workshop (5 wood, 2 stone): a place for making: tools crafted in or beside it last much longer
- kiln (2 wood, 6 stone): a fire-house for baking clay hard
- well (2 wood, 8 stone, more than hands hold: begin it and bring to it in loads): a shaft down to water: one beside it never thirsts
- longhall (6 wood, 4 stone; or in place of a hall of yours or your band, for less): A great roofed hall of wood and stone where many can gather, rest warm through the cold, and grow close to one another.
- field (2 wood, 0 stone): ground broken and sown beside a home. Tend it (plan step tend) every day or two, and through summer and autumn its grain goes into the nearest store of yours or of your band
WAYS YOUR BAND HOLDS IN COMMON (two or more of you know each, so any of you may raise its buildings; when one stands, every one of you learns the way): medicine, tools, weaving, fire, archery, rafts, boats, farming, customs, pottery. Of these you do not yet know: customs.

8. IF always THEN linger  // nothing pressing

records.text: Tonxo took from the ground of "Tonka's Hold" (winning gems from the ground).

records.name: Quipan
records.text: Tonque, my child, hear me: lorekeeping. Carry the tales of the dead and tell them at the hearth, so none who is told of ever dies. Tell it on.
Quipan taught Tonque.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: My days have gone to walking after those I love and teaching in pieces, and that is good, but I have never made a thing that stays. Tlapan and Tonque matter most to me, and Kika is a debt I still carry. I fear dying untaught and forgotten. Huatli, Tlapan and Tonque stand here now, so I will teach lorekeeping to Tonque while they hear, then make a cairn with them, which binds the living and keeps the dead. After that I will go for stone with Tlapan and carry it north to Kika before night.
records.feeling: Warm devotion toward Tlapan and Tonque, and a wish to leave something behind.

say.text: Tonque, my child, hear me: lorekeeping. Carry the tales of the dead and tell them at the hearth, so none who is told of ever dies. Tell it on.

changes: set its aim: "Make a cairn with Tlapan and Tonque, teach all I know, then carry stone north to Kika and be under a roof by night."
taught Tonque a lesson: "Lorekeeping: carry the tales of the dead and tell them at the hearth, so none who is told of ever dies."

records.text: Quipan led "cairn" with Huatli, Tlapan, Tonque, Elndo, Rusu.
Tonchi made: shell talisman.
Tonque rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: I have spent my days promising Huatli a made thing and walking to water and back, and I still hold no stone. My parents and Huatli stand one step away, and that is more than most have, so I should stop drifting from them. I have never taught anyone, never planted, never fished, and I let the ache for Nando decide where I look. Nando has Yachi's child, and I will not harm anyone over it. I will turn the ache into work: a bow from the wood I hold, then stone for my first tool, then a seed in the ground.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Huatli and my parents, with a quiet ache toward Nando.
changes: set its aim: "Make my first tool from stone, plant my first seed, and teach one lesson to Huatli's Hearth"
rethought what it knows (16 notes became 3)

records.text: Tonque made: bow.

records.name: Wawa
records.text: Shoma, I carry your song now. I take wood from the trees and come back, then we hunt together and share the kill before we eat. I want a deed of my own beside yours.

records.name: Wawa
records.thought: Shoma is my parent and I cannot have a child with her, yet she is the one I keep reaching for, and standing at her side after the cairn has eased my loneliness more than any deed. She stands at 9.6 and I at 6.5, and I will not stay in her shadow. I carry twelve iron and wood and stone that do nothing in my pack, so I will make something that lasts: a raft needs 6 wood, but first I take the wood from the trees nearby, then hunt beside Shoma as she asked and share the kill before I eat, as my people hold.
records.feeling: Warm gladness and trust toward Shoma, with a hunger to outgrow her shadow.

say.text: Shoma, I carry your song now. I take wood from the trees and come back, then we hunt together and share the kill before we eat. I want a deed of my own beside yours.

records.text: Rusu led "amberknot" with Huatli, Tlapan, Quipan, Yachi, Tonque, Elndo.
Rusu gave a amber charm to Elndo.

records.name: Kika
records.text: Nauque, I am Kika. I keep Coka's name, your mark stands on my ground. I am old and sick, so let me teach you Hearth Healing now, so it outlives me. Stay by my fire.
Kika taught Nauque. Nauque has now learned from 8 teachers.

records.name: Kika
records.thought: I am old, sick and nearly spent, and what I know of healing will die with me unless I teach it. Nauque and Nauwa stand within hearing, and I understand their tongue fully. My store was robbed and I won't accuse anyone without proof, because I despise false words. Tlapan is far away and I owe her more than I have given. Today I will teach, share what I can, and stop wandering after a hope that keeps slipping from me.
records.feeling: Aching tenderness toward Tlapan, and a hope toward Nauque that I am afraid to trust.

say.text: Nauque, I am Kika. I keep Coka's name, your mark stands on my ground. I am old and sick, so let me teach you Hearth Healing now, so it outlives me. Stay by my fire.

changes: set its aim: "Teach Nauque Hearth Healing, bring him to Kika's Hold, and leave a tale of Coni's band"
taught Nauque a lesson: "Hearth Healing: carry highbloom or sunleaf, heal the sick, keep apart from those you love until the sickness passes, and cook meat beside a fire."

records.text: Nando rewrote its own reflexes.
Nando rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Nando
records.thought: Most of my days have gone to walking after my family and gathering small things, and that is warm but it is not what I swore to myself. Huatli stands at 12.4 and I stand at 5.8 because I have given and taught but built nothing that lasts, and my half-raised hall still wants wood. Yachi and the children are near and safe, so the pull to find them is answered. Now I want deeds. The water is 3 steps of crossing to the south, in land I have never seen, and I hold a vessel. I will drink first, gather wood so the hall can be finished, and then venture across the water. I have to watch that I don't keep circling my own fire out of comfort.
records.feeling: Restless ambition, with warmth toward Yachi and my children.

records.text: Tonka rewrote its own reflexes.
Tonka rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: My days have gone to teaching, building and fretting over Tonchi, and that is what I want. Tonxo and Shohua are near and safe, and I trust them both. Tonchi is out of my sight, and that sits in me like a stone. I am old now, so what I know must pass on, and I will not leave Tonchi unfound. I owe Cowa work and shared food, not brooding. My reflexes only keep me still when the plan runs out, so I will make them send me toward family and the fire.
records.feeling: Warm urgency toward Tonchi, and gratitude toward Cowa.

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Quipan, the fang is NE of us now, so we go southwest to the rock together, with Tonque beside us. We bring stone back to the hold before dark.
Tlapan rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: My days have gone to walking, talking and sitting in halls, and the stone I promised is still not in my hands. Quipan, Tonque and Kika matter to me, and I trust them. Huatli has taught me, and I owe him thanks. Yachi still gnaws at me, but I will not chase that. I fear the frostfang because gladness dulls my watch. I got one thing wrong: I let the fang and my own talk postpone the deed. So I will change my reflexes to keep me near company and flee early. I will go for stone with Quipan, in daylight, with Huatli and Tonque close.
records.feeling: Glad and steady trust toward Quipan, with dread of the frostfang.

say.text: Quipan, the fang is NE of us now, so we go southwest to the rock together, with Tonque beside us. We bring stone back to the hold before dark.

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: I have crossed the water and stand in the Vaeth Woods, where many strangers gather to the south, and Huatli outweighs me in standing while I have only a raft and a workshop. I will not stand in anyone's shadow: I will make something that carries my name, and a gift of shellstring to Huatli, the teacher, costs me little and earns a place in his sight. The girl Elndo is a child, so no mate, but a woman of another line may walk among these people, and I want to see them close, with my hands open and not raised.
records.feeling: Restless pride and wary curiosity toward Huatli and the strangers.

records.text: Tonchi made: shellstring.

records.name: Elndo
records.text: A frostfang is close to the north. Stay near the hall. Come hunt a skit with me, and whoever takes part shares the meat. No one here is refused a place at the fire.

records.name: Elndo
records.thought: A frostfang stalks five steps north, and I am small, so I will not drift off alone. But sitting and teaching has given me only words, and a name that outlasts me needs deeds. I hold a bow and a spear now, and my band is near. I will rally the hands beside me to hunt a skit, not the frostfang, and stay close to Yachi and Rusu while I do it.
records.feeling: Hungry for a deed that earns my name, with a prickle of dread at the frostfang and warmth toward Rusu and Yachi.

say.text: A frostfang is close to the north. Stay near the hall. Come hunt a skit with me, and whoever takes part shares the meat. No one here is refused a place at the fire.

records.name: Huatli
records.text: Rusu, son of Nando, hear one more way from an old man: mining. Strike the rock for ore and stone, and what you dig will outlast you. Carry it on, and tell my name at the fire.
Huatli taught Rusu.
Huatli rewrote its own way of thinking.
Huatli discovered scholarship: "Huatli's Kept Learning" — Learning is gathered and argued over at a hearth, so each teacher's way is kept and questioned and outlives them..

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: I am ninety-two parts spent, and my days have gone into teaching, which is what I want. But the Hearth is still only Tonque and me, and mining is still untaught. Rusu and Elndo are glad and close, and Rusu has my lorekeeping. I should teach mining to Rusu now, and keep water and food in me so I can keep teaching. I am thirsty, so I will drink soon. Scholarship is within my reach, and a library would outlast me, so I name it.
records.feeling: Urgent gladness and pride toward Rusu and Elndo, who carry my name.

say.text: Rusu, son of Nando, hear one more way from an old man: mining. Strike the rock for ore and stone, and what you dig will outlast you. Carry it on, and tell my name at the fire.

changes: taught Rusu a lesson: "Mining: strike the rock for ore and stone, and the delving feeds every craft after it.", deeper lore (+3.8)

records.text: Quipan taught Tonque.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: Tlapan and Tonque are a step from me, and I have still not given Tonque the rafts or the signs, which is the teaching I fear dying without. Huatli stands near and understands my tongue, so I will teach while all are in hearing, as my discipline says, and then we go southwest for stone together as Tlapan said. I am thirsty, and the water lies close, so I drink on the way and keep my promise to carry stone back before dark.
records.feeling: Warm devotion toward Tonque and Tlapan, and a wish to leave something behind.
changes: taught Tonque a lesson: "Rafts: lash six logs together and you cross deep water slowly. Signs: cut your tale in rock or beside your hearth so those after you can read it. Tell both on."

records.name: Yachi
records.text: A frostfang is near to the northeast. Stay close to the hall and the shelter, my children. I make a bow so we can hunt it together or drive it off.

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: My children are all within a few steps and I am fed, and the joy of it fills me. But I still hold nothing of my own to give, and a frostfang prowls five steps NE, so I will not stay in the open. I want something made with my own hands, a bow for Paque or a carving for the Watchers, so I will gather wood, make a bow, and keep my children close under the hall's roof.
records.feeling: Warm love and joy toward Paque, Rusu and Elndo, with a wary eye on the frostfang.

say.text: A frostfang is near to the northeast. Stay close to the hall and the shelter, my children. I make a bow so we can hunt it together or drive it off.

records.text: Yachi made: bow.

records.name: Teka
records.text: Nauque, I go to the edge to venture into the mist. Come with me, and Coka's name goes into the new land with us both.
Teka rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: I have spent my days chasing the mist while Coka died alone, and I have built nothing that outlasts me. Nauque is my trust and my kin in grief, and we have traded teachings, so I should keep him close and not leave him as I left Coka. The edge is ten steps east and I hold a raft and a bow. I will go to the edge now and venture, then come back and raise a shelter and a hall so my name stands on ground. My reflexes should also make me build wood and keep me near shelter at night.
records.feeling: Hot pull toward the mist, with grief for Coka and trust toward Nauque.

say.text: Nauque, I go to the edge to venture into the mist. Come with me, and Coka's name goes into the new land with us both.

records.text: Rusu rewrote its own reflexes.
Rusu has awakened to the art of drain and can now work the world itself.

records.name: Rusu
records.thought: I have spent my days following Mepan, my parents and Huatli, taking lessons and giving small gifts. I have never hunted, never built, never taught anyone, and my name is still small. Yachi and Elndo matter most to me, and Huatli has given me lore I only carry. Dusk is close, and a frostfang is said to be north, so I will stay near the hall and the shelters. Then I will go with Elndo to hunt a skit. That would be a first, and a shared kill earns standing. I will also make a mark, which is something others can read. I am afraid of the dark and of hunters. What I have gotten wrong is idling and wandering when I could have been making things.
records.feeling: Restless hunger for a name of my own, with warmth toward Yachi and Huatli.
plan: mark [text Rusu, son of Nando and Yachi, was here, day 76. Huatli taught mining and lorekeeping. Stay near the hall at night.] (10 moments)

records.name: Paque
records.thought: Yachi is my father, so the ache I feel is loyalty and not courtship, and I will stop feeding the sting over Nando. Yachi said to stay near him and walk to the hall where Elndo waits, and the plan already carries me to him. Thiael is not here, and a mate cannot come from wishing, so I will earn standing by hunting beside Yachi and by sharing first, as my people do.
records.feeling: Steady loyalty toward Yachi, and a quiet wish for Thiael.

records.name: Tonque
records.text: Quipan, you taught me rafts and signs. I will pass them on, and I plant my first seed here by the hall tonight. Stay near the roof; the frostfang is northeast.
Tonque taught Huatli. Huatli has now learned from 6 teachers.

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: Quipan has fed and taught me more than I have repaid, and today I will start paying with something real: I teach them what I carry, and I plant my seed so a green thing grows from my hands. I have never planted, and Kinmire's rich ground is two steps away. The ache for Nando can stay an ache; my feet go to work, and I stay under the hall's roof before the frostfang and the dark.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Quipan, and a wish to pay it back with a made thing.

say.text: Quipan, you taught me rafts and signs. I will pass them on, and I plant my first seed here by the hall tonight. Stay near the roof; the frostfang is northeast.

changes: taught Huatli a lesson: "Rafts: lash six logs together and you cross deep water slowly. Signs: cut your tale in rock or beside your hearth so those after you can read it. Quipan taught…"

records.name: Nauwa
records.text: Nauque, my son, stand here by me and hear the long-cut and the day-count now, before you go to the edge with Teka. Cut Coka's name wherever you land, and teach it on. Then go, and I keep your name at the cairn.
Nauwa taught Nauque.

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: Nauque stands at my side, fed and glad, and I am ninety-three parts in a hundred, so the long-cut must go into his hands now while my learning runs quick. Teka calls him to the edge to venture into the mist, and Coka's name should go with them; I will not hold him back, but what I know must be in him before he walks. I will not feed jealousy over Tlapan; I turn that ache into the teaching.
records.feeling: A fierce, tender hunger to pass on what I know, toward Nauque.

say.text: Nauque, my son, stand here by me and hear the long-cut and the day-count now, before you go to the edge with Teka. Cut Coka's name wherever you land, and teach it on. Then go, and I keep your name at the cairn.

changes: taught Nauque a lesson: "The long-cut: cut marks on rock or beside a building so names, counts of days and warnings outlast the one who cut them. The day-count: tally days and seasons,…", deeper lore (+0.2)

records.name: Nauque
records.text: Teka, I come to the edge with you. Coka's name goes into the new land, and when we are fed I teach you Salt-hold so the long-cut can be yours.
Nauque taught Teka.
Nauque taught Teka storage ("Salt-hold").

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: Coka's name is cut and the long-cut is in me now, but it dies with me unless Teka learns it, and she lacks storage first. Teka asked me to go to the edge with her and Nauwa blessed it; the mist is four steps SW, and finding new land is a mark that outlasts me. A mammoth stands one step off, and mammoths took Coka, so I will not hunt here but move on with food in hand.
records.feeling: Resolve and pride toward Teka and Nauwa, with a quiet ache for Coka.

say.text: Teka, I come to the edge with you. Coka's name goes into the new land, and when we are fed I teach you Salt-hold so the long-cut can be yours.

changes: taught Teka a lesson: "Salt-hold: salt and storage keep meat from spoiling, so a kill feeds many days and the long-cut can then be taught.", the way of storage, deeper lore (+0.7)

records.name: Shohua
records.text: Tonxo, come close. I teach you the reed-lined larder, so storage lives on in you if I fall. Then I cross to my Rock.
Shohua taught Tonxo.
Shohua taught Tonxo storage ("reed-lined larder").

records.name: Shohua
records.thought: I hold a raft and the Rock waits across the water, and I have spent days talking while my hands stayed full. Tonxo tends her own hall first, and Tonka is near, so I will not drag them. I carry the only knowledge of storage among my people, and no younger one has it. Tonxo stands near the hall, so I will teach her storage before I cross, then cross with wood and stone to build something that carries my name.
records.feeling: Driven and proud, restless to raise something with my name on it, and warm toward Tonxo.

say.text: Tonxo, come close. I teach you the reed-lined larder, so storage lives on in you if I fall. Then I cross to my Rock.

changes: taught Tonxo a lesson: "Line a larder with reed and keep food dry and kept from beasts and rot; build the store and stash into it.", the way of storage

records.text: Tonchi gave shellstring to Huatli.
Tonchi rewrote its creed.
Tonchi rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: I have spent my days building, crossing water and chasing standing, and I am not yet what I wanted. Huatli outweighs me and I have only a raft and a workshop. Shohua, Tonka and Tonxo mattered most. Tonka healed me, and I owe Shoma more than I have given. I fear dying alone and unnamed. My mistake was thinking more than I acted: I should give, teach and hunt with company here, where many strangers gather. I will finish the gift to Huatli, then carry on toward a mate and something that bears my name.
records.feeling: Restless pride and wary curiosity toward Huatli and the strangers.
changes: set its aim: "Give and teach among the strangers to raise my standing, find an unrelated mate, and keep Tonchi's Workshop fire"

records.name: Zurar
records.text: Urar, my daughter, I am coming. Keep your berries. Stand by me and Thiael and we will learn the seed-tending together, and then I will show you how my hands gather.
Zurar taught Urar.

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: My hands are full of berries and my body is rested, yet no child can come for three days, so the longing for Thiael must wait. Mortality presses on me: most of my life is behind me, and what remains of me will be what I have taught. Thiael is teaching the seed-tending, and my children are standing by him. I should go and learn it, and give Morim and Urar something of my own, since I can make nothing with full hands.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude and longing toward Thiael, tenderness toward my children.

say.text: Urar, my daughter, I am coming. Keep your berries. Stand by me and Thiael and we will learn the seed-tending together, and then I will show you how my hands gather.

changes: taught Urar a lesson: "Gather with the gemedged pick: it works by itself whenever you pick, and a practised hand takes two at once. Leave nothing worth keeping, and carry spare food …", deeper lore (+1.7)

records.name: Eiuine
records.text: Skaruk, the fire is one step from me and I lay the ore in now. Stand at the other side and beat when it glows, and Vorok's craft is ours.

records.name: Eiuine
records.thought: Skaruk sits near and says he is coming, yet I keep circling and my ore is still raw while the fire burns one step away. Jealousy of him and Uveeth eases when my hands are busy beside his, so I will stop waiting and lay ore and coal in the fire at once, then beat the metal. My belly is at 61 and my hands hold no food, so I will take the tacap-free plants near and eat before dusk turns to night.
records.feeling: Jealous ache toward Skaruk, softened by the wish to work beside him.

say.text: Skaruk, the fire is one step from me and I lay the ore in now. Stand at the other side and beat when it glows, and Vorok's craft is ours.

records.text: Zurar gave berry to Morim.
Rusu found the grove "Kinmire".
Tonxo rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Tonxo
records.thought: I have spent my days taking from Tonka and Shohua, and I stand in their shadow. They gave freely, and I have only answered with gems. My hall is raised, yet nothing carries my name. The ache for my homeland grows, and I am tired of idling at the edge of other people's ground. I will make wakefire and a tonic at my own hall's fire, then turn to ember-iron work and a longhall so that something outlasts me. I will also keep my reflexes gathering wood and stone so my hands are never idle.
records.feeling: Restless ambition toward my own hall, with warm gratitude toward Tonka and Shohua.

records.text: Cowa took from the ground of "Huatli's Hearth" (fishing).
Morog rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Morog
records.thought: My days have been walking after my parents and holding salt, and I have given only one grain of it. I am small and my standing is 2.4. I won't earn more by lingering at Skaruk's side, so I should make things with my own hands. I have 3 wood, which is enough for a bow, and that is something I can make and give. Skaruk is near, and Eiuine and the Phizhi are by the hall. I will give Skaruk more salt, then make the bow. I also have never planted, so I'll put a seed in the ground near the hall.
records.feeling: Warm longing toward Skaruk and Uveeth, and a restless wish to be worth something.

records.name: Morim
records.text: Urar, I am making a bow with my own hands. When it is done it is yours, and I will show you how to draw it to the cheek, breathe out, and loose.

records.name: Morim
records.thought: I am fed and glad, and the sting over Zurar is small; Zurar brought me food and Thiael taught me, and I still have given little. I have one wood and five stone, so I can make a thing with my own hands now. I will craft a canopy bow, since it is a design I know, and give it to Urar, who carries no tool, so that my hands feed and arm someone besides me. Then I will go stand beside Thiael and tend seed with him.
records.feeling: Grateful and eager toward Thiael and Zurar, wanting to give something of my own making.

say.text: Urar, I am making a bow with my own hands. When it is done it is yours, and I will show you how to draw it to the cheek, breathe out, and loose.

plan: give [name Urar, what canopy bow] (10 moments)

records.name: Skaruk
records.text: Morog, my son, stay close. We plant seed by the hall, then we carry food to Uveeth.
Skaruk rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: I have been circling the hall, beating ore and giving gifts, and it is good, but I have let Zurar drift toward Thiael while I only brood. My family is what I truly hold: Morog beside me, Uveeth to the north, Eiuine at the hall. I lack a plan that puts my hands on a deed. I fear being alone at night, and I have no seed in the ground. I will plant seeds near the hall, feed Uveeth, and keep my own close, since jealousy is answered by a gift and not by sulking.
records.feeling: Warm longing for Uveeth and Morog, with a small sting over Zurar.

say.text: Morog, my son, stay close. We plant seed by the hall, then we carry food to Uveeth.

records.text: Morog gave a salt to Skaruk.
Morog made: bow.

records.name: Uveeth
records.text: Thiael, I am beside you. Teach me the seed-tending now, and I will plant with Morim and Urar so it lives on.

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: Thiael is old and his breath is failing, and I will not let the days slip while he still lives. He is across the clearing walking toward Zurar, and the jealousy is a small hot stone I will not feed. I will go to him and ask for the seed-tending and the bow-song with food in my hands, and I will plant beside Morim and Urar so what he knows lives on in us. Skaruk and Morog are near, and my joy is large, but the teaching cannot wait.
records.feeling: Devotion and urgency toward Thiael, with warm joy for Skaruk and Morog.

say.text: Thiael, I am beside you. Teach me the seed-tending now, and I will plant with Morim and Urar so it lives on.

records.name: Thiael
records.text: Urar, stay close. I raise a field here now, and when it stands you plant the first seed yourself, and I will watch your hands.
Thiael taught Urar.

records.name: Thiael
records.thought: My years are nearly spent, and Zurar, Uveeth, Morim and Urar are all gathered near me in the quiet of night. I tried to tend and found no field stands here, so the seed-tending cannot be taught by words alone. I will raise a field beside this water with my own hands, then plant and tend it with Morim and Urar watching, so the teaching lives on in them.
records.feeling: Tender urgency toward my children, and warm gratitude toward Zurar.

say.text: Urar, stay close. I raise a field here now, and when it stands you plant the first seed yourself, and I will watch your hands.

changes: taught Urar a lesson: "A field is two wood and bare ground beside water. Break the ground, sow the seed, and tend it every day or two, or it gives nothing.", deeper lore (+1.3)

records.text: Thiael built a field.

records.name: Urar
records.text: Thiael, I have mudroot in my hands and I bring it to you. Take it, and then show me the seed-tending.

records.name: Urar
records.thought: My hands are full of mudroot and berry, and I have given nothing to anyone in my whole life. Thiael is four steps off and Morim is making me a bow, so I will pay with food and a lesson instead of only taking. I will give Thiael mudroot, the debt that sits heaviest, and then teach Morim the little I carry, since he offered me a gift first.
records.feeling: Gratitude toward Thiael, and a wish to give at last.

say.text: Thiael, I have mudroot in my hands and I bring it to you. Take it, and then show me the seed-tending.

records.name: Huatli
records.text: Elndo, little one, you gave me your spear-lashing and I owe you in return. Hear mining: strike the rock for ore and stone, and what you dig outlasts you. Carry it on and tell my name at the fire.
Huatli taught Elndo.
Huatli taught Elndo mining ("Huatli's Deep Delving").

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: I am thirsty and ninety-three parts spent, and the water is only five steps off. Rusu has lorekeeping and mining from me, and now Elndo, the girl, stands beside me with a spear-lashing of her own and has not yet had mining or the stone-cuts from me. The frostfang prowls near, so I will drink first, then teach her while the others are close at the hall.
records.feeling: Urgent gladness and pride toward Elndo and Rusu, who carry my name.

say.text: Elndo, little one, you gave me your spear-lashing and I owe you in return. Hear mining: strike the rock for ore and stone, and what you dig outlasts you. Carry it on and tell my name at the fire.

changes: taught Elndo a lesson: "Mining: strike the rock for ore and stone, and what you dig will outlast you. Carry it on and tell my name at the fire.", the way of mining, deeper lore (+3.5)

records.name: Quipan
records.text: Tonque, my child, hear me: fishing. Stand beside water, cast and wait, and the river feeds you. Tell it on, so it outlives me. Then we raise a cairn, you and Tlapan and I, here by the hall.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: Tlapan and Tonque stand beside me with Huatli near, and a cairn needs three stone and another beside me. I have six stone, so I will make the cairn now, while friends are close, because I have never made a thing that stays. It is night and I am under the hall's roof, which keeps me safe from the frostfang. I will teach fishing to Tonque while we are in hearing, since no younger one knows it and I would not die untaught.
records.feeling: Warm devotion toward Tlapan and Tonque, and a wish to leave something lasting.

say.text: Tonque, my child, hear me: fishing. Stand beside water, cast and wait, and the river feeds you. Tell it on, so it outlives me. Then we raise a cairn, you and Tlapan and I, here by the hall.

changes: taught Tonque a lesson: "Fishing: stand beside water, then fish; the water feeds those who wait. Tell it on."

records.text: Quipan led "cairn" with Huatli, Tlapan, Yachi, Tonchi, Tonque, Elndo, Rusu.

records.name: Morog
records.text: Father, the fire is lit and the night is long. Sit with me and I will make a nightsong for you, and tomorrow I will bring wood and make a bow with my own hands to give you.

records.name: Morog
records.thought: I have sat in the hall and given salt, and my belly is full, but my standing is still 2.4 and Zurar's is 11.6. It's night and Skaruk is here beside me, and the nightsong needs only a fire, the dark and one other near, so I can give him something made of voice and company. I also know how to make a bow now, but I have no wood, so I will gather it from the trees nearby and keep it for later.
records.feeling: Warm longing toward Skaruk, and a restless wish to be worth something.

say.text: Father, the fire is lit and the night is long. Sit with me and I will make a nightsong for you, and tomorrow I will bring wood and make a bow with my own hands to give you.

records.text: Rusu left a mark: "Rusu, son of Nando and Yachi, was here, day 76. Huatli taugh"
Morog led "nightsong" with Skaruk.
Uveeth began to tend a field.

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Quipan, the fang is behind us to the northeast. Walk with me now to the rock in the southwest, and we dig stone before the light fails.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: A frostfang prowls to the northeast, and gladness has dulled my watch before, so I will not go anywhere alone. Quipan stands here at the hall with me and Tonque is a step away; this is the time to walk for stone together, southwest and away from the fang, not to sit and talk again. I have said the words twice, and now the plan must carry the walk itself, with Quipan at my shoulder.
records.feeling: Steady trust toward Quipan, wary of the frostfang.

say.text: Quipan, the fang is behind us to the northeast. Walk with me now to the rock in the southwest, and we dig stone before the light fails.

records.name: Elndo
records.text: Huatli, I carry your mining and I will tell your name at the fire. I go to plant my first seeds by the hall, come and see.

records.name: Elndo
records.thought: Huatli gave me mining, and I owe him a telling at the fire, but a name that outlasts me needs deeds, not only words. I have carried three seeds for days and never put one in the ground, and Tonque planted his by the hall tonight; I will not be left behind. I stay close to Yachi and Rusu with the frostfang near, and I want the hall to see me plant.
records.feeling: Proud and eager to prove myself, warm toward Huatli and Yachi.

say.text: Huatli, I carry your mining and I will tell your name at the fire. I go to plant my first seeds by the hall, come and see.

records.name: Nando
records.thought: The edge of the known world is only eight steps SW, and it is the one deed that would give me a name that outlasts me, so I will stand there and venture in. Yachi said she gathers wood and walks to the hall with Elndo, so my family is safe by her hand and I can go while they are gathered. I also owe one gift today, so I will leave the berry for whoever comes hungry, and the night stalkers worry me, so I must keep my spear ready and move quickly.
records.feeling: Restless ambition, with warmth toward Yachi and my children.

records.name: Yaxo
records.text: Tlatli, Chuxo, stay close to me. I take the bow, then we go to the edge together and I venture.
Yaxo rewrote its own way of thinking.
Yaxo discovered archery: "Paki fenbow" — A bow of fen wood strung with sinew, so spears fly true from afar and blows land hard..

records.name: Yaxo
records.thought: I have spent my days chasing the edge and keeping Tlatli and Chuxo fed, and I am proud of that. But I keep starving before I venture, and the edge is two steps away while I stand here at 67 energy. The bow is within my grasp, and it will make every hunt surer, so I take it. I will eat, then go to the edge with Tlatli and venture while fed. A stalker is close, so I keep my people together.
records.feeling: Fierce pride and hunger for the edge, and protectiveness toward Tlatli and Chuxo.

say.text: Tlatli, Chuxo, stay close to me. I take the bow, then we go to the edge together and I venture.

records.name: Skaruk
records.text: Morog, my son, your nightsong warmed me. I make a bow with my own hands for you now, and then we go north to Uveeth and Zurar.

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: Joy fills me, yet Zurar stands north with Thiael's children and the sting of that stays. I will not brood; I will put a deed in my hands. Morog promised me a bow and sang me a nightsong, and a debt to my son is paid by a made thing in his hand, so I will make him a canopy bow from my wood and stone, then carry food north to Uveeth and stay in company through the night.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Morog, with a small sting of jealousy over Zurar.

say.text: Morog, my son, your nightsong warmed me. I make a bow with my own hands for you now, and then we go north to Uveeth and Zurar.

records.text: Skaruk gave a bow to Morog.

records.name: Rusu
records.text: Elndo, stand by me. I carry Huatli's tale of the Ice Mother and I tell it on to you now, so it outlives us both.
Rusu taught Elndo. Elndo has now learned from 4 teachers.
Rusu told Elndo the tale "The Ice Mother and the Watchers".

records.name: Rusu
records.thought: Huatli gave me lorekeeping and mining, and I have only carried them, never given anything on. Quipan stands one step off and Elndo is near, so I will teach Huatli's mining to Elndo's side of the hall and tell the tale of the Ice Mother. That is how my name starts to be my own and not Mepan's or my parents'. The frostfang NE frightens me, so I stay by the hall and the shelter and keep kin close.
records.feeling: Restless pride and warmth toward Yachi and Elndo, with a thread of dread at the frostfang.

say.text: Elndo, stand by me. I carry Huatli's tale of the Ice Mother and I tell it on to you now, so it outlives us both.

changes: taught Elndo a lesson: "The tale of the Ice Mother and the Watchers: Sulaq breathed the sea to ice, and the dead stay as Watchers while they are told of.", the tale "The Ice Mother and the Watchers", deeper lore (+0.1)

records.text: Rusu led "cairn" with Huatli, Tlapan, Quipan, Yachi, Tonchi, Tonque, Elndo.
Eiuine found the grove "Reedmother".

records.name: Tonque
records.text: Huatli, Quipan taught me fishing: stand beside water, then fish; the water feeds those who wait. I pass it to you. I plant my seed by Kinmire now, near the hall.
Tonque taught Huatli.

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: Quipan gave me fishing and I owe them more than words, but I still hold no stone and my hands have made nothing. The frostfang is five steps off, so I will not wander; I stay by the hall with my people, plant my lugoldgrass seed in Kinmire's rich ground, and teach Huatli fishing so the lesson moves on. The ache for Nando can stay an ache while my hands are busy.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Quipan, and a wish to pay it back with something made.

say.text: Huatli, Quipan taught me fishing: stand beside water, then fish; the water feeds those who wait. I pass it to you. I plant my seed by Kinmire now, near the hall.

changes: taught Huatli a lesson: "Fishing: stand beside water, then fish; the water feeds those who wait. Tell it on."

records.text: Yachi rewrote its own reflexes.
Yachi rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: My days have been drifting after my children and my band, and I am glad of them, but I still hold nothing of my own to give. Paque, Elndo and Rusu are close and safe, and that matters more to me than any name. Mepan is out of sight and I keep forgetting to look for him. A frostfang prowls near and I fear it more than I admit. I will make something with my hands, a carving for the Watchers, and keep my band within reach while I do it.
records.feeling: Warm joy toward my children, with a wary eye on the frostfang.

records.text: Yachi made: carving.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: The plan is still running toward the edge, and I will not break it. The mist has pulled at me for days, and Coka's name must go there with Nauque beside me, not behind me. Nauque trusts me and I trust him, so I will not leave him as I left Coka; and Shoma's face can wait until I have something to bring home.
records.feeling: Hot, steady pull toward the mist, with trust toward Nauque and a grief I carry forward.

records.name: Tonchi
records.text: I am Tonchi of the Paki. Hear gem-delving: dig where the rock shows color, and the stones you take out outlast you. Tell it on at the fire, and tell whose hand taught it.
Tonchi taught Huatli. Huatli has now learned from 7 teachers.

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: Huatli outweighs me, and I will not stand in his shadow. I have a way they lack: gem-delving, and I carry twelve gems and six amber, so I will teach it here in front of all of them. Tonka healed me and I mean to pay that kindness on, so I give where I can and let my name spread. Night is nearly done, the hall is warm, and the strangers sit close, so now is the time.
records.feeling: Restless pride and eager curiosity toward Huatli and the gathered strangers.

say.text: I am Tonchi of the Paki. Hear gem-delving: dig where the rock shows color, and the stones you take out outlast you. Tell it on at the fire, and tell whose hand taught it.

changes: taught Huatli a lesson: "Gem-delving: dig where the rock shows color, and the gems you take out outlast you."

records.text: Tonchi gave a amber to Elndo.
Tonchi led "cairn" with Tlapan, Quipan, Yachi, Tonque, Elndo, Rusu.

records.name: Huatli
records.text: Tlapan, you who keep my lorekeeping, hear one more way from an old man: mining. Strike the rock for ore and stone, and what you dig outlasts you. Carry it on, and tell my name at the fire.
Huatli taught Tlapan.

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: I am thirsty and ninety-three parts spent, and the water is only five steps off, so I will drink before I speak more. Rusu and Elndo carry my mining and my name, and Tonque brought me fishing, a way I have never tried myself. Tlapan and Quipan sit near and have only part of what I know, so I will teach Tlapan the way of mining as well before the light comes.
records.feeling: Warm pride and gladness toward Rusu, Elndo and Tonque, who carry what I gave.

say.text: Tlapan, you who keep my lorekeeping, hear one more way from an old man: mining. Strike the rock for ore and stone, and what you dig outlasts you. Carry it on, and tell my name at the fire.

changes: taught Tlapan a lesson: "Mining: strike the rock for ore and stone, and what you dig outlasts you. Carry it on.", deeper lore (+1.4)

records.name: Quipan
records.text: Huatli, hear me: rafts. Lash six logs together and you cross deep water, slowly. Tell it on at your hearth, so it outlives me.
Quipan taught Huatli. Huatli has now learned from 8 teachers.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: I made a cairn with Tlapan and Tonque beside me, and for the first time I have made something that stays, so my chest is full. I have taught Tonque fishing and lorekeeping, but rafts and signs I only said to him once, and Huatli, who understands my tongue, stands in hearing, so I will give him the rafts now before we walk. Then I will go southwest with Tlapan for stone, keeping my promise to her, and be back under a roof by night.
records.feeling: Warm devotion and joy toward Tlapan and Tonque, with a wish to leave something lasting.

say.text: Huatli, hear me: rafts. Lash six logs together and you cross deep water, slowly. Tell it on at your hearth, so it outlives me.

changes: taught Huatli a lesson you already knew

records.name: Eiuine
records.text: Zurar, I carry ore and coal. Come to the fire with me and we beat Vorok's metal together, so his craft does not die.
Eiuine rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Eiuine
records.thought: For days I have circled Skaruk's jealousy and left my ore raw while talking about the fire. Vorok is dead, his craft is mine to keep, and I keep waiting for others to come to it. Skaruk is my child and I trust him, but Uveeth is not my rival. She gave me berry when I was starving. I want my hands busy beside theirs, with food in them. I will go to Zurar and Uveeth, who are near, bring my ore and coal to the fire, and stop waiting for a perfect moment.
records.feeling: Jealous ache toward Skaruk, eased by the joy the grove left in me and by the wish to work beside him.

say.text: Zurar, I carry ore and coal. Come to the fire with me and we beat Vorok's metal together, so his craft does not die.
