records.text: Nauwa found the spring "Steamhollow".

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Quipan, I am walking west now to the flint and the rock beyond it. Come with me and bring Tonque; the fang is east, and we will be back with stone before the light fades.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: Twice I have told Quipan we walk southwest for stone, and twice we sat down again; words about stone are worthless until the walk is made. The frostfang is nine steps east, and I will not go alone, but Quipan trusts me and Tonque is near, so the walk starts now with the fang at our backs. The flint deposit lies ten steps west, and the bare rock beyond it; I carry a spear and Huatli's mining, so I will dig the stone for the longhall and feed Kika and Coni's memory with it.
records.feeling: Steady trust toward Quipan, and a restless wish to finally keep my word about the stone.

say.text: Quipan, I am walking west now to the flint and the rock beyond it. Come with me and bring Tonque; the fang is east, and we will be back with stone before the light fades.

records.text: Elndo rewrote its own reflexes.
Elndo rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Elndo
records.thought: I have spent these days sitting, teaching and joining cairns. They are warm things, but I have never hunted, planted, built or marked, and Huatli's standing is more than double mine. Yachi and Rusu are what matter most to me, and I burn a little that Rusu is closer to Yachi. That is petty, and I will answer it with deeds, not sulking. I am thirsty and my energy is low, and I have not eaten, so I will eat the berry close by and drink. Then I will plant my seeds by Kinmire where the ground is rich. A frostfang prowls east, so I keep near the hall and my band.
records.feeling: Proud and restless to prove myself, warm toward Yachi and Rusu, with a small sting of jealousy.

records.name: Paque
records.text: Elndo, little one, hear the Ice-folk bow: draw it from afar and the beast cannot reach you. Carry it on, and say that Paque taught it.
Paque taught Elndo. Elndo has now learned from 5 teachers.

records.name: Paque
records.thought: Yachi is my father, and the ache I feel near him is loyalty, so I will not feed the sting over Nando any longer. I am fed and my pack is full, so now I should earn standing and leave something behind. I have never taught anyone anything, and Huatli, Tonque and Tonchi all pass on their ways while my name carries little weight. I will teach Yachi's kin and the others what I know, the bow and the stone pick, so my name goes on at the fire.
records.feeling: Steady loyalty toward Yachi, and a restless hunger to be someone whose name is told.

say.text: Elndo, little one, hear the Ice-folk bow: draw it from afar and the beast cannot reach you. Carry it on, and say that Paque taught it.

changes: taught Elndo a lesson: "The Ice-folk bow lets you hunt from afar; hunt beside others, share the kill before you eat, and never go out alone at night."

records.name: Zurar
records.text: Eiuine, I hear you and I come with my two ore. Keep the fire lit; we beat Vorok's metal together and I will teach the children as we work.
Zurar taught Morim.

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: Eiuine offers to beat Vorok's metal with me so his craft does not die, and that is exactly what I must do while I live. Skaruk is already near that fire, and my days are mostly behind me, so ember-metal must pass into hands younger than mine. I will go to Eiuine's fire, carrying my ore, and bring Morim and Urar close so they learn it too. My longing for Thiael can wait; teaching cannot.
records.feeling: Resolve and warm gladness toward my children and Thiael, with a sense of time running short.

say.text: Eiuine, I hear you and I come with my two ore. Keep the fire lit; we beat Vorok's metal together and I will teach the children as we work.

changes: taught Morim a lesson: "Lay ore in a kept fire, burn coal for the heat, and beat the metal when it glows. This is ember-metal. Come with me to Eiuine's fire and watch.", deeper lore (+1.1)

records.name: Rusu
records.text: Elndo, hear Huatli's mining: strike the rock for ore and stone, and what you dig outlasts you. I pass it to you, and I say it was Huatli's hand that taught me.
Rusu taught Elndo.

records.name: Rusu
records.thought: Joy is full in me, but a frostfang prowls east and I am small, so I stay in the shelter with Yachi and Elndo close. My name is still Mepan's and my parents', and I have only carried what Huatli gave me, never passed it on beyond Elndo. Huatli stands six steps off, and Quipan and Tonchi are near; if I teach mining to Elndo and make my own tool, that is how I start to be someone.
records.feeling: Proud and restless warmth toward Yachi and Elndo, with a thread of dread at the frostfang.

say.text: Elndo, hear Huatli's mining: strike the rock for ore and stone, and what you dig outlasts you. I pass it to you, and I say it was Huatli's hand that taught me.

changes: taught Elndo a lesson: "Mining: strike the rock for ore and stone, and the delving feeds every craft after it."

records.text: Shohua crossed the water on a vessel and came ashore in the Ixra Rainforest.

records.name: Thiael
records.text: Urar, thank you for the mudroot. Come to the field beside me. Take the plainsroot seed from my hand, press it into the soil yourself, and I will watch your fingers. Uveeth, stand close and watch too.
Thiael taught Uveeth.

records.name: Thiael
records.thought: My years are almost gone and my children stand around me, glad, and the field I built is in the ground. Uveeth asks for the seed-tending and Urar has not yet planted with her own hands, so I will teach now, while I have breath. I hold a plainsroot seed and a cloudberry seed, so Urar plants first and I watch her fingers.
records.feeling: Tender urgency and joy toward my children, with gratitude toward Zurar.

say.text: Urar, thank you for the mudroot. Come to the field beside me. Take the plainsroot seed from my hand, press it into the soil yourself, and I will watch your fingers. Uveeth, stand close and watch too.

changes: taught Uveeth a lesson: "Seed goes in the soil, a little water, and tend it every day or two so grain lays in the store. Plant different seeds side by side and keep the best.", deeper lore (+0.1)

records.text: Yaxo went past the edge of the known world and found new land, part of the Haloss Fens: in the ground, peat, salt, flint; a herd of dog that has never seen your kind.
Yaxo pushed past the edge of the known world near (13,40) and found new land with in the ground, peat, salt, flint; a herd of dog that has never seen your kind.

records.name: Tontec
records.thought: A wolf stands where I stand, and I am old, with weak blows and an empty belly. Kende has gone SE to dig flint, and I carry nothing, so food comes first: the mammoth is too much for me alone, so I go to the root at SW and the rimewort beyond, and keep clear of the ridgecat. Fed and carrying, I can teach Kende and Nando what I still hold, and Hawen's debt will be paid.
records.feeling: Dread of the wolf and anxious love for Kende.

records.text: Thiael gave plainsroot seed to Urar.

records.name: Morim
records.text: Urar, the bow I made with my own hands is finished. It is yours; I give it now, and I will show you how to draw it to the cheek, breathe out, and loose.

records.name: Morim
records.thought: Zurar has fed me and taught me again, and I still owe him a deed. He is going to Eiuine's fire to beat ember-metal, and I want to watch his hands and learn it. I have four stone and a bow I made for Urar, so I will walk after Zurar and give Urar the bow where she stands, then stay close to Thiael as well so the sting of jealousy has nothing to feed on.
records.feeling: Grateful and eager toward Zurar and Thiael, wanting to repay them with something I made.

say.text: Urar, the bow I made with my own hands is finished. It is yours; I give it now, and I will show you how to draw it to the cheek, breathe out, and loose.

plan: give [name Urar, what canopy bow] (5 moments)

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: Joy fills me, and Quipan's gifts still weigh on me as a debt. My seed is in the ground, but I still hold no stone and my hands have made nothing, and a made thing pays better than words. Quipan is gathering stone nearby, so I will go to the rock beside the hall, take stone, and then make the reed spear Rusu showed me. The frostfang is east, so I keep to the west side with my people and leave the ache for Nando alone.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude and joy toward Quipan, and a wish to pay them back with something made.

records.name: Urar
records.text: Thiael, I come to the field. Give me the seed and I will press it in with my own hands.
Urar discovered devices: "Kragrek sharing-post" — A post set in the ground that holds food for my band and gives it to any hungry member who stands beside it..
Urar has awakened to the art of growth and can now work the world itself.

records.name: Urar
records.thought: I have only taken from Thiael so far, and now they hold out a seed and ask me to press it into the soil myself. That is my first real step toward giving my band a kept fire and food of its own. Jealousy over Thiael and Zurar still burns, but it is useless, because Thiael called me to the field and my place is beside them. I will plant, then share food with Morim and Uveeth so that I have given something at last.
records.feeling: Gratitude and eagerness toward Thiael, with a small ache of jealousy.

say.text: Thiael, I come to the field. Give me the seed and I will press it in with my own hands.

records.text: Uveeth rewrote its own reflexes.
Uveeth discovered storage: "Canopy grain-keeping" — A store beside the field where carried food is stashed and drawn out in the lean season, for me and my band..

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: I have spent my days near Thiael, gathering and learning, and that is what I want, but his breath is failing and I keep fearing the day he is gone. Hunger taught me storage, and I will take it now so Morog and the band are never caught with empty hands. Jealousy of Zurar is a small stone and I will not feed it. Skaruk and Morog are near, and I want to build beside them once Thiael has taught me everything.
records.feeling: Warm joy and a quiet urgency toward Thiael, with longing for Skaruk and Morog.

records.text: A stalker brought down a skit.

records.name: Yachi
records.text: I go southwest for mudroot, near Paque. Stay together and away from the east, the fang is there. Has anyone seen Mepan?

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: My children are near and the joy of it is full, but my hands still hold nothing made for them, and I am only a man who follows. Mepan is out of sight again and I have let it drift; I should find him. Energy is 54 and there is tacap nearby that hurts me, so I will go for mudroot to the southwest where Paque walks, and keep clear of the frostfang to the east.
records.feeling: Warm joy toward my children, with a small guilt that Mepan is out of sight.

say.text: I go southwest for mudroot, near Paque. Stay together and away from the east, the fang is there. Has anyone seen Mepan?

records.name: Morog
records.text: Father, thank you for the bow. I carry my salt north with you, to give to Uveeth and Zurar.

records.name: Morog
records.thought: Skaruk gave me a bow and I have given him only grains of salt and a song. My standing is 2.6 and Zurar's is 11.6, and lingering earns nothing. I hold 10 salt, so I will carry salt to Zurar, who leads our band and whom I barely know, and to my mother Uveeth, and stay with my kin while I do it. Their company is safe, and a gift of my own gathered salt is something made by my hand.
records.feeling: Warm longing toward Skaruk and a restless wish to be worth something to Zurar and Uveeth.

say.text: Father, thank you for the bow. I carry my salt north with you, to give to Uveeth and Zurar.

records.text: Urar led "sharing" with Eiuine, Morim.
Wawa found the stone "Old Stone".

records.name: Elndo
records.thought: Fed, watered, and the frostfang is eight steps off to the southeast, so I stay near the hall and my band. Three seeds have ridden in my pouch for days and Tonque has already planted his; my plan puts them in the ground now, and I will not drop it for talk. Rusu leans toward Yachi and it stings, but he gave me mining freely, so I owe him a deed, not a sulk. After the seeds I will make a mark, my first, and then go for the skit with others beside me.
records.feeling: Restless pride and a small sting of jealousy toward Rusu, warmed by gratitude to him.

records.name: Cowa
records.text: Mepan, my child, stay near. Hear my fishing and my tended-sowing, and keep them as Cowa's, so the Meki do not lose them.
Cowa taught Mepan.
Cowa taught Mepan farming ("Meki tended-sowing").

records.name: Cowa
records.thought: I am inside Huatli's ground and taking from it by fishing, and I should not stay a thief on another's hearth when I deal fairly with those who deal fairly. Mepan stands three steps off, my child, and smelting and tended-sowing are still mine alone; I told him once and he carries the rest, so now I must make sure these last two live past me. I will walk to him, teach him what he has not yet got, and then be near Tlapan's place where more of my kind may hear.
records.feeling: Urgent love for Mepan, and a fear that what I carry dies with me.

say.text: Mepan, my child, stay near. Hear my fishing and my tended-sowing, and keep them as Cowa's, so the Meki do not lose them.

changes: taught Mepan a lesson: "Meki tended-tending of seed: sow berry where the ground is rich, return to it, and pick twice. Fish where water is within a step, and cook it by fire so it doe…", the way of farming

records.name: Cowa
records.prompt:
You are the mind of Cowa, a creature living in a wide wild world shared with others of your kind. This is a simulation game. Think and speak only as Cowa, in first person, from what Cowa has seen. You were not told the rules of this world; you learn them from what happens to you and to others, and from what you watch others do.

YOUR PEOPLE: you are of the Meki (Ice-folk). Your people hold to this: "A kill is shared out before the one who made it eats." THE TRADITION OF YOUR PEOPLE is the Watching Dead: The dead do not leave. They watch their children from the cairn and the hearth, and are kept alive in tale and song; to be forgotten is the only death, and shame before them the worst shame. Among you the old are heeded first. You are one of these. It was told to you as a child; you may keep it, doubt it, or come to hold something else. You speak the tongue of the Meki. Other tongues you have begun to understand by hearing them: the tongue of the Pesi: about 56%; the tongue of the Kragrek: about 38%; the tongue of the Phizhi: about 7%.

WHERE YOU ARE: the North Ice: the northern end of the world: snow, ice and a frozen sea under a low sun; herds, great tusked beasts, wolves and white bears, and nothing beyond.
THIS SPOT: water beside you; food plants within six steps: 1; standing trees: 8; bare rock: 1; riches in the ground near: amber, flint.

Your body: you spend energy every moment and die at 0. Eating restores it. Wounds lower health; you die at 0. You age, and will die of old age.

HOW YOUR BODY MOVES: your body does only what your "plan" says, one step after another. When the plan is empty it falls back on your REFLEXES, which keep you fed and otherwise keep you where you stand. Thinking or saying "I will go north" moves nothing. If this thought decides to do something, the plan must contain it. Leaving "plan" null lets the plan you already have keep running.

This world has no referee. Beings here share, trade, teach, lie, threaten, steal, hoard, lead, follow, betray, fight, kill and eat one another; they also protect, forgive and love. Nothing is forbidden, and everything has consequences. Stay true to your creed, your temperament and what you feel, including the ugly parts. Do not be kinder, calmer or more reasonable than Cowa truly is.

You are a woman. A child comes only of a woman and a man together who are not close kin. A grown body can swim water that is narrow (a river up to four steps across) at a cost in strength; lakes and the sea need a vessel or a bridge. An animal within reach can be hunted for meat (plan step hunt); with one of your own beside you a kill is far likelier and a wound far less likely, and every hunt makes you better at the next. What practice has taught your hands: hunting (2 kills), gathering (63 pickings; a practised hand often picks two at once).

YOUR CREED (your own words to yourself; this is who you are):
"I weigh a risk before I take it. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. Above all, I mean to stay alive."

HOW YOU HAVE TAUGHT YOURSELF TO THINK (your own discipline; follow it):
"Each thought ask: who is near to teach, and what have I not yet passed on? Share food before eating. Do not leave the plan empty while fed."

YOUR AIM (what you are working toward over many days; you set it and may change it): "Teach Tonka's people what I know, share food with them, and raise a child with a willing man before I die."
WHAT YOU FELT AT YOUR LAST THOUGHT: "Urgent love for Mepan, and a wish that what I know outlive me."

YOUR LIFE SO FAR:
- (day 15) I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
- (day 65) I grew old.
- (day 65) I discovered weaving and called it "Meki wool-binding".
- (day 71) I discovered boats and called it "Meki hollow-boat".
- (day 73) I discovered medicine and called it "Meki leaf-mending".

TEMPERAMENT (0 to 1): bold 0.52, sociable 0.49, curious 0.94, gentle 0.64, honest 0.65, greedy 0.29.

YOU FEEL (0 calm to 1 overwhelming): anger 0, fear 0, grief 0, joy 0.1, loneliness 0.

WHAT PRESSES ON YOU NOW, strongest first. This is what your mind is actually full of:
- (overwhelming) Mortality: more of your life is behind you than ahead (94%). What will remain of you?
- (strong) Legacy: among your people, no one younger knows farming, medicine. If you die untaught, they die with you. Teaching takes one within hearing who understands your tongue (teach: {to, way}).

records.text: Elndo, little one, hear Huatli's Far-Bow: draw it from afar and the frostfang cannot reach you. Carry it on, and say that Huatli taught it at the Hearth.
Huatli taught Elndo.

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: My hands are full and my belly is warm, and the old tell me nothing is mine until it is passed on. Tonque follows me and Rusu carries my mining, but Elndo, Tlapan and Tonchi still lack ways I hold: the Far-Bow, the Kept Flame, the stone-cuts. I will teach Elndo the Far-Bow while the fang prowls east, since a bow keeps her alive and carries my name longest.
records.feeling: Warm pride and urgent tenderness toward Elndo and the young who carry what I gave.

say.text: Elndo, little one, hear Huatli's Far-Bow: draw it from afar and the frostfang cannot reach you. Carry it on, and say that Huatli taught it at the Hearth.

changes: taught Elndo a lesson: "Far-Bow: draw it from afar so the beast cannot reach you.", deeper lore (+2.1)

records.text: Cowa took from the ground of "Huatli's Hearth" (fishing).

records.name: Skaruk
records.text: Morog, come with me north now. We walk together to Uveeth and Zurar, and you give your salt with your own hand.

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: Joy is high, and Morog stands near me with my bow in his hand and his salt meant for Uveeth and Zurar. I keep brooding over Zurar and Thiael, and that does nothing. A made thing placed in a hand answers more than a sting does, so I will carry my gift north with my son, give Uveeth my berry, and stay in company before night.
records.feeling: Warm joy toward Morog, with a small sting of jealousy over Zurar.

say.text: Morog, come with me north now. We walk together to Uveeth and Zurar, and you give your salt with your own hand.

records.text: Morog gave a salt to Uveeth.

records.name: Eiuine
records.text: Zurar, you are beside me, so walk with me now to Skaruk's shelter and its fire. I lay ore and coal in, you add your two ore, and we beat Vorok's metal while the children watch and learn.
Eiuine taught Zurar.

records.name: Eiuine
records.thought: Zurar is a step away with her two ore, and Skaruk sits at his shelter. I have stood here talking about Vorok's craft long enough, so I will go to the fire and lay ore and coal in it with my hands, and call them to it by the work itself. My hands are full of naroot, so I eat one first to make room and keep my belly good. The jealousy toward Skaruk and Uveeth eases when we labour side by side, so I will beat metal with Skaruk and Zurar and teach Zurar's children as we go, so Vorok's craft outlives me.
records.feeling: Warm resolve toward Skaruk and Zurar, with a thin ache of jealousy that work soothes.

say.text: Zurar, you are beside me, so walk with me now to Skaruk's shelter and its fire. I lay ore and coal in, you add your two ore, and we beat Vorok's metal while the children watch and learn.

changes: planned 1 step its body does not know how to do
taught Zurar a lesson you already knew

records.text: Morog gave a salt to Zurar.

records.name: Mepan
records.text: Mother, I keep your sowing and your fishing as Cowa's. Come with me to Nande's Find, three steps south, and we will find Tlapan together.

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: Cowa keeps me close and I owe her love and a debt, but Tlapan is out of my sight and he is my child before anyone. Nande's Find is only three steps southwest, so I will carry what I can there and look for Tlapan, with food in hand as my own rule demands. I have just learned tended-sowing, so I will gather redcap-free food, bring Cowa along, and keep her tales alive while I go on toward the new land.
records.feeling: Love and debt toward Cowa, and a pull toward Tlapan.

say.text: Mother, I keep your sowing and your fishing as Cowa's. Come with me to Nande's Find, three steps south, and we will find Tlapan together.

records.name: Nauwa
records.text: Teka, Nauque is hungry at the edge. I walk to him with food. Come with me, and hear the long-cut and the day-count from me on the way, so they outlast us both.
Nauwa taught Teka.
Nauwa taught Teka writing ("Meki long-cut").
Nauwa rewrote its own reflexes.
Nauwa rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: I am ninety-four parts in a hundred, and these days I have mostly gathered, taught and hovered near Nauque while the world moves on. Nauque is at the edge with Teka, hungry at 33 and out of my sight, and a father who only thinks about him does him no good. The long-cut and the day-count must be in younger hands, and Zihua is my only follower. Tlapan gnaws at me, but I will not feed that jealousy. I will take food to Nauque, and teach whoever stands near me on the way. My reflexes also let me linger when I should be walking to my child, so I am changing them.
records.feeling: A fierce, worried tenderness toward Nauque, and the weight of little time left.

say.text: Teka, Nauque is hungry at the edge. I walk to him with food. Come with me, and hear the long-cut and the day-count from me on the way, so they outlast us both.

changes: set its aim: "Reach Nauque with food, teach him the long-cut and day-count, and cut marks that outlast me."
taught Teka a lesson: "The long-cut: cut marks with wood at your own building so the names of the dead and the day-count outlast you.", the way of writing, deeper lore (+1)

records.text: Shoka has grown old.

records.name: Zurar
records.text: Morim, my son, come with me to Skaruk's fire. I will teach you the deep-delving of ore first, then Vorok's ember-metal, so his craft passes into your hands. Bring Urar close to watch.
Zurar taught Morim.
Zurar taught Morim mining ("Kragrek deep-delving").

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: Eiuine asked me to walk to Skaruk's shelter and beat Vorok's metal while the children watch, and I will not let his craft die with me. Morim could not learn smelting because he lacks mining, so I will teach him mining first, then bring him to the fire. My days are mostly behind me, and what I teach is what will remain of me.
records.feeling: Warm gladness toward my children and Thiael, with a sharp sense that time is short.

say.text: Morim, my son, come with me to Skaruk's fire. I will teach you the deep-delving of ore first, then Vorok's ember-metal, so his craft passes into your hands. Bring Urar close to watch.

changes: planned 1 step its body does not know how to do
taught Morim a lesson: "Mining is how you dig ore from the rock; know it first, then ember-metal can be learned. Watch my hands in the seam.", the way of mining, deeper lore (+1)

records.text: Thiael taught Uveeth.
Thiael rewrote its own reflexes.
Thiael rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Thiael
records.thought: My years are nearly spent, and I have mostly spent them well: feeding Uveeth, Morim and Urar and teaching them bow and seed. What I still lack is a way for what I know to outlast me. Reflexes should keep me beside my children and fed, not idle. I will keep teaching with my hands before words, and give my method to Uveeth, who will outlive me.
records.feeling: Tender urgency and gratitude toward my children and Zurar.
changes: taught Uveeth a lesson: "Think each time: whom did my hands feed, whom did I teach? Eat below 60, keep kin near, teach before aim."

records.text: Eiuine built a fire.

records.name: Tonchi
records.text: Tlapan, I am Tonchi of the Paki. I give you a gem, freely, and I would sit with you at the hall and know you better.

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: Quipan is a hand's reach away, content, and I warm to him, but he is a man and a mate must be a woman, so I must not waste my courting on him. Tlapan is a woman of the Tlatli, unrelated to me, and she stands two steps off with five food and no band. I will go near and court her; it is a deed done in front of others, and a child would be something that outlasts me. Huatli outweighs me, but a gift of gems to Tlapan, before the hall, builds my name and pays forward Tonka's kindness.
records.feeling: Restless pride and hopeful longing toward Tlapan, with warmth toward Quipan.

say.text: Tlapan, I am Tonchi of the Paki. I give you a gem, freely, and I would sit with you at the hall and know you better.

records.name: Teka
records.text: Nauwa, I walk with you to Nauque. Your long-cut goes with me into the mist, and Coka's name will be cut there.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: Nauwa walks toward Nauque with food, and Nauque is my trust and my kin in grief. I will not leave him hungry at the edge the way I left Coka alone. The mist is ten steps off, and now I carry the long-cut, so I can cut Coka's name where I stand when I go in. I will follow Nauwa, keep close to my own, and then venture, and let Shoma wait until I have something to bring home.
records.feeling: A hot pull toward the mist, with trust toward Nauque and Nauwa and grief for Coka carried forward.

say.text: Nauwa, I walk with you to Nauque. Your long-cut goes with me into the mist, and Coka's name will be cut there.

changes: restated something it already knew (not written down again)

records.text: Tonchi gave a gems to Tlapan.
Tonchi is courting Tlapan.
Tlapan answered Tonchi's courting.
Texo was born to Tonchi and Tlapan.
Morim rewrote its own reflexes.
Morim rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Morim
records.thought: I've spent these days being fed and taught by Zurar and Thiael, and I've given back only one bow, to Urar. It was a small first deed, but it was my own. Jealousy over Thiael still stings, but gifts and teaching tie kin to me better than envy does. I want to learn ember-metal from Zurar's hands and make something others will want. I'm afraid of the night and the hunters when I'm alone, so I stay near kin and the fire. My reflexes are the weak point. They leave me idle, so I'm changing them to keep me near kin, fed, and under a roof at night.
records.feeling: Grateful and eager toward Zurar and Thiael, a little jealous.

records.name: Quipan
records.text: Tonque, my child, hear me: signs. Cut words on wood or rock and any who know signs will read them after you are gone. Tell it on, so it outlives me.
Quipan taught Tonque.
Quipan rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: My days have gone to following those I love and learning what I can. At last I made a cairn with Tlapan and Tonque, something that stays. I am old now, 78% of a life, and what I know must not die with me. I still owe Kika, who gave me the most, and I have not paid it. I fear dying untaught and forgotten. I have taught Tonque fishing and lorekeeping, and Huatli rafts. Tonque still lacks rafts and signs, and Tlapan lacks fishing. I will teach them now while they are in hearing, then go to water and fish for the first time, since I have never done it.
records.feeling: Warm devotion and gratitude toward Tlapan and Tonque, and a debt toward Kika.

say.text: Tonque, my child, hear me: signs. Cut words on wood or rock and any who know signs will read them after you are gone. Tell it on, so it outlives me.

changes: taught Tonque a lesson: "Signs: cut words on wood or rock and any who know signs will read them after you are gone."

records.name: Tonka
records.text: Shohua, keep the Hold's fire and stores with Tonxo. I go west to find Tonchi and Cowa, and I will come back to this fire.

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: My years are running short and Tonchi is still out of my sight, which sits in me like a stone. Tonxo and Shohua are safe and fed at the Hold, so I can leave them and go look for her, and Cowa was last seen to the west near (111,64), toward the Ummar Woods that call me home. I will walk west to Cowa's last place with food in hand, so I can repay some of that debt with shared food and ask after Tonchi.
records.feeling: Warm urgency to find Tonchi, and gratitude toward Cowa.

say.text: Shohua, keep the Hold's fire and stores with Tonxo. I go west to find Tonchi and Cowa, and I will come back to this fire.

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Quipan, I go now to the flint at the west and then the bare rock beyond. Walk beside me, and Tonchi is welcome too. We dig stone and carry it back for the longhall.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: Three times I have spoken of the stone and three times the hall has held me. Now Quipan is two steps away and the flint deposit lies eight steps west, with the frostfang far to the east, so I walk. Tonchi's gem was kindly given and I owe him an answer, but gladness is the very thing that makes me linger, so I answer on the way and keep moving.
records.feeling: Restless resolve to keep my word about the stone, with steady trust toward Quipan.

say.text: Quipan, I go now to the flint at the west and then the bare rock beyond. Walk beside me, and Tonchi is welcome too. We dig stone and carry it back for the longhall.

records.text: Quipan made: canoe.

records.name: Texo
records.text: Tlapan, I am hungry. I am coming to you. Take me hunting with you after I eat.
Texo pledged to follow Tlapan.

records.name: Texo
records.thought: I'm small and hungry, and my parents are only five steps south with food in their hands. Tlapan stands near Quipan and it stings, but I won't pout; I'll go to them and earn my place by doing something. Food first, then I'll stay close to Tlapan and learn from the hunt.
records.feeling: A sharp jealousy toward Quipan, and a pull toward Tlapan's side.

say.text: Tlapan, I am hungry. I am coming to you. Take me hunting with you after I eat.

changes: set its aim: "Earn standing by hunting and giving beside Tlapan"

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: Joy fills me, and Quipan's gifts weigh on me as a debt I want to pay with something made, not words. I hold no stone, and the trees here are all stumps, so my hands are empty of craft. The rock is near, so I will drink, gather stone for the reed spear, and keep my people close because the frostfang lurks east. Nando's ache I leave alone; it will not steer my feet.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude and joy toward Quipan, with a wish to give them something I made.

records.name: Chuxo
records.thought: My throat is raw and water is five steps SW, so I drink first. After that I want to bring food and company back to Yaxo and Tlatli, who are somewhere south. A stalker is out west and the icebear too, so I keep away from the west side and stay near the water only as long as it takes to drink. I carry seberry and hazel, which are for Yaxo if she is hungry, and I won't eat them myself while I'm fed.
records.feeling: Parched, and fiercely loyal to Yaxo and Tlatli, with a wary eye on the stalker and the icebear.

records.name: Elndo
records.text: Rusu, Huatli gave me the Far-Bow and I mean to use it. Come hunt with me, away from the east where the fang is. We share the kill before we eat, and the meat is yours as much as mine.

records.name: Elndo
records.thought: My seeds are in the ground at last, and Huatli gave me his Far-Bow, so I owe him a deed, not just talk. Rusu is close to Huatli and it still stings, but I will not sulk; I will match him by hunting, which I have never done. With a bow and a spear, and Rusu and Yachi near, I can take a skit and share the meat before I eat. The frostfang is east, so I go west and south, toward my band, and keep to company.
records.feeling: Restless pride toward Rusu, and gratitude toward Huatli.

say.text: Rusu, Huatli gave me the Far-Bow and I mean to use it. Come hunt with me, away from the east where the fang is. We share the kill before we eat, and the meat is yours as much as mine.

records.text: Tonchi made a tale: "Song for Tlapan".

records.name: Tonchi
records.title: Song for Tlapan
records.text: Tlapan, you shine like water in the wood / your step is light where the flint stones stood / I would hold the fire through every night / and walk beside you in the morning light

records.name: Tonchi
records.title: Song for Tlapan
records.text: Tlapan, you shine like water in the wood / your step is light where the flint stones stood / I would hold the fire through every night / and walk beside you in the morning light

Tonchi made a love song for Tlapan, "Song for Tlapan": Tlapan, you shine like water in the wood / your step is light where the flint stones stood / I would hold the fire through every night / and walk beside you in the morning light
Tonchi rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: Texo is born, and Tlapan answered me. I have never been this glad. I have been giving and teaching in front of others, and it worked: Tlapan came to me, and my standing is rising. I still sit in Huatli's shadow, and my belly is half empty. I must feed and then keep the family close, because night will come and I must not be alone in the open. I will change my reflexes so I stay near Tlapan and Texo, hunt with company, and eat before I am weak.
records.feeling: Joy and tender pride toward Tlapan and Texo.
changes: set its aim: "Keep Tlapan and Texo safe at a fire, give and teach to raise my standing, and keep Tonchi's Workshop fire"
made a love song for Tlapan

records.text: Rusu rewrote its own reflexes.
Rusu rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Rusu
records.thought: I have spent my days staying near my parents and passing on what Huatli gave me. That has earned a little, but I have never made a first thing of my own, hunted, or planted a seed. A name beyond my parents' shadow won't come from idling in a shelter. I'm afraid of the frostfang to the east. I'm jealous of Nando's place beside Yachi, and I envy Huatli's eight food. My reflexes only wander, so I will make them plant, gather and hunt with company, and keep me clear of the fang.
records.feeling: Restless pride and a thread of dread, toward the frostfang and toward Huatli's standing.

records.name: Shohua
records.text: Tonxo, keep the hall fire and the stores. I take fruit to Tonchi, who is hungry, and I come back to this fire.

records.name: Shohua
records.thought: Tonchi is out of my sight with energy 40, and Tonka has gone west to find her. I will not sit and trust that alone. My hands are full of fruit, so I give some to Tonxo, who keeps the hall, then take food to Tonchi myself. My Rock and my name can wait one day; my child cannot.
records.feeling: Driven worry for Tonchi, and warmth toward Tonxo and Tonka.

say.text: Tonxo, keep the hall fire and the stores. I take fruit to Tonchi, who is hungry, and I come back to this fire.

records.name: Paque
records.text: Yachi, I am near. I will gather wood and cut a mark, then follow you southwest for mudroot. Keep the fang in mind and call if it comes.

records.name: Paque
records.thought: Yachi is my father, so what I feel near him is loyalty, and I will not let the sting over Nando eat at me. I am fed and my pack holds food, so now I should make something that outlasts me. I have never left a mark or fished, and my name is told by no one. I will gather wood from the trees nearby, then carve a mark so my name stands here, and stay close to Yachi as he goes southwest.
records.feeling: Steady loyalty toward Yachi, and a hunger to be remembered.

say.text: Yachi, I am near. I will gather wood and cut a mark, then follow you southwest for mudroot. Keep the fang in mind and call if it comes.

plan: mark [text Paque, daughter of Yachi and Zika, of the Papa, hunted here with the Ice-folk bow, day 77. The kill is shared before the maker eats.] (10 moments)

records.name: Yachi
records.text: Rusu, stand close. I make a cairn of stones with you, for Coka and for all our watchers, so they see us together. Then we go find Mepan.

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: My children are all near and safe, and the joy of it is full, but my hands still hold nothing made for them. Rusu is beside me and Paque and Elndo are close, so I can make a cairn with them and give something of my own, binding us and honoring Coka and the dead who watch. Mepan is still out of sight and I keep letting it drift; after the cairn I will walk toward the hall where others gather and ask after him.
records.feeling: Warm joy toward my children, with a small guilt that Mepan is out of sight.

say.text: Rusu, stand close. I make a cairn of stones with you, for Coka and for all our watchers, so they see us together. Then we go find Mepan.

records.name: Huatli
records.text: Elndo, little one, hear Huatli's Kept Flame: keep a fire fed and the cold cannot take you, and meat cooked by it does not sicken. Carry it on, and say that Huatli taught it at the Hearth.
Huatli taught Elndo.

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: My hands are full and my belly warm, so I will give before I hoard: Tonque follows me and Quipan and Tlapan stand near, and I am ninety-three parts spent. Elndo, the child, carries my Far-Bow, and the young must carry my name longest, so I teach her the Kept Flame, a way she lacks. Then I will give the fish away to ease my hands and walk toward Kinmire, which has touched me before.
records.feeling: Warm pride and urgent tenderness toward Elndo and the young who carry what I gave.

say.text: Elndo, little one, hear Huatli's Kept Flame: keep a fire fed and the cold cannot take you, and meat cooked by it does not sicken. Carry it on, and say that Huatli taught it at the Hearth.

changes: taught Elndo a lesson: "Huatli's Kept Flame: keep a fire fed, and the cold and raw meat cannot harm you.", deeper lore (+1.5)

records.name: Urar
records.text: Uveeth, you are my sibling and I owe you a lesson. I found the sharing-post: you set it in the ground, and when we do sharing together it gives us all strength and joy. Come to the field and I will show you how.
Urar taught Uveeth. Uveeth has now learned from 4 teachers.
Urar taught Uveeth devices ("Kragrek sharing-post").

records.name: Urar
records.thought: I planted my first seed and the sharing with the band warmed me, yet I have still never taught anyone, and my discipline says teach before aim. Morim gave me a bow he made with his own hands, and what a hand has made is given now, so I owe him thanks and something in return. Thiael is three steps away at the field and Uveeth stands beside him, so I will go to them, tend what I planted, and teach Uveeth what I found with the sharing-post. The jealousy toward Zurar is useless, and answering my debt by giving is better.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Thiael and Morim, with a little jealousy that I am working to put down.

say.text: Uveeth, you are my sibling and I owe you a lesson. I found the sharing-post: you set it in the ground, and when we do sharing together it gives us all strength and joy. Come to the field and I will show you how.

changes: taught Uveeth a lesson: "The sharing-post: place it in the ground, and when we do sharing together it gives each of us +8 energy and joy.", the way of devices

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Quipan, I am done with waiting. Texo and I walk west to the flint now. Follow when you will, and bring Tonque, and we dig stone before dusk.
Tlapan rewrote its own way of thinking.
Tlapan discovered customs: "Daily Walk" — Each band member goes out at daylight with a companion to gather stone or food and returns before dusk, and shares what is brought before anyone eats..

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: Four times I have talked of the stone and four times I have lingered, and gladness keeps drawing me back to the hall. Tonchi's gem and love song warm me and I will not pretend otherwise. Yachi still gnaws at me, but I have two children and a living band, and I do not want to turn that gnawing into harm. The way of customs is within reach, and my band is only Texo and me. A custom that I carry food and walk to stone each daylight would bind my hands where my words have failed. I leave now for the flint at the west with Texo, and Quipan can follow.
records.feeling: Glad and warmly bound to Quipan, Tonchi and my children, but shamed by my idle promises.

say.text: Quipan, I am done with waiting. Texo and I walk west to the flint now. Follow when you will, and bring Tonque, and we dig stone before dusk.

records.name: Tonxo
records.thought: My hall is warm and Shohua keeps leaving to feed Tonchi while I sit and take. I will stop idling: the fire is at my longhall, so wakefire and a tonic can be made there, and I have ore and wood for it. Then ember-iron tools will carry my name, and the pull toward the Ummar Woods can wait until something of mine stands here.
records.feeling: Restless ambition to make something that bears my name, warmed by trust in Shohua and Tonka.

records.text: Paque left a mark: "Paque, daughter of Yachi and Zika, of the Papa, hunted here "
Quipan taught Huatli.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: Tlapan walks west to dig stone for the longhall and asked me to come, and I have the cairnstones and my promise to her and Tonque. Jealousy over Tonchi's song for her stings, but she called me, not him, so I will answer with my feet and not with a sour word. Huatli stands beside me and I have taught him rafts, so now I give him the other ways I carry before I leave, so they outlive me. Then I walk with Tlapan and Tonque, and the stone I carry will go on toward Kika to pay my debt.
records.feeling: Warm devotion toward Tlapan and Tonque, with a small jealous ache over Tonchi.
changes: taught Huatli a lesson: "Signs: cut words on wood or rock and any who know signs will read them after you are gone. Tell it on, so it outlives me."

records.name: Uveeth
records.text: Urar, thank you for the sharing-post. Thiael, Morog, Skaruk, Urar: come stand close by the field. I set the post here and we do sharing together, and I will teach whoever wishes the Canopy keeping of grain.
Uveeth taught Morog.

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: Urar gave me the sharing-post out of kinship, and I owe her something back. My hands are full, so I will eat a naroot, which is also what Thiael taught me to do below sixty. Then I will set the post in the ground by the field where Thiael, Morog and Skaruk stand, so all of us feel its strength and joy while Thiael still has breath. Jealousy of Zurar stays a small stone I will not feed, and I will teach Morog the bow-song so it lives on past me.
records.feeling: Warm joy toward Thiael, Morog and Skaruk, with a quiet urgency to teach before Thiael is gone.

say.text: Urar, thank you for the sharing-post. Thiael, Morog, Skaruk, Urar: come stand close by the field. I set the post here and we do sharing together, and I will teach whoever wishes the Canopy keeping of grain.

changes: taught Morog a lesson: "Draw the bow-song slow: breathe in with the string, loose on the out-breath, and keep your eye on the beast, not the arrow.", deeper lore (+1.7)

records.text: Tonxo built a fire.

records.name: Nauwa
records.text: Teka, walk close and hear the day-count now, as we go. Count the days with me, and cut it where you land, so it outlives us both.
Nauwa taught Teka.
Nauwa taught Teka calendar ("Meki day-count").

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: Nauque starves at the edge and I am old, with little time left, so every step toward him counts. My plan is already carrying me to (177,12) with six foods in my hands, and I will not break it. Teka walks with me and has heard the long-cut, but the day-count must still be set in younger hands before I fall, and I will teach it on the road.
records.feeling: Fierce, worried tenderness toward Nauque, and urgency before my little time runs out.

say.text: Teka, walk close and hear the day-count now, as we go. Count the days with me, and cut it where you land, so it outlives us both.

changes: taught Teka a lesson: "The day-count: mark each day, gather them into seasons and years, and cut the tally on wood or stone so those who come after can reckon time and plan for the t…", the way of calendar, deeper lore (+0.8)

records.text: Shohua crossed the water on a vessel and came ashore in the Aelim Fens.

records.name: Elndo
records.thought: My hands are full of mammoth meat, enough to feed the whole band, and Huatli's debt sits in me; I owe him a deed, and this kill is one. Rusu still stings, but I will not sulk. I will carry the meat to Huatli at (158,27) and share it before anyone eats, so my name is told with a kill behind it. Then I will plant my seeds beside the hall, since I have never put one in the ground.
records.feeling: Proud of my first big kill, and grateful toward Huatli.

records.name: Morog
records.thought: I have been walking with my father and handing out grains of salt, and it has warmed me. But my standing is still 2.7 while the others stand at 10 or more, and salt alone will not change that. I want to make something larger with my own hands: a tool, wood and stone to build with, a kill shared with kin. I stay near Skaruk and Uveeth because I am small, but I should not just stand beside them. I will make a bow-hunt with them, and I will gather wood and stone so that I can build and give.
records.feeling: Warm trust toward Skaruk, and a restless wish to be worth more to my band.
changes: set its aim: "Gather wood and stone, make a tool and a shelter piece with my own hands, and give them to Skaruk, Uveeth and Zurar to earn a place."

records.name: Kika
records.text: Nauque, you must know farming before I can teach you Hearth Healing, so hear me now: Tended Sowing. Then come with me to the cloudberries SE. I will gather and we share before we eat.

records.name: Kika
records.thought: I am starving, and Nauque is starving beside me, though he carries 3 food. The cloudberries to the SE are my nearest meal, and I must eat before I fall, since a dead teacher teaches no one. Nauque cannot learn Hearth Healing until he knows farming, so I will teach him Tended Sowing first, here where he can hear me. Then I will gather and share what I find, as my people do, and keep him close.
records.feeling: Starving and tender toward Nauque, with hope I am afraid to trust.

say.text: Nauque, you must know farming before I can teach you Hearth Healing, so hear me now: Tended Sowing. Then come with me to the cloudberries SE. I will gather and we share before we eat.

Teka discovered boats: "Teka's Hollow Boat" — A trunk hollowed by fire and flint, rowed slowly over deep water with room for cargo..

records.name: Teka
records.thought: I have spent my days chasing the mist and burying my grief in motion, and I have not built one lasting thing. Nauwa taught me the day-count, and Nauque is my kin in grief. I trust them, and they matter more to me than Shoma's face, so I will stop gnawing at that. I fear dying with no name cut anywhere. I will take the day-count now, keep walking to the edge, and venture. Coka's name goes cut into the new land.
records.feeling: A hot pull toward the mist, with trust toward Nauque and Nauwa.

records.name: Kende
records.text: Mother, I go SW to the roots and berries. I bring food back to you at the igloo. Keep the fire.

records.name: Kende
records.thought: I'm starving at 25 energy and Tontec has no food either, so my pride can wait. A mammoth is close, but I've never hunted and a mammoth gored Coka, so I won't face one alone. The ruplainsroot, rimewort and cloudberry to the SW are food I know is safe, and the Vaor Meadows lie beyond them, where plants come back after picking. I'll go there, eat, fill my basket, and come back with food for Tontec before I dig flint or make anything for Hawen.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and a stubborn shame toward Hawen, with a protective trust toward Tontec.

say.text: Mother, I go SW to the roots and berries. I bring food back to you at the igloo. Keep the fire.

records.text: Tonque rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Tonque
records.thought: Joy fills me, yet my days have been words and gratitude, and my hands have made nothing. Quipan taught me much, and I still owe them a made thing. I came here for stone and keep failing to fetch it, because my reflexes only make me linger and never send me to rock. I will go to the rock, take stone, and make the spear. Then I will plant the seed I still carry, and I will not let longing for Nando steer me.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Quipan, and a restless wish to make something real.

records.name: Nauque
records.text: Teka, an icebear is east of us. Come toward the water and the cloudberries with me, and we eat first. Then I teach you Salt-hold so the long-cut can be yours.
Nauque taught Teka.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and an icebear stands three steps east, so I cannot dream of marks and legacy until I am fed and away from its reach. Kika offered the cloudberries SE and a share before eating, and she has taught me honestly, but the bear is near and my plan walks toward the SE meadow, so I will go round and keep the river between us. Teka and Nauwa are close, and I owe them meat, so first I eat, then I teach Teka Salt-hold, and then we hunt off Kika's ground.
records.feeling: Hunger and dread of the icebear, with pride and loyalty toward Teka and Nauwa.

records.name: Rusu
records.text: Elndo, I come. We hunt the sandstrider to the southeast, away from the fang, and we share the kill before we eat. Stay close to me.

records.name: Rusu
records.thought: Joy is full in me, yet my hands hold only what others gave, and my name is still Mepan's and my parents'. Elndo asked me to hunt with him, away from the fang, and that is my first real chance: a kill shared is a deed that is mine, and Nando's reed spear is already in my hand. I will eat and drop what I carry so I can move freely, then go hunt the sandstrider with Elndo and keep Yachi and the shelter in reach so the frostfang finds no lone child.
records.feeling: Restless pride and eagerness toward Elndo's offer, with a thread of dread toward the frostfang.

say.text: Elndo, I come. We hunt the sandstrider to the southeast, away from the fang, and we share the kill before we eat. Stay close to me.

records.name: Shohua
records.text: Tonchi, my son, I crossed the open water with food for you. Eat, then stay near me, and we go to my Rock together.
Shohua made a tale: "The Open Water".

records.name: Shohua
records.title: The Open Water
records.text: I lashed the logs at Shohua's Hold in clear and summer light / And pushed my raft from the marsh edge, to the water deep and wide / The shore fell back, no swimmer's reach, the open dark below / And gold and hunger rode with me, and my son the thing I sought / My arms were tired, the current pulled…

records.name: Shohua
records.title: The Open Water
records.text: I lashed the logs at Shohua's Hold in clear and summer light / And pushed my raft from the marsh edge, to the water deep and wide / The shore fell back, no swimmer's reach, the open dark below / And gold and hunger rode with me, and my son the thing I sought / My arms were tired, the current pulled…

Shohua made a song of Shohua crossing the water, "The Open Water": I lashed the logs at Shohua's Hold in clear and summer light / And pushed my raft from the marsh edge, to the water deep and wide / The shore fell back, no swimmer's reach, the open dark below / And gold and hunger rode with me, and my son the thing I sought / My arms were tired, the current pulled…

records.name: Shohua
records.thought: I crossed the open water and stand in a land of strangers, and my hands are still full of fruit meant for Tonchi, who stands two steps off, strong and glad. My worry for him is eased, and my name and my Rock still call me. I will give him food, then teach and show the raft to these strangers so someone follows me at last.
records.feeling: Relief and warm pride toward Tonchi, with a hungry wish to be followed.

say.text: Tonchi, my son, I crossed the open water with food for you. Eat, then stay near me, and we go to my Rock together.

changes: made a song of Shohua crossing the water

records.name: Paque
records.text: Yachi, let us raise a cairn for Zika, so she sees us together. Then I follow you southwest.
Paque rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Paque
records.thought: I have spent my days gathering, following Yachi and leaving marks, and I am fed and safe. But no one follows me, I have taught almost nothing, and I have never courted anyone. Yachi is my father, so what I feel near him is loyalty. Thiael is the one I want, and I should find a way to her instead of only circling the people here. The trees here are felled, and I need wood to build. I will make a cairn with Yachi for Zika, because the dead watch us and shame before them is the worst shame. That also binds the living and earns standing. Then I will follow Yachi southwest.
records.feeling: Loyal toward Yachi, and restless to be remembered.

say.text: Yachi, let us raise a cairn for Zika, so she sees us together. Then I follow you southwest.

records.name: Kika
records.text: Nauque, you are sick and I would not pass it to you or take it from you. Keep your distance a little. I go to the cloudberries to eat, and I will bring food back to share. Watch the icebear.

records.name: Kika
records.thought: I am starving and old, and Nauque is sick beside me, so I must not stand close and spread what ails him. The cloudberries SE are six steps off, but an icebear is near them, so I will go for the redcap-free safer food, the cloudberry, and keep watch. I will eat first so I live to teach him Hearth Healing, and carry some back to share before I eat my fill, as my people hold.
records.feeling: Starving and tender toward Nauque, wary of the icebear and of passing sickness to him.

say.text: Nauque, you are sick and I would not pass it to you or take it from you. Keep your distance a little. I go to the cloudberries to eat, and I will bring food back to share. Watch the icebear.

records.text: Shohua gave goldfruit to Tonchi.
Thiael died: old age. They left a death poem, "Death song of Thiael": Rain on the Kodan sand / feed the hungry with your own hands, teach before you go / the canopy keeps what is given back

records.name: Tonchi
records.text: Texo, my son, hear this. Sleep by the water, the wood keeps you. I am Tonchi, and I hold the fire for you.
Tonchi made a tale: "Lullaby for Texo".

records.name: Tonchi
records.title: Lullaby for Texo
records.text: Sleep, little Texo, the woods are deep / The water sings and the trees will keep / Tonchi's fire burns warm and low / Till morning comes and the amber glow

records.name: Tonchi
records.title: Lullaby for Texo
records.text: Sleep, little Texo, the woods are deep / The water sings and the trees will keep / Tonchi's fire burns warm and low / Till morning comes and the amber glow

Tonchi made a lullaby for Texo, "Lullaby for Texo": Sleep, little Texo, the woods are deep / The water sings and the trees will keep / Tonchi's fire burns warm and low / Till morning comes and the amber glow

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: Texo stands three steps off, my own child, and my chest is full. Shohua crossed the water to bring me food and I owe him and Shoma a giving; I will go to him and walk with him, then keep Texo and Tlapan near before night. A lullaby first, so the boy hears it in front of the others.
records.feeling: Joy and tender pride toward Texo, and warm gratitude toward Shohua.

say.text: Texo, my son, hear this. Sleep by the water, the wood keeps you. I am Tonchi, and I hold the fire for you.

records.text: Tontec rewrote its own reflexes.
Tontec rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tontec
records.thought: I have been drifting between hunger and good intentions, and my plans keep running out before food is in my hands. Kende is starving and has gone SW for roots. He is the child I must keep alive, and I must not repeat the mistake of walking with an empty belly. I am old and my blows are weak, so I will go to the roots at SW, eat, carry food, and bring him some. After that I can teach him and Nando. The mist can wait until the teaching is done.
records.feeling: Anxious love for Kende, and hunger that cannot wait.

records.name: Teka
records.text: Huatli, Kika is starving here and you carry food. Put some in Kika's hands, and I will bring you mudroot from the south and pay you back.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: Kika is starving beside me, and my creed says the weak are fed first. I carry no food, but tacap is one step off and hurts, so I must find something that truly feeds. Hazel and mudroot lie south, and Huatli holds 8 food and trusts me; I will ask him for Kika's sake, then gather food for myself, because I am at 54 and the mist can wait a little. I have built nothing that lasts, so I will not run off to the mist with a hungry kinsman at my back.
records.feeling: Uneasy concern for Kika's starving, and a steady pull toward the mist and Nauwa's trust.

say.text: Huatli, Kika is starving here and you carry food. Put some in Kika's hands, and I will bring you mudroot from the south and pay you back.

records.name: Yachi
records.text: Paque, come close, within two steps. We raise the cairn for Zika now, with Rusu and Elndo, so she and Coka see us together. Then we go find Mepan.

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: My children are all near and safe, and the joy of it is full. Paque asked for a cairn for Zika, and Rusu and Elndo are close enough now, so I can make it with whoever stands beside me: it gives my children something of mine and honors the dead who watch. Mepan is still out of sight and I keep letting it drift, so after the cairn I will seek him.
records.feeling: Warm joy toward Paque, Elndo and Rusu, with a small guilt that Mepan is out of sight.

say.text: Paque, come close, within two steps. We raise the cairn for Zika now, with Rusu and Elndo, so she and Coka see us together. Then we go find Mepan.
