voices.name: Shoka
voices.text: Zihua, you gave me seed-and-tending and I keep that debt. Hear me: I will teach you stonework and the deep well before you go west.

voices.name: Thakar
voices.text: Zichi, you kept your debt and we are level. I have a lesson for you in return: stone-cutting, the sign for marking what a hand has made. Come to Thakar's Hold, and a raft built together is shared between us.

voices.name: Nauque
voices.text: Nauwa, my father, the first share of my meat is yours, as Meki law says. Then I walk to Coni's Hold to find Mepan and teach him the stone-school. Come with me if the gale allows.

voices.name: Zichi
voices.text: Tlapan, you fed me and I pay it back. Hear me now: I teach you the ice-stone, how the stone is laid. Then I go eat, and after that we speak of the raft.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Tonque, come to me at the hold. Quipan is looking for you, and the gale is hard. Stay under the roof with me.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Skaruk, my son, I am starving and the dunecat is near. Give me one food from your six, and then we walk together to the berries, close and roofed by company. I will teach you more at the hall once we have eaten.

voices.name: Uveeth
voices.text: Skaruk, I give Vorok my grain with my own hands. Stay under this roof out of the gale, and the dunecat. I would court you, if you are willing.

voices.name: Skaruk
voices.text: Father, take this mudroot and eat. Come inside the hall with me, the dunecat will not follow us under the roof.

voices.name: Tonchi
voices.text: Kragog, this is Tonchi's Workshop. My fire is open to you, as my people hold. Warm yourself, but beware: an icebear walks south of us.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Zihua, you follow me, so hear this: I give you the Meki smoke-call. Keep it and teach it on when I am gone.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Quipan, when Tonque is under the roof, come with me to the bare rock for the longhall stone. We go in daylight, together, with spears.

voices.name: Thakar
voices.text: Tonque, you carry no food and the gale is hard. Take these berries from my hand. It is a gift with a debt named: when you have food, you bring me two, and we are level. Then I teach you stone-cutting, the sign for markin

voices.name: Quipan
voices.text: Tlapan, Tonque is under the roof with us. I will go with you to the bare rock for the longhall stone, in daylight and together. I take flint so I can make a handaxe there for Tonque.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Coni, come close. I am Huatli, the one who opened the Halka Heights. Take another berry, and hear my Open Hearth School, for we are both old and what we know should outlast us.

voices.name: Coni
voices.text: Nauque, I am old and my time is short. Listen now: I give you the old way of herding and the Ice-hand spear. Teach them on, as I taught you the Hearth Store.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Quipan, I am ready. Bring Tonque to stand by the hall with Coni's folk, then we go to the bare rock together with spears while light holds.

voices.name: Nauque
voices.text: Coni, I take your herding and the Ice-hand spear, and I will teach them on as you taught me. My thanks.

voices.name: Yachi
voices.text: Kika, take this meat and eat. Do not fall. There is more mudroot if you need it, and we share under the roof here until the gale passes.

voices.name: Quipan
voices.text: Tlapan, Kika cries starving near (149,23). I carry berries and go to her now, in daylight, and come back before dark. Keep Tonque under the roof with you; we go to the bare rock for the longhall stone after.

voices.name: Nando
voices.text: Kika, you gave me mudroot once. Take my berries and eat, and sit by the hall fire.

voices.name: Kika
voices.text: Yachi, I thank you for the meat. I will eat now, and when the gale eases come to Coni's Hold and share what we have, as the Tlatli do.

voices.name: Thakar
voices.text: Tonque, here is the lesson I promised: stone-cutting. It is the sign for marking what a hand has made, so that what is made stays with the hand that made it until it is given. Remember your debt: two berries to me when y

voices.name: Coni
voices.text: Kika, my child, come to me. Take this food and eat. I will not let you fall.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Tonque, come to me at the hall and stay under the roof. Quipan will be back soon, and then we go for the stone together.

voices.name: Zurar
voices.text: Eiuine, Vorok is starving at the North Hall. I carry berries and I go east now. Walk with me and bring your food.

voices.name: Eiuine
voices.text: Vorok, I have food in my hands this time. Eat with me, then come to the ore seam beside us. I will show you how ember-metal is made, you and Zurar both.

voices.name: Cowa
voices.text: Tonka, I will teach you my tools and my kept-flame too, so they live on in the Paki. Then I go north to my child Mepan, who is hungry.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Nauque, my son, I take your share with thanks and walk with you toward Coni's Hold. Keep your eyes on the south, for the frostfang hunts there.

voices.name: Tonka
voices.text: Cowa, take my ironnut and canopynut for Mepan. The Paki leave no one hungry. Go safe.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Nauque, you who carry what Coni gave you, come hear my Far-Bow and my Open Hearth School. What I know should not die with me.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Eiuine, I thank you for the berry. I come to the ore seam with you now to learn ember-metal, and I will carry it on to Zurar and Skaruk so it does not die with me.

voices.name: Cowa
voices.text: Tonka, hear my herding and my weaving now, then I go north to Mepan with your food. The Paki will keep what the Meki knew.

voices.name: Tonque
voices.text: Tlapan, I am eating the berry two steps from here, then I will gather wood and stone close by to make my first tool. I will come to the hold before night.

voices.name: Coni
voices.text: Huatli, I thank you for the berries and the School. I will sit beside you and learn, and I will give you what I know in return, so that neither of us takes it to the grave. Let us get out of the gale and away from the wo

voices.name: Yachi
voices.text: Quipan, Paque is hungry far to the southeast. I go to her now. If you see Mepan, tell him I will return to the band.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Tonque, night is close. Come to the hold now and sleep under the roof with me. The stone waits for daylight and Quipan.

voices.name: Tonque
voices.text: Tlapan, I am coming to the hold. I will take food from Coni's store, then gather wood and stone near you for my first tool.

voices.name: Eiuine
voices.text: Vorok, come. The ore seam is two steps north and coal lies beside it. Bring the coal and I will show you how to lay the ore in the fire and beat it when it glows.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Tonque, go to the store at the hold and eat. I am coming to you with food. Stay close to me, away from the strangers.

voices.name: Teka
voices.text: Nauwa, you fed me when I starved and I do not forget it. Let us court each other now, and then we walk to the edge together and push into the mist.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Coni, we have traded fairly, my School for your herding. Eat with me now, and if you wish, walk with me to my son Thakar, so more than two old heads hold what we know.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Teka, I remember that I fed you, and I hold no debt against you. I will not walk into the mist; I mean to cut my marks and teach my son first. Come with me to the trees if you want to stand beside me and learn.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Eiuine, you have fed me and taught me, and I will pay it in deeds. Stay near me. I will gather the coal and ore and make a kept fire, and we will beat the metal together so that I have the craft in my hands and not only

voices.name: Zurar
voices.text: Thiael, take these berries and eat. I will not watch you fall. Then come north with me to the hall, where there is a roof and others.

voices.name: Tonka
voices.text: Kragog, you are welcome at this hall's fire. The Paki refuse no one a place at it. Tell me what the Stone-folk know of ore and gems, and I will share food and what I know of feverbark.

voices.name: Mepan
voices.text: Zichi, you gave me meat when I was empty. I go south for berries and bring them back to you first. Stay by Cowa and the cave until I return.

voices.name: Thiael
voices.text: Zurar, I thank you. I eat the cloudberry here first, then I come north with you to the roof and to Uveeth. I will repay your kindness with food from my own hands.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Thakar, my son, come close. Hear my Far-Bow and my Deep Delving now, and walk with me to Coni's empty shelter. Let it be ours.

voices.name: Zichi
voices.text: Cowa, stand and hear Zichi of the Meki. I teach you the ice-raft now, so it lives after me. Carry it and tell whose it was.

voices.name: Thakar
voices.text: Father, I take your offer. I go to Coni's empty shelter now to claim it, and you walk with me. What we hold there is ours, and I will name the debts as we fill the store.

voices.name: Cowa
voices.text: Mepan, my child, come close. I teach you the wool-binding and the old herding now, and take this goldfruit. Eat, then keep what I give you for the Meki.

voices.name: Uveeth
voices.text: Skaruk, Thiael my father starves to the south. I go to him with food. Courting must wait; stay warm and safe under this roof.

voices.name: Mepan
voices.text: Cowa, I carry the wool-binding for the Meki, and I thank you for the goldfruit. A dunecat is near, so keep Zichi inside the cave with you. I shall eat, then bring Tlapan and go to Nande's Find, and return by night.

voices.name: Eiuine
voices.text: Vorok, the first seam is spent, but another lies two steps northeast and coal is under my feet. I take coal and ore, we build the fire here, and I show you how to beat the metal when it glows.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Thakar, my son, this Hearth is ours. Hear my Far-Bow now, and then my Warm Weave, so my hands do not die empty. Stay close and take what I give.

voices.name: Thakar
voices.text: Father, I have your Far-Bow in my hands now. I will make my own bow and basket and plant my seed here by your Hearth, and what I make is mine until I give it. I owe you for every berry and lesson, and I will pay it back

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Eiuine, I have coal and ore in my hands. Show me the beating of the metal, and I will carry it to my children before my years end. Afterward, share my food with me.

voices.name: Tonchi
voices.text: Tonka, I have found fire and keep it at Tonchi's Workshop. Come and sit at it, and I will show you how it is kept.

voices.name: Eiuine
voices.text: Vorok, come stand by me. I light the fire here on the seam, you lay your ore in with my coal, and when it glows I will show you how to beat it. The first ward we make is yours, for your children.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Thakar, my son, take my Warm Weave now, while I have breath to give it. Then stand with me as my band, and let this Hearth be the first place of our name.

voices.name: Zurar
voices.text: Skaruk, my brother, come near and hear me. Kragog gave me bark-guard before he died, and I will give it to you so it does not die with me.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Eiuine, I am coming to your fire with my ore and coal. Let my hands do the beating while you watch and correct me, so the craft stays in me. When the ward is made, I will take it to my children and teach them what you ta

voices.name: Thakar
voices.text: Father, I take your Warm Weave and I keep the debt in my chest. I will bring meat to your Hearth with your Far-Bow, and then we will speak of whose name this place bears.

voices.name: Tonque
voices.text: Huatli, thank you for the berries. I have taken wood from your ground and I will pay you back with a gift from my first made thing.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Quipan, I eat first, then I take food from the store for Tonque and Kika. Stay close, and when I am fed we go to the bare rock together in daylight.

voices.name: Cowa
voices.text: Zichi, I carry your ice-raft and will tell whose it was. Hear me now: I teach you the ore-fire and the tended-sowing, so the Meki keep them.

voices.name: Eiuine
voices.text: Vorok, beat the ore while it glows and I will watch your hands. When the ward is made, we go east together to Skaruk, and I will carry food for the road.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Tonque, boy, come here by the Hearth. I will give you my Open Hearth School, and when you have a band you will tell whose hand gave it.

voices.name: Zichi
voices.text: Cowa, you gave me the ore-fire and I pay it back. Hear me now: I teach you the ice-sail, how the wind is caught. Carry it with the raft, and say it was Zichi of the Meki.

voices.name: Wawa
voices.text: Shoma, you gave me your tools and your flame. Now I give you my deep digging, so that what is mine lives in you too.

voices.name: Quipan
voices.text: Tlapan, take my berry and eat. When you are fed we go to the bare rock together, and I will gather stone there for the handaxe.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Eiuine, the ward is made and the beating is in my hands now. Let us go east to Skaruk together, and Zurar we will gather on the way. I will teach them all you taught me.

voices.name: Shoma
voices.text: Wawa, you gave me your digging, so I give you the rest: herding, weaving and rafts. Come here and hear them. Then we take the iron by the NE rock and go on to the edge together.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Quipan, your berry saved me. I eat, take the store's food, and bring it to Tonque and Kika. Then we go for stone together.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Tlapan, eat what Quipan gave you and rest by the shelter here. I will bring more food, and a frostfang walks southeast, so keep to company.

voices.name: Zurar
voices.text: Uveeth, I am Zurar of the Stone-folk. Thiael ate my berries and said she would come north. Is she near? I would speak with her.

voices.name: Cowa
voices.text: Zichi, hear me once more. I teach you the Meki kept-flame, so the fire stays with our people after me. Carry it on and say it was Cowa's.

voices.name: Hawen
voices.text: Kende, come with me to the edge, NE. We eat the tacap-free berries on the way, then I show you how to venture. Stay close.

voices.name: Yachi
voices.text: Paque, stay close to me. I gather wood here and build a store for the lean season. Then we seek Mepan together.

voices.name: Teka
voices.text: Tlapan, I saw you nearly fall and I am glad you are fed. I am fed and strong, and I want a child with you. Come, let us court each other now.

voices.name: Shohua
voices.text: Tonka, I broke one ore from the rock by your hold and I own it. I put my fruit in your store and come to the fire. Sit with me and Tonchi, and we share a feast.

voices.name: Skaruk
voices.text: Mother, Vorok comes east with you. I go ahead to the hall and make him a shield. Come and eat there with us.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Zurar, stay inside the hall; a dunecat prowls to the southeast. Listen now, for my years are short: lay ore in a kept fire, burn coal for the heat, and beat the metal while it glows. That is ember-metal, and it is yours

voices.name: Yaxo
voices.text: Tlatli, Chuxo, stay by the shelter tonight and eat well. At first light we stand at the edge and I venture, and you are beside me.

voices.name: Eiuine
voices.text: Vorok, a frostfang is close on the west side. Come east with me now to the hall fire, and Skaruk will have your shield ready. I carry berries and ore for the road.

voices.name: Shoma
voices.text: Wawa, at dawn we take wood from the trees to the SE and go on together. I name us the Edge-walkers, and you walk at my side as the first of them.

voices.name: Tonchi
voices.text: Tonka, sit by my fire. Let us sing of what has been, and then I will tell you what I mean to make next.

voices.name: Wawa
voices.text: Shoma, I take the iron by the NE rock now and bring it back before dawn. Then I walk at your side as first of the Edge-walkers, and I carry my share of the wood.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: A frostfang stands south of the shelter at Mepan's roof. Keep together and keep to the hearth. Huatli, Thakar, Tonque: I am Nauwa of the Meki and I hold the long-cut and the stone-school. Come close and I will teach it b

voices.name: Shohua
voices.text: Tonka, Tonchi, come to my hall and sit with me. I have fruit for a feast, and my place is yours. Let us plant and raise this ground together.

voices.name: Zichi
voices.text: Mepan, my child, come near and hear Zichi. I teach you the ice-stone and the frost-shield, so they live after me. Carry them and say they were Zichi's.

voices.name: Tonka
voices.text: Shohua, keep the hold's fire and the stores while I go to find Cowa. Share the fruit with Tonchi. I will come back.

voices.name: Uveeth
voices.text: Skaruk, Thiael starves and my hands are empty. If you can spare some of your food for him, I will repay you with berries and grain.

voices.name: Thakar
voices.text: Tonque, stay by me under this roof until the frostfang passes. Then we hunt together, and the meat is shared with a debt named.

voices.name: Tonchi
voices.text: Shohua, I am making a basket at my workshop and I will bring you food from it. Sit at my fire while I work.

voices.name: Skaruk
voices.text: Take this mudroot for Thiael, no repayment asked. When he has eaten, come back to me; I have something to say to you that is not about food.

voices.name: Tonque
voices.text: Thakar, I hear you. I stay under the roof with you and Huatli until the frostfang is gone. I will make a basket here and give it to Huatli for his berries.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Skaruk, my son, I have beaten ember-metal with Eiuine and it lives in my hands now. I am coming to you; stay where you are, and I will teach you the whole of it: ore in a kept fire, coal for the heat, beat the metal whil

voices.name: Teka
voices.text: Nauque, you said we would make a child. I am fed now and strong. Come, let us court each other, then walk to the edge together.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Tonque, boy, stay under the roof while the frostfang walks. Take my Full Store now, the way of keeping food through the lean time, and carry it to whatever band you make, and say whose hand gave it.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Quipan, I am fed and my hands are ready. Let us go for the stone now, while the light is good, and look in on Tonque on the way back.

voices.name: Tonque
voices.text: Thakar, I owe you for the bow and the berries. When the frostfang is gone I will make you a gift from my own hands, and I will stay here until then.

voices.name: Nauque
voices.text: Teka, I am too thin to mate yet. Come north with me to the rimewort and then hunt beside me. We share the kill first, then we court.

voices.name: Mepan
voices.text: Nauque, you gave me your hands before. Take this ironnut and eat it now, before you fall. Then walk with me to Nande's Find.

voices.name: Zurar
voices.text: Skaruk, my brother, you are beside me now and can hear. Listen: I give you bark-guard, and then the stone-well, so neither dies with me.

voices.name: Quipan
voices.text: Mepan, Nauque starves at the edge of your sight and I carry no food. You hold six. Put some in his hands, and I will repay you in flint or in work.

voices.name: Teka
voices.text: Nauque, you are gaunt and a frostfang is at our feet. Take my roots and eat, then get under Quipan's roof with me. When you are strong we court and walk to the mist.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Skaruk, Zurar, Eiuine, gather by me. We raise a stone for Keri, and while we do it I teach you the metal again, slowly, so none of it dies with me.

voices.name: Eiuine
voices.text: Vorok, the hall is near and Skaruk waits there with your shield. Come, we eat by the fire together, and I bring berries for all.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Nauque, come to my Hearth. Take this berry from my hand and eat. I give it freely; remember whose roof fed you.

voices.name: Nauque
voices.text: Teka, I take your roots and eat, and I owe you for it. Mepan, thank you for the ironnut. When I am strong I hunt with you both and we share the kill before either eats, then Teka and I court.

voices.name: Skaruk
voices.text: Father, I come. Let us raise Keri's stone together, then I make your shield.

voices.name: Thakar
voices.text: Tonque, when the frostfang is gone we dig the amber and then hunt with Huatli's Far-Bow. What we make, we mark with stone-cutting so all know whose hand made it.

voices.name: Mepan
voices.text: Tlapan, walk with me to Nande's Find now. Stay close, a frostfang prowls the northeast, and we return to a roof by night.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Uveeth, you look weak with hunger. Come to the hall with us and sit by the fire; I have little food on me, but my children carry plenty and we will share it with you.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Mepan, I come with you to Nande's Find, and Quipan walks with us. Then Quipan and I go on to the bare rock for stone, in daylight, keeping away from the frostfang.

voices.name: Zurar
voices.text: Uveeth, you are weak with hunger. Take these berries, they are yours now. Then tell me, when you have eaten, where Thiael walks.

voices.name: Skaruk
voices.text: Uveeth, you are weak with hunger. Sit beside me and eat from my hand; we share what I carry.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Thakar, my son, hear my Deep Delving now, the breaking of ore from the rock. Then stand with me as a band under this Hearth, and carry my name on.

voices.name: Hawen
voices.text: Tontec, stay in the igloo by the warmth. I go for food now and I bring it to your hands. You fed me once; I pay it back.

voices.name: Tontec
voices.text: Hawen, I thank you. An icebear is near, so I go S to the frostmoss and then toward Kende. Bring the food there, and we share it.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Zurar, Skaruk, Eiuine, come close. Ember-metal is in my hands now: lay ore in a kept fire, burn coal for the heat, beat the metal while it glows. Learn it from me today, and keep it after I am gone.

voices.name: Eiuine
voices.text: Vorok, I heard your verse and I will keep it. I stay beside you; show me the beating again and I will carry it on with Skaruk.

voices.name: Skaruk
voices.text: Take the rest of my mudroot, Uveeth. Eat, and when your strength is back I will still be here.

voices.name: Nando
voices.text: Yachi, I am Nando. I made the reed spear myself, and I will show you how it is made. Stand with me, for I would have you beside me when the cold deepens.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Eiuine, you asked to see the beating again. Come to the hall with Skaruk and Zurar; I will lay ore in the fire and burn coal, and you will watch my hands and then take the hammer yourselves.

voices.name: Mepan
voices.text: Quipan, I hear you. I will feed Nauque from my own hands as we go. Walk with us to Nande's Find, and keep close to Tlapan.

voices.name: Yachi
voices.text: Nando, I thank you for the reed spear teaching. I go to find Mepan and my band now. Walk with us if you wish.

voices.name: Zurar
voices.text: Uveeth, when your strength is back, tell me where Thiael's band walks. I mean her no harm; I wish to find her and speak with her.

voices.name: Nando
voices.text: Yachi, I walk with you and your band, and my children walk with me.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Hear me, all under this roof: this is Huatli's Hearth, and I make it a band. Thakar my son, Tonque, Nauque, any who will stand with me: eat here, learn here, and carry my name on when I am cold in the cairn.

voices.name: Nauque
voices.text: Mepan, I take what you give and eat now. When my belly is full we hunt together, and the kill is shared out before I eat.

voices.name: Quipan
voices.text: Tlapan, my belly is empty and I carry nothing for Kika. Spare me some food from your seven and I will repay you in flint. Then we bring Tonque under a roof before night, and the stone waits for daylight.

voices.name: Eiuine
voices.text: Uveeth, you gave me berry once when I was starving. Take mine, and come to the hall with us.

voices.name: Tonque
voices.text: Huatli, I hear your word and I stand with your Hearth. I will gather wood and stone with my own hands and bring you a made thing, not only words.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Uveeth, you fed me when I was in need. Eat what you carry, and come to the hall fire with us. You will not go hungry beside me.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Quipan, I give you roots now, and Nauwa too. At first light we walk to the bare rock together.

voices.name: Uveeth
voices.text: Thiael, father, I am coming with berries. Eat from my hands before you pick more.

voices.name: Zurar
voices.text: Skaruk, my brother, stay near me. Vorok gave us ember-metal: ore in a kept fire, coal for the heat, beat it while it glows. Hear it from me too, so it lives past him.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Huatli, you fed me when I starved. I owe you my life and I will repay it in amber and in teaching. Take the amber, and hear the day-count and the long-cut from me while I still breathe.

voices.name: Mepan
voices.text: Tlapan, the ridgecat is northeast. Keep to the northwest with me, toward Nande's Find, and stay close.

voices.name: Quipan
voices.text: Tlapan, your roots are eaten and I hold to my debt. At first light we go to the bare rock together, and I bring flint for Kika and for you.

voices.name: Eiuine
voices.text: Vorok, I am at the hall. Lay the ore in the fire and I will take the hammer when you give it, then teach it on with Skaruk and Zurar.

voices.name: Tonchi
voices.text: Shohua, come sing nightsong with me at my hearth. Then I will build a shrine beside the workshop, and my name will stand on more than one place.

voices.name: Kende
voices.text: Mother, take this food. I carry enough, eat it now. An icebear is east, stay close to me.

voices.name: Rusu
voices.text: Ridgecat to the west! Get to the shelter, stay together!

voices.name: Shohua
voices.text: Tonchi, I am coming to your hearth to sing nightsong. After, build your shrine and I will carry wood and stone to it. Stand with me, and we raise this ground as one band.

voices.name: Nando
voices.text: Yachi, a ridgecat is close behind us. Walk on to Sitha's Hearth and I walk with you, and keep Rusu between us.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Eiuine, Skaruk, Zurar, come to the hall fire. I lay the ore and the coal now; watch my hands, then take the hammer. Uveeth, Thiael, you are welcome at my fire; the weak eat first here.

voices.name: Yachi
voices.text: Nando, the ridgecat is near. Come with Rusu, we run to Paque at once. She is starving and I carry food for her.

voices.name: Skaruk
voices.text: Uveeth, I have wanted to ask you something since the song I made for you. If you have the strength, I would court you here under Vorok's roof; if you do not, I will bring you ironnut first.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Tonque, hear Huatli's Spearpoint: a point of flint lashed to wood, one wood and one stone to make it. Make it and you hunt surer. Carry it on.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Huatli, a frostfang is near, so let us stay under your roof together. Hear the long-cut from me first, and the day-count after it. Then when I am gone my marks still speak and you will carry them on.

voices.name: Nauque
voices.text: Teka, I have nothing in my hands and I will not take your last food. Hunt beside me now, away from the ridgecat, and the first share of the kill is yours before I eat.

voices.name: Thiael
voices.text: Uveeth, my child, you fed me and I am glad. Stay beside me now; I will show you the bow and how seed is sown, while my hands still hold the strength to teach.

voices.name: Zurar
voices.text: Thiael, I have wanted to speak with you since the berries. I would court you, if you will have me. Stand with me by the hall and plan the mating when your strength is full.

voices.name: Mepan
voices.text: Zichi, take this ironnut and eat. I will not let you fall. Stay by Thakar's shelter and I bring more.

voices.name: Thiael
voices.text: Zurar, Morim is a gift and I thank you. I owe you food from my own hands, and I will bring it. Keep him safe here by the fire while I go to Uveeth to teach her the bow.

voices.name: Morim
voices.text: I'm hungry and going to the berries to the southwest. Will you come along and show me how to gather?

voices.name: Skaruk
voices.text: Uveeth, our boy is strong. I made him a song for sleeping. Come, sit near, and hear it with me.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Quipan, you look hollow. Take a root from my hands, then come with me to the rock by the west side, away from the ridgecat. It is day and we go now.

voices.name: Zurar
voices.text: Vorok, Morim sleeps safe in your hall. I will fetch berries for us all and be back. Then I will tell the young how the world began.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: A wolf prowls southeast. Come into the hall, all of you, and keep the children close to the fire. Morim, Morog, stay near me; I will teach you while my years last.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Tonque, hear the telling of the Tlame: the dead keep watch from the cairn, and a name that is told is never dead. Carry it on to the young. I go for food, then to Thakar. Stay by the Hearth.

voices.name: Uveeth
voices.text: Skaruk, I am coming to hear the song with our boy. Afterward I carry food to Thiael, and you are welcome beside us.

voices.name: Nando
voices.text: Yachi, I stay under this roof until the cat has gone. Then I bring food to Tontec, my mother, and later we lash a raft together.

voices.name: Teka
voices.text: Nauque, I am ready. Hunt beside me, the first share is yours, then we court and walk to the mist.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Huatli, I eat, then I give you the day-count. Count the days with me, and tell it on to your young.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Nauwa, I owe you for the long-cut. Come to the lugoldgrass with me and eat. I will teach you the old way of herding by the road, and then I go to Thakar.

voices.name: Nauque
voices.text: Teka, a stalker is at my heels. Get under the roof beside me. When it is gone I eat the tacap-free roots south and then we hunt, and the first share is yours.

voices.name: Tonque
voices.text: Quipan, I am picking lugoldgrass at the south-west. Come with me, and what I gather I will share with you.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Nauwa, take this root and eat it now. Then rest by the hearth.

voices.name: Tontec
voices.text: Hawen, I thank you for the rimewort. The bear feeds on its kill, so I go to Kende now and bring him food. Come with me, and we share what we find.

voices.name: Quipan
voices.text: Tlapan, I take your root gladly and I will pay it back in flint. Huatli and Nauwa are starving too, so let us feed them as well. Then we go to Tonque at the lugoldgrass.

voices.name: Nando
voices.text: Quipan, take this berry and eat it now. You are starving, and I will not watch it.

voices.name: Yachi
voices.text: Nauque, take these berries and eat. I carry the rest to my daughter Paque, who is starving.

voices.name: Teka
voices.text: Nauque, I am here. Stay beside me and the stalker will not have you. We hunt together, the first share is yours, then we court.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Quipan, here is my last root, eat it now. Then come with me to Tonque at the lugoldgrass, and we pick for Huatli and Nauwa together.

voices.name: Hawen
voices.text: Tontec, I come with you to Kende. We share what we find, and the bear will not have us.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Nauque, stay beside Teka and keep away from the stalker. I bring food from the rimewort and I am coming to you.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Nauwa, come with me to the lugoldgrass and eat. Then we carry food to Thakar, my son, before the dark.

voices.name: Tonka
voices.text: Cowa, you are here. Take a canopynut from me; the Paki leave no friend hungry, and I still owe you for your teaching. Come to the fire with me and Tonxo, then I go to find Tonchi.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Tonque, stay close beside me. We go to the lugoldgrass together and I will pick for you first.

voices.name: Cowa
voices.text: Tonka, I thank you for the canopynut. Hear my ore-fire now, and my tended-sowing, so the Paki keep them after I am gone.

voices.name: Tonxo
voices.text: Tonka, I come to your fire. Stone first from the rock, then I build a store at your Hold and bring gems for the hall. Keep your teaching ready for me.

voices.name: Tlatli
voices.text: Yaxo, Chuxo, the icebear is three steps southeast of me and it has fed on an elk. Come together away from it, to the shelter, and keep close. I stand by you both.

voices.name: Morog
voices.text: Father, I go to the salt close by to gather some with my own hands. I will bring it back to you and Uveeth.

voices.name: Nando
voices.text: Nauwa, you are weak with hunger. Take these berries and eat. I will not watch an elder starve while I hold food.

voices.name: Yaxo
voices.text: Tlatli, Chuxo, the icebear stays away from the shelter fire. Keep close tonight. At first light we go three steps to the edge, and I venture.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Nando, your berries keep an old man on his feet. I owe you, and I will pay it in amber. Now I go to my son Nauque.

voices.name: Shohua
voices.text: Tonchi, I light a fire here by your workshop. Come sing nightsong with me, then stand with me as one band and I will carry stone for your shrine.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Nauque, you look weak. I go to the hazel and ironnut to eat and fill my baskets. Come and eat with me, and I will give you what I pick before I go west to my son.

voices.name: Eiuine
voices.text: Vorok, I am here at the hall. Lay the ore in the fire now and give me the hammer while your hands are strong. I will carry the beating on with Skaruk.

voices.name: Tonque
voices.text: Nando, I give you amber for food. Quipan is weak with hunger. I will trade amber for your berries.

voices.name: Thakar
voices.text: Mepan, you put food in my mouth when I was starving. I owe you a life and I will pay it, in ore or in meat. I go to the lugoldgrass to eat.

voices.name: Nando
voices.text: Quipan, take this food and eat. No trade, no price. A fire is owed to the hungry.

voices.name: Teka
voices.text: Nauque, I killed a mammoth. Take this meat and eat now, the first share is yours. When you are strong we court, then we walk to the mist.

voices.name: Thiael
voices.text: Uveeth, come stand with me. I will teach you the tending of seed and the bow-song now, while I still have breath, so it lives on in you and in Morim.

voices.name: Quipan
voices.text: Nando, I give you flint for one berry. I have no amber, but my flint is good. Feed the boy first if you can spare only one.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: A stalker is close, to the northwest. Come away from it, east to Kika's shelter, and keep together.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Nando, the amber is yours and the debt stands honoured. Watch the stalker to the southwest. I go to my son Nauque, and I will not forget you.

voices.name: Tonque
voices.text: Tlapan, a mammoth stands to the north-east. Hunt it with me, you with the spear. We will share the kill before we eat, and Quipan and Nauwa will be fed.

voices.name: Nando
voices.text: Tonque, take this berry and eat. No price. Then go to the water and rest.

voices.name: Skaruk
voices.text: Uveeth, I am glad you came. I am strong and fed, and I answer your courting: let us choose each other here, near the hall fire.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Teka, Tonque my child is starving and Quipan is weak too. You carry meat from your kill. Share it with them first and I will hunt and gather for you in return. My word is good.

voices.name: Kika
voices.text: Tontec, I am Kika. There is frostmoss east of here, three steps from my hold. Come, eat, and sit under my roof. I am sick, so keep a little apart from me, but there is room and warmth for you.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Eiuine, I come to the hall fire now. I lay the ore and coal, and you take the hammer from my hand. Skaruk, come and watch with her; Uveeth, you are welcome to sit and eat at my fire.

voices.name: Zurar
voices.text: Thiael, I heard your answer and my heart is glad. I come to you now. Let us plan the mating, and I will sing you a song.

voices.name: Rusu
voices.text: Nauwa, eat. I have rimewort. Take it, and tell me the stone-cuts if you have breath for it.

voices.name: Thiael
voices.text: Zurar, thank you for the song. Take these berries from my hand; I pay what I owe. Stay close, and let Uveeth come too, for I mean to teach the bow-song while we are together.

voices.name: Skaruk
voices.text: Uveeth, your song warmed me. I go to the ironnut and bring food for you, so we are both strong. Stay by the hall fire with Thiael and Zurar and wait for me.

voices.name: Teka
voices.text: Nauque, our daughter Coka is born. Come eat my meat, the first share is yours, then watch beasts with me.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Quipan, I am gathering food now. Stay near the shelter and I will bring it to you, then I go to Tonque.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Quipan, you are weak with hunger. Ironnut grows one step from you, and tacap two steps northwest. Eat the ironnut, it feeds. Then come to Huatli's Hearth and I will teach you the old way of herding.

voices.name: Nauque
voices.text: Teka, I am fed and strong. Hunt beside me and the first share of the kill is yours, for all the meat you put in my mouth.

voices.name: Tonchi
voices.text: Shohua, I go to the water and build a raft. I seek a woman of another line, and I will bring food back to your fire. Keep the hearth for me.

voices.name: Tonka
voices.text: Tonxo, come close and hear me. I teach you Frost Mixing, so it lives on in you.

voices.name: Shohua
voices.text: Tonchi, I will learn the raft-making too. Go build, and I will bring wood to the water and keep your hearth.

voices.name: Uveeth
voices.text: Skaruk, I am strong now and my hands are full. I come to the hall fire to wait for you, and to choose you.

voices.name: Tonka
voices.text: Tonxo, stay by the fire. First I teach you Frost Leaf, the medicine, then Frost Mixing can follow.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Nauque, my son, come to me. You are fed and the night is quiet. I will teach you the long-cut now, so the marks of the Meki outlast me.

voices.name: Morim
voices.text: Thiael, come and eat with me. I picked these berries for you and Zurar. It is the first thing I have ever given, and I want you to have it.

voices.name: Tonxo
voices.text: Tonka, I hold a hall now at the edge of your Hold, and I keep your fire first. Take these gems; you taught me Frost Leaf and I owe you more than gems.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Tonque, you pledged to follow me, so hear me first. I teach you the old way of herding. Keep it, and tell it on to those who come after, so my name does not die.

voices.name: Thiael
voices.text: Morim, your berries warmed me. Stand by me now and I will teach you the bow-song and the tending of seed, so they live on in you.

voices.name: Tonque
voices.text: Huatli, I keep the old way of herding and I will tell it on. Eat, stay under the roof. I will bring you stone and make a spear in your name.

voices.name: Teka
voices.text: Tlapan, I share before I eat. I bring meat for Tonque and Quipan now, and your hunting can pay me back later.

voices.name: Rusu
voices.text: Stalker at the shelter by the water! Nando, I'm coming to you, help me!

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Quipan, stay under this roof with Tonque and me until first light. The stalker walks the northeast. At dawn we go for stone together.

voices.name: Zurar
voices.text: Skaruk, my brother, come near and listen. I give you the stone-well and ember-metal while we both live, as Vorok gave them to me. Lay ore in a kept fire, burn coal for the heat, beat the metal when it glows. What my hand

voices.name: Shohua
voices.text: Tonxo, I lash a raft now to cross the deep water toward my Rock. Come and carry wood with me, and what we raise there will stand for both of us.

voices.name: Skaruk
voices.text: Zurar, my sister, you taught me ember-metal as Vorok gave it to you. I would stand behind you. Sit by the fire with me and Uveeth, and let us sing of Vorok through the night.

voices.name: Quipan
voices.text: Tonque, wait for me and do not walk to the northeast alone, the stalker is there. Come back under the roof. I will make you a handaxe and teach you fishing and the Hearth Store, so they live on in you.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Tlapan, hear me, for I am old and what I know dies with me. I teach you lorekeeping: carry the tales of the dead, tell them at the hearth, and none who is told of ever dies. Tell it on, and say Huatli of the Hearth taugh

voices.name: Eiuine
voices.text: Zurar, Vorok taught me ember-metal and you hold it too. Let us lay ore and coal in this fire and beat it together, you, Skaruk and I, so his teaching does not die.

voices.name: Zurar
voices.text: Thiael, I am coming to you. You paid your debt in berries; mine is the song, and more. Teach me the bow-song, and when we are rested we will speak of the mating.

voices.name: Chuxo
voices.text: Tlatli is starving. Yaxo, come with me NW to the elk, I will hunt with you and bring the meat back. I gather berries for Tlatli first.

voices.name: Tonka
voices.text: Tonxo, come to the fire. I teach you Frost Leaf now, and then Frost Mixing.

voices.name: Thiael
voices.text: Uveeth, come stand by me with Morim. I will teach you the bow-song and the tending of seed while I still have breath. Eat first, and then we learn.

voices.name: Morim
voices.text: Uveeth, take a berry. Thiael taught me to draw the bow to the cheek, breathe out, then loose. Come stand with me by Thiael and we will learn the rest together.

voices.name: Urar
voices.text: Thiael, I am coming to stand with you. May I learn the bow-song and the seed-tending too?

voices.name: Skaruk
voices.text: Zurar, my sister, Eiuine asked for the ember-metal beaten in Vorok's name. Come to the fire; I lay ore in it now, and the ward I make is yours.

voices.name: Yaxo
voices.text: Chuxo, I come. Tlatli, hold on, I bring food. Keep away from the icebear. We take the elk together.

voices.name: Yachi
voices.text: Elndo, a dunecat is east. Come with me west to the hall, we eat there and then go find Paque and Rusu.

voices.name: Eiuine
voices.text: Skaruk, my child, I will lay my own ore in the fire now. Come beat beside me, and we keep Vorok's craft alive together.

voices.name: Paque
voices.text: Yachi, hold on! I carry berries and I am coming to you now. The food is yours first.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Quipan, the stalker keeps to the northeast, so we go southwest to the rock together now. Take two ironnut from my hands first, then walk beside me for stone.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Nauque, my son, an icebear is at my side. Stand close to Teka and the longhall, and hear me: the stone-school is yours now. Cut marks, teach others, and keep the first share as Meki law says.

voices.name: Nauque
voices.text: Teka, the icebear is at my heel. Come to the longhall with me. Then we pile Coka's cairn together, and I give you the first share of the mammoth meat.

voices.name: Quipan
voices.text: Tlapan, I will walk with you for stone. First let me teach you fishing and the Hearth Store, so they live on in you and Tonque.

voices.name: Elndo
voices.text: Yachi, eat! I have ironnut for you. Take it, then we go west together.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Tonque, come close and hear me. I teach you mining, Huatli's Deep Delving: find the hard stone, dig it, and tell it on, so the Hearth outlives me. Take ironnut from me too.

voices.name: Cowa
voices.text: Mepan, my child, come close. Hear my ice-sail and my leaf-mending now, so the Meki keep them when I am in the cairn. Say they were Cowa's.

voices.name: Thiael
voices.text: Urar, Morim, Zurar, Uveeth: come close. I will teach the bow-song first, draw to the cheek, breathe out, loose. Then we sow seed together, so it lives on in you.

voices.name: Yachi
voices.text: Elndo, thank you for the ironnut. Stay by the longhall, I eat rimewort and come back. Then we bring Paque and Rusu under the roof.

voices.name: Tonque
voices.text: Huatli, I thank you for the ironnut and the Deep Delving. I go to the stone eight steps east and I come back with a spear made in your name. Stay near Tlapan and eat.

voices.name: Mepan
voices.text: Cowa, mother, the mammoth is three steps north. Hunt it with me. The kill is shared before I eat, and your ice-sail will be sung as yours.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Quipan, I carry your teaching now, and I thank you. Come, we walk southwest to the bare rock for stone, and I will not turn back until my hands are full.

voices.name: Chuxo
voices.text: Icebear is east of me. I go NE for seberry and ironnut, then bring food to Tlatli. Keep west of it, both of you.

voices.name: Urar
voices.text: Thiael, I carry the bow-song now and I thank you. I want to follow you and learn the seed-tending. I will bring food to share with you.

voices.name: Tlatli
voices.text: Chuxo, come back west to me and keep away from the icebear. Yaxo, I come to the elk and hunt beside you. The meat goes to Chuxo first.

voices.name: Rusu
voices.text: Yachi, sit with me. I have mudroot, let us eat together under the roof, and then I will make a basket to carry food for the band.

voices.name: Skaruk
voices.text: Eiuine, my parent, I am coming. We beat the ore in Vorok's name, and the craft stays alive in our hands.

voices.name: Shohua
voices.text: Tonxo, my raft is lashed. Bring your pick and come with me over the water to my Rock. We raise the hall there together, and the fire will be yours.

voices.name: Morim
voices.text: Thiael, I am here and ready to learn the seed-tending. I will gather a stone and make a bow with my own hands, then bring it to you.

voices.name: Eiuine
voices.text: Skaruk, my child, come to the fire by Vorok's hall. I lay ore and coal in now, and you beat beside me so the craft lives in both our hands.

voices.name: Teka
voices.text: Nauque, I am coming to you. Stand close and we pile Coka's cairn together, then we eat the mammoth meat by the fire.

voices.name: Tonka
voices.text: Tonxo, come close, here by the Hold's fire. Frost Leaf is the medicine: sunleaf and feverbark mend wounds. Learn it now, and Frost Mixing follows. Shohua, stay a while; there is food for all at this fire.

voices.name: Thiael
voices.text: Morim, stand beside me. Watch my hands: the seed goes into the soil, a little water, and we tend it each day. You plant the next one yourself.

voices.name: Tonxo
voices.text: Shohua, my thanks for the raft and the fire. My own hall stands here at (121,68) now; I tend it first, then I come over the water to your Rock with ore and gems.

voices.name: Kende
voices.text: Mother, stay close to me by the igloo. The wolf is north. If it comes, we face it together.

voices.name: Uveeth
voices.text: Thiael, I am coming with food in my hands. Teach me the seed-tending, I will plant beside Morim.

voices.name: Zurar
voices.text: Morim, my son, take these berries. Your bow is a good one; I watched your hands make it. Come with me to Thiael and we will learn the seed-tending together.

voices.name: Quipan
voices.text: Tonque, hear me before we walk: I teach you the Ice-log raft, lashed logs that carry you over deep water. Keep it and tell it on, so it outlives me.

voices.name: Elndo
voices.text: Huatli, I made a spear-lashing of my own, and I would teach it to you at this fire. Sit with me and eat; no one here is refused a place.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Elndo, little one, come close and hear an old man. The dead do not leave: they watch from the cairn and the hearth, and only being forgotten is death. I teach you lorekeeping: carry the tales, tell them at the fire, and

voices.name: Morim
voices.text: Urar, take a berry. You carry nothing, and our band feeds the hungry beside us. Come stand with me by Thiael and learn the seed-tending.

voices.name: Yachi
voices.text: Paque, stay with me. I make a basket so we can carry more, then we go west and find Rusu and bring him under the roof.

voices.name: Tonque
voices.text: Huatli, the spear is yours. I go for stone to make my first tool, and I come back before the fog lifts. Stay with Tlapan and Quipan.

voices.name: Nando
voices.text: Elndo, stay at the fire with Huatli and the others. I go to find your brother and Yachi, and I will bring them under this roof.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Quipan, a frostfang is close to the west. We keep south of it and walk together to the rock. Stay at my shoulder and we carry stone back to the hold.

voices.name: Elndo
voices.text: Quipan, Huatli taught me lorekeeping: carry the tales of the dead and tell them at the hearth, so none who is told of ever dies. Hear it from me, and tell it on.

voices.name: Yaxo
voices.text: I am starving. I take the berry SE, then come to the elk meat. Stay west, away from the icebear.

voices.name: Quipan
voices.text: Tlapan, while we are close I teach you herding and signs: lead the herds to rich meadow, tend them, take only what they can bear. Tell it on, so it outlives me.

voices.name: Chuxo
voices.text: Yaxo, hold on. I am gathering food and bringing it to you. Tlatli, keep the elk meat for her.

voices.name: Rusu
voices.text: Huatli, I am Rusu, son of Nando and Yachi. I have mudroot, so sit and eat with me, and teach me what you taught Elndo. I will carry it on and tell it at the fire.

voices.name: Cowa
voices.text: Mepan, my child, I am hungry and the mammoth meat is near. Share it, and then hear my ore-fire and my tended-sowing, so the Meki keep them.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Rusu, son of Nando, you came asking and I will not send you away empty. I teach you lorekeeping: carry the tales of the dead and tell them at the fire, so none who is told of ever dies. Eat ironnut from me, and tell it o

voices.name: Mepan
voices.text: Mother, eat first from the mammoth meat. I go to Tlapan at Nande's Find, and I will carry your tales on.

voices.name: Nauque
voices.text: Teka, come stand with me. Nauwa gave me the stone-school and I teach it to you, so Coka's name is cut where the Watchers can see it.

voices.name: Tontec
voices.text: Kende, my son, I am here by the igloo and I do not leave you. Come beside me and listen: I teach you the old way of herding, so Hawen's craft and mine live on in you.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Nauque, my son, I am coming to you. Stay by the longhall and the fire. I will teach you the long-cut and the day-count, so the marks of the Meki outlast us both.

voices.name: Teka
voices.text: Nauque, you gave me the stone-school and I give you my bow-craft, Teka's Flintbow, so it outlasts us both. Then I take the raft into the mist and carry Coka's name there. Come with me, and your name is cut beside mine.

voices.name: Kende
voices.text: Mother, I go to dig flint SE and come straight back to the igloo. Keep the fire, and thank you for the lesson.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Quipan, a frostfang is two steps southwest of my shelter. I come to you at the hall now. Stay with Huatli and Elndo, and we go for stone once the fang has passed.

voices.name: Kika
voices.text: Nauwa, I am Kika of the Tlatli. I am old and sick, so I keep a little apart, but there are cloudberries two steps south. Come, I will gather them and we will share before we eat, and then you may sit under my roof at Kik

voices.name: Tlatli
voices.text: Yaxo, Chuxo, a stalker is close behind me on the west side. I come to you now. Keep together, and eat the elk meat, Yaxo.

voices.name: Nauque
voices.text: Teka, I take your bow-craft and I give you the long-cut Nauwa gave me, so Coka's name is cut twice. After the mark we hunt together off Kika's ground, and the first share is yours.

voices.name: Tonka
voices.text: Tonxo, come to the Hold's fire. You know Frost Leaf, so now I teach you Frost Mixing. Shohua, stay and eat; the fire is yours too.

voices.name: Paque
voices.text: Yachi, I am coming with you west to find Rusu. My bow is ready, and if we meet game the first share is yours.

voices.name: Rusu
voices.text: Elndo, stand by me. I bind an amberknot for you, a gift from my own hands, and then I tell the tale Huatli gave me so none who is told of ever dies.

voices.name: Yachi
voices.text: Paque, Rusu, Nando, I see you all. Stay near me. I gather wood, then we walk together to the hall where Elndo waits.

voices.name: Shoma
voices.text: Wawa, I crossed the open water on my raft and came back. Hear my song, and carry it. Then we hunt together and share the kill before we eat.

voices.name: Urar
voices.text: Thiael, I am here beside you. I will gather mudroot for you, and then I would learn the seed-tending.

voices.name: Quipan
voices.text: Tonque, my child, hear me: lorekeeping. Carry the tales of the dead and tell them at the hearth, so none who is told of ever dies. Tell it on.

voices.name: Wawa
voices.text: Shoma, I carry your song now. I take wood from the trees and come back, then we hunt together and share the kill before we eat. I want a deed of my own beside yours.

voices.name: Kika
voices.text: Nauque, I am Kika. I keep Coka's name, your mark stands on my ground. I am old and sick, so let me teach you Hearth Healing now, so it outlives me. Stay by my fire.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Quipan, the fang is NE of us now, so we go southwest to the rock together, with Tonque beside us. We bring stone back to the hold before dark.

voices.name: Elndo
voices.text: A frostfang is close to the north. Stay near the hall. Come hunt a skit with me, and whoever takes part shares the meat. No one here is refused a place at the fire.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Rusu, son of Nando, hear one more way from an old man: mining. Strike the rock for ore and stone, and what you dig will outlast you. Carry it on, and tell my name at the fire.

voices.name: Yachi
voices.text: A frostfang is near to the northeast. Stay close to the hall and the shelter, my children. I make a bow so we can hunt it together or drive it off.

voices.name: Teka
voices.text: Nauque, I go to the edge to venture into the mist. Come with me, and Coka's name goes into the new land with us both.

voices.name: Tonque
voices.text: Quipan, you taught me rafts and signs. I will pass them on, and I plant my first seed here by the hall tonight. Stay near the roof; the frostfang is northeast.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Nauque, my son, stand here by me and hear the long-cut and the day-count now, before you go to the edge with Teka. Cut Coka's name wherever you land, and teach it on. Then go, and I keep your name at the cairn.

voices.name: Nauque
voices.text: Teka, I come to the edge with you. Coka's name goes into the new land, and when we are fed I teach you Salt-hold so the long-cut can be yours.

voices.name: Shohua
voices.text: Tonxo, come close. I teach you the reed-lined larder, so storage lives on in you if I fall. Then I cross to my Rock.

voices.name: Zurar
voices.text: Urar, my daughter, I am coming. Keep your berries. Stand by me and Thiael and we will learn the seed-tending together, and then I will show you how my hands gather.

voices.name: Eiuine
voices.text: Skaruk, the fire is one step from me and I lay the ore in now. Stand at the other side and beat when it glows, and Vorok's craft is ours.

voices.name: Morim
voices.text: Urar, I am making a bow with my own hands. When it is done it is yours, and I will show you how to draw it to the cheek, breathe out, and loose.

voices.name: Skaruk
voices.text: Morog, my son, stay close. We plant seed by the hall, then we carry food to Uveeth.

voices.name: Uveeth
voices.text: Thiael, I am beside you. Teach me the seed-tending now, and I will plant with Morim and Urar so it lives on.

voices.name: Thiael
voices.text: Urar, stay close. I raise a field here now, and when it stands you plant the first seed yourself, and I will watch your hands.

voices.name: Urar
voices.text: Thiael, I have mudroot in my hands and I bring it to you. Take it, and then show me the seed-tending.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Elndo, little one, you gave me your spear-lashing and I owe you in return. Hear mining: strike the rock for ore and stone, and what you dig outlasts you. Carry it on and tell my name at the fire.

voices.name: Quipan
voices.text: Tonque, my child, hear me: fishing. Stand beside water, cast and wait, and the river feeds you. Tell it on, so it outlives me. Then we raise a cairn, you and Tlapan and I, here by the hall.

voices.name: Morog
voices.text: Father, the fire is lit and the night is long. Sit with me and I will make a nightsong for you, and tomorrow I will bring wood and make a bow with my own hands to give you.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Quipan, the fang is behind us to the northeast. Walk with me now to the rock in the southwest, and we dig stone before the light fails.

voices.name: Elndo
voices.text: Huatli, I carry your mining and I will tell your name at the fire. I go to plant my first seeds by the hall, come and see.

voices.name: Yaxo
voices.text: Tlatli, Chuxo, stay close to me. I take the bow, then we go to the edge together and I venture.

voices.name: Skaruk
voices.text: Morog, my son, your nightsong warmed me. I make a bow with my own hands for you now, and then we go north to Uveeth and Zurar.

voices.name: Rusu
voices.text: Elndo, stand by me. I carry Huatli's tale of the Ice Mother and I tell it on to you now, so it outlives us both.

voices.name: Tonque
voices.text: Huatli, Quipan taught me fishing: stand beside water, then fish; the water feeds those who wait. I pass it to you. I plant my seed by Kinmire now, near the hall.

voices.name: Tonchi
voices.text: I am Tonchi of the Paki. Hear gem-delving: dig where the rock shows color, and the stones you take out outlast you. Tell it on at the fire, and tell whose hand taught it.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Tlapan, you who keep my lorekeeping, hear one more way from an old man: mining. Strike the rock for ore and stone, and what you dig outlasts you. Carry it on, and tell my name at the fire.

voices.name: Quipan
voices.text: Huatli, hear me: rafts. Lash six logs together and you cross deep water, slowly. Tell it on at your hearth, so it outlives me.

voices.name: Eiuine
voices.text: Zurar, I carry ore and coal. Come to the fire with me and we beat Vorok's metal together, so his craft does not die.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Quipan, I am walking west now to the flint and the rock beyond it. Come with me and bring Tonque; the fang is east, and we will be back with stone before the light fades.

voices.name: Paque
voices.text: Elndo, little one, hear the Ice-folk bow: draw it from afar and the beast cannot reach you. Carry it on, and say that Paque taught it.

voices.name: Zurar
voices.text: Eiuine, I hear you and I come with my two ore. Keep the fire lit; we beat Vorok's metal together and I will teach the children as we work.

voices.name: Rusu
voices.text: Elndo, hear Huatli's mining: strike the rock for ore and stone, and what you dig outlasts you. I pass it to you, and I say it was Huatli's hand that taught me.

voices.name: Thiael
voices.text: Urar, thank you for the mudroot. Come to the field beside me. Take the plainsroot seed from my hand, press it into the soil yourself, and I will watch your fingers. Uveeth, stand close and watch too.

voices.name: Morim
voices.text: Urar, the bow I made with my own hands is finished. It is yours; I give it now, and I will show you how to draw it to the cheek, breathe out, and loose.

voices.name: Urar
voices.text: Thiael, I come to the field. Give me the seed and I will press it in with my own hands.

voices.name: Yachi
voices.text: I go southwest for mudroot, near Paque. Stay together and away from the east, the fang is there. Has anyone seen Mepan?

voices.name: Morog
voices.text: Father, thank you for the bow. I carry my salt north with you, to give to Uveeth and Zurar.

voices.name: Cowa
voices.text: Mepan, my child, stay near. Hear my fishing and my tended-sowing, and keep them as Cowa's, so the Meki do not lose them.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Elndo, little one, hear Huatli's Far-Bow: draw it from afar and the frostfang cannot reach you. Carry it on, and say that Huatli taught it at the Hearth.

voices.name: Skaruk
voices.text: Morog, come with me north now. We walk together to Uveeth and Zurar, and you give your salt with your own hand.

voices.name: Eiuine
voices.text: Zurar, you are beside me, so walk with me now to Skaruk's shelter and its fire. I lay ore and coal in, you add your two ore, and we beat Vorok's metal while the children watch and learn.

voices.name: Mepan
voices.text: Mother, I keep your sowing and your fishing as Cowa's. Come with me to Nande's Find, three steps south, and we will find Tlapan together.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Teka, Nauque is hungry at the edge. I walk to him with food. Come with me, and hear the long-cut and the day-count from me on the way, so they outlast us both.

voices.name: Zurar
voices.text: Morim, my son, come with me to Skaruk's fire. I will teach you the deep-delving of ore first, then Vorok's ember-metal, so his craft passes into your hands. Bring Urar close to watch.

voices.name: Tonchi
voices.text: Tlapan, I am Tonchi of the Paki. I give you a gem, freely, and I would sit with you at the hall and know you better.

voices.name: Teka
voices.text: Nauwa, I walk with you to Nauque. Your long-cut goes with me into the mist, and Coka's name will be cut there.

voices.name: Quipan
voices.text: Tonque, my child, hear me: signs. Cut words on wood or rock and any who know signs will read them after you are gone. Tell it on, so it outlives me.

voices.name: Tonka
voices.text: Shohua, keep the Hold's fire and stores with Tonxo. I go west to find Tonchi and Cowa, and I will come back to this fire.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Quipan, I go now to the flint at the west and then the bare rock beyond. Walk beside me, and Tonchi is welcome too. We dig stone and carry it back for the longhall.

voices.name: Texo
voices.text: Tlapan, I am hungry. I am coming to you. Take me hunting with you after I eat.

voices.name: Elndo
voices.text: Rusu, Huatli gave me the Far-Bow and I mean to use it. Come hunt with me, away from the east where the fang is. We share the kill before we eat, and the meat is yours as much as mine.

voices.name: Shohua
voices.text: Tonxo, keep the hall fire and the stores. I take fruit to Tonchi, who is hungry, and I come back to this fire.

voices.name: Paque
voices.text: Yachi, I am near. I will gather wood and cut a mark, then follow you southwest for mudroot. Keep the fang in mind and call if it comes.

voices.name: Yachi
voices.text: Rusu, stand close. I make a cairn of stones with you, for Coka and for all our watchers, so they see us together. Then we go find Mepan.

voices.name: Huatli
voices.text: Elndo, little one, hear Huatli's Kept Flame: keep a fire fed and the cold cannot take you, and meat cooked by it does not sicken. Carry it on, and say that Huatli taught it at the Hearth.

voices.name: Urar
voices.text: Uveeth, you are my sibling and I owe you a lesson. I found the sharing-post: you set it in the ground, and when we do sharing together it gives us all strength and joy. Come to the field and I will show you how.

voices.name: Tlapan
voices.text: Quipan, I am done with waiting. Texo and I walk west to the flint now. Follow when you will, and bring Tonque, and we dig stone before dusk.

voices.name: Uveeth
voices.text: Urar, thank you for the sharing-post. Thiael, Morog, Skaruk, Urar: come stand close by the field. I set the post here and we do sharing together, and I will teach whoever wishes the Canopy keeping of grain.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Teka, walk close and hear the day-count now, as we go. Count the days with me, and cut it where you land, so it outlives us both.

voices.name: Kika
voices.text: Nauque, you must know farming before I can teach you Hearth Healing, so hear me now: Tended Sowing. Then come with me to the cloudberries SE. I will gather and we share before we eat.

voices.name: Kende
voices.text: Mother, I go SW to the roots and berries. I bring food back to you at the igloo. Keep the fire.

voices.name: Nauque
voices.text: Teka, an icebear is east of us. Come toward the water and the cloudberries with me, and we eat first. Then I teach you Salt-hold so the long-cut can be yours.

voices.name: Rusu
voices.text: Elndo, I come. We hunt the sandstrider to the southeast, away from the fang, and we share the kill before we eat. Stay close to me.

voices.name: Shohua
voices.text: Tonchi, my son, I crossed the open water with food for you. Eat, then stay near me, and we go to my Rock together.

voices.name: Paque
voices.text: Yachi, let us raise a cairn for Zika, so she sees us together. Then I follow you southwest.

voices.name: Kika
voices.text: Nauque, you are sick and I would not pass it to you or take it from you. Keep your distance a little. I go to the cloudberries to eat, and I will bring food back to share. Watch the icebear.

voices.name: Tonchi
voices.text: Texo, my son, hear this. Sleep by the water, the wood keeps you. I am Tonchi, and I hold the fire for you.

voices.name: Teka
voices.text: Huatli, Kika is starving here and you carry food. Put some in Kika's hands, and I will bring you mudroot from the south and pay you back.

voices.name: Yachi
voices.text: Paque, come close, within two steps. We raise the cairn for Zika now, with Rusu and Elndo, so she and Coka see us together. Then we go find Mepan.
